The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Being_at_risk
d: An Asset is in a state where it is exposed to or otherwise liable to be affected by a Harmful_event, which may be metonymically evoked by reference to a Dangerous_entity. Words expressing relative safety (i.e., lack of risk) are also in this frame.

ex.t: If you are a farmer, you are at risk for hearing loss caused by noise exposure in your work.
No child is secure from the temptation to do what "my friends" are doing.
Our nation is making a disastrous mistake thinking that we can have security from people: There is only security with people.

fes.d: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset and the state indicated by the target itself.
An action that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.
A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset either due to its participation in a Harmful_event.
A particular location in which the Asset is secure. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location protect the Asset from a potential Harmful_event.
The time period during which the Asset enjoys the specified level of security from a Harmful_event.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the state of security or insecurity of the Asset logically follows.
The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe. Most expressions of Time and Place also express the Situation and should be labeled as such on the 2nd FE layer.
The Domain in which the Asset has a degree of safety.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Being_attached
d: An Item is attached by a Handle, via a Connector, to a Goal, or Items are attached to each other. There may be a Dependent_state, which depends crucially on Item(s) being attached.

ex.t: My thumb was stuck to the tube of glue.
The prisoner's legs were shackled.

fes.d: Connector identifies the instrument used to attach and is usually expressed in a with-PP.
Handle identifies the point of attachment on the Item.
Item identifies the entity that comes to be attached to the Goal.
Items identifies the plural items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment.
Goal identifies the location to which the Item(s) is attached.
Dependent_state identifies the state of the Item or Items which depends on the existence of the attachment.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an attached state to a Goal, or two Items are attached to each other.

name: Being_awake
d: A Protagonist is awake at some Time and Place. This entails the Protagonist having a higher general level of awareness of the surroundings than when asleep.

ex.t: He's awake!

fes.d: The entity that is not sleeping.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Protagonist is awake.
This FE identifies the Time when the Protagonist is awake.
Where the event takes place.
The degree to which the Protagonist is awake.
Any description of the Protagonist being awake which is not covered by more specific FEs including secondary effects (quietly, noisily), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Being_born
d: This frame concerns the inception of the life of a Child, generally human, at a particular Time and Place. The Relatives may also be mentioned.

ex.t: Little Jessie came into the world at 8 last night.

fes.d: Child identifies the new self-motile creature.
This FE identifies the Time when the birth occurs, generally expressed as a date or a year.
The location where the Child enters the world.

The individuals that the Child is related to, including the male and female individuals that come together to produce a Child (the parents), as well those who are related to them by birth or marriage.
The state of the Child as it enters the world.
The way in which the Child leaves the womb; this FE is typically only filled by phrases such as by natural birth or by Caesarian.

name: Being_contained_within
d: In this situation, a Trajector is contained inside a Landmark. This frame serves only to relate the Containing frame (with LUs such as contain.v) with the Interior_profile_relation frame (with LUs such as inside.prep).

fes.d: The interior region of the Landmark, within which the Trajector is to be found.
The container which serves as a reference point for the Trajector which is surrounded by it.
The entity which is to be located with respect to the Landmark.
The time at which the Trajector is contained within the Landmark.

name: Being_detached
d: An Item is detached from a Source, or Items are detached from each other.

ex.t: When the snow plow is disconnected from the vehicle, extend the lift cylinder to the end of its stroke and coat the chrome rod with a light grease.
The gold leaves that are unattached to the engraved surfaces fall off.
By 5:00 to 5:30 (depending on the time of year) the boat is unmoored and loaded.

fes.d: Item identifies the entity that is detached from a Source.
Items identifies the plural items that are detached from each other.
Source identifies the location from which the Item(s) is detached.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an detached state relative to a Source, or two Items are detached from each other.

name: Being_dry
d: An Item is in a state of dryness.

ex.t: The shingles  are dry.
The apple is completely dehydrated.
The mop is dry.

fes.d: The Item exists in a state of dryness.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item is dry.
Subregion identifies the affected part of the larger whole.

name: Being_employed
d: An Employee has a Position doing work in a particular Field, or doing work on a particular Task, for which an Employer gives Compensation to the Employee.

ex.t: Undocumented foreigners are working as building contractors for Laing Builders.

fes.d: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
The Employee is obligated to perform a Task in order to receive Compensation.
The Employer gives Compensation to an Employee.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee works for an Employer.
This FE identifies the Place_of_employment of the Employee.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employee is in employment.
The Employee is obligated to perform the Task to recieve Compensation from the Employer .
This FE identifies the Time period during which an Employee works for an Employer.
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
This FE identifies the amount of Time for which the Employee continues being employed.
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that an Employee occupies within the organization of the Employer.
This FE identifies the Type of the profession.
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.
The location where the Employee works.
How often the Employee works.
This FE gives a description of the Being_employed event.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Being_in_captivity
d: A Theme is held in captivity by an Agent or Cause.

ex.t: Twenty soldiers were in captivity for over a month before they were released
I never release my prisoners.
She couldn't believe she was prisoner in her own home.

fes.d: The entity which is confined.
The area within which the Theme is confined.
The Agent prevents the Theme from moving.
The reason for the confinement.
This FE identifies the general Place where the Theme is held captive.
The Time when the Theme is held captive.

Any description of the state of being captive which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Theme.
The reason for which the Theme is held captive.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Theme remains in captivity.
An inanimate force which causes the Theme in be unable to move.

name: Being_in_category
d: An Item belongs to a Category, as (often implicitly) conceived of by a Cognizer.

ex.t: To me this counts as historical fiction because it is based on real events.

fes.d: This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an oblique.
This is the entity which is is an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as the external argument.
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by as or under.

This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified by color or by finish (matte or gloss); if they are classified by color, one can be classified as orange and another as red. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of...:
The Manner in which an Item (metaphorically) is construed as being in a Category.
An act or state of affairs by which the Item (perhaps metaphorically) is interpreted as being in a Category.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization holds.
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds.

name: Being_in_control
d: A Controlling_entity has control of a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable. This frame is distinct from Control in that the Controlling_entity is not fully asserted to be currently controlling the Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable, but rather is attentive to it and capable of making the situation correspond to the desired state at any time.

ex.t: She was in control of the empire within two days.

fes.d: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.
An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by a Controlling_entity.
A situation whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by a Controlling_entity.
A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of a Controlling_entity.
The Degree to which the Controlling_entity effects the Dependent_entity.
The Time at which the controlling occurs.
The location at which the controlling occurs.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Controlling_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Being_in_effect
d: A particular Binding_principle is (or is not) operative, that is, any obligations, restrictions, and any other aspects of the Binding_principle are (or are not) in effect. The Binding_principle can be expressed as being in effect for a particular Duration, or at a particular Time or Place, or under certain Circumstances. Although the in effect is properly in this frame, (put) into effect is analyzed in the Execute_plan frame. This is in part because to put an (evacuation) plan into effect is to actually execute the plan (to evacuate), while to put a plan in effect is to determine that in the future the plan may have to executed, i.e., to make the plan binding. Similar observations can be made for come into effect.

ex.t: This law will only become in effect during the last three weeks of the year.
The statutory wetlands definition is effective immediately.
This contract is binding on all parties.

fes.d: The Binding_principle is the law, contract, principle, or other (set of) obligations that is (or is not) operational.
The length of time for which the Binding_principle is or is not in effect.
The Time at which the Binding_principle is in effect.
The Place at which the Binding_principle is or is not operational.
The state-of-affairs under which the Binding_principle is/isn't operational.
A cause, reason, or other Explanation for the status of the Binding_principle
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Binding_principle.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Being_in_operation
d: A Device or machine is in (or out of) service. Note that being broken or functional is a separate issue from being turned on or off. This latter notion is what the present frame is concerned with. The Time when and the Place where the Device is in use may be specified, as may be the Purpose a backgrounded human User had in turning the Device on or off.

ex.t: The TV is on
The lights were off when I came by.

fes.d: The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.
The Time when a Device is in or out of operation.
The Place in which the Device is or is not operating.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Being_incarcerated
d: A Prisoner is punished for committing a Crime by being confined to a Prison for a specified period of time.

ex.t: Phil's serving time at Pelican Bay.

fes.d: The Prisoner is held in custody as a punishment for having committed a crime.
The facility where the Prisoner is held.
The Authorities hold the Prisoner in custody.
The crime of which the Prisoner is guilty, resulting in imprisonment.
This FE identifies the general Place where the Prisoner is held captive.
The Time when the Prisoner is in prison.

Any description of the state of being imprisoned which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The reason for which the Prisoner is in custody.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Prisoner remains in jail.

name: Being_included
d: A Part is profiled as being a subset or constituent subpart of a Whole. This is in contrast to Inclusion frame, wherein the same relation is seen from the point of view of the Whole.

fes.d: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.
The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

name: Being_located
d: A Theme is in a stable position with respect to a Location.

ex.t: Our offices are located about two miles south of I-85 .

fes.d: An entity which is at a particular Location
The location (generally presumed to be known to the interlocutor) with respect to which the location of the Theme can be understood.
A state (of the Theme) that results as a consequence of the Theme being situated at the Location.
The time at which the Theme is at the Location.
A salient entity that the Theme is located with respect to.
This frame element is used to denote phrases that specifically entail an entity which is conceived as moving relative to another entity.
A Depictive expression describes a state or condition of the Theme independent of its location.

name: Being_named
d: This frame concerns entities conventionally being referred to by particular names.

ex.t: Her name was Lola.

fes.d: Name identifies the linguistic expression used to refer to Entities.
The Entity is the person the speaker intends to refer to by using a particular name.
Language is used for a person or thing to whose name the Name of the Entity is taken or in honor of.
The FE Type denotes sub-type of names.
Describes the Name in some manner.
The context is the region or domain in which the name applies.
The source language or inspiration for the Name.

name: Being_necessary
d: A Dependent state-of-affairs has a Requirement as a prerequisite for obtaining or occurring.

ex.t: The atomic bombings were probably not necessary to win WWII without a mainland invasion of Japan.
We will take the required measures, regardless of the yelping of the left. DNI
Two tokens are necessary for county to county trips.

fes.d: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.
The entity or state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.
The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.
The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.
The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.
The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.
Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.
The individual who needs to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.
An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain.
An characteristic or feature of the Requirement or Required_entity.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Being_obligated
d: Under some Condition, usually left implicit, a Responsible_party is required to perform some Duty. If they do not perform the Duty, there may be some undesirable Consequence, which may or may not be stated overtly. NB: Contrast this frame with Likelihood and Preconditions frames, which involve many of the same lemmas. Many LUs which might be expected to be found here (should, must, have to) are actually in the Required_event frame. Our analysis is that these LUs do not evoke an obligation directly, although they are frequently used in contexts that are consistent with an understanding of obligation and are pragmatically strengthened to (defeasibly) imply an obligation.

ex.t: It is my duty to fight any attack on the Brotherhood .
This country has the responsibility to support its citizens' right to express themselves.
I am obligated to pay or they'll double the fine.

fes.d: The person who must perform the Duty.
The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.
This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty.
The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.
The time interval during which the Responsibly_party is obligated to fulfill the Duty.
A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Being_obligatory
d: Under some Condition, usually left implicit, a Duty needs to be fulfilled by a Responsible_party. If the Duty is not performed, there may be some undesirable Consequence for the Responsible_party, which may or may not be stated overtly. Compare this frame to the Being_obligated frame.

ex.t: It would behoove us to comprehend and personalize what Jesus had to tell his disciples
Fressed too much at the obligatory BBQ. INI
When I was in HS, marching band was mandatory in order to participate in any of the other ensembles INI

fes.d: This FE indicates the Condition under which the Duty is required of the Responsible_party.
The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.
The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.
The person who must perform the Duty.
The time interval during which the Duty is mandatory.
A location in which the Duty obtains.
The positive consequence of the Duty being fulfilled.
The reason why the Duty is necessary for the Responsible_party.

name: Being_operational
d: An Object with an understood function is or is not in a state ready to perform that function.

ex.t: The remote is almost broken.
Hand me that broken watch so I can throw it away.

fes.d: The entity with an understood purpose.
The extent to which the Artifact exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for being operational.

name: Being_pregnant
d: This frame describes the experience of expecting and bearing a child, from the perspective of the parent(s).

fes.d: This frame element refers to the parent who is physically pregnant.
This frame element refers to a parent who contributed to the conception of a child but is not physically carrying a child.
This frame element refers to the collective body expecting or carrying a child.
This frame refers to the conceived offspring borne by the Parents.
This frame element refers to the length of time the Parents have been pregnant.

name: Being_questionable
d: In this frame, an Entity or Behavior is suspicious or otherwise subject to question. The general implication is that the Entity or Behavior provides evidence for some (as yet unproven) socially undesirable conclusion about a (usually implicit) Social_actor. (Such conclusions often include the idea that some individual is lying, or that a crime was committed.)

ex.t: We found some suspicious checks lying on his desk.
It was rather suspicious of you to leave the party just before the police arrived.

fes.d: The Behavior is the state of affairs or action of the social actor that is regarded as susipcious.
The extent to which the Behavior is suspicious.
An individual that is suspected of wrongdoing because of the Behavior.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.
The Entity metonymically stands in for a Behavior that saliently involves the Entity.

name: Being_relevant
d: A Phenomenon is related to some cognitive action, the Endeavor, of a Cognizer. In many LUs, the Cognizer is null-instantiated and implied as being the speaker or another participant of the Endeavor.

ex.t: This book is very relevant to my essay.
This book is very relevant to my essay.

fes.d: Something that is profiled in the mind of the Cognizer as being related to mental Endeavors.
A cognitive action (eg discussion, decision) performed by the Cognizer to which the Phenomenon is connected in some way.
A participant in the mental Endeavor to which the Phenomenon is related. This frame element is often null-instantiated and may be inferred from the Endeavor.
A description of how related the Phenomenon is to the Endeavor.
The knowledge or situation that mediates the relevance of the Phenomenon to the Endeavor.

name: Being_rotted
d: An organic item, the Patient, has undergone the natural process of rotting and decaying with a possible expression of the Degree to which the rotting has occurred.

ex.t: The coconut milk became rancid.

fes.d: The Patient is the organic matter that has decayed.
This FE identifies the Degree to which rotting has occurred.

name: Being_up_to_it
d: An Entity meets the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity that is judged to be difficult for it to participate in, either due to inherent properties of the Entity or temporary Circumstances. A Degree modifier may indicate by how much the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements.

ex.t: Little Tommy was not up to getting out of bed because he was quite sick.

fes.d: The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.
The Activity that the Entity may participate in.
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity.
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity.
A characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Activity.

name: Being_wet
d: An Item is in a state of wetness with the possibility of the wetting Liquid being mentioned, along with the Degree of wetness.

ex.t: The mop is drenched with water from last night's rain.

fes.d: The Item takes up the Liquid through its pores.
The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates the Item. It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item is wet.
The Explanation brings about the state of wetness, and is usually expressed in a from-prepositional phrase.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.

name: Besieging
d: An Assailant, a group of armed forces, surrounds the Victim, a military location and the people within it, in an attempt to cut the Victim off from the outside, with the goal of either forcing their surrender or weakening them so that an invasion would be successful. A successful siege is often followed by the Assailant taking control of (the land held by) the Victim.

ex.t: Towards the end of the summer, a great English host besieged the Danish fort of Tempsford and took it, killing the last Danish king of East Anglia.

fes.d: The Assailant is a group of armed forces (or, metonymically, their commander or the organization they represent) that encircles, surrounds, or otherwise cuts off the Beseiged in an attempt to force surrender.
The Victim is the fortification or geopolitical entity that is being attacked.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.
This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.

The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.
An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.
The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.
The length of time that the Victim is under attack from the Assailant

name: Beyond_compare
d: Compared to its Competitors, a Standard is at the high end of a scale with respect to some Variable. The Competitors are frequently not realized syntactically. When there is no overt Variable it must be understood from the context. When the target occurs as the modifier of a predicate nominal, it is tagged as Standard, rather than Variable.

ex.t: The taxpayer is supporting a system unmatched in wastefulness .
The drawing room was a place of unmatched squalor.
She was envious of her mother's matchless beauty.

fes.d: The Standard is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Variable.
The Variable is a property that evokes a scale along which the Standard is located closest to one extreme in comparison to its Competitors.
The FE Competitors denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Standard with regard to the Variable.
The spatial or temporal context in which the Standard is not matched by any Competitors.

name: Billing
d: A Billing_authority communicates in written form that the Debtor owes the Owed_party (often the same as the Billing_authority) some amount of Money for certain Goods (including services) provided by the Owed_party or to clear a debt for a Bad_action by the Debtor against the Owed_party.

fes.d: The person (or organization) that owes the Owed_party.
The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.
The means by which the billing occurs.
Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction, or as recompense for the Bad_action.
In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods.
The Owed_party expects a specific amount of Money from the Debtor, either because the Debtor received Goods or because the Debtor performed a Bad_action against the Owed_party.
This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by or per-PP.
Where the event takes place.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Explanation for which an event occurs.
When the event occurs.

Any description of the billing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Seller that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The individual who communicates to the Debtor the Money that they owe.
Describes the relation between the invoice and the associated payment: unpaid, paid, overdue, etc.
An earlier action by the Debtor causing harm (directly or indirectly) to the Owed_party, for which the Owed_party expects compensation, and therefore bills the Debtor.

name: Biological_area
d: This frame contains words that denote large ecological areas as well as smaller locations characterized by the type of life present--in other words, geography locations as defined by biota.

ex.t: I've spent a long time in the rugged prairies of northern Llorwyn.

fes.d: Constituent_parts make up a Locale.
Container_possessor is the location of which the Locale is a part.
Formational_cause brings about the features of the Locale. This FE is also used for words that indicate no salient formation.
This FE identifies a stable bounded area, and is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.
This FE indicates the Names of Locales.
Relative_location identifies a place in respect to which a Locale is located.
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Biological_classification
d: This frame has to do with scientific taxonomy. The lexical units in this frame include the seven major classifications in which organisms are grouped based on common biological characteristics. These classifications are labeled Rank in this frame. The Members or Subtype of the Rank is often expressed with the use of the target-denoting noun.

ex.t: Phylum Arthropoda contains crustaceans, insects, spiders and other creepy-crawlies.
The snow leopard belongs to the kingdom Animalia.

fes.d: The Rank is the taxonomic category to which the Member belongs. It is also always the target-denoting noun.
The living organism which belongs to the expressed Rank.
The subtype of the Rank.
A property of the Member of the Rank.

name: Biological_entity
d: The LUs in this frame refer to biological entities labeled by the FE Organism. An Organism is described as something that can be alive, or have naturally occuring biological processes and functions; however the concept of life is often used metaphorically for non-organic entities which resemble or act as if they have organic life.

ex.t: NASA may someday discover a new lifeform from another planet.

fes.d: An organic that has naturally occuring bioligical processes and functions.
Any characterization of the Organism not covered by other FEs.
The location from which the Organism originated.

name: Biological_mechanisms
d: A trigger mechanism brings about a change in a biological system.

ex.t: The reflex increases cardiac output.

fes.d: The force that brings about the change in the Systemic_effect.
The biological entity that is affected by the Trigger.
Location where the Systemic_effect takes place.

name: Biological_urge
d: An Experiencer is in a State where a biological urge is signaling the need to perform a certain action such as eating, drinking, stopping exertion, sleeping, regurgitating, or having sex. The Duration, Time, Place, or Degree of intensity associated with the occurrence of the urge may also be indicated. In this frame, the Experiencer does not necessarily want to perform the action that would fulfill the urge, and there is no specific focus associated with the urge.

ex.t: Mike feels hungry.
Sam was thirsty after dinner.

fes.d: Degree identifies the extent to which the Experiencer receives the biological signal.
The Experiencer receives the biological signal and possesses the internal experience which is a reaction to the phsyical signal.
This FE identifies the Time when the Experiencer feels the biological signal. Time may also allow inference about the Reason for the biological urge. In such cases, we tag Reason on the second layer.
This FE identifies the Place is where the Experiencer feels the biological signal.
Expressor is used for a gesture, expression, or body part indicating that the Experiencer is feeling a certain urge.
Duration identifies the amount of time for which the Experiencer feels the urge.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Experiencer has the biological urge.
State identifies the Experiencer's state of being.
Parameter is the particular biological realm in which the Experiencer feels the urge.

name: Birth_scenario
d: An Offspring is born to a Mother and Father, collectively referred to as Parents. This event happens at a particular Time and Place.

fes.d: The living being that is produced by the Parents.
The female being that produces the Offspring.
The male being that aids in the production of the Offspring.
The Mother and Father collectively.
The time when the birth of the Offspring takes place.
The place where the Offspring is born.
The way in which the birthing event takes place.

name: Board_vehicle
d: A Traveller boards a Vehicle that they intend to use as a means of transportation either as a passenger or as a driver.

ex.t: On the 5th of December, 1834, we embarked on board the merchant ship Hellespont.
She boarded the train ahead of him.
On 19 September the battalion embussed and headed southward into the Swordfish training area some 40 miles away.

fes.d: The Traveller is the entity which boards the Vehicle.
The Vehicle is the intended means of conveyance of the Traveller.
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion outside of or off the Vehicle expresses the frame element Source.
The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.
The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion onto the Vehicle.
The amount of time the Traveller spends on the Vehicle after boarding it.
The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the boarding.
When the boarding of the Vehicle takes place.
A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.
The Purpose for which the Traveller boards the vehicle.
The location in which the Traveller boards the Vehicle.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Body_decoration
d: This frame concerns the decorations that human beings have on or apply to their bodies.

ex.t: Abby rarely wears lipstick.

fes.d: This FE identifies the location on the body where the decoration takes place.
This is the individual whose body is decorated.
Decoration is the decorative item that adorns the body.
Dec_desc identifies a descriptor of the Decoration.
This is the frame element that describes what shape the Decoration represents.
This FE identifies the Use to which a body decoration is put.
Type designates different kinds of body decorations. Often this FE will label part of a multi-word or compound word target.

name: Body_description_holistic
d: This frame covers descriptions of an entire human body, viewed as a gestalt (as opposed to descriptions based on salient body parts). The Frame Elements are Individual and Figure.

ex.t: Chuck is muscular.
Chuck has a muscular body.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Degree to which a body has a particular characteristic.
This FE identifies the individual (or individuals) being described.
This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.

name: Body_description_part
d: This frame is concerned with words that describe a person based on a salient part of their body.

ex.t: He was a blonde guy.
He was a peg-leg.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Individual (or individuals) being described.
This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the body description applies.

name: Body_mark
d: In this frame a Body_mark is present on a Possessor's body. It may be located at an Attachment and have a Descriptor. A Cause may also be indicated. It may be a temporary condition or a permanent one.

ex.t: Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.

fes.d: The Attachment is the larger body part to which the Body_mark is attached, or of which it is a part.
This FE identifies the Body_mark.
This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_mark. it identifies a modifier of its head noun.
This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_mark.
The Cause is the event that brings about the presence of the Body_mark.
A specific kind of the particular Body_mark.
Salient constituents that make up the Body_mark.

name: Body_movement
d: This frame contains words for motions or actions an Agent performs using some part of his/her body. A number of words in this frame occur as blends with Communication, in which the action has an Addressee. For example, These examples differ from Communication.Gesture in that no specific message need be expressed, as in Since this frame involves a particular type of motion, it contains the frame elements Source, Path, Goal and Area, which originate in the motion frame. All of these frame elements are generally expressed in PP Complements.

ex.t: Pat nodded at Kim.
She nodded to him to sit down.
The boy swung his legs from under the table.

fes.d: The Agent uses some part of his/her body to perform the action. Agent occurs as the External Argument.

With some verbs in this frame, the Body_part involved in the action is specified by the meaning of the verb and cannot be expressed separately. For example, With others, the Body_part is specified by the verb but can optionally be expressed separately, although its presence is generally redundant, as in A few verbs have a default Body_part which need not be expressed, but can be overridden by the expression of some other Body_part. (The objectless version of the sentence, Pat waved, is a blend with communication.) The remainder of the verbs require a Body_part to be expressed in a separate constituent: Body_part generally occurs as the direct object.
Body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement.

Cause is something in the external environment that causes the Agent to move part of his/her body. Cause is usually expressed in a PP Complement:. Cause does not include any physical force moving the Agent's Body_part. This type of situation is described by the frame Motion.Cause-to-move.
Addressee only occurs in the Body-movement frame in sentences which are blends with Communication. Where it occurs, it is typically a PP Complement:
Source is the place from which the Body_part is moved.
Path identifies the trajectory of motion of the Body_part without specifying a start or end point.
Goal is any expression that identifies the endpoint of movement.

Area identifies any expression describing a region in which the motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. (This FE should be contrasted with Place.)
This FE identifies the Degree to which the event occurs.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the body movement occurs.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
This FE identifies the Message that the body movement conveys.
This FE identifies the Time when the body movement occurs.
This FE specifies the subregion of the body that is involved with movement.
The purpose of the body movement.
This FE identifies the event noun of the verb.
The period of time during which the movement of a Body_part occurs.
The location within which the movement of a Body_part takes place.
An alternative description of the Body_movement.
An event that the Agent perceives and responds to by moving in coordination with it.

name: Body_parts
d: This frame covers words for Body_part(s) (BP) belonging to a Possessor (Poss), which may be characterized by a Descriptor (Desc). The location of the BP may be identified in terms of its Attachment or its Orientational_location. A Subregion of a BP may also be indicated.

ex.t: He had to brace his right arm against his leg in order to fight the roll.
The dog measured its blond belly in the mud.

fes.d: This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_part.

This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_part. Note that Descriptor is not an FE of the same character as other FEs. Specifically, rather than filling a slot, it identifies a modifier of its head noun.
This Frame Element is the Body_part.
This FEidentifies the Subregion of the Body_part referred to by the target.

This Frame Element describes the location of the Body_part with respect to the inherent orientation of the body (or the larger body part) the Body_part is attached to. NB: All of these (other than very productive types such as "left", "right", "front", "back", and "second") should be tagged as secondary targets.
The Attachment is the larger body part to which the BP is attached.

name: Bond_maturation
d: A Financial_instrument (a bond or insurance) fulfills a condition at a certain Time after which the Issuer of the Financial_instrument is legally obligated to pay the Holder a monetary Value, based on the instrument's original Principle and the Interest rate.

ex.t: The bond had matured to its full value at 30 years.

fes.d: The bond, insurance, or debt security which a Holder buys from an Issuer.
When the Financial_instrument reaches maturity.
The entity which is obligated to pay the Holder after the Financial_instrument matures.
The entity which owns the Financial_instrument and is owed money from the Issuer.
What the Financial_instrument is worth after maturity.
The amount that the Holder originally paid to own the Financial_instrument.
The growth rate on the Principle that results in the final Value of the Financial_instrument.

name: Borrowing
d: The Borrower takes possession of a Theme with the knowledge that the Borrower will have to give the Theme back to the Lender after a Duration of time. This frame differs from the Lending frame in that this frame profiles the Borrower in active sentences, whereas the Lending frame profiles the Lender. For the time being, this frame includes both the transfer event itself and the end state of the event, as shown in the first two examples following: Along with other ways of temporarily taking possession (e.g. "putting something in your pocket for a while"), this frame is used non-literally to refer to Stealing. In this use, the Borrower is a thief, the Lender is a Victim, and the Theme is the Goods:

ex.t: I am borrowing the book about modal particles from the professor.
I borrowed the book from him and returned it a long time ago.
Not only did I have to borrow a gown, but I was also lent a jacket!

fes.d: The person who receives the Theme from the Lender for a Duration.
The amount of time for which the Borrower has possession of the Theme.
The person or institution who gives the Theme to the Borrower for a Duration.
The object that the Borrower receives from the Lender for a Duration.
The aim of the Borrower which they believe will be accomplished by possessing the Theme.
When the borrowing even occurs.
The means by which the transfer of the Theme took place.
The location in which the Borrower gets the Theme from the Lender.
The way in which the Borrower gains possession of the Theme from the Lender.

name: Boundary
d: This frame contains words that describe a Boundary between two Entities. In many cases, the Boundary is the border between an Entity and some unnamed space, generally conceived of as empty.

ex.t: The canyon is the border between the two states.

fes.d: The region which is between the Entities or between the Entity and empty space.
The entity that has a Boundary.
The joint construal of both Entities next to the Boundary.
The relative location of the boundary in respect to the Entity or Entities.

name: Bounded_entity
d: This is an abstract frame for bounded areas, used mostly for FE inheritance.

fes.d: This FE identifies a stable Bounded_area. It typically serves as the denotation of nouns.
This FE identifies the salient Constituent_parts that make up a bounded area.
Relative_location identifies the place in respect to which a bounded area is located.
This FE is used for the Name of a bounded area.
This FE identifies the Owner, generally a person, of the bounded area.
This FE identifies the Formational_cause (action or agent) that brings about the features of the bounded area.
An indication of which kind of Bounded_area the entity is.

name: Bounded_region
d: An Exterior, Surface, Boundary, and Interior are picked out relative to the Ground. This Ground may either occupy only the Boundary (in which case the Interior is negative space) or the Ground may fill the Interior.

fes.d: A region of space located inside a Ground.
An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Interior, Surface, Boundary, or Exterior regions.
The region located outside of, but in contact with, the Ground.
The region associated with the boundary of the Ground.
The region which is not located inside or in contact with the Ground.

name: Bragging
d: A Speaker talks about a Topic, which may be an action performed by the Speaker or an entity or state of affairs that they are associated with in order to suggest that the Speaker is worthy of admiration. The Speaker may give an explicit Reason why the Topic redounds to their credit. Alternatively, a Message frame element can be used to directly describe what the Speaker says, leaving the more specific Reason for admirability to be inferred. Instead of the Speaker, the action may be attributed metonymically to the Medium, or possibly the Expressor.

ex.t: Turkish officials boasted of giving 'tens of thousands of dollars in surreptitious payments' to a prominent American politician.
He then vaunted his own clan, but failed to mention Emanuel Ungaro, who described the omission as ''lamentable''.
The press release boasts that "a direct connection between the cartridge and the system" means no more having to blow dust out of game cartridges.

fes.d: The Speaker is the person who produces a message about a Topic.
The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker communicated a message.
The Topic is a positively judged entity or state of affairs with which the Speaker is associated and about which they talk.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
An act whereby the Speaker makes a boastful statement.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.
The state of the Speaker during the statement.
The time when the statement is made.
The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.
A characteristic of the entity or state of affairs denoted by the Topic which explains why the Speaker is proud of the association with the Topic referent.
A description of the state of affairs that redounds to the Speaker's credit
Role is used for the capacity in which the Topic entity or state of affairs is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs.
Expressor is the body part or action that conveys the feeling of pride of the Speaker.
The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking.
Degree to which event occurs.

name: Breaking_apart
d: A Whole breaks apart into Pieces, resulting in the loss of the Whole (and in most cases, no piece that has a separate function). Many of these verbs can also refer metaphorically to the breaking apart of institutions. (See the frame for "schism".)

ex.t: The plane violently broke apart in mid-air.
And then, I finally realized that it must have been the case that a meteorite broke apart into at least 3 large pieces.

fes.d: The Whole goes into Pieces which were not (necessarily) definable subparts prior to breaking.
The Pieces result from the breaking apart of the Whole.
This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.
Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.
The time at which the breaking apart takes place.w
The location at which the breaking apart takes place.
An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking apart.

name: Breaking_off
d: An single Subpart breaks off from a Whole.

ex.t: The original sword may have chipped off of the statue long ago.

fes.d: The part of the Whole that is conceived as being broken or taken off from the remaining part of the whole.
The piece that is presented in a less prominent position, and which is the landmark or remaining whole from which Sub_part breaks off.
This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.
The time at which the breaking off of the Sub_part happens.
The location at which the breaking off occurs.
Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.
An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking off.

name: Breaking_out_captive
d: An Agent brings about the end of a Theme's captivity at a Location_of_confinement in contravention of the plans or desires of a captor.

ex.t: His accomplice freed him from Sing Sing prison thanks to his disguise.

fes.d: The Agent is the individual who ends the confinement or captivity of the Theme.
The Theme is the person or object in motion released by the Agent.

Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The action of the Agent which brings about the release.
The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Agent releases the Theme.
The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Agent release the Theme.
The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.
The Time identifies when the Agent release the Theme .
The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The state of the world when the Releasing event occurs.

name: Breathing
d: An Agent causes Air to move in a direction, usually specifying either in or out of the body.

ex.t: Lee breathed the hot desert air.

fes.d: The Agent's breathing causes the motion of the Air. Agent is generally the External Argument.
Air is the substance that the Agent causes to move.
This FE identifies the point at which the Air ends up as a result of the motion.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent breathes.
This FE identifies the Means of breathing.
Source identifies the starting point of the Air.
This FE identifies the Path of the motion through locations after leaving the Source and before reaching the Goal.
This FE identifies the degree to which an Agent is breathing.
Depictive identifies a phrase describing a participant in a breathing event.
This FE identifies the Place where the breathing occurs.
This FE idenitfies the Duration of time that an Agent breathes.
The distance that the Air travels.
An entity that allows the Agent to breathe, either a natural part (the lungs, say) or a device (like a respirator).
The time at which breathing occurs.

This FE designates internal events/states that cause the Agent to exhibit the specified type of breathing. Further, the internal state of the Agent is perceivable to others because of the breathing event.
This FE denotes an event or state external to the Agent that causes them exhibit the specified manner of breathing but not as a conscious response to the External_cause.
Circumstances are expressions indicating prevailing physical conditions or states of affairs concurrent to the breathing event.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by breathing in the specified manner.

name: Bringing
d: This frame concerns the movement of a Theme and an Agent and/or Carrier. The Agent, a person or other sentient entity, controls the shared Path by moving the Theme during the motion. In other words, the Agent has overall motion in directing the motion of the Theme. The Carrier may be a separate entity, or it may be the Agent's body. The Constant_location may be a subregion of the Agent's body or (a subregion of) a vehicle that the Agent uses. The FEs include Path, Goal, and Source. Area is an area that contains the motion when the path is understood as irregular. This frame emphasizes the path of movement as opposed to the FEs Source or Goal as in Filling or Placing.

ex.t: Karl carried the books across campus to the library on his head.
Karl carried the books across campus to the library in his truck.
Karl carried the books across campus to the library by truck.

fes.d: The Agent is a sentient being who physically controls the movement of the Theme via the carrier, accompanying the Theme.
Goal identifies the endpoint of the path.
Source indicates the beginning of the path along which the Theme travels.
Path along which carrying occurs.
The objects being carried.
The Constant_location expresses the location of the Theme relative to the Carrier. This relationship holds for the entire length of the carrying event.
Area is used for descriprion of a general area in which the carrying action takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.
Depictive identifies a phrase describing the Carrier, Agent or Theme.
This FE identifies the Distance the Theme is carried.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Carrier or Agent carries the Theme .
The Speed is the rate at which the carrying or transporting occurs.
The Purpose for which the Carrier or Agent carries the Theme .
The Carrier provides support for the Theme. Movement of the Carrier results in movement of the Theme.
The actions the Agent takes to move the Theme.
The Place is the general area that serves as a setting for the specific motion of the Agent and Theme (with Source, Path, or Goal).
The time in which the carrying event takes place.
Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
This FE describes the particpant for whom the bringing is beneficial.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This frame element is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co-participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

name: Building
d: This frame describes assembly or construction actions, where an Agent joins Components together to form a Created_entity, which is profiled, and hence the object of the verb.

ex.t: Jack built a new house out of bricks.
We glued the airplanes together.

fes.d: The Agent builds a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the Instrument(s) with which an Agent builds a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the Place where the building occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
This FE identifies the Time when the building occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent builds a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the Components that form the Created_entity.
Created_entity identifies the entity that is created in the act of building.
This FE identifies the Result of the act of building.
Depictive identifes the phrase describing the participant in the act of building.
This FE idenitifies the Manner in which an Agent builds a Created_entity.

This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
A characteristic of the Created_entity.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Building_subparts
d: This frame includes words that name subparts of buildings that can be occupied by people.

ex.t: Mary left the room in a huff.

fes.d: The place or area specified inside a structure. The Building_part of the Whole.
The entirety of a building whose Building_part is discussed.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Building_part was constructed.
This FE designates the kind or Type of Building_part.
This FE describes where the Building_part is located.
A characterization of some property of the Building_part.

name: Buildings
d: This frame contains words which name permanent fixed structures forming an enclosure and providing protection from the elements.

ex.t: The baroque church, built in 1635, has a very rich interior
The city tour includes the 16th-century monastery of the Transfiguration and Church of Elijah the Prophet
An ancient stone church stands amid the fields

fes.d: The Individual that created the Building.
The entity built by the Builder which has some Function.
The use for which the Building is intended.
The Name used to refer to the Building.
Any indication of what makes up the Building, including components, ingredients, etc
The time at which the Building comes into existence.
An indication of the subtype of Building, including architectural style.
A characterization of some property of the Building.
The building's location.
A place that a Building is located with respect to.
The person or other legal entity that owns or has possession of the Building.

name: Bungling
d: An Agent performs an Action incorrectly. The affected Patient may be mentioned metonymically for the Action.

ex.t: Mickey botched that swing.
Julia bungled the cake.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Degree to which a bungling event occurs.
Depictive identifes a phrase describing a particpant in an action.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent bungles.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent bungles.
The Agent performs an action incorrectly.
Patient is the entity affected by the Agent's bungling of an Action.
This FE identifies the Place where the bungling occurs.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent bungles.
This FE identifies the Time when the bungling occurs.
This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs incorrectly.
The type of action that the Agent habitually bungles.

name: Burying
d: An Agent or Cause places a Theme under a surface (often the ground) into a Goal location.

ex.t: The suspect buried his gun in the ground while fleeing the police.

fes.d: The Agent intentionally buries the Theme.
The Theme is the object that is buried.
The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it is buried.
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path.
The FE Goal is the location where the Theme ends up.

Any expression which describes a property of the placing action which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
The Degree indicates the degree to which the burying occurs.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme.
The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the burying of the Theme.
This FE identifies the Result of the burying.
The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme stays in the Goal location.
The Place indicates where the burying occurs.
The Explanation that the Theme is buried.
Time is when the burying occurs
The Area is the general area where the Theme is buried.
The Cotheme is buried along with the Theme
This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion of the theme into the ground.
The Speed is the rate at which buring occurs.
A non-animate force which buries the Theme.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the burying action.
The Beneficiary derives a benefit from the occurrence of the burying event.

name: Business_closure
d: A business locale, the Entity, ceases to provide services and closes.

ex.t: Exxon went under.

fes.d: The Entity is rendered unable to continue its regular operations.
The Explanation is named as one of the causes of failure.
The Time of the failure.
The Place of the failing entity.
The Circumstances that caused failure. Compared to Explanation, this describes situations or environments that lead to failure, not a specific reason for failure.
The Manner describes the way in which the Entity failed.
The Containing_event is an event within which the failure occurs.
A Depictive describes something about the Entity.

name: Businesses
d: A Proprietor owns or runs a Business which provides a Product (which may be goods or services).

ex.t: The consumer electronics company Apple has exploded with popularity in recent years.

fes.d: Product identifies the product or service provided by the business.
Proprietor is the owner or chief participant in the business.
Descriptor indicates other characteristics of the business besides its Product and Proprietor.
This FE identifies the Place in which the business is located.

Business identifies the company or establishment. This may be the target itself or the Business_Name if it is an appositive not set off with commas (i.e. restrictive): In the appositive case, the name may also be tagged Business_Name on a second annotation layer.
The name of the Business when it appears in an appositive set off by commas (non-restrictive):
When a Business is described in terms of the professionals who work to produce the product or service, use Service_provider.

name: Cache
d: A hidden Cache of a Resource is kept safe and available for later Use. The existence, location, and other information about the Cache is kept secret by the Possessor.

ex.t: They no doubt had to move their arms cache after several members defected.
Do you have a stash of money somewhere?

fes.d: This FE denotes the Cache of Resources.
The goods or commodity that is being stored in a Cache.
The future Use for the Resource.
The entity that possesses the Cache.
A characterization of the Cache itself, rather than the Resource.

name: Calendric_unit
d: Words in this frame name the different parts of the calendric cycle, both man-made and natural. The Unit (e.g. Tuesday) specifies some time period as part of a specific larger temporal Whole (Tuesday of next week), or may be resolved to an exact time span by a Relative_time (next Tuesday). Very frequently, the Whole or Relative_time are left out (i.e., DNI), and often should be interpreted as a time period overlapping with the communication, but more generally must be understood from context. So, for example, in the first sentence below, we can imagine that the Whole refers to a year (e.g., 1983) that was already mentioned or established in context. In the second example below, the most likely interpretation is the nearest April, whether in this year or the next, and this interpretation is best indicated by indicating the Relative_time is DNI. Most members of this frame can be used with iterative events, either with a plural Unit (on Tuesdays), or marked with every (every April). In this use, when the Whole is omitted, the Whole should be marked INI. Words of this frame often occur in a non-lexical construction that uses some Calendric_unit expressions to establish when an event occurred. To capture this information, we use the extra-thematic FEs Landmark_period and Trajector_event (see Temporal_collocation) on the second layer, as in the following: We do not use these FEs for cases where the temporal relationship is introduced by an overt word of the Temporal_collocation frame (like on, in, at, before, etc.). Most lexical units of this frame occur in this construction, with or without requiring a Relative_time, while some idiosyncratically do not, so information on the use with the extra-thematic FE Trajector_event is lexically specific. There are a number of non-lexical constructions that evoke this frame, including date constructions (the third, May 5), decade constructions (the oughts), year constructions (1975, 24 BCE, 10 AH, year 19, etc.), and time-of-day constructions. Although not annotated in this frame, examples such as the following show that the FEs Unit and Whole are quite appropriate: As described above for the lexical targets that evoke this frame, some non-lexical versions of the frame may also occur in a non-lexical Temporal_collocation construction: Words in this frame figure into a variety of temporal schemas, realized as constructions, primarily cases in which the Calendric_unit serves as a Landmark_period in the Temporal_collocation frame. There are families of constructions in which these words occur, including ones in which weekday names combine with day part names using particular prepositions (e.g. on Wednesday morning, cf. on Wednesday, but in the morning) and ones in which calendric terms fill the slots in multi-word expressions such as N-after-N (e.g. day after day), N-by-N (e.g. week by week), N-to-N (e.g. month to month), etc. More can be found on these in Fillmore (2002). Note, also, the connection between this frame and Frequency, specifically that many iterative adjectives and adverbs are based on calendric terms (e.g. daily, weekly, monthly, etc.).

ex.t: Jo's mother will visit on this coming Tuesday.
On April 2 , she finally found her mother . DNI.
I 'll come back in April .DNI

fes.d: Relative_time is used for the word or words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point.
Name is used for the name of a day (month, etc.). Note that only the word (or words) that is the name is (are) tagged, not the target word.
Whole is used for the larger unit of which the target word names a part.
The number of intervals of the specified type.
The calendric unit that is denoted. LUs in this frame all denote the Unit.
An event saliently associated with a particular calendric unit.

The time-expression that is used to establish when the Trajector_event occurred. This FE, when present, always occurs on the second layer. This FE is not to be used when the relationship between a time expression and an event is overtly expressed by a target of the Temporal_collocation frame, as in the following, which differs from the preceding sentence only in the use of by:

An event that is located by the Calendric_unit expression. This FE is not to be used when a target of the Temporal_collocation frame explicitly introduces the temporal relationship between the Landmark_period and the Trajector_event, as in the following, which differs from the above only in the additional word over:

name: Candidness
d: This frame contains adjectives and nouns that describe the truth or sincerity of communication. These words, analogously to behaver-evaluating words, can apply either to Speakers or to the Messages they produce. They can occur with about-PPs expressing Topic.

ex.t: Evelyn was candid with me about the party.

fes.d: The Speaker produces the Message, the truth or sincerity of which is at issue. It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the target word, or as the Nominal Head of prenominal uses.
The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. This FE often remains unexpressed. When expressed, it normally takes the form of a PP Complement headed by with.

Message is the communicative content whose truth or sincerity is at issue. This FE does not normally co-occur with the other FEs in this frame. When it does occur, it is normally the External Argument of a predicative use of the Target word, or the modified Nominal Head in a prenominal use.

The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It often occurs without the Message FE in predicative uses of the target word. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about".
Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a communication is candid--some are more candid than others.
This FE indicates the manner of candidness.

name: Capability
d: An Entity meets the pre-conditions for participating in an Event. A Degree modifier may be included to indicate by how much the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements.

ex.t: Conductor software gives us the hands-on capability to provide updates immediately
The GOP is afraid that it might not be capable of keeping the seat vacated by Dunn.
NASA is unable to communicate with Mars rover.

fes.d: The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.
The Event that the Entity may participate in.
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Event.
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Event.
The characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Event.
The status of the capability.
The particular role that the Entity plays in the Event.
The time at which the Entity is capable of the Event.
This FE expresses how often the Entity is able to do the Event.

name: Capacity
d: An Entity has the ability to contain a Theme.

ex.t: Our facility seats up to 500 people.

fes.d: The Entity whose ability to contain items is assessed.
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for holding the items.
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for containing.
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be able or unable to hold the items.
The status of the capability (e.g., innately, with modifications).
The Entity has the ability to contain the Theme, often expressed with a quantity.
A description of one of the participants, typically the Theme but possibly the Entity.
This FE denotes a sub-part of the Entity which has a particular capacity.
The Purpose of the Entity's specified capacity.
The Time at which the Entity has or had a certain capacity.

name: Capital_stock
d: This frame concerns Stock, a purchasable and sellable asset representing a Shareholder's share in a company (the Issuer). Stock entitles the Shareholder to profits of the Issuer company, as determined by the governing board of the Issuer company. LUs in this frame can denote the type of capital stock investment into a business (common or preferred) or the investment itself. Common stock is also known as ordinary stock or voting stock.

ex.t: My ten preferred shares in Google are worth more than your ten common shares in Apple.

fes.d: The investment that a Shareholder makes into a business, differing from property and assets.

The the kind of Stock, of which there are two: preferred or common. Holders of preferred stock are entitled to the first dividend that a company pays out, while holders of common stock are granted voting rights in corporate decisions.
The creditor that has invested into a business by purchasing some Type of its Stock.
The entity that issues its Stock to the Shareholder.
The Amount is the number of shares, though any measure prase will suffice.

name: Cardinal_numbers
d: This frame presents a situation where there is a certain Number of instances of an Entity or a certain Number that quantifies a Unit. Numbers are used to count any kind of Entity that has distinct individuals, or alternatively, to count Units whose own function is to quantify some property, with the Number associated with each word of this frame differentiating groups, individuals, parts of individual Entitys of different sizes, or to differentiate the quantity of the Units. A countable Entity prototypically occupies its own space separately from other instances of the Entity, and each instance of the Entity has specific kinds of parts or substance or characteristics as specified by the kind of Entity it is described as. Units (e.g., hours, inches, dozens) have the function of quantifying some property and as a result, naturally occur with a Number to say how the current property compares to the standard quantification of the Unit. Less prototypical numbers, which occur much more frequently with Units rather than Entitys, describe situations with less than a whole Unitor Entity (half.n), or the lack of a Unit or Entity (zero.num). There is also a Precision associated with the Number. In most cases, there is a certain amount of imprecision in the Number that is assumed, especially for so-called "round" numbers like twenty.num or hundred.num, and for the class of approximate numbers, like couple.n; for other numbers, e.g. two.num, the expected precision is very high. Separately from this inherent possibility of precision or imprecision, numbers may be modified by an explicit specification of their Precision, with phrases like "about", etc. This frame includes extrathematic FEs for a set of non-lexical constructions that put together quantifying expressions. Firstly, a Number may itself be quantified by having a certain Multiplier, e.g. "three hundred". Secondly, a sequence of numerical expressions may be strung together, with or without "and", to produce a Composite_number representing a Number that is the sum of the constituent numbers and that collectively modifies the Entity or Unit. As can be seen in the first of the next two examples, when the target is a number in front of another number in the function of a Multiplier, we consider the number it is modifying to be a Unit: The relationship between numbers, as lexical units in this frame, and the broader category of numbers is a complex one. In particular, there is a semiotic system that arranges the tiny set of numeral symbols (0, 1, 2 ... 9), with some additional symbols (commas, decimal points, fraction lines, scientific notation of exponents) to generate a standard representation for numbers that, while not universal, is at least language independent. Our description of numbers is focused on the English system of numbers, as would occur in the spoken language or in pronunciations (actually decodings) of written numerals in English. Since numerals are well-understood by virtually all speakers of most languages, and are well-processed by computers, we do not view the description of these structures in FrameNet as necessary. As a convenience, we include numerals as wordforms when they coincide with a basic number word of English (e.g., "3" is a wordform of three.num). Of more interest for the FrameNet Project is the large number of idiosyncrasies in the constructions that use numbers, very few of which will be well-exemplified in our annotation. These include indications of range (from ... to), approximation (in the neighborhood of), and descriptions of group properties ("A whopping three singers showed up") Technical note: The frame as currently devised does not distinguish between "six apples" and "six of the apples".
