It is clear that in the first case, we are talking about six entities that fit whatever properties apples have. In the second case, however, there is a specific set of apples that was already under discussion, and the six apples are members of this set. There is a way of understanding this second case in terms of the first, namely, that "six of the apples" is interpreted as six entities with the property of being members of the given set of apples. Since understanding the second case involves an additional notion of set membership, this could be indicated with a different FE than any we currently have in this frame, perhaps *Set, which is in an exclusion relation with Entity. However, the major semantic distinction between these two types of Entity is whether there is a definite set, and this distinction is independently indicated by the definite article in examples like "six of the apples".

ex.t: Only two senators voted in support of the president .
Dr. Malik has confined almost a score of such unfortunates in his basement, you know.
We endured forty days of snow .

fes.d: This FE identifies the Number.
This FE identifies the Entity enumerated by the Number. In many cases, the Target is used to multiply another number. In this case, the second number is labeled as "Unit":

This FE identifies the Precision to which an Entity approximates a Number. In the case where a number is modified by a Multiplier, we have found it more plausible that phrases expressing Precision modify the main number (thus "million" in the first example, not "two"):
How many times larger the group of Entitys is than the base Number.

The total number of instances of the Entity. This FE should be used when more basic number expressions are used together to form a Composite_number whose value is the sum of the constituent numbers. It is annotated on a second FE layer. For cases where a number is used to multiply another number, use Multiplier.

A Unit expresses some quantification of some property of an entity, event, or situation by providing a base value of the property combined with a Number expressing how the current value for the property relates to the Unit. As units that specify a quantity property, numbers themselves can be used as Units.

name: Carry_goods
d: A Distributor sells, lends, or otherwise distributes a class of Goods. In the prototypical case, the Distributor is a retailer who generally keeps some type of Goods on site for the purpose of selling it to a buyer. Extensions include lending Goods (e.g., libraries, movie rental outlets), organization-internal distribution (as in a hospital), or other non-commercial distribution centers. The Goods are constrained to be a type of item (e.g., canned goods, antique dressers) rather than a particular or unique item (e.g., Smith's last self-portrait, that guitar I saw here last week). Note that a Distributor may carry some particular goods, but may not have it on hand at that exact moment.

ex.t: Trader Joe's carries a wide variety of foods, drinks, and househole necessities.

fes.d: The Distributor maintains a store of Goods for the purpose of selling or otherwise distributing them.
The Goods are kept on hand and distributed by the Distributor.
The Time when the Distributor carries the Goods.
The Place indicates where the carrying of Goods occurs.

Any description of the storing of goods which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of a Distributor that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).
This FE indicates the length of time that the Distributor carries the Goods.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Catastrophe
d: The words in this frame involve an Undesirable_event which affects the Patient negatively. No agent need be involved.

ex.t: The first calamity was a disastrous trade war with Holland.
It is sad to have to make a living by grubbing around in the dirt of a national calamity.
The result has been catastrophic.

fes.d: The undesirable event which occurs.
Where the Undesirable_Event takes place.
When the Undesirable_Event occurs.
The entity that experiences the Undesirable_Event.
This FE identifies the Degree to which event occurs.
Manner of performing an action
This FE indicates the Circumstances under which a warning applies. (Proper only to betide.)
The cause of the Undesirable_Event.

name: Catching_fire
d: A Fuel, some flammable object or substance, ends up on fire. In this frame, the cause of the fire is not the primary concern, but rather the fact that a fire started. In rare cases, only the Fire is mentioned and the associated Fuel is not. This frame does not include phrases like "a fire broke out" or "the conflagration started in the bedroom" as these are deemed to be compositional (see Process_start and Fire_burning).

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire begins to burn.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire begins to burn.
The total material currently involved in combustion, including both the parts of the Fuel currently undergoing chemical alteration and the partially ionized gas that results from this process.
The entity that is begins to undergo rapid chemical alteration leading to damage or destruction.
Any description of the Fire event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
A description of why the event happened.

name: Categorization
d: A Cognizer construes an Item as belonging to a certain Category. In this process, the Cognizer may either passively perceive the Item and note that it fits the Criteria for a Category, or, alternatively, actively examine the Item for certain Criteria that define a Category (or set of Categorys). Most members of the frame can also describe a resulting cognitive state of the Cognizer with respect to the Item and Category which no longer requires the current perception or consideration of the Item. A few LUs (e.g. peg.v, pigeonhole.v) do not readily allow stative interpretation, and a few LUs (e.g. deem.v, regard.v) only allow stative interpretation.

ex.t: You 've already stereotyped me as a bimbo, have n't you?

fes.d: This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument.
This is the entity which is construed or treated by the Cognizer as being an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as an Object.
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by as or under.

This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified by color or by finish (matte or gloss); if they are classified by color, one can be classified as orange and another as red. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of...:
Manner of performing an action
An act whereby the Cognizer categorizes.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The reason for which the Cognizer categorizes the Item in the given way.

name: Causation
d: A Cause causes an Effect. Alternatively, an Actor, a participant of a (implicit) Cause, may stand in for the Cause. The entity Affected by the Causation may stand in for the overall Effect situation or event. Those frames that inherit the Causation frame have as their background the idea that some event is responsible for the occurrence of another event (or state). In the inheriting frame, typically an FE like Agent or Causer is proposed in the place of the Actor, but in the daughter frames, as in this frame, the Actor is semantically dependent on the idea of a Cause (an event or state-of-affairs) that the Actor is a participant in. Similarly, most inheriting frames profile only the Affected entity, not the full Effect situation which is often incorporated into the frame or the particular target. So, for example, paint.v in the Filling frame entails the final situation of something (the Affected) being covered in paint (the Effect).

ex.t: He made me angry.
If such a small earthquake causes problems, just imagine a big one!
The strange mutations of the rumor mill in the end led to it being said that he was actually a woman.

fes.d: A force, process, or event that produces an effect.
Agents in a joint or reciprocal action (e.g. exchange)
A positive or negative evaluation of the Phenomenon.
Where the event takes place.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's influence on the character of the event (eagerly, quietly).
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
An action through which the Actor or Cause accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
How often the action denoted by the target occurs.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Causation_scenario
d: A Cause brings about an Effect that would not have occurred otherwise, simultaneously preventing an Averted_situation, which is what would have occurred without the Cause. The Effect and the Averted_situation are thus mutually exclusive alternatives prior to the Cause event. In most cases, either the Effect or the Averted_situation is clearly most prominent; this is especially true in the case where the Cause is the action of an Agent, who normally conceives of their action as either bringing about a desirable Effect or avoiding an undesirable Averted_situation. In frames that inherit from this one, the Cause is either an event, or an entity that plans or directly causes the Effect may metonymically stand in for the Cause event.

fes.d: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The Effect is the event which results from the Cause.
The situation that would be the case if the Cause event did not occur or the Cause state were not the case.
The time at which the Cause occurs and Effect takes place or the Averted_situation does not occur as expected.
The location at which at which the Cause occurs and Effect takes place or the Averted_situation does not occur as expected.

name: Cause_bodily_experience
d: An Agent or Cause affects a Body_part of an Experiencer so that the quality of the Experiencer's perceptual experience of the Body_part is qualitatively changed.

ex.t: Chandra massaged Liliana's wrist because it was injured.
Chandra massaged Liliana's wrist because it was injured.

fes.d: The Agent is the person causing a bodily experience in the Experiencer.
The Experiencer is the being or entity whose experience changes. If the Experiencer is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Experiencer FE is tagged on a second FE layer.
Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
Degree is the degree to which the Experiencer's bodily experience is affected.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
Place identifies the place where the bodily experience is caused.
Time identifies the time when the experience-causing event occurs.
>The Body_part identifies the location on the Experiencer's body where the bodily experience takes place.
This FE is any object manipulated by the Agent to cause the experience.
Purpose identifies the state-of-affairs that an Agent hopes to bring about by causing an experience in the Experiencer.
Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action or the affected entity.
This FE identifies the event within which the bodily experience is caused.
A fact or action somehow related to the Experiencer that the Agent responds to by causing an experience in the Experiencer.
Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent or Cause causes an experience.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that affects the Experiencer's Body_part.
The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part in which the experience occurs.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the causal event and any of its participants.
How often the Cause_bodily_experience event occurs.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_bodily_experience event to its end.
This FE indicates that the Cause_bodily_experience event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_bodily_experience event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
A description presenting a separate aspect of the experience-causing event.
The length of time from when the Cause_bodily_experience event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Cause_change
d: An Agent or Cause causes an Entity to change, either in its category membership or in terms of the value of an Attribute. In the former case, an Initial_category and a Final_category may be expressed, in the latter case an Initial_value and a Final_value can be specified.

ex.t: Our storylines follows the saga outlined by the Ultima Series, but we have modified it in order to make our writing more cohesive.
I don't think you can turn that rabbit into a hat.
How can a guy that changed his name from Bob Craft to Jack Ass declare anyone defamed his character?

fes.d: The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.
The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change.
The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.
The value that the Attribute assumes as a result of the change that the Entity is caused to undergo.
The value that the Attribute has before the change takes place.
The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.
The extent to which the initial and final categories or values differ from each other.

Any description of the event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change in the Entity.
A characteristic of the Entity for which a value can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement , or observation.
The abstract or concrete thing or situation that the Agent causes to change.
An event that causes a change in the Entity.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.
An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Entity.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The location where the change of the Entity is caused.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The particular role that the Agent plays in the Cause_change event.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Cause_change_of_consistency
d: In this frame an Agent or Cause changes the consistency of a Patient from its Initial_state to a Result. This may take place under certain Circumstances for a Purpose or Reason in a certain Manner. A Change_agent can also be used. Note that this frame contrasts with Cause_change_of_phase in that this frame describes causation of a change in a Patient within a particular phase.

ex.t: Donna thinned the soup with chicken broth.
The high temperatures curdled the milk.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs.
Degree to which the Patient changes consistency.
This is the original state of the Patient.
The Manner in which the Patient's consistency is changed.
Where the the Patient changes consistency.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Patient's consistency is changed.
Result is the result of the change of consistency.
The Speed at which the change of consistency occurs.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
When the Patient changes consistency.
Patient is the entity that undergoes a change.
The Agent causes the change of consistency in the Patient.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the consistency of the Patient.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the consistency of the Patient.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the consistency of the Patient.
The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Patient.
The Change_agent is the substance used to change the consistency of the Patient.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a Container in which the Patient is changing consistency.
The Hot_cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.

name: Cause_change_of_phase
d: A Cause or Agent causes a Patient to undergo a change of phase. The Result of the change may be given, along with the Initial_state and the Circumstances under which the change can occur. Note that this frame contrasts with Cause_change_of_consistency in that this frame describes causation of a change of a Patient between different phases (i.e. solid to liquid or frozen to "unfrozen").

ex.t: Bob melted the butter.
Sally defrosted the chicken to eat for dinner.

fes.d: The Agent causes the Patient to change phase.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally affects the Patient
The Patient undergoes a change of phase brought about by the Agent.
This FE identifies the place where change of phase occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent affects the Patient,
This FE identifies the Time at which the change of phase occurs.
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the phase change occurs
Degree to which the Agent changes the phase of the Patient
This is the original state of the Patient.
Result is the result of the change of phase.
The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Patient.
This FE identifies the Container that holds the Patient whose phase is being changed .
The length of time for which the Agent changes the phase of the Patient.
The Depictive describes the state of the Agent or Patient at the time of phase change.
The Medium is the substance which surrounds the Patient and facilitates its phase change.
The Hot_cold_source is the source of the heat or cool.

name: Cause_change_of_position_on_a_scale
d: This frame consists of words that indicate that an Agent or a Cause affects the position of an Item on some scale (the Attribute) to change it from an initial value (Value_1) to an end value (Value_2). The direction of the change (Path) can be encoded as well as the magnitude of the change (Difference). The rate of change of the value (Speed) can optionally be indicated as well as a second scale (Co_Variable), which the values are correlated with.

ex.t: The company is raising the final dividend from 4.34p to 4.57p, to boost the total by 5.3 percent to 6.36p.
Similarly, a consumer boom will encourage the authorities to increase interest rates in order to keep money supply on target.
United Way of Central Indiana adds value to your investment.

fes.d: The person who causes an entity (Item) to change its positon on a scale with respect to some property (Variable).
The distance between the orginial value (Value-1) and the final value (Value-2) of the entity on the scale (Variable).
The scale along which the Item ranges in value.
The initial value of the entity (Item) along the scale.
The final position on the scale that the entity (Item) assumes.
The Co-Variable is the scale that the (dependent ) Variable is measured against.
Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Item) along the scale between its initial (Value-1) and its final position (Value-2).
The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.
The entity whose position along a scale is being changed.
An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the position of the Item on the scale.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
When the event occurs.
The force that causes the change.

Any description of the Agent changing the value of an Attribute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location where the Agent changes the value of an Attribute.

name: Cause_change_of_strength
d: An Agent causes a Patient to be more strong, often resulting in something that is more secure and safe.

ex.t: Local Serbs are strengthening their grip on a narrow corridor along the Sava River between two large Serbian areas.

fes.d: The Agent fortifies the Patient.
The Patient is the entity that is being made stronger.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
The resultant state of the action.
An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The time at which the Agent makes the Patient stronger.
The location at which the Agent fortifies the Patient.
An event which causes the Patient to become stronger.
This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
The Circumstances of the world at the time of the event (which do not bear directly on the event itself).

name: Cause_emotion
d: An Agent acts to cause a Experiencer to feel a certain emotion.

ex.t: I was so offended by her behaviour towards me.
It does not matter if the cartoon is insulting to men.

fes.d: The Agent is the person who's action's cause an emotion in the Experiencer.
The Experiencer feels an emotion as caused by the Agent.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The tool used by the Agent to cause an emotion in the Experiencer.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Experiencer.
In what way the Agent causes an emotion in the Experiencer.
This FE describes the event as a whole, often as a VPing.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
This FE describes the reason for the state of affairs described by the target.
For how long instances of an Agent causing the Patient an emotion has repeatedly occured.
When the Agent causes emotion in the Experiencer.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The Event is the occasion or happening that evokes emotions in the Experiencer. This Event occurs as the direct result of a sentient being's actions.
Type designates the kind of emotion that the Agent causes the Experiencer to have.
Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Agent causes the Experiencer to feel an emotion.
The location where the Agent causes the Experiencer to feel the emotion.

name: Cause_expansion
d: An Agent or non-human Cause causes an Item to change its physical size. The Size_change of an Item may be explicitly indicated or characterized in terms of Initial_size and/or Result_size. In the default case, expansion is along all dimensions, but sometimes the Dimension of expansion is incorporated or made explicit.

ex.t: If the design crashes too often, then try lengthening the wings by a few centimeters, to perhaps 30cm total. CNI INI
As the juice churned with natural process of changing into wine, the gas it created would expand the balloon, and when the balloon eventually deflated, it was ready to drink.

fes.d: With some words in this frame, an Agent who causes the change in size of the Item may be present. The Agent typically occurs as the External Argument of a verb.
The Item is frequently the External Argument of verbs or the NP Object if an Agent is expressed.
Initial_size is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit. Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-from Complement.
Result_size is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by to.
Size_change identifies the amount by which the size of an Item changes.
Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent brings about the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Manner of performing an action.
The feature that the size of the Item is varied in step with.
This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.
Rate identifies the rate of change of the value.
The Cause is a non-human entity which brings about the change in size.
The Elapsed_time is the amonut of time in which the change occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent causes the Item to expand.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent cause the expansion of the Item.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.

name: Cause_fluidic_motion
d: An Agent or a Cause causes a Fluid to move from a Source to a Goal along a Path or within an Area.

ex.t: I splattered red paint nearby.

fes.d: The animate protagonist who causes the Fluid to move.
An event or force that causes the Fluid to move.
The entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way. It is not necessarily in a liquid state but is construed that way.
The location that the Fluid occupies initially.
Goal is the location the Fluid ends up in as a result of the motion
The trajectory along which the Fluid moves, exclusive of the Source and Goal.
The setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place along an unspecified Path.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Time when the fluidic motion event is caused.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in causing the Fluid to move.
A state of the Fluid that results from the motion event.
The location where the motion takes place.
The entity manipulated by the Agent which causes the Fluid to move.
An action of the Agent which brings about the motion of the Fluid.
The state-of-affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by causing motion.
The distance travelled by the Fluid.

name: Cause_harm
d: The words in this frame describe situations in which an Agent or a Cause injures a Victim. The Body_part of the Victim which is most directly affected may also be mentioned in the place of the Victim. In such cases, the Victim is often indicated as a genitive modifier of the Body_part, in which case the Victim FE is indicated on a second FE layer.

ex.t: Rod saw his father beating his mother.
In the end Wormtongue is fed up with being beaten so he cuts Saruman's throat to free himself.
A mother stabbed to death by her husband made a secret will stating that he must never be allowed to care for their son.

fes.d: Agent is the person causing the Victim's injury.
The Victim is the being or entity that is injured. If the Victim is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Victim FE is tagged on a second FE layer (see 3rd example).
Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
Degree is the degree to which the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
The Manner in which the Agent acts upon the Victim.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
Place identifies the place where the harm causing event occurs.
Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.
The Body_part identifies the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.
This FE is any object used to cause the injury.
Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.
Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
This FE identifies the event in which the harm is caused.
A fact or action somehow related to the Victim that the Agent responds to by causing harm to the Victim.
Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that inflicts harm on the Victim
The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part which is harmed.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Cause_harm event and any of its participants.
How often the Cause_harm event occurs.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_harm event to its end.
This FE indicates that the Cause_harm event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_harm event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
A description of the harm event which significantly displays a different aspect.
The length of time from when the Cause_harm event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Cause_impact
d: An Agent causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee, or manipulates two (or more) Impactors so that they make mutual forcible contact.

ex.t: He slammed his fist down on the table and bellowed something unintelligible.

fes.d: The Force is the amount of force in the course of the impact.
The Impactee is the entity which is hit by the Impactor.
The Impactor is the entity that hits the Impactee because of the Agent's efforts.
The Impactors are the multiple entities that collide.
The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
Where the event takes place.
This FE identifies the Result of the impact.
This FE indicates the Speed of the Impactor (or Impactors at impact.
Subregion identifies the part of the larger whole which was hit.
This FE identifies the Time when the impact occurs.
The Agent causes an impact.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects an Impactee.
The FE Means identifies the means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
The FE Purpose identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects the Impactee.
This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which the Agent repeatedly causes impacts.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee.

name: Cause_motion
d: An Agent causes a Theme to move from a Source, along a Path, to a Goal. Different members of the frame emphasize the trajectory to different degrees, and a given instance of the frame will usually leave some of the Source, Path and/or Goal implicit. The completion of motion is not required (unlike the Placing frame, see below), although individual sentences annotated with this frame may emphasize the Goal. This frame is very broad and contains several different kinds of words that refer to causing motion. Some words in this frame do not emphasize the Manner/Means of causing the motion (transfer.v, move.v). For many of the others (cast.v, throw.v, chuck.v, etc.), the Agent has control of the Theme only at the Source of motion, and does not experience overall motion. For others (e.g. drag.v, push.v, shove.v, etc.) the Agent has control of the Theme throughout the motion; for these words, the Theme is resistant to motion due to some friction with the surface along which they move. This frame is used in a very large number of productive metaphors, not all of which can be outlined here. The most salient types include causing an entity, construed as a Theme, to change state from an initial state (Source) via an intermediate state (Path) to a final state (Goal): A particularly divergent subtype casts changing someone's intentions as changing their location: Another subtype is specifically about causing a change in quantity (the Theme) through some sequence of values (Source, Path, and Goal): Another type, with many subtypes, involves causing an action or state (construed as a Theme) to have an effect on another person or location or conceptual domain. In such cases, theGoal is used for the final affected domain, and Source for initial affected domain, Path for an intermediate affected domain, and Distance for degree of difference between original application of the action and final: All of the foregoing metaphorical uses are annotated in this frame and marked "Metaphor", since they seem to be semantically motivated and not lexically idiosyncratic. This frame contrasts with the following frames which talk about an Agent changing a Theme's position with respect to a landmark (either Source or Goal): In Placing, the figure (Theme) is profiled as the object, and ends up on the ground (Goal). The focus is on the final stage of motion, in which the Theme ends up at the Goal, and usually stably remains there. In Filling, the ground (Goal) is profiled as the object, and the figure (Theme) ends up on the ground (Goal). In Removing, the figure (Theme) is profiled, and is removed from the ground (Source). In Emptying, the ground (Source) is profiled and the figure (Theme) is removed from it. Words of this frame also differ from the words of the Bringing frame in that they are more general: either the Agent has a momentary interaction with the Theme that causes its motion, unlike the continuous causation of Bringing, or the Agent continuously acts on the Theme, but there is no supporting object that helps with the motion like the Carrier of the Bringing frame.

ex.t: She threw her shoes into the dryer .
The mechanic dragged the jack out from under the car .
We will move the sofa out of the room through the french doors, down the stairs, and onto the sidewalk .

fes.d: The Agent is the one whose action causes the motion of a Theme. The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.
The FE Theme is generally an NP Object.
The FE Source is the starting point of motion.
The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
The FE Goal is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion.
The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.

The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.
The state of a participant during the action
Degree to which event occurs
The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Subregion identifies the part of the Theme that makes contact with the resulting location. When Subregion is expressed, there usually is no Goal expressed.
Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes the Theme to be set in motion.
An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme. It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.
The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).
The time at which the motion of the Theme occurs.
A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
The Agent's manipulation of the Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Handle. The Handle is usually expressed as a PP
A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.
The amount of time that the action requires.

name: Cause_proliferation_in_number
d: An Agent (or inanimate Cause) affects a Set so that the number of entities that make up the Set changes from an Initial_number to a Final_number. Alternatively, the situation can be described in terms of an Initial_state and a Final_state. In some cases the Attribute (i.e., number) or Difference in number may be mentioned.

ex.t: More and more resources have been devoted to halting rogue nation's proliferation of controlled nuclear technology.

fes.d: The person who causes the Set to increase in number.
The distance between the orginal value (Initial_number) and the final value (Final_number) of the Set.
The scale along which the Set ranges in, i.e., number.
The initial number of entities in the Set.
The final number of entities in the Set.
The Co-Variable is the scale that the amount of the Set is measured against.
Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Set) along the scale between its Initial_number and its Final_number.
The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.
The entity whose amount is being changed.
An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the number of the Set.
The purpose for which the proliferating of the number of a Set is performed.
When the proliferating occurs.
The force that causes the change.

Any description of the Agent changing the number of the Set which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location where the Agent changes the number of the Set.
The state of the Set before it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.
The state of the Set after it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.

name: Cause_temperature_change
d: In this frame, an Agent changes the temperature of an Item. A Temperature_goal can specify the desired temperature. A Temperature_change can also be indicated. The Temperature_start indicates the initial temperature.

ex.t: Margaret Anne chilled the salad to 30 degrees.
Heat the water 30 degrees.

fes.d: The Agent performs the intentional act which changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
The Item undergoes the temperature change.
The Temperature_goal is the temperature to which the Agent is heating or cooling the Item.
The Temperature_change is the amount of difference between the intial and goal temperatures.
Temperature_start is the initial temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
Result is the resultant state of the Agent changing the temperature of the Item.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that changes the temperature. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The length of time for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.
This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Item.
The Hot_Cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.
This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the temperature change occurs.
The degree to which the Item approaches (an implicit) Temperature_goal, which is often construed to be the ambient temperature.

name: Cause_to_amalgamate
d: These words refer to an Agent joining Parts to form a Whole. (The Parts may also be encoded as Part_1 and Part_2.) There is a symmetrical relationship between the components that undergo the process, and afterwards the Parts are consumed and are no longer distinct entities that are easily discernable or separable in the Whole.

ex.t: Chuck merged the corpora.
Chuck merged the corpora into a database.
Chuck merged the BNC with the AP Corpus into a database.

fes.d: In causative uses of these verbs there is an Agent responsible for amalgamating the Parts. The Agent is generally the External Argument (or the object of a PP-by in passives).
This FE identifies Whole as the entity resulting from combination of Parts. When overtly expressed, it is usually a PP Complement (often headed by into).
This FE identifies the Parts entities being combined, and is often expressed in a single plural NP, usually the direct object of a verb.
This FE identifies the first of two Parts mentioned. It is most often the NP-Object of a verb.
This FE identifies the second of two Parts mentioned. It is usually a PP Complement.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the amalgamating occurs.
This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.
This FE identifies the Means by which the amalgamating occurs.
This FE is used for indicating the Result of amalgamating.
The state of the Parts during the amalgamation. Often it refers to the proportion of the Parts to one another.
The state of affairs that the Agent seeks to bring about by the Amalgamation.
The location that the event occurs.
The time at which the amalgamation occurs.

name: Cause_to_be_dry
d: An Agent causes a Dryee (either a surface or an entire entity, inside and out) to become dry. This should not include examples like "drying tears" or "drying spills" as these are in the Removing frame.

ex.t: Michael dried the clothes.
Abby dried out the room with a dehumidifier.

fes.d: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the Dryee to become dry.
The Dryee is the entity which has the water removed from it.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an the Agent dries the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which Agent intentionally affects the Dryee and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of dryness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE identifies the length of Time that the drying takes.
This FE identifies the Temperature at which heat is applied to the Dryee.
The degree to which the Dryee ends up dry.

name: Cause_to_be_included
d: An Agent or Cause makes a New_member part of Group. The Group may be represented by an individual Existing_member if it implies the existence of a set of members.

ex.t: I added a new rock to my collection.
He decided he needed to add a red tie to the blue tie in his closet.

fes.d: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the New_member to become part of the Group.
Something that is already a member of the Group and represents the Group as a whole.
An item that becomes a part of the Group.
The Group is anything that can be conceptualized as a complex collection of parts or ingredients, including through metonymy like containers or locations, which New_members can join.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that is responsible for causing a New_member to enter a Group.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the inclusion of a New_member.
This FE identifies when the inclusion of the New_member to the Group occurs.
The manner in which the Agent acts.
This FE identifies what the Agent hopes to accomplish by including a New_member to a Group.
The location in which a New_member is entered into a pre-existing Group.

name: Cause_to_be_sharp
d: An Agent or Cause makes a Patient sharper or duller. An Instrument or Means may be mentioned.

ex.t: John is in the basement sharpening his axe.

fes.d: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the sharpening (or dulling) action.
The Agent causes the Patient to become more or less sharp.
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient, causing it to change in sharpness.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent sharpens the Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent sharpens the Patient.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent sharpens Patient.
The Patient is the entity that is sharpened.
The manner in which the Agent changes the sharpness of the Patient.
The state of affairs that the Agent is responding to by executing the sharpening act.
The extent to which the Patient's sharpness is affected by the Agent.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of sharpness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The resulting configuration of the Patient.

name: Cause_to_be_wet
d: An Agent causes a Patient to be wet with a Liquid. In this frame, the Liquid can be a liquid or gas. Patients are porous objects, but not hollow (like containers).

ex.t: Jo soaked the dog with water.
Ellen wet the sponge with water.

fes.d: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the Patient to become wet.
The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates or covers the Patient. It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with.
The Patient takes up the Liquid through its pores or has the Liquid covering its surface.
This FE identifies the Manner or way in which the Agent wets the Patient.
This FE identifies the Means by which an the Agent wets the Patient
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent wets the Patient.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent wets the Patient and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent wets the Patient.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally wets the Patient.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of wetness.
Degree to which the Agent wets the Patient.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE describes the reason for the state of the Cause_to_be_wet event.

name: Cause_to_burn
d: A Cause event brings about and potentially maintains the burning of Flammables. Often, an Agent stands in for the intentional action the brings about the fire, or an Actor stands in for the action that brings about the fire unintentionally.

fes.d: The individual that intends a fire to burn and brings it about.
The Flamables is the the object that burns as a result of the Cause, Agent, or Actor.
The cause of the fire.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Kindler that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An event brought about by the Cause or the Kindler that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
This FE describes the Kindler as being in some state during the action.
The individual who, while actively performing an action, unintentionally causes the Flammables to burn.

name: Cause_to_continue
d: An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to continue.

ex.t: The goaltenders kept the game going with terrific saves.

fes.d: The individual who causes the Process to continue or the State to be maintained.
A Process that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.
The State that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.
The length of time for which the Agent maintain the State or Process.
The event by which an Agent or Cause maintains the State or Process.
An event that causes the Process or State to be maintained.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by maintaining the State or Process.
An entity directed by the Agent that maintain the State or Process.
The time at which the Process continues.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location at which the Process continues.

name: Cause_to_end
d: An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to end.

ex.t: Bush may lift sanctions on his own, despite opposition.

fes.d: A Process which is ended by the Agent or Cause.
An action of the Agent that causes the Process or State to end.
The location where the Process or State is caused to end.
The Explanation for why the Process or State is ended.
The Time when the Process or State is ended.
The Degree to which the Process or State is brought to an end.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event that causes the Process or State to end.
The Manner of causing the Process or State to end.
The individual who causes the Process or State to end.
An event that causes the Process or State to end.
A State which is ended by the Agent or Cause.

name: Cause_to_experience
d: An Agent intentionally seeks to bring about an internal mental or emotional state in the Experiencer. This frame in closely related to Experiencer_obj.

ex.t: Samantha terrorized the children into screaming.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally tries to bring about an internal mental or emotional state.
The Agent is an External Argument of the target word and purposefully arouses an emotional state.
The Experiencer is the person the Agent causes to have a particular emotional state.
This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which the Agent affects the Experiencer.
What the Agent intends to make the Experiencer do by causing a certain experience and the Experiencer actually does.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent affects the Experiencer.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent affects the Experiencer
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent brings about the emotional state.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent brings about the emotional state in the Experiencer.
Degree to which the Experiencer ends up feeling an emotion.

name: Cause_to_fragment
d: An Agent suddenly and often violently separates the Whole_patient into two or more smaller Pieces, resulting in the Whole_patient no longer existing as such. Several lexical items are marked with the semantic type Negative, which indicates that the fragmentation is necessarily judged as injurious to the original Whole_patient. Compare this frame with Damaging, Render_non-functional, and Removing.

ex.t: He ripped up the letter faster than you can say "Jack Robbins". INI
Don't go in there or you 'll be torn to bits! CNI
She shattered the vase with a casual backhand blow to make it look like there had been a struggle. INI

fes.d: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Whole_patient being broken into Pieces.
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Whole_patient to accomplish its fracture.

Any description of the fracturing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the breakage.
The entity which is destroyed by the Agent and that ends up broken into Pieces.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent breaks the Whole_patient into pieces.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the break-up of the Whole_patient.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent breaks up the Whole_patient.
The fragments of the Whole_patient that result from the Agent's action.
The degree to which the fracturing is completed.
The part of the Whole_patient which is directly affected by the breakage.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Agent presses the Whole_patient.
An event which leads to the fragmentation of the Whole_patient.

name: Cause_to_land
d: An Operator maneuvers onto land a Vehicle which typically does not operate on land, e.g., an airplane or boat.

ex.t: The terrified pilot landed the passenger-filled airplane into the river.

fes.d: The Vehicle ends up stationary on land.
Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.
Goal is any expression that tells where the Vehicle ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.

A Manner expression describes a property of landing which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Operator lands a Vehicle.
Cotheme is a second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
This FE identifies the Time when the Operator lands teh Vehicle.
The New_situation are the state of the Goal when the Vehicle arrives.
The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Operator or Vehicle upon arrival.
The time period within which the landing event repeats multiple times.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the landing event itself and any of its participants.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the landing event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of Event_description
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.
How often the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.
This FE identifies the Place where the landing occurs.
The Operator maneuvers the vehicle onto land. A skilled pilot would never set a plane down in weather like this.

name: Cause_to_make_noise
d: An Agent manipulates a Sound_maker or a Cause causes the Sound_maker to emit a sound.

ex.t: The monks would ring the bell until sundown.

fes.d: The individual that manipulates a Sound_maker so that it makes Noise.
The entity that produces the Noise, as a result of the action of the Agent.
The Subregion is the sublocation of the Sound_maker from which the sound is emitting.
The location from which an Agent or Cause acts to project sound from a Sound_maker toward an (implicit) perceiver.
The state of one of the primary participants (either Agent or Sound_maker) during the course of the sound-making event.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action directly due to the Agent or Cause that results in the Sound_maker emitting noise..
The inanimate force of nature that causes the Sound_maker to produce noise.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
The state-of-affairs or action that the Agent wishes to bring about by performing the action.
The time at which the noise is produced.
The location at which the sound is produced.
The number of times the Sound_maker makes noise per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.
Used for expressions that indicate the number of times Sound_maker makes noise.

name: Cause_to_make_progress
d: An Agent works on a Project so that it reaches a more advanced and desirable state.

ex.t: I improve FrameNet.

fes.d: The object or idea that undergoes change due to the efforts of the Agent.
The former state of the Project.
The state of the Project following an advance.
The time at which the progress occurs.
The rate at which the change happens.
A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way); in addition, it may describe characteristics and states of the Agent that also affect the development.
The period over which the Agent develops the Project.
The amount of advancement that the Project has attained.
The relevant dimension of development.
The individual that brings about the development of the Project.
The location at which the the Project progresses.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent progresses the Project.
The action of the Agent which enables the advancement.

name: Cause_to_move_in_place
d: An Agent causes a Theme to move with respect to a certain Fixed_location, generally with a certain Periodicity, without undergoing unbounded translational motion or significant alteration of configuration/shape.

ex.t: Paul shook the remote control frantically.

fes.d: Theme identifies the object involved in motion.
This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
Manner of performing an action
The Means is the way in which the motion in place is instigated.
Degree to which event occurs
The number of times the Theme returns to a state in a given duration.
The point or set of points that define the limits of motion for the Theme. For spinning motions, it is the axis, for vibrating it is a boundary, for swinging it is a point.
The Agent performs the intentional act.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
Angle identifies the amount that the Theme turns.
The Agent's manipulation of an Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Locus. This FE is usually expressed as a PP Complement.
This FE identifies the part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Theme.
Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the motion in place.
This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, that express the Direction of the swinging, vibrating or rotating.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Cause_to_perceive
d: An Agent, Actor, Entity, or Medium causes a Phenomenon to be perceived by a Perceiver. With an Actor, Entity, or Medium, the Perceiver is usually unspecified. NB: This may change in the future, but as of now this frame subsumes three closely-related cause/perceiver alternations: a.) perception of a specific Perceiver caused by an Agent, b.) perception of some implicit audience caused, possibly unintentionally, by an Actor, and c.) perception of some implicit audience caused by a Medium or Entity. Perhaps this frame is too broad - the different subject FEs seem to all indicate different ways of "showing."

ex.t: Aileen showed Rob the book.
He exhibited great interest in the project.
The second scene depicts  Dad  holding the ball for a place kick.

fes.d: The Agent intentionally creates a situation in which the Perceiver observes or experiences the Phenomenon.
The Phenomenon is an entity or idea that is perceived by the Perceiver.
The Perceiver is made to have a perceptual experience by the Agent.
The instrument or method by which the Perceiver was shown the Phenomenon.
A description of the way in which the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
When the event occurs.
Frequency describes how often the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
The location where the Agent causes the perception of the Perceiver.
The purpose of the Agent in creating the perception of the Perceiver.
An Actor is a sentient being who is exhibiting, possibly uninintentionally, some Phenomenon.
An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.
The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.
A Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the Actor or Co-participant Agent.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Cause_to_resume
d: An Agent acts so as to cause some process to begin again after an interruption or suspension.

ex.t: The two countries revived diplomatic relations after a lull of five years.

fes.d: A sentient being acts with the intention of causing a process to begin again.
The process which begins again after a suspension.
The period of time during which the process is suspended.
The time at which the process is restarted.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that causes the process to resume. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The location where the Agent causes the Process to resume.
The intentional act performed by the Agent that results in the resumption of the Process.
A description of the manner in which the Agent causes the resumption of the Process.
The length of time for which the Process continues after being started by the Agent.

name: Cause_to_rot
d: An Patient, which is an organic substance, undergoes the natural process of decay due to a Cause (or Agent).

ex.t: Moisture rotted the bread.

fes.d: The Agent intentionally brings about the decay of the Patient.
The Patient undergoes decay.
A depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
The Result of causing the Patient to rot.
An act performed by an Agent, or a sub-event centered around a Cause that leads it to cause the Patient to rot.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The time at which the Cause causes the Patient to rot.
The location at which the Cause acts upon the Patient.
An event which causes the Patient to rot.
The Agent may use an instrument to bring about the rotting.

name: Cause_to_start
d: A Cause, animate or inanimate, causes a process, the Effect, to begin. .

ex.t: The murder of Sergei Kirov set off a chain of events that culminated in the Great Terror of the 1930s.
Space email sparked astronaut jealousy.
A crime surge in a former coal town prompted a crackdown on illegal immigrants

fes.d: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Cause initiates.
This FE identifies the Place where the Effect occurs.
The Means is the way in which the Cause causes the process to begin.
This FE is for the Time when causing to start occurs
Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Cause results in the Effect.
To what end the Cause caused the Effect.
This FE identifies the first Co-timed_event of the started Effect.
The way in which the Cause causes the Effect.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
The reason why or the way in which the Cause causes the Effect.
The state of the world at the time when the Cause produces the Effect.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
A consecutive event to the starting of the Effect.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.
This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness

name: Cause_to_wake
d: An Agent or Cause causes a Sleeper to transition from the Sleep_state to wakeful consciousness.

ex.t: The earthquake woke me from a nightmare.

fes.d: Where the event takes place.
The person or being that is sleeping.
When the event occurs.
The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent wakes the Sleeper.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which an intentional act is performed. Mary woke him because he looked troubled.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
This describes the state out of which the Sleeper is awakened.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The degree to which the Sleeper ends up awake.

name: Ceasing_to_be
d: An Entity ceases to exist.

ex.t: Entire platoons have mysteriously vanished from battle, leaving enemy weapons to slice through empty air.

fes.d: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.
This is the Place where the new Entity ceases to exist.
This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity ceases to be.
This FE labels the Explanation of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.
This FE identifies the components into which the Entity dissipates.
This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.
The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.
This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which habitual or iterative actions are performed.
The way in which the Entity disappears.
The completeness of the disappearance of the Entity

name: Certainty
d: This frame concerns a Cognizer's certainty about the correctness of beliefs or expectations. It only includes uses where a Cognizer is expressed.

ex.t: Lermontov was certain he would come to the party.

fes.d: The Cognizer is the person whose certainty or uncertainty is at issue.
The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer has a certain/uncertain belief about.
The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.
This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer is certain or uncertain.
The FE Manner denotes the manner of the certainty or uncertainty.

The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the mental state of the Cognizer. Notice that we do NOT tag possessives such as 'her mother's' or 'on her face' that occur within the noun phrase of which the target adjective is a part. In sentences such as NOTE: We do NOT tag 'have' and its subject since the governor relationship is between the verb 'have' and the noun that the target adjective modifies rather than between the target adjective and the verb 'have'.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The reason for which the Cognizer is certain.

name: Change_accessibility
d: An Agent causes a Useful_location to become accessible (or non-accessible) to a Theme to a certain Degree. Instead of the Useful_location, the scene may be described with reference to a Portal (or part of the Portal, e.g., a door) to the Useful_location.

ex.t: They've blockaded the entrance -- no one can get in or out.
Police have cordoned off the area where the crime occurred.
The area has been barricaded to anyone but law enforcement officials.

fes.d: The Agent blocks access to the Useful_location.
The Useful_location is the place the Theme is headed towards and the Agent has changed the accessibility of.
The Theme is headed towards, or has an intention or tendency to head towards, the Useful_location, but is potentially blocked due to actions of the Agent.
The degree to which the Useful_location is or is not accessible.
The Agent may regulate access to the Useful_location by regulating access to a Portal, including a part of the portal that could block potential Themes, such as doors or gates.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action carried out by the Agent to bring about the change in accessibility.
The Time when the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.
The general Place where the blocking or allowing of access occurs.
The Purpose for which the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.
A portion of the Useful_location, usually its edge, where accessibility is blocked.
The Agent uses the Instrument to block access, often by placing the Instrument such that it cannot be traversed.

name: Change_direction
d: A Theme that is in motion assumes a new Direction in which it moves.

ex.t: We took our chances and turned right by a petrol station and, bingo, there she was--Fir Park.
Molly followed silently as Desmond left the large paneled hall and turned right through a swing door into a long, bare corridor.
Cross O'Connell Bridge and continue along D'Olier Street, make a right turn onto College Street. CNI

fes.d: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not required to be an animate mover, so it is different from a self-mover.
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, excluding directional expressions.
Any expression which indicates where the Theme ends up as a result of the change of direction. .

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Theme that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way.
The Speed is the rate at which the Theme changes direction.
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:
A phrase describing the state of the Theme during the act of changing direction.
The Place is the setting where the change of direction during the Theme's motion occurs.
The configuration formed by the Path that the Theme traverses during the change of direction.
The new direction in which the Theme continues its motion.
The time at which the change of direction takes place.
The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.
A factor which explains the change of direction of the Theme.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the change of direction occurs and which the change of direction is taken to be a part of.
The number of times that a change of direction occurs.

A larger conceptualization that includes the change of direction as an integral part. The change of direction expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
An unexpected event that affects the Theme, which is enabled by, and occurs after, the change of direction.

The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the change of direction event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.
The angle between the old and the new Direction in which the Theme moves.
The situation that results from the change of direction

name: Change_event_duration
d: In this frame, an Agent or Cause changes the duration of an Event. The Event will then take place for a New_duration, rather than the Initial_duration. This can be done with by certain Means, in a certain Manner or to a certain Degree.
