fes.d: Speaker is the sentient entity that delivers the Message.
The Addressee refers to the one toward whom the Communication_noise is directed. Addressee generally occurs in to or at PPs.

Message has a number of different realizations in this frame, including that-clauses, direct quotes, infinitival complements, for-to phrases, and NP Objects. Quoted Messages may either precede or follow the External Argument and verb, or may be discontinuous.
Topic occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by about.
Medium is used for a physical entity or channel that transmits the Message. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by on or in.
This FE identifies the state of the Speaker during the communication.
Manner describes the manner or style in which the Communication_noise is delivered.

The Communication_noise may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement.
Degree to which event occurs
The Means by which the Speaker communicates.
The Voice describes the Speaker's utterance or other message-encoded production.
This FE identifies the Place where an event occurs.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

This FE indicates that the communication act denoted by the target is in response to an earlier communication act in which the roles of Speaker and Addressee were reversed. This is conceptually akin to the Communication_response frame in which the targets themselves denote the responsive nature of the act.
This FE identifies the Time where the Communication noise event occurs.

name: Communication_response
d: This frame deals with a Speaker communicating a reply or response, a Message, to some prior communication or action, the Trigger.

ex.t: The landlord has not yet replied in writing to the tenant objecting the proposed alterations.DNI
"No, I do not agree with you," responded another officer to the CEO. DNI

fes.d: The Speaker is the sentient entity that communicates the reply or response. It is expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of a Target verb or as the Genitive modifier of a Target noun:
This is the person to whom the response is communicated. When expressed, this FE occurs as the direct object of a Target verb, or in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to":
The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a direct quote or a clause.
Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun Target:
As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in":
The Trigger is the prior communication or action to which a response is given. It can occur as an NP Object or a PP Complement.
Manner of performing an action
Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.
This FE identifies the Means by the Speaker achieves the communication of the response Message .
The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement:
The location in which the Speaker makes a verbal response.
The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.
An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.
The Duration of the communication response.

name: Commutation
d: An Executive_authority exchanges one penalty, the Original_punishment, for another less severe one, the New_punishment. The Offender is who received the Original_punishment is usually expressed as a modifier.

ex.t: On December 15, 1971, Governor Winfield Dunn conditionally commuted his sentence to twenty years.
On December 15, 1971, Governor Winfield Dunn conditionally commuted his sentence to twenty years.
She served about two years before President Carter commuted her sentence.

fes.d: The individual who was convicted of a crime and given a sentence (the Original_punishment).
The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to commute punishments.
A state of affairs that the Executive_authority is responding to in commuting the Original_punishment.
The time at which the Original_punishment is commuted.
The punishment the Offender was originally sentenced to.
The new reduced form of punishment that the Executive_authority orders for the Offender.

Any description of the commutation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Executive_authority that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location where the Executive_authority commutes the Original_punishment.
An action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the commutation.

name: Commutative_process
d: LUs in this frame describe a commutative operation of arithmetic, e.g. addition and multiplication, involving two numbers, labeled Term1 and Term2 or, collectively, Terms. When referencing the process, the numbers can be vague and are often omitted through indefinite null instantiation. There may also be a Calculator who applies the operation.

ex.t: Add three to five.
Any kid knows addition. INI

fes.d: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.
The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.
Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.
An entity that uses the arithmetic operation.

name: Commutative_statement
d: LUs in this frame describe a stative relationship between two numbers,Term1 and Term2 or, collectively, Terms, via a commutative arithmetic operation. The numbers are specifically expressed, along with the Result of the operation.

ex.t: The sum of two and three is five.
That's three times the amount I asked for!

fes.d: The number or role of a number that comes from the interaction of Term1 and Term2 via a commutative operation.
The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.
The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.
Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.

name: Compatibility
d: Item-1 and Item-2 are compatible with each other if they can exist or function together in some context without problems, conflict, or other undesirable situation. The set of Item-1 and Item-2 may be expressed jointly as Items. The Degree to which the Items are compatible may also be indicated, as may be a Parameter along whose lines the Items are compatible.

ex.t: Make sure your site is compatible with any browser.
Our software applications are compatible.

fes.d: The Frame Element Item_1 marks the grammatically more prominent of the two entities, i.e.the subject in active clauses, when they are expressed separately.
The Frame Element Item_2 marks the grammatically less prominent of the Items when they are expressed separately.
This FE is used when the Items are expressed jointly in a phrase, either a plural or a coordinated NP.
This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate the extent to which two Items are compatible.
This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate a Parameter or respect in which the Items are said to be compatible, not in conflict.

name: Competition
d: This frame is concerned with the idea that people (Participant_1, Participant_2, or Participants) participate in an organized, rule-governed activity (the Competition) in order to achieve some advantageous outcome (often the Prize). Rank and Score are different criteria by which the degree of achievement of the advantageous outcome is judged.

ex.t: He and I played tennis.

fes.d: This FE identifies the first (or only) participant in a competition.
This FE identifies the second participant in a competition.
This FE is used for plural NP participants in a competition.
This FE is used for the name of the competition.
This FE is used for the score in a game. EX: The Yankees won the game by two points.
This FE is used for the ranked results of a competition, and is translatable into a numerical value.
This FE indicates a prize won in a competition.
This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition.
Where the event takes place. A constituent tagged as Place may require annotation on a secondary FE-layer.
The way the Participants compete.
The action the Participants (or Participant_1) are involved in that constitutes a Competition.
The period of time when the Competition occurs.
This FE is used to describe the length of time over which competition occurs.
This FE is used to describe the intended outcome of the competition.
This FE describes the intensity of competition.
This FE expresses how often the Competition occurs.

name: Complaining
d: A Complainer communicates their negative emotional reaction to some state of affairs in a Complaint to an Addressee. As an alternative to the specific Complaint, the Topic of the speaker's Complaint may be specified. Likewise, instead of (or in addition to) the Complainer, a Medium may be stated.

ex.t: The top US commander in Iraq complained to the Pentagon last winter that his supply situation was so poor that it threatened Army troops' ability to fight.
He said he will lodge a complaint with the ACCC. DNI
On the rare occasions I complained to him about media bias, Peter immediately ordered up a story that included conservative objections to mainstream reports .

fes.d: The Complainer is the sentient entity that produces the Complaint (whether spoken or written).
The Addressee is the person to whom the Complaint is communicated.
The lamentable situation that the Complainer is communicating to the Addressee.
The Topic is the subject matter to which the Complaint pertains.

Any description of the complaining event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Complainer that affect the action (presumptuously, bitterly, vociferoursly ).
Frequency is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
An act whereby the Complainer makes a complaint.
The emotional or physical state of the Complainer that leads to their complaining.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Complainer to transmit the Complaint.
The state of the Complainer while making the Complaint.
The Time when the complaint is made.
This FE specifies the location where the complaining takes place.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular complaining event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
Degree selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes. This often means that the Explanation causes the complaint, but not in all cases. In particular, there are cases when the connection is a bit weaker than normal for causation. In these instances, cause is mediated by some actor responding in a complex way to the situation. Such cases are not paraphrasable in the language of direct causation.
An event or state which results from the complaining.

name: Completeness
d: A Whole, an entity with a substructure, is assessed for whether or not it has all the necessary parts that are defined for it or for an entity of its kind. The entity can be a concrete physical thing, an abstract thing, or a process with goals or sub-goals. When the entity is a process with a goal, then what is assessed for completeness can either be the extent to which all candidate participants are involved in or affected by the process, or the stage that the process has reached. Thus the last of the above examples can either mean that all parts of the model are understood or that the model is fully understood as opposed to, for instance, merely intuitively apprehended.

ex.t: What happens after the PPB investigation is complete?
Enter the number of days since the last complete backup was made.
This distinguishes them from organisms in the phylum Platyhelminthes, who have only an incomplete digestive tract.

fes.d: An expression indicating a deviation of the actual level of completeness from the level indicated by the target.
The entity that is being assessed for having all its necessary parts or not.
The interval of time when the completeness of the entity is assessed.

name: Compliance
d: This frame concerns Acts and State_of_Affairs for which Protagonists are responsible and which either follow or violate some set of rules or Norms.

ex.t: A lot of people suspect that blocking savers' access to their money violates the new constitution's explicit ban on compulsory loans to the government.
Not that by adhering to the subject-before-predicate principle, the translator of the above extract has had to ignore the principle of end-weight.

fes.d: The Protagonist's behavior is in or out of compliance with norms.
This FE identifies the Act that is judged to be in or out of compliance with the Norms.
A State_of_affairs may violate a law or rule.
This FE identifies the rules or Norms that ought to guide a person's behavior.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the compliance ocurrs.
Depictive identifies any description of the Actor or Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the compliance occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which the compliance is (or is not) accomplished.
This FE identifies the Result of compliance.
This FE identifies the Time when the act of compliance or non-compliance occurs.
The Explanation for complying with the Norm.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Concessive
d: A speaker marks a Conceded_state_of_affairs as being or implying a contradiction to the Main_assertion. Some LUs specify the Main_assertion, others the Conceded_state_of_affairs, as referring to the preceding discourse (i.e. DNI), while yet others are conjunctions joining the two.

ex.t: Although she had some trouble , she was able to finish about two hours early .
Nevertheless , we did win . DNI
I wanted to come , but I did n't remember where the party was .

fes.d: A proposition or set of propositions that the speaker wants the addressee to believe or take for granted. This statement is not asserted, but presupposed by the speaker of the sentence, and is mentioned to contrast with the Main_assertion. It would or could seem to predict a situation different than the Main_assertion, but, for reasons left implicit, this normal prediction is contradicted by the fact that the Main_assertion and the Conceded_state_of_affairs are both simultaneously true.
An entity which metonymically stands in for an associated Statement.

The statement that the speaker wishes to assert or offer as their main contribution to the discourse, which is be modified or hedged in some way by the Conceded_state_of_affairs. The force of the contribution of the Main_assertion is presented as undiluted by the fact that something different from the Main_assertion would normally by predicted, based on the facts in the Conceded_state_of_affairs.

name: Condition_symptom_relation
d: A Patient has a Medical_condition that can be understood by its Symptoms. This frame has been constructed to list all the ways to speak of relating a Patient, a Medical_condition, and Symptoms, including LUs that are also related to much more general frames like Causation (e.g. cause.v).

ex.t: Neurally mediated syncope is thethe most common cause of syncope.
Tietze Syndrome and Costochondritis Tietze syndrome manifested by painful swelling of one or more costochondral articulations

fes.d: The person who has a Medical_condition associated with Symptom.
A holistic description of the medical state of the Patient (or a part of the state of the Patient), which may or may not indicate the cause of a deviation from normal.
A deviation from normal function or feeling which is noticed by a Patient or physician, indicating the presence of a Medical_condition
Specific type of people in which a Medical_condition is normally found
When a Symptom or Medical_condition occurs.
The location where a Medical_condition presents.
The commonality of a Medical_condition or Symptom
The degree to which a Medical_condition is associated with a Symptom(s).
Explanation for why a Symptom(s) or Medical_condition(s) occur.
Genetic, Biological, and Environmental Influences affect Medical_conditions

name: Conditional_occurrence
d: A Consequence is presented as occurring if the Profiled_possibility occurs. See Conditional_scenario for further information.

ex.t: If you take too long , the train will leave without you .

fes.d: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Negated_possibility.
The situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.

Pragmatically emphasizes a speaker's assumption of the truth of the Profiled_possibility for the conversation's duration. This FE does not occur for all LUs in the frame, and is closed-class, limited to the word 'always'.

name: Conditional_scenario
d: In this scene, two mutually exclusive possibilities are presented, the Profiled_possibility and the Opposite_possibility, each of which has a consequence associated with it, the Consequence (associated with the Profiled_possibility) and the Anti_consequence (associated with the Opposite_possibility). Usually, the Consequence and Anti_consequence are also mutually exclusive, but in some cases (especially with "even if") the same Consequence results regardless of whether one considers the Profiled_possibility or the Opposite_possibility. Neither of the possibilities is asserted and neither can simply be merged with a factual understanding of the world. Both possibilities are presented as uncertain, and the Profiled_possibility may be further characterized with a neutral stance towards it, or with a doubtful, negative stance, depending on the specific lexical unit introducing the conditional and what verb forms are used in the Profiled_possibility. The most common use of lexical units connected to the Conditional_scenario is for prediction; in this case the conditionals pair up possibilities with predicted consequences. Subtypes of this use include, but are not limited to: (1) contingencies: (2) conditional promises (usually when making a deal): (3) threats (which are inherently conditional): (4) hypotheticals, especially when a different choice was made in the past and one imagines it would lead to a different outcome: (5) descriptions of general rules of the world: (6) descriptions of the characteristics of individual entities or persons that have an effect under certain circumstances: Speech act conditionals: Lexical units of these frames can also be used in a pattern called a "Speech Act conditional". In this case, the conditional presents a statement that is relevant to the conversation if the Profiled_possibility holds. The relevance of the statement is a Consequence of the Profiled_possibility, but there is no distinct alternative intended, so this usage does not normally allow distancing verb forms (see Dancygier and Sweetser 2005: 114-115). As shown in the above example, we annotate the potentially relevant statement as Consequence. This is based on an analysis of the filler of the Consequence as metonymically expressing a message similar to "it is relevant to say the following: ...". Such cases should be tagged with the clause-level tag "Speech act". Thus in the following example, it is relevant for the speaker to explain the situation by saying "no, she's not my wife" if the other person is wondering about that possibility: Metalinguistic conditionals: In addition, conditionals can be used to talk about the actual encoding of a message and usually encode a strong opinion about the appropriateness or inappropriateness of a description, often in contrast to someone else's contrary opinion. Such sentences should be tagged "Metalinguistic", as in the following: Epistemic conditionals: Finally, conditionals can be used to profile a reasoning process. While all conditionals mark the connection from a hypothetical situation to an associated conclusion, many conditionals specifically highlight this process of thinking about the connection, especially when the reasoning is cooccurring with speaking, and most obviously when reasoning from effects to causes. In such cases as the following, we mark the clause as "Epistemic": Many sentences are vague about exactly to what degree they profile the reasoning process, so sentences like the following can be legitimately labeled "Epistemic" or not: Special constructions: Conditionals interact significantly with ellipsis constructions, particularly because they often occur in parallel structures in which different possibilities are being contrasted, or cases in which there is a contrast between what is always true and what is only conditionally true. In these cases, the Profiled_possibility and the Consequence or Anti_consequence may be abbreviated under the same conditions that apply to ellipsis in the rest of the language. See the following examples: In these examples, "an additional day or two" is understood as "she would stay an additional day or two", based on the immediately preceding sentence. This is a general construction that allows a finite sentence that is parallel to an immediately adjacent clause to be abbreviated just to the content in addition to or contrasting with the adjacent clause. Since it must be interpreted as a full clause and occurs in exactly the places a clause is expected, we actually annotate the PT of the Consequence as "Sfin" in these cases. The adjective "necessary" in the Profiled_possibility, however, is not licensed by a general construction that allows an adjective like necessary to be used arbitrarily in the kinds of places a clause would be found. Therefore, in this case, we consider the adjective to represent a separate valence with PT "AP".

ex.t: If you read caerfully, you 'll see the letters are swapped.
Unless you read carefully , you wo n't understand what I said .
If it rains, the ceremony will be under the tent.

fes.d: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Opposite_possibility.
The implicit situation that is mutually exclusive with the Profiled_possibility.
The situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.
The situation that follows as a result of the Opposite_possibility.

name: Conduct
d: An Agent acts in a certain Manner either generally or under some particular Circumstances. The conduct may also be directed specifically towards an Affected_party.

ex.t: He pledges to conduct himself with honesty and humility.
This year they have behaved themselves particularly impudently.
His appearance was as immaculate as ever and his bearing composed and dignified.

fes.d: This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.
This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.
A person to whom behavior is directed by the Agent.
This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.
The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.
The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.
The way in which the Agent behaves in the specified manner.
The Domain of human behavior in which the Agent acts in a certain Manner
The extent to which the (usually 'good' or 'bad') conduct of the Agent deviates from some standard or norm
An explicit point to which the conduct of the Agent is compared.

name: Conferring_benefit
d: A Benefactor confers a Beneficial_situation to a Beneficiary. Unlike in Commerce_scenario, the recipient is not necessarily required to pay for the good or service that they receive. Therefore, the element of benevolence is profiled. Dual FE-layer annotation:

ex.t: His presence at the summit did not BENEFIT diplomatic relations in the slightest.
His
The foundation's 50m donation BENEFITS the country's educational system immensely.

fes.d: The Benefactor is the person or thing that gives an advantage to the Beneficiary.
The Beneficiary is person or thing that receives an advantage from the Benefactor.
The Beneficial_situation is the item or action that is given to or done for the Beneficiary by the Benefactor. A change of possession can, but does not have to occur.
The degree to which the Beneficiary gains an advantage from the Benefactor.
The Domain describes the type of advantage that is conferred.
A Subset of beneficial situations is selected from the set of beneficial situations in a specific domain, though the domain need not be explicitly named.

name: Confronting_problem
d: An Agent becomes involved in an Issue which has negative consequences for them. The Agent will normally respond to resolve the Issue.

ex.t: I confronted both issues.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Issue that the Agent deals with.
The Agent is the person who is acting to deal with the Issue.
This FE identifies the Place where the intentional act occurs.
This FE identifies the reason why the Agent confronts the issue.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.
This FE identifies the way in which an Agent goes about facing the Issue.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Domain within which the Agent acts.
The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The Result describes the resulting outcome of the confronting act.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.
This FE gives a description of the confronting event as a whole.

name: Connecting_architecture
d: An entity is integrated into a building as a Part of a (possibly unexpressed) Whole which may refer to the whole building or merely to a sub-part of the building. The Part itself connects locations within the building to each other, Connected_locations. If a particular point of view is adopted in the context of real or imagined motion, then one of the locations can be construed as Goal and the other as Source.

ex.t: It was of great interest to me to see the star signs of Taurus the Bull and Leo the Lion on the staircase to the upper Palace.
All visitors may use the elevator between the Main Level and the Upper Level instead of the main staircase
The window into the garden was open.

fes.d: A Part of a larger architectural unit, the Whole.
An architectural unit which includes the Part.
A property relating to the Part.
This is a property of the Part that situates the Part within the Whole.
Any indication of what makes up the Part, including components, ingredients, etc.
The Individual who creates the Part.
The Source is one of the Connected_locations treated as source.
Two or more named locations that are connected by the architectural Part.
The Direction is the direction or directions the Part of connecting architecture runs.
The Goal is one of the Connected_locations treated as a goal

name: Connectors
d: The Connector is an artifact created to affix a Connected_item or to bind onto a Fixed_location and is primarily so used. A more specific Use may also be specified. Certain words in this frame (e.g. bond, chain in the phrase in chains) indicate specifically that the Connector is being used to immobilize something. Connectors have a wide variety of physical forms: long, thin, and flexible for tying (ropes, bonds, withies); solid, with a shape corresponding to holes in the entities to be connected (bolts, nails, pegs); and liquid (glues, adhesives, pastes).

ex.t: A waterproof adhesive should be used for this exterior job.
His bonds had to be loosened before they could be cut.
She jerked on His neck rope again, to keep his attention.

fes.d: Connector identifies the entity or substance that forms the bond that maintains the Item in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a "with"-PP.
This FE identifies the entity that is attached to the Connector in such a way as to stabilize their position or to immobilize them.
This FE identifies the location to which the Connector is attached.
The items that a Connector usually attaches or the type of activity the attaching is generally for.
Material identifies the material of which the Connector is made.
Type designates the type of Connector. Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.
The term used to refer to a Connector.
The individual or group that creates a Connector.
The time at which the Connector comes to be.
A characteristic of the Connector.

name: Conquering
d: This frame describes a Theme losing its autonomy and perhaps sustaining material damage as the result of a successful invasion on the behalf of a Conqueror.

ex.t: The Spaniards conquered the Incas with both the Cross and the arquebus
He said that the aim had been the takeover of the Soviet government by "advocates of swift privatization"
The Romans fell to the Goths in 410 AD.

fes.d: The Conqueror is the entity that overtakes the Theme.
The Theme is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Conqueror.
This FE describes the intensity and extent of the conquering event.
The manner in which the Conqueror takes over the Theme.
The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Conqueror.
The location where the Conqueror takes over the Theme.
The Time at which the Conqueror seizes the Theme. .
The reason why the Conqueror seized the Theme.
The tool used by the Conqueror to seize the Theme.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
Frequency is the number of times the Conquering event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Contact_image_schema
d: A Profiled_region occupies the space in contact with the Ground.

fes.d: A region of space in contact with a Ground.
An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Contacting
d: A Communicator (whose Location may be indicated) directs a Communication to an Addressee at a particular Address. Note that no actual successful communicative act is implied, only the successful completion of acts which would establish the communication. (In other words, Mari can e-mail Jon without Jon ever reading it.) NB: The Address or Location_of_communicator may be a virtual address, such as an e-mail or telephone number.

ex.t: Disgruntled voters phoned Congressman Neil at his Washington residence with complaints about the recent increases in corporate welfare.
She tried to call from the payphone down the street.

fes.d: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a message to another person.
The physical or abstract setting in which the message is conveyed.
The person that receives the message from the Communicator.
This FE is used for a (metaphorical) place in a system of communication where Communicators and Addressees can access the system.
The information that the Communicator wishes to impart to the Addressee, often to get a particular response. In this frame the Communication is not necessarily received by the Addressee.
This FE identifies the Purpose for the Communicator contacting the Addressee. Often, this FE is used to identify a PP-for which indicates what the Communicator is attempting to obtain.
This is the subject matter to which the message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about".
The location occupied by the Communicator.
This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.
The Intermediary is the person who facilitates the contact.
The Depictive notes the state of one of the participants in the contacting event.
The number of times a Communicator contacts the Addressee per unit of time.
Any description of the nature of the action (e.g. "the same way"), including especially internal states of the Communicator that also influence the way the action is carried out.
An action of the Communicator that enables them to make contact.

name: Container_focused_placing
d: An Agent or Cause affects a Goal location by moving a Theme, but without necessarily filling or covering it. This frame is for Inheritance purposes.

fes.d: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.
The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location.
The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion.
The Path is the trajectory of the motion.
The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.
Degree to which the filling occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action.
The Manner in which the filling occurs.
The Means by which the filling occurs.
The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.
The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal.
When the filling occurs.
Where the filling takes place.
The purpose for which the Agent fills the Goal.
The Instrument with which the filling occurs.
The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs.
An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Container_focused_removing
d: An Agent or Cause partially or totally changes the state of a Source object, towards having less of the Theme. This frame is primarily for Inheritance.

fes.d: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying.
The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of".
The Source is the region or container which is emptied of something. In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object.
The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.
The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.
The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.
Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying.
The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.
The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.
The Result of the Agent emptying the Source.
This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source.
The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying.
The location where the emptying takes place.
The time at which the emptying takes place.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Containers
d: This frame covers entities which are prototypically conceived of and created to fulfill the function of containing--i.e. Containers that contain objects or substances, the Contents. This can be expressed as a complement , and includes potential or intended contents. A Container may also have an Owner, a current Relative_location, Material from which it is constructed, a method of Construction, and a Type. Note the connection between words in this frame and those in the Filling, Emptying, and Fullness frames.

ex.t: a bag of popcorn
underwear drawer
Chuck's suitcase

fes.d: Container is an object which is conventionally used as a container. Target words in this frame are tagged with this frame element.
Contents is the object(s)/stuff contained in the Container.
Material identifies the material of which the Container is made.
Type designates the type of Container. Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.
Relative_location is the location of the Container.
Construction indicates the action (or causer) which creates the Container.
Owner identifies the owner of the Container.
Use identifies the purpose for which an artifact is constructed and the activity with which it is associated, or the Contents protypically contained in the Container.
This FE identifies a Part of the Container.
The Descriptor describes some aspect of the Container.

name: Containing
d: In this frame a Container holds within its physical boundaries the Contents.

ex.t: The box holds three hundred pictures.

fes.d: The Container is the physical object which holds within its boundaries the Contents
The Contents is the substance or objects contained within the physical bounds of the Container.
The time at which the Container holds the Contents.

name: Containment_scenario
d: In this situation, a Container has within it some Contents. The Container has an Interior, a space which is potentially empty, but instead is occupied with the Contents.

fes.d: The non-point-like entity which has a Boundary which (largely or completely) separates the Interior region from the Exterior region. It normally also has a Portal which links the Interior and Exterior regions.
The (finite) region which is inside the Boundary of the Container, disjoint from the Exterior, and overall closer or included in the Container.
A (relatively small) region which goes through the Boundary, connecting the Interior and Exterior of the Container.
Thing or substance located within the Container.
The period or moment in which the Contents occupy the Interior of the Container.

name: Contingency
d: The answer to one open question, the Outcome, is dictated (partially or completely) by the answer to another open question, the Determinant, i.e. if the answer to the Determinant is known, the answer to the Outcome can be predicted. The Degree of predictive power and the Circumstances under which the dependency holds can also be expressed.

ex.t: Economic policy is partially a function of cultural values.
Well, that depends ... DNI
In Mediaeval times, status was dependent on birth.

fes.d: An open question that is (to some degree) predictable from the Determinant.
An open question that determines the Outcome.
The amount of predictive power supplied by the Determinant with respect to the Outcome.

The conditions under which the Determinant dictates the Outcome. Oftentimes it is expressed in a fashion similar to Time and Place in other frames, but such cases are actually metonymic for the prevailing conditions of the Time and/or Place.

name: Continued_state_of_affairs
d: A State_of_affairs has held and continues to hold up to the Reference_occasion.

ex.t: To date, the Department already has numerous requests for new systems to be developed.
SAGE has no activities planned as of yet.
PBGC guarantees the benefit that you had earned up to the date of plan termination

fes.d: A state which holds prior to and up through the Reference_occasion.
The time or event (normally speech time) with respect to which the State_of_affairs is located.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Contrary_circumstances
d: An Event takes place despite the existence of an Adversity that would otherwise support Contrary_circumstances or results.

ex.t: He finished the race despite his ankle breaking.

fes.d: The Event that occurs despite an Adversity that would seem to contradict the possibility of its occurence.
The Adversity is a state of affairs or entity that hinders or negatively affects the Event.
The Contrary_circumstances are the circumstances that would normally be expected to occur given the presence of the Adversity.

name: Contrition
d: An Experiencer feels bad about a choice, an Action, or a failure to do something, which they now consider to have been a mistake or wrong. The emotional state of the Experiencer may be showing in gestures or facial expressions, viz. an Expressor.

ex.t: Smithers did not repent of his crime.
It is God who rejoices at the repentance of his sinner.

fes.d: The FE Experiencer indicates the person who experiences the emotion about their prior action.
The FE Action marks expressions that indicate a prior action that the Experiencer has come to feel bad about.
The FE Degree marks expressions that indicate how badly the Experiencer feels about their prior action.
The FE Expressor marks expressions that indicate a gesture or body part which is displaying the Emotional_state of the Experiencer.
The FE Authenticity marks expressions that indicate whether the Experiencer genuinely feels contrite or just acts as if they did.
The FE Emotional_state is modified by an adjective that indicates the Experiencer is contrite.

This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.
The Time at which the Experiencer or the Expressor is contrite.
The way in which the Experiencer or Expressor has contrition.

name: Control
d: A Controlling_entity, Controlling_situation, or Controlling_variable control a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable. The latter, dependent, element or some aspect of it is not just influenced, but determined by the controlling element.

ex.t: Can you control the robot?
Although you may not be able to control every situation, you can control your reaction.
Students do not have control over the temperature of the heating water.

fes.d: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.
An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by a Controlling_entity or an Controlling_situation.
A scalar variable (with unspecified value) which has an effect on the Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.
A situation whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by a Controlling_entity, Controlling_situation, or Controlling_variable.
A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of a Controlling_entity, a Controlling_situation, or a Controlling_variable.
A situation whose temporal or other characteristics control a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.
The Degree to which the Controlling element affects the Dependent element.
The Time at which the controlling occurs.
The location at which the controlling occurs.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Influencing_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Controller_object
d: This frame contains items which, when manipulated, alter the function of some device, internal or external.

ex.t: This button makes the radio turn on.

fes.d: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use. This is often an incorporated FE.
The use for which an control is intended.
An individual or individuals that bring the Control into existence.
The time at which an Control comes into existence.
The term used to refer to an Control.
An indication of the subtype of Artifact.
Any indication of what makes up the Control, including components, ingredients, etc.
The entity which the Control controls.

name: Convey_importance
d: Through a Message, a Speaker (sometimes encoded metonymically by a Medium) communicates the relative importance of the state of affairs denoted by the Message.

ex.t: Reid emphasized that he and Dean meet every month.
Above all , Mr Tsongas stressed the need for his message to be heard.
Professor Perkin has stressed how favourable Britain 's situation was .

fes.d: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.
The Addressee is the audience to which the Speaker communicates the Message.
The proposition whose denotation the Speaker presents as important.
The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, in particular secondary effects (loudly), general descriptions comparing events (the same way), and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Means by which the Speaker communicates the importance of the state of affairs denoted by the Message.
The time at which the Speaker communicates a Message.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Speaker conveys a Message whose denotation they present as an important fact to be aware of.
The degree of importance that the Speaker conveys the Message's denotation as having.
The location where the Speaker delivers the Message.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative. Period_of_iterations can co-occur with either the peripheral FE Duration or the extra-thematic FE Duration_of_final_state (although these cannot occur together).
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Convoy
d: A Convoy consists of several Vehicles which move together to transport Cargo from a Source to a Goal.

ex.t: A convoy of several dozen vehicles was stopped at the border for several hours while border guards inspected their cargo.
Trained gunmen hijacked a medical supply convoy headed for the city.
The southbound convoy of two vans and several armored vehicles arrived safely 10 hours after it had departed.

fes.d: The constituent vehicles that make up the Convoy.
The group of vehicles transporting the Cargo.
This FE describes a property of the Convoy rather than the Vehicles and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.
The term used to refer to the Convoy.
The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Convoy.
The Possessor of the Convoy. Often a nation or organization that wants the Cargo transported.
The Cargo are the goods and/or individuals transported by the Convoy. This FE also covers the intended use of the transported goods.
The Source is the beginning of the path along which the Convoy travels.
The Path along which the Convoy travels.
The Goal is the endpoint of path along which the Convoy travels.
The direction in which the Convoy travels.

People and possibly other elements of the convoy who support and defend the transport of the Cargo are the Support. In military contexts, this typically consists of soldiers and military vehicles who provide defense for the conveying Vehicles and Cargo.
The general Place where the Convoy is operating.

name: Cooking_creation
d: This frame describes food and meal preparation. A Cook creates a Produced_food from (raw) Ingredients. The Heating_Instrument and/or the Container may also be specified.

ex.t: Caitlin baked some cookies from the pre-packaged dough.

fes.d: The Cook prepares the Produced_food.
The Produced_food is the result of a Cook's efforts.
This FE identifies the Heating_Instrument with which the Cook prepares the Food.
This FE identifes the Container that holds the food being produced. Things that apply the heat directly are Heating_Instruments, e.g. crock-pot, electric griddle.
This FE identifies the Place where the cooking creation occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which the cooking creation is performed.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the cooking creation is performed.
Recipient identifies the person for whom the food has been prepared.
This FE identifies the Time when the cooking creation occurs.
This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the cooking creation performed.
This FE identifies the Ingredients which are altered by the Cook to create the Produced_food.

name: Corporal_punishment
d: Blend of Rewards_and_punishments and Bodily_injury in which the Agent performs some action intended to cause Bodily harm to the Evaluee as a consequence of some action or belief of the Evaluee (the Reason).

ex.t: The Sheriff flogged him for his crimes.

fes.d: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.
The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward.
Where the event takes place.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
When the event occurs.
Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:
Manner of performing an action
Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a for-PP, e.g.
Result of an event
This FE is the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
Degree to which event occurs
This frame element marks a quantity related to the seriousness of the punished behavior.

name: Correctness
d: A particular piece of Information is evaluated for its accuracy. The Degree of correctness may also be expressed. The Source of information may also metonymically stand in for the Information.

ex.t: Is your reputation at risk due to incorrect information?
If your dealership service people make such totally wrong claims, I would be uncomfortable trusting their warranty claims too.
All users must verify the correctness of their own information.

fes.d: The Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.
The degree to which the Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.
The aspect of reality which is accurately modeled by the Information.
The aspect of the Information which accurately models reality.
How often the Information is correct.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The Source is the agent who holds the correct/incorrect information.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame, which typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame.
The way in which the Source is correct/incorrect.
The Time at which the Information or the Source is correct.
The physcial context that the Information is found in.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
The outcome of the correctness if the Source or Information.
The event which communicates the Information.
The Topic about which the Source has accurate information.

name: Corroding
d: In this frame the Patient, an inorganic item, undergoes a chemical process which renders it less useful, desirable or stable.

ex.t: The bike rusted.
The metal corroded into a mass of slime.
The bikes rusted from their former beauty.

fes.d: Initial_state is the original state of the Patient.
This FE identifes the Duration of time for which the Patient corrodes.
The Place where the Patient corrodes.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Patient corrodes.
This FE identifies the Result of the change of phase.
The Time when the Patient corrodes.
The Patient undergoes a change.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Patient corrodes.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE identifies the Speed at which the Patient corrodes.

name: Corroding_caused
d: In this frame, the Patient, an inorganic item, undergoes a chemical process caused by another entity, which renders it less useful, desirable or stable. The process may or may not be under the control of an Agent.

ex.t: The metal was corroded by the water.
Acid rain corroded the metal into a mass of slime.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cause corrodes the Patient.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Cause corrodes the Patient.
This FE identifies the Initial_state of the Patient.
This FE identifies the Place where the Cause corrodes the Patient.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Patient is corroded.
This FE identifies the Result of the caused corrosion.
This FE identifies the Time when the Cause corrodes the Patient.
The Patient is corroded by the Cause.
This FE identifies the Speed at which the Cause corrodes the Patient.
The Subregion identifies the part of a larger whole that is affected.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cause corrodes the Patient.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Cause corrodes the Patient.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Patient is corroded.
Cause identifies an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that corrodes the Patient. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Cause.
The individual that corrodes the Patient.
The Agent may use an Instrument to cause the corrosion.

name: Cotheme
d: This frame contains words that necessarily indicate the motion of two distinct objects. The Theme is typically animate and is expressed the same way a Self-mover is expressed in the Self-motion frame--i.e. as the subject of a target verb. The Cotheme may or may not be animate and is typically expressed as a direct object or an oblique. Source, Path, Goal, and the other frame elements common to motion words also regularly occur with the words in this frame.

ex.t: She accompanied him in the ambulance to Hollywood Memorial Hospital.
Police persue teenage joyrider across three counties.
My pursuit of academic superiority shows that I was still striving to be the person my parents wanted me to be.

fes.d: This is the entity, frequently a living being, which moves in relation to the Cotheme. Normally the Theme frame element is expressed as an external argument.
This frame element is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:

Source marks any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the motion of the Cotheme. In prepositional phrases, the object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

Path marks phrases that describe the Theme and Cotheme's trajectory of motion and which are neither expressions of the Source nor the Goal of motion. The notion Path also includes directional expressions.

Any expression which tells where the Cotheme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Note that if the Cotheme is animate, the Theme need not also end up in the same place. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance.

Phrases marked with this frame element describe a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Any expression which characterizes the extent of the motion of the Theme and Cotheme expresses the frame element Distance.

Area marks expressions which describe a general area in which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element.
This frame element marks a depictive phrase describing the Theme.
An Event in which the Cotheme is involved. Usually this is some kind of travel.
This frame element expresses the Means by which a (volitional) Theme moves in relation to the Cotheme.
Phrases marked with this frame element mark resultant states that the Cotheme can reach due to the motion event.

This frame element denotes the means of conveyance on which the Theme is traveling. The Mode_of_Transportation can be the Theme's own body or a vehicle. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
Phrases that describe the rate of motion of the Theme are marked Speed.
Phrases that denote a physical path on which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place are marked Road.
The amount of time for which motion occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the motion occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which a Theme moves.
The Following_distance is the distance between the Theme and Cotheme.
The Handle is active zone of the Cotheme.
The Place is the location which provides a setting for a defined motion (that is one with Source, Path or Goal).
Some event or state of affairs that leads to the Theme following the Cotheme.
The direction in which the Theme and Cotheme move.

name: Counterattack
d: An Assailant physically attacks a Victim (which is usually but not always sentient), causing or intending to cause the Victim physical damage. The attack is a response to an earlier attack by the Victim on the current Assailant (or by actors associated with the Assailant or Victim). A Weapon used by the Assailant may also be mentioned, in addition to the usual Place, Time, Purpose, Reason, etc. Sometimes a location is used metonymically to stand for the Assailant or the Victim, and in such cases the Place FE will be annotated on a second FE layer.

ex.t: Are we counterattacking them just to keep them off balance?

fes.d: This FE is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's attack.
An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.
The person (or other self-directed entity) that is responding to a prior attack by attempting physical harm to the Victim.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.
This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.
A state of affairs that the Assailant is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Victim.
This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.

The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describeing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the Attack occurs.

This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.
The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Examples include once, twice, [Cardinal expression] + times, a lot.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.
The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Court_examination
d: A Questioner asks a Witness (or defendant) questions in the context of a court procedure.

ex.t: We 'd like to cross-examine the witness if we can.

fes.d: The individual who asks a Witness questions.
A person who is present in a courtroom in order to give some form of evidence, has been sworn in, and is being examined by a Questioner.
The subject matter to which the examination pertains.
When the examination occurs.
Where the examination takes place.
The Manner in which the Questioner examines the Witness.
The Purpose of the examination.
The Means by which the Questioner examines the Witness.
How long the examination takes place.

name: Craft
d: A particular Activity, performed conventionally or habitually by more than one Practitioner within a Culture, is described in terms of its method.

ex.t: One lived-in cabin also had a grassy roof, as if the craft of thatching had died out locally

fes.d: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Activity that is being performed habitually or conventionally.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose Activity is at issue.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Place in which the Activity is performed.
This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the Activity.
A Culture within which the Activity is performed.

name: Create_physical_artwork
d: A Creator creates an artifact that is typically an iconic Representation of an actual or imagined entity or event. The Representation may also be evocative of an idea while not based on resemblance.

ex.t: Diagrams must be clearly drawn on construction paper. CNI
I took his picture and told him that if it came out well I would make him a copy.
In about 1305 and 1306 Giotto painted a notable series of 38 frescoes.

fes.d: An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.
The time at which a Representation is created.
The entity that is created to represent either iconically or abstractly.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).
This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.
This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.
The physical location that holds the Representation.
An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.
The location in which the Creator produces the Representation.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the creation of the Representation ogically follows.
The entity which the Creator uses to create the work of art.
An action performed by the Creator which brings about the creation of the Representation.
A characteristic of the Creator or the Representation.
A representation of the entity depicted which the Creator uses as a reference in the creation of the Representation. For instance, another piece of art, a photograph, or his/her memory.

name: Create_representation
d: A Creator produces a physical object which is to serve as a Representation of an actual or imagined entity or event, the Represented.

ex.t: Epstein saw the machine-man and carved him in shiny metal.
Picasso drew some violent looking birds.
Towards the end of his life, Munch painted himself as a ghost.

fes.d: The entity produced by the Creator to evoke in an audience the idea of the Represented.
An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.
The time at which a Representation is created.
The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Representation.
A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is presented.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).
This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.
This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.
The physical Material that is used in the production of the Representation.
An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.
The location in which the artist produces the representation.
The entity used by the Creator to make a Representation of the Represented entity.
The action of the Creator that allows them to make a Representation of the Represented entity.
Iterations is the number of times the Creator creates the representation.
A representation of the Represented which the Creator uses as a reference in the creation of the artwork. For instance, another piece of art, a photograph, or his/her memory.

name: Creating
d: A Cause leads to the formation of a Created_entity.

ex.t: Dr. Frankenstein created a monster.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Components that are attached together to form a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the entity that the Agent intentionally creates.
This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action. We wandered around naked. Cicadas screech unseen from within.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.
This FE identifies the Manner in which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.
This FE identifies the place ehere the Agent intentionally creates the new entity.
This FE identifes the Time when an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
This FE identifies the instrument with which an Agent intentionally creates a Created_entitiy.
A secondary agent with whom the Creator intentionally creates the Created_entity.
The Creator creates a created entity.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Creator intentionally creates a new entity.
The Creator's intended purpose for the Created_entity.
The Beneficiary benefits in some way from the creation of the Created_entity.
The Role that the Created_entity takes (or is intended to take, if there is a Creator).
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The individual who is intended to receive the Created_entity.

name: Crime_scenario
d: A (putative) Crime is committed and comes to the attention of the Authorities. In response, there is a Criminal_investigation and (often) Arrest and criminal court proceedings. The Investigation, Arrest, and other parts of the Criminal_Process are pursued in order to find a Suspect (who then may enter the Criminal_process to become the Defendant) and determine if this Suspect matches the Perpetrator of the Crime, and also to determine if the Charges match the Crime. If the Suspect is deemed to have committed the Crime, then they are generally given some punishment commensurate with the Charges.

fes.d: The individual which is under suspicion of having committed the Crime.
The individual that commits a Crime.
An act, generally intentional, that matches the description that belongs to an official Charge.
A description of a type of act that is not permissable according to the law of society.

The group which is responsible for the maintenance of law and order, and as such have been given the power to investigate Crimes, find Suspects and determine if a Suspect should be submitted to the Criminal_process.

name: Criminal_investigation
d: This frame describes the process that involves the inquiry and determination by an authority, the Investigator, of the circumstances surrounding an Incident perpetrated by a Suspect.

ex.t: The police are investigating the bank's reported loss of several thousand dollars from their downtown branch's top security vault. DNI
Authorities are investigating several murders. DNI

fes.d: The Investigator is the person or agency that investigates the Suspect of a crime (Incident).
The Investigator attempts to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the Incident, which is typically a criminal act (murder, robbery) or the result of such an act (death, loss of money).
When the Investigator investigates the Incident.
The length of the investigation.
This FE denotes the Suspect that is investigated by the Investigator.

name: Criminal_process
d: A Suspect is arrested by Authorities on Charges related to an Offense, then is arraigned as a Defendant. If at any time the Defendant pleads guilty, then the Defendant is sentenced, otherwise the Defendant first goes to trial. During trial, the Defense and Prosecution present arguments on behalf of and against the Defendant, respectively. If the Jury comes up with a guilty verdict at the end of the trial, the Defendant is sentenced. In the end, the Defendant is either released or is given a Sentence by a Judge at the sentencing. The Core roles in this frame and its subframes include Authorities, Charges, Court, Defendant, Defense, Judge, Jury, Offense, Prosecution, and Suspect. Non-Core roles include Place, Time, Victim, and Witness.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Court involved in a trial.
This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
The Defendant is charged with an Offense.
The Judge heads the Court where arraignment occurs and the case is tried.
This FE identifies the attorney(s) prosecuting the Defendant.
This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.
The Defense represents the interests of the Defendant.
This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.
This FE identifies the Offense which the Defendant is accused of committing.
The Authorities charge the Suspect with commiting a crime, and take him/her into custody.
The Suspect is taken into custody by the Authorities, under suspicion of having committed a crime.
A person who is present in a courtroom in order to give some form of evidence, has been sworn in, and is being examined by the Prosecution or Defense.
The Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that has in some way been harmed or wronged by the Defendant.

name: Cure
d: This frame deals with a Healer treating and curing an Affliction (the injuries, disease, or pain) of the Patient, sometimes also mentioning the use of a particular Treatment or Medication. This frame differs from Medical_intervention in that this frame deals only with cases in which the Patient is cured of the Affliction, not just treated for the Affliction.

ex.t: Isis then cured Re by reciting a spell.
Another student became convinced that God was going to heal the clergyman of his cancer.

fes.d: The Healer, anyone who treats or cures the Patient, occurs as the External Argument of verbs:

This is the sufferer of the injury, disease or pain and can occur as an NP Object in this frame. However, Patient may not be expressed as a separate Frame Element but frequently occurs as the possessor of the Affliction, an example of FE Conflation: (See section on Conflation.) The Patient may therefore not be tagged in a sentence although explicitly identified.
The Frame Element Affliction is generally the NP Object of a verb, frequently incorporating the Patient as a possessor, as described above:

The FE Treatment is used for treatments and means, distinguished by separate FEs in FN-1. A method used to treat the Affliction can be the External Argument of these verbs, or expressed in a PP Complement: Target nouns (e.g. therapy, treatment, etc.) will NOT be tagged with this FE.
Degree to which event occurs
Manner of performing an action
The injested, applied, injected, etc. substance designed to cure the Patient. Note the tight relationship between Treatment and Medicine.
The Reason for which an intentional act is performed.
Where the event takes place.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
When the event occurs.
The Body_part is the specific area of the Patient's body which is treated.
The period of time that the Patient recieves the Treatment.

name: Custom
d: A Behavior is classified as entrenched for a Protagonist or a Society. The Behavior may be associated with a particular Domain of experience and described with a Descriptor. This indicates that the Behavior is commonly performed by the Protagonist or members of the Society.

ex.t: It is an old Jewish custom.
He was unaware of the Japanese custom of waiting until the giver had departed.
The ancient tradition of swan-upping has been taking place on the river Thames.

fes.d: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the entrenched Behavior.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose entrenched Behavior is at issue.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the area of human experience to which the Behavior belongs.
This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the entrenched Behavior.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a region where the Behavior is entrenched.

name: Cutting
d: An Agent cuts a Item into Pieces using an Instrument (which may or may not be expressed).

ex.t: At the ceremony, the CEO cut the red ribbon hanging across the main entrance into a glorious confetti.

fes.d: The Agent is the person cutting the Item into Pieces.
The Instrument with which the Item is being cut into Pieces.
Where the slicing takes place.
The purpose for which the Item is being sliced into Pieces.
When the slicing occurs.
An act of the Agent that accomplishes the slicing.
The item which is being cut into Pieces.
The Result of the Item being sliced into Pieces.
Manner in which the Item is being cut into Pieces.
The Pieces are the parts of the original Item which are the result of the slicing.

name: Cycle_of_existence_scenario
d: An Entity comes into being, exists for some time, and ceases to be.

fes.d: Concrete or abstract entity that did not exist, then came into existence, then (potentially) ceased to exist.

name: Cycle_of_life_and_death
d: A Protagonist is born or sprouts, lives, dies, and then is dead.

fes.d: Protagonist identifies the being or entity that is dead or alive.

name: Damaging
d: An Agent affects a Patient in such a way that the Patient (or some Subregion of the Patient) ends up in a non-canonical state. Often this non-canonical state is undesirable, and some lexical units (marked with the Negative semantic type) specifically indicate that the Patient is negatively affected. Some lexical units of this frame indicate by what means the Patient is altered (e.g., scrape.v) and in some cases give some indication of the detailed effect on the Patient (e.g., score.v, chip.v), and in other cases, both are specified (tear.v). For another set of lexical units, the action and its result are much less specified (e.g., damage.v). Compare this frame with Destroying, Cause_to_fragment, and Render_nonfunctional.

ex.t: That idiot just dented my car!
Some ne'er-do-wells defaced the Park's wall with spray paint to show their anger at local natural resources allocation policy.
Please don't damage the goods.

fes.d: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the damage to the Patient.
The degree to which the Patient is damaged.
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Patient to accomplish the damage.

Any description of the action of damaging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the damage.
This FE identifies the location of the scene where a Agent damages a Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the damage to the Patient.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.
The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the damaging.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent damages the Patient.
The entity which is affected by the Agent so that it is damaged.
