A description of the state of the Patient after the damaging has taken place, including descriptions of the severity and the permanence of the damaged condition.
Result of the Agent's action.
An event which leads to the damage of the Patient.

name: Daring
d: An Agent performs some Action which is considered imprudent. This frame is distinct from Attempt in that the danger that the Agent puts themselves in by performing the Action is profiled. The danger is not spelled out, but generally the Action has a possibility or likelihood of causing social or physical harm to the Agent.

ex.t: I risked taking another look.

fes.d: The individual that performs the Action, resulting in danger to themself.
This FE denotes the Action taken by the Agent.
The purpose for which the Action is performed.
The Explanation the Agent takes the risk.
The time at which the Agent dares to perform the Action.
The location where the Agent risks doing the Action.

Any description of the risking action which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Dead_or_alive
d: A Protagonist is in the dynamic, maintained state of being alive or has exited this state.

ex.t: Frank's dead body was apalling.

fes.d: Explanation identifies any object or event that brings about the death of the Protagonist.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a Protagonist is dead or alive.
Protagonist identifies the being or entity that is dead or alive.
This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.
The time in which the Protagonist is dead or alive.

name: Death
d: The words in this frame describe the death of a Protagonist. A Cause of death may also be expressed obliquely.

ex.t: The machine was not switched off, but Mr. Lavelle died of natural causes, police said.
To avenge the death of a son is not hasty work, if he is to be honored.

fes.d: The FE Protagonist is the being or entity that dies. With verbs in this frame, the Protagonist is the External Argument.
The FE Explanation expresses any object or eventuality that brings about the Protagonist's death.
Some measure of the event, generally frequency.
The FE Depictive denotes the state of the Protagonist as the death occurred.
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The FE Result indicates what occurs as the result of the death of the Protagonist.
The FE Place indicates where the death takes place.
The FE Time denotes when the dying or killing occurs.
This FE identifies the larger event in which the Protagonist dies, i.e. changes from living to dead.
An individual negatively affected by the death of the Protagonist.

name: Deception_end
d: A Deceiver succeeds or fails in causing a Victim to have a misunderstanding about a Topic.

fes.d: The Victim is the target of the deception.
The Deceiver attempts to make the Victim unable to know about or detect the truth about a Phenomenon or Topic.
The Phenomenon is presented to the Victim as a way to mislead about the Topic.
The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.
When the deception fails or succeeds.
The location where the deception fails or succeeds.

name: Deception_scenario
d: Deception is a scenario in which a Deceiver attempts to make it such that a Victim comes to an incorrect understanding about a Topic. This may be done by presenting a misleading Phenomenon to the Victim, or by concealing the existence of items which the Victim may be interested in. Note that the Victim is not necessarily aware of the (possible) existence of the Topicor items related to it.

fes.d: The Victim is the target of the deception.
The Deceiver attempts to make the Victim unable to know about or detect the truth about a Phenomenon or Topic.
The Phenomenon is presented to the Victim as a way to mislead about the Topic.
The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.

name: Deception_success
d: A Deceiver successfully causes a Victim to end up with incorrect beliefs about a Topic. The Victim comes to these beliefs from perceiving a Deception.

fes.d: The person who acts so as to give the Victim an incorrect idea about a Topic.
The person who receives an incorrect idea because of the Deceiver's actions.
The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.
The action performed by the Deceiver to fool the Victim.
The time at which the deception occurs.
The location at which the deception occurs.
The Phenomenon, as percieved by the Victim, causes the Victim to have an incorrect understanding about a Topic.

name: Deciding
d: A Cognizer makes a Decision, which may be about an entity or a course of action. How (and whether) this frame is distinct from Choosing is currently up for debate.

ex.t: Mo decided to quit the program.

fes.d: The Cognizer decides on a course of action.
Decision identifies the entity or course of action upon which the Cognizer decides.
A Cognizer makes a Decision from among a set of Possibilities.
The time or time period over which the Cognizer makes the decision.
The place where the Cognizer makes the decision.
The Manner in which the Cognizer makes a Decision
The Cognizer intends the Decision to fulfill an Inherent_purpose .
The conditions under which the Cognizer makes a Decision.
The reason for which the Cognizer makes the Decision.

name: Defending
d: A Defender responds to an Assailant's attack on a Victim by directly, and usually violently, countering it.

ex.t: Samantha stalwartly defended the gateway from the wraiths, crouching low over Stephen's prone form.

fes.d: This FE is the being or entity that responds forcefully to the Assailant's attack.
An entity used by the Defender fend off the Assailant .
The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Defender that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Defender that accomplishes their defense of the Victim.
This FE identifies the place where the Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant.
A state of affairs that the Defender is responding to that leads them to protect the Victim.
This FE identifies the time when the Defender takes forceful action against the Assailant.

The starting-point of the motion of the Defender or projectiles of the Defender as they move toward the the Place that the Assailant is occupying. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.
The state of the Defender or Victim during the Assailant's attack.
The individual or entity that is under attack from the Assailant .
The location of the Assailant or the weapons of the Assailant.

name: Degree
d: LUs in this frame modify a gradable attribute and describe intensities at the extreme positions on a scale.

ex.t: She is very brave.
It is that simple!
The feuds are so vicious because the stakes are so low.

name: Degree_of_processing
d: A Material has been processed (generally industrially) to some Degree in order to make it more useful for some (usually implicit) function. In some cases, an Alterant is used to process the Material.

fes.d: The Alterant causes a change in the Material.
The substance which is altered in some useful way.
The amount to which a Material has undergone processing.

name: Delimitation_of_diversity
d: An Item which encompasses characteristics or types whose diversity is indicated by adducing a Limit1 and a Limit2 which differ considerably from each other. In some cases, the Limit2 and Limit1 are construed together as Limits. Alternatively, the values of a particular Variable for the Item and its Limits may be profiled.

ex.t: Prices range from 10 to 20 dollars.
Prices range from 10 to 20 dollars.

fes.d: The entity whose scalar property is specified.
The scalar property that the Item possesses.
The first-mentioned possibility of the range of variation.
The second item of the range of variation.
The range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies.
The deviation of the Upper_limit and the Lower_limit from each other (and thus from some single value).

name: Delimited_state_scenario
d: A State (often an ongoing process) is ongoing for some period of time.

fes.d: A quantity or other characterization of the State's absolute duration.
An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.

name: Delivery
d: A Deliverer hands off a Theme to a Recipient or (more indirectly) a Goal location, which is accessible to the Recipient.

ex.t: The staff of Ebags delivered the umbrella well ahead of schedule.
In each class a dove flew in and delivered a red rose to Ginny.
The Pontifical Delegation for the delivery of the Icon of the Kazan Mother of God will arrive tomorrow.

fes.d: This is the person who completes the movement of the Theme after having transported it.
The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.
The objects being delivered.
The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.
Depictive phrase describing the Deliverer or Theme

Any description of the delivery event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
This is the Recipient of the sent Theme.
The Purpose of the delivery.
The Explanation for the delivery.
When the delivery takes place
An additional theme delivered along with the main Theme.
A container in which the Theme is delivered.
The location at which the delivery takes place.
The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Theme.
The conditions under which the delivery takes place.
The location of the Theme before the delivery process begins.
The Means are intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the package to the Goal.
The path along which the Theme moves while being delivered.
The person for whom the Delivery action occurs.
This FE applies to appraisals of the Delivery event.
The length of time from when the Delivery event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Deny_or_grant_permission
d: In this frame, an Authority allows a Protagonist to know (in some way) that they may or may not engage in an Action. For lexical units of this frame marked with the semantic type "Negative", e.g., authorize.v, the Authority has the power to tell the Protagonist not to do something, but does not do so. It is assumed that if the Protagonist engages in the Action without permission, then the Authority will punish the Protagonist in some way, at least with disapproval; if the Authority grants permission, however, the Authority is agreeing not to impose a punishment on the Protagonist for performing the Action.

ex.t: The police officer forbid me from turning around .
My mother okayed me to go to the movies with Simon .
The teacher gave the children permission to eat their lunch outside.

fes.d: The Authority orders the Protagonist to not engage in a particular Action.
The Protagonist wants to engage in an Action, but is ordered not to by the Authority.
The Action is what the Protagonist seeks to do, but is ordered not to.
The Time is when the denying of permission occurs.
The Place is where the denial of permission occurs.
The Purpose is what the Authority hopes to accomplish by denying permission.

In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function. First, it applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. The second subgroup consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier. What that role is depends only on the predicate heading the modifier phrase.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
A category that the Action fits into, which dictates the Action's being permitted (in accord with some implicit Principle.)
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
How often the event occurs.
A description of the Authority or the Protagonist while they are involved in the action.
A holistic description of the event (the same way), or a description of the Authority that also affects the overall event (carefully).
The action performed by an Authority that brings about the Denying or Granting Permission.

name: Departing
d: An object (the Theme) moves away from a Source. The Source may be expressed or it may be understood from context, but its existence is always implied by the departing word itself.

ex.t: The plane leaves at seven.DNI.
His departure from the dock was delayed by hundreds of tearful farewells.
We all exited the room slowly.

fes.d: This is the object which moves. It may be an entity which moves under its own power, but it need not be.

All the verbs in this frame express some change of location, away from one place and to another. Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Theme, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context.
Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'.
This FE labels any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels.
The action of the Theme which results in its departure.
This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Theme is moving.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.
The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a prepositional phrase generally headed by 'with' or 'along with'.
The distance that the Theme has traveled.
The Time at which the departure takes place.
The Frequency is the rate at which each Theme departs.
The Journey is the trip or expedition on which the Theme embarks.
The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.
Depictive identifies a phrase which describes the Theme at the time of departing.
The Explanation is the motivation or explanation for why the Theme departs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Theme departs from the Source.
The length of time that the Theme stays away from the Source location.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

This FE describes of the state of affairs denoted by the Departing event as role fillers in other frames; the state of affairs reported Departing event is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

name: Deserving
d: The existence of a State_of_affairs is sufficient reason for taking an Action . The agent who is justified in taking the suggested Action is not part of the immediate scene, however.

ex.t: The underwater sequences warrant the price of the admission alone.
'Desperate situations call for desperate measures ," said Mr Eames grandly.

fes.d: An Eventuality or an Entity that is taken to constitute sufficient reason for taking another Action.
An Action that is taken to be justifiable given the State_of_Affairs.
How sufficiently State_of_affairs can be considered a reason for the Action.
The general spectrum of reasoning along which the State_of_affairs is a justification.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Deserving event and any of its participants.

name: Desirability
d: This frame concerns an Evaluee being judged for its quality, i.e. how much it would probably be liked. In many cases, the Evaluee is implicitly judged good or bad relative to other instances of its type. The Evaluee's desirability is determined by one or more Parameters, which are scalar properties of the Evaluee. The evaluation may also explicitly be relativized to a set of Circumstances, a Comparison_set of entities that belong to the same class as the Evaluee, or an Affected_party. The Degree of goodness or badness may also be expressed. Note: With some targets, desirability is conventionally aligned with quantity, i.e., GOOD is MORE.

ex.t: The view was astonishing.
On clear days, the view was excellent.
The book is astounding in its scope.

fes.d: The Evaluee is being judged for its quality.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Evaluee is judged good or bad.
Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the quality of the Evaluee is being judged.
This FE marks expressions that denote a scalar property of the Evaluee with respect to which the Evaluee is judged.
This FE marks expressions that indicate what class of things or events the Evaluee is being judged against.
The Affected_party indicates entities that benefit or suffer from the good or bad quality of the Evaluee.
The Frame Element Depictive encodes a state that the Evaluee is in and which does not represent a temporary or hypothetical set of Circumstances.

name: Desirable_event
d: A particular State_of_affairs is desirable. The State_of_affairs may be required to achieve a Purpose. A set of Circumstances may be specified under which the assessment of desirability holds.

ex.t: You should take the doses about 12 hours apart and at the same time each day.
If the metal is seriously rusted or warped, it should be repaired or replaced with a chimney top damper.
To ensure that, you should have no CLASSPATH set.

fes.d: The State_of_affairs that the speaker finds desirable.
The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the State_of_affairs has the specified assessment of desirability.
The event or state of affairs that is achieved by bringing about the desirable State_of_affairs.
The extent to which the specified desirability of the State_of_affairs deviates from the expected desirability.

name: Desiring
d: An Experiencer desires that an Event occur. (Note that commonly a resultant state of the Event will stand in for the Event.) In some cases, the Experiencer is an active participant in the Event, and in such cases the Event itself is often not mentioned, but rather some Focal_participant which is subordinately involved in the Event. Generally, the use of a word in this frame implies that the specific Event has not yet happened, but that the Experiencer believes that they would be happier if it did. Sometimes the Time_of_event, Purpose_of_event, or the Location_of_event are mentioned without the explicit mention of the Event.

ex.t: I only wanted one piece of candy.
The company was eager for him to leave as soon as possible.
Susan really wishes that you 'd listen to her.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.
The change that the Experiencer would like to see.
This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.
The Degree is a the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.
The way in which the Experiencer desires something.
An aspect of the Experiencer that causes a desire.
The Purpose_of_event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.
The time that the Event would ideally occur.
The Location_of_event is the place involved in the desired Event.
The Time is when the Experiencer desires something.
Where the event takes place. Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame.
The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something.
The Role is a role filled by a Focal_participant in the Event that the Experiencer desires.

name: Destiny
d: An State_of_affairs will come to hold with respect to a Protagonist at some future time. The Protagonist is not conceived of as having control over whether the State_of_affairs will hold: obscurely related previous actions or circumstances, or some hidden power may have already determined that it will occur.

ex.t: Exile was his fate and he triumphantly turned it into the fruit of his life.
One could say that it was Indonesia's destiny to initiate the decolonization process.
The sun's ultimate fate is as a white dwarf, a dense, cold core the size of the earth.

fes.d: The State_of_affairs that is destined to occur to the Protagonist.
The Protagonist is the one for whom the future State_of_affairs is destined.
A description of the sort of State_of_affairs that will occur.
The Role filled by the Protagonist in his/her destiny.
The time for which the Protagonist's future is determined.
The location in which State_of_affairs is destined to occur to the Protagonist.
The way in which the State_of_affairs is destined to occur to the Protagonist.

name: Destroying
d: A Destroyer (a conscious entity) or Cause (an event, or an entity involved in such an event) affects the Patient negatively so that the Patient no longer exists.

ex.t: An asteroid obliterated the dinosaurs.

fes.d: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Patient's destruction.
The degree to which the destruction is completed.
An entity directed by the Destroyer that interacts with a Patient to accomplish the Patient's destruction.

Any description of the process of destruction which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Destroyer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Destroyer that accomplishes the destruction.
This FE identifies the place where the Destroyer destroys the Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which a Destroyer causes the destruction of the Patient.
A state of affairs that the Destroyer is responding to in destroying the Undergoer.

This FE identifies the Result of an event on the Patient. This FE is very rare in this frame, and since the Patient is destroyed by this process, the Result is generally constrained to indicate the Patient 's resulting inexistence.
The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the destruction.
This FE identifies the time when the Destroyer destroys the Patient.
The entity which is destroyed by the Destroyer.
The event or entity which is responsible for the destruction of the Patient.
The category in which the Patient is destroyed.
How often the Cause or Destroyer destroys the Patient.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
Medium expresses the Medium in which the Patient is destroyed by the Cause or Destroyer. This FE is generally used in Metaphorical uses of this frame.

name: Detaching
d: The Detaching frame covers two situations: a scene in which somebody causes one thing to be physically detached from something else; or a scene in which somebody causes two things to be disconnected from each other. In the first, the frame includes an Agent who detaches an Item from a Source, creating an asymmetric relationship between the Item and the Source. In the second, the Agent attaches two Items to each other, where each serves as a Source relative to the other, creating a symmetric relationship between the two Items. Note in both cases, after the removal of the connector, the Items that were formerly attached re-appear as the two separate or potentially separate entities that they were throughout.

ex.t: They finally unchained me from my desk at work and I'm leavin town.
Before adding a new area of color, he detached the canvas from the stretcher and laboriously scraped away the old paint in that spot.
She unhooked the leash from Patty's collar, and pulled her up on the couch.

fes.d: The individual that causes the Item and Source to come apart by manipulating the connector.
This FE identifies the Item that the Agent detaches from the Source.
This FE identifies the Result of a detaching event.
Source identifies the location to which an Item was attached before getting detached.
This FE identifies the plural Items that are detached from each other, resulting in their separation. Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Source can occur.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent detaches an Item or Items.

Any description of the detaching event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent detaches an Item or Items.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent intentionally detaches an Item or Items.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent detaches the Item from the Source.

This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent detaches an Item or Items. Typically, it transmits the force applied by the Agent, and is not left behind as a participant in the resultant state.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up detached.

name: Detaining
d: The Authorities hold a Suspect under suspicion of having committed a crime (Charges). The Holding_location and period of detention (Duration) may also be specified.

ex.t: The police held Mr. Smith in the slammer on charges of killing his lawyer.

fes.d: The Authorities hold the Suspect in custody.
This FE identifies the crime with which the Suspect is charged.
Where the detaining takes place.
This FE identifies the person who is taken into custody and held, under suspicion of having committed a crime.
When the detaining occurs.
This FE identifies the place where the Suspect is confined.
This FE identifies the length of time that the Suspect spends in confinement.
This FE identifies the law, act, or precedent that allows the Authorities to detain the Suspect.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Authorities detain a Suspect.
This FE identifies the state of the Suspect being held.

name: Detonate_explosive
d: An Agent causes an Explosive device to explode.

ex.t: Who detonated that bomb?

fes.d: The Agent detonates the Explosive.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent detonates the Explosive.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent detonates the Explosive.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent detonates the Explosive.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent detonates the Explosive.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Explosive causes damage to surrounding objects when operated by the Agent.
The Outcome is the failure or success of the Agent's detonating the Explosive his or her Purpose.
An event within which the Agent detonates the Explosive. Often, the Containing_event will also give an indication of the Agent's Purpose.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."
This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Explosive or the detonation act and modifies the expected value for it.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
An implement used by the Agent to detonate the Explosive.

The Victim (typically an individual or structure) is targeted by the explosion or inadvertantly damaged by the explosion. May be indicated explicitly with on or against, but is often implied by place expressions, in which case the FE is indicated on the second layer.

name: Differentiation
d: Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer being aware (or not being aware) of the difference between two Phenomena, which may be expressed jointly or disjointly.

ex.t: It is very difficult for people to visually distinguish between living and non-living things from such a great distance .

fes.d: The cognizer is the person (or other sentient being) who potentially determines that two Phenomena are distinct from each other. It is normally expressed as an External Argument:

The phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed as separate constituents. When they are, one is typically expressed as an NP Object, and the other as a PP Complement headed by from: In this case, the phenomenon expressed more prominently as an NP Object is called Phenomenon_1:
See Phenomenon_1, above. The phenomenon expressed less prominently as a PP complement is called Phenomenon_2:

Both phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed jointly by the same constituent: Such constituents are assigned the FE Phenomena. They are always plural, as in the above example, or involve conjunction:

This is a property that is potentially used by the Cognizer to distinguish one phenomenon from another. It is normally expressed as a PP headed by a preposition such as from, by, or on the basis of: General Grammatical Observations: Verbs in this domain often occur with the modal auxiliary can.
Degree to which event occurs
State of a participant while the action is ongoing.
Manner of performing an action
An intentional action performed by the Cognizer that allows them to differentiate the Phenomena.
The Circumstances describe the situation in which the Cognizer evaluates the Phenomena.

name: Difficulty
d: An Experiencer has an easy or difficult time carrying out an Activity. The ease or difficulty associated with the Activity seems to often be associated with a prominent participant. However, we consider this impression to be due to the syntax and pragmatics of the relevant sentence constructions and employ no special FE for such participants. The Degree of ease or difficulty is often specified as well as a set of Circumstances. A Parameter may be mentioned that indicates in which respect the Activity is judged to be easy or difficult. Unmarked LUs of this frame indicate that something is easy, while LUs of this frame that mean the opposite of easy are marked with the semantic type "Negative", as in difficult.a, arduous.a, and a bitch.n.

ex.t: (1) John is easy to please.
(2) It is easy to get Alex annoyed.
(3) Smithers is very tough for me to please.

fes.d: This Frame Element marks expressions indicating the Activity that the Experiencer finds difficult or easy. In many cases, the relevant Activity has to be inferred from the context.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Degree of difficulty that the Experiencer has in carrying out the Activity.

This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions in which the Activity is being experienced and which influence the Experiencer's perception of how easy or difficult the Activity is.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate which person judges carrying out the Activity to be easy or difficult.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a respect in which the Activity is judged easy or difficult to carry out by the Experiencer.
The experience of the Activity by the Experiencer may be compared to a Standard situation, which may be evoked either as an event or state, or by reference to a salient participant.
The time at which the Activity takes place.

lus.n: like taking candy from a baby.adv

name: Dimension
d: This frame concerns words that express an Object's position on a scale, its Measurement, with respect to some attribute, its Dimension. Location, identifying the sub-region of the Object where the Dimension is measured, may also be expressed. Adjectives in this frame must appear with a measurement expression like 5 cm. Note the tagging of six feet on the GF and PT layers in the following sentence. The GF of six feet is Dep and the PT is NP.

ex.t: The tower is 10 feet tall.
The new vase is 5 cm in circumference at the top.
The woman was six feet tall.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Dimension which is measured. Most LUs in this frame incorporate the Dimension.
Object identifies the item which is measured along one of its Dimensions.
Measurement identifies the extent of the Object along the specified Dimension.
Locus identifies the sub-region of the Object where the Dimension is measured.
The relevant dimension of development.
FOR REFRAMING!

name: Direction
d: This frame covers the basic uses of direction words like the adverbs east, up, and forward. These are used either to talk about a direction of facing (e.g., facing outward, pointing left, looking downward, turn east) or to talk about actual or metaphorical motion (went up, traveling due north). Lexical units of this frame typically have a semantic type that refers to the means of determining the direction (e.g. forward.adv has the semantic type Landmark_front, meaning that "forward" is defined with respect to the direction from the center of some entity to its front, however defined). Nevertheless, some words like way.n are used exactly when normal means of specifying direction are not available. This frame is most frequently used to describe the motion of something along the Path from the Landmark, which is normally implicitly identified as the location of the viewpoint: In such cases, a Distance from the Landmark can also be given: It can often be used for direction of facing, which is not compatible with the Distance frame element: Although rare for certain lexical units (e.g., upward.adv), most words in this frame are commonly used in a fictive motion pattern to identify locations that can be reached by moving in the indicated way from the Landmark: In this fictive motion case, the Domain and the Independent_variable are both spatial, and should be marked as metaphorical. Note this differs from members of the Directional_locative_relation frame (e.g., above.prep), which can only be used for relative static positions, and not for facings or for directions of motion: vs. A potential point of confusion is that the Directional_locative_relation frame is also used for cases in which adverbs like east.adv, etc. are followed by "of", since such expressions can only be used of static relative positions and not facings: Another potential point of confusion is that nouns referring to directions can be used for facings if they are preceeded by the word "to". Since this use of to.prep can be found with a broader class of words like side.n, we interpret this sense of to.prep as mapping relative postitions (belonging to the Directional_locative_relation frame) to true Directions, in the sense of this frame. This applies to expressions like "to the east", as well as "to both sides" and "to the rear". In the future, we may add these as multi-word members of the frame. In the following case, the Domain is "potency" and the Independent_variable is, as usual, time; again, the example should be marked as metaphorical. In mathematical terms, all of these uses can be understood as a Path, made up of a set of positions in some N-space Domain (by default spatial, or metaphorically, other domains), being determined as a function of a Landmark (which may be incorporated and is usually implicit) and some one-dimensional Independent_variable (time, or, metaphorically, other domains). The Domain and/or the Independent_variable are normally incorporated in the basic definition of the target; thus, for example, up.adv, by default, indicates the Domain is space, and time is the Independent_variable. From a linguistic point of view, we consider these literal spatio-temporal uses to be basic, and other cases, where space is replaced by some other kind of quantity, is to be understood as metaphorical.

ex.t: We went north . DNI
After she was knocked on the head , it seemed like everything had moved three feet to the left . DNI
Look left and you 'll see it . DNI

fes.d: The point of reference from which the rest of the Path is reckoned.
The one-dimensional set of locations.
The kind of space in which the set of points of the Path is defined.

The one-dimensional variable with respect to which the positions on the Path are reckoned. For normal motion, the positions on the Path are with respect to time, while for directions of facing, the positions are merely reckoned with respect to another spatial dimension, the distance from the Landmark in the specified direction. As these features are the default, literal interpretation of targets of this frame, this frame element is only to be used for metaphorical examples like the following:
How much movement in the stated direction along the Path from the Landmark there has been.

name: Directional_locative_relation
d: A Figure is located relative to a (presumably more easily located) Ground, asserting that the Figure lies (approximately) on line from the Ground whose direction is established by semantic types of the particular LUs.

ex.t: The plane landed 10 miles due north of Lake Travis in an empty field .

fes.d: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.
The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location in a certain direction specified by the particular LU. The Figure can be an entity or an event.

An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative). This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way' and 'all the way' indicating distance and difficulty of access.

This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs: up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').
The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.

This FE identifies the Distance between the Figure and the Ground. This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region. Note that a number of frequent adverbial targets identify the Ground, with the location of an implicit viewer, so Distance is effectively measured from the viewpoint location in these cases.

An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over). Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.

An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target. This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.

A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time. This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path). While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion, or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the example below).

name: Disaster_scenario
d: This frame covers the large scenario for characterizing disasters, including the occurrence of particular types of disasters and the range of responses to disasters.

fes.d: The individual or group that is responding to a disaster with directed action.
The Victim (typically a large group) which is affected by the disaster event.
This FE identifies the place where the Undesirable_event occurs.
Directed action leading to recovery, rescue, or general mitigation of distress due to an ensuing disaster.
This FE identifies the time when the disaster scenario occurs.
The length of time between the instantiation of the Disaster and the conclusion of the Response.
An event of great proportional magnitude with evidence leaving blame to which only the stars might answer. A disaster is an indisputably ill-fated occurrence.

name: Discussion
d: Two (or more) people (the Interlocutors, also encodable as Interlocutor_1 and Interlocutor_2) talk to one another. No person is construed as only a speaker or only an addressee. Rather, it is understood that both (or all) participants do some speaking and some listening--the process is understood to be symmetrical or reciprocal. This frame differs from the Chatting frame in that the Interlocutors have a particular question that they are attempting to decide or understand.

ex.t: I would rather discuss politics with anyone but him.
World leaders met to discuss global warming on the coldest day of the year.

fes.d: In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Interlocutor_2. That is, Interlocutor_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Interlocutor_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Interlocutor_1, not necessarily that of Interlocutor_2 or the group of Interlocutors as a whole.

In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Interlocutor_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with). Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Interlocutor_2.

In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Interlocutors. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Interlocutors is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Discussion frame, it is possible for the Interlocutors role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.

Topic expresses the subject that the Interlocutors are trying to come to some agreement about. It may refer, for example, to an undesirable issue that the Interlocutors want to have the proper response to, or it may refer more directly to an unresolved question.
The linguistic system(s) used by the Interlocutors to discuss something.
Amount_of_discussion applies to phrases expressing how thoroughly a Topic has been discussed.
This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing Interlocutor_1 or the pair of Interlocutors.
This frame element marks phrases that expresss the Manner in which one or both of the Interlocutors communicate.
This Frame Elememt marks constituents expressing the means the parties to the conversation use to talk to each other.
The Duration of the conversation.
The goal that Interlocutor_1 or the Interlocutors jointly have, i.e. the state of affairs that they wish to bring about by the conversation.
The time at which the discussion takes place.
The location at which a discussion takes place.
The device or system that facilitates a discussion.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
This FE denotes an event that occurs or a state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the discussion takes place and of which it is taken to be part.
The number of times the discussion happens in a given period of time.
The general field or area in which the discussion takes place, or which shapes the discussion or its topic.

name: Disembarking
d: A Traveller leaves from or dismounts a Vehicle.

ex.t: The passengers disembarked in Southampton.
They then informed the passengers that, if the aircraft were to leave the runway, they would likely be deplaning through the rear cabin doors.

fes.d: The Traveller is the entity which disembarks from the Vehicle.
The Vehicle is the means of conveyance that the Traveller disembarks from.
The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.
The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion off or out of the Vehicle.
The amount of time the Traveller spends off or outside of the Vehicle after disembarking from it.
The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the disembarking.
When the disembarking of the Vehicle takes place.
A theme that leaves the Vehicle together with the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.
The Purpose for which the Traveller disembarks from the vehicle.
The location in which the Traveller disembarks from the Vehicle.
The location that the Traveller reaches by leaving the Vehicle.

name: Disgraceful_situation
d: An implicit cognizer judges that a particular State_of_affairs for which a Protagonist is responsible is socially unacceptable.

ex.t: He called it a disgraceful situation. INI
To my mind it was undoubtedly the most utterly shameful act the chess world had witnessed since 1485. INI
It is not at all shameful for a man to allow himself to be ruled by others.

fes.d: The entity or event which brings disgrace upon the Protagonist.
The person or organization responsible for the occurrence of the State_of_affairs.
The extent to which the State_of_affairs diverges from the social norm for things of its kind.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the judgment of disgrace logically follows.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Dispersal
d: An Agent or a Cause disperses or scatters Individuals from the Source,a relatively confined space, to a the Goal_area, a broader space.

ex.t: She scattered his ashes in the bay.

fes.d: The Agent disperses or scatters the Individuals.
The Individuals are scattered by the Agent.
Source is the relatively confined space from which an Agent scatters the Individuals.
Goal_area identifies the broader space to which the Agent scatters the Individuals
An event or force that causes that Individuals to disperse.

Any description of the dispersing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (eagerly, carefully).
The Time when the Individuals are dispersed.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the dispersal.
A state of the Individuals that results from the dispersal.
The trajectory along which the Individuals move.
The Place where the dispersing event happens.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in dispersing the Individuals
The distance that the Individuals move from their original location, the Source.
The rate of motion of the Individuals, usually in terms of how long it takes for them to leave the Source and end up in the Goal_area.

name: Distant_operated_IED
d: A improvised explosive device, the Bomb, is rigged to detonate when it receives a signal, typically by a wire that leads to a trigger. The trigger may be operated directly by the Detonator, in which case the weapon is known as a CWIED (command wire IED). Or, the triggering mechanism may be activated wirelessly, such as by a cell phone. In this case, the weapon is called an RCIED (remote control IED).

ex.t: These photographs were taken in the wake of a CWIED attack on the British.
The purpose of this device is to prevent an RCIED from detonating.

fes.d: The Bomb is set off by the Detonator at a distance, injuring or damaging a Target.
The type of activity that the Bomb is generally involved in. Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Bomb belongs to.
The substance that makes up the Bomb.
The person that wishes to attack the Target and who activates the Bomb.
This FE identifies a part of the Bomb. This includes parts that aid in the detonation or damaging, or mere attachments.
The term used to refer to the Bomb.
The time at which a Bomb comes into existence.
The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Bomb.
A description or characteristic of the Bomb not covered by more specific FEs.
The intended or actual target of the Bomb.

name: Distinctiveness
d: A Feature of an Entity serves to distinguish the Entity from other members of its type which have a different value for the Feature. Note that the Entity is often implicit.

ex.t: His distinctive flowing gait and skill with the rapier set him apart from his fellows.
The swinging axe-kick was characteristic of Xena.

fes.d: The aspect of the Entity which makes it different from the other members of its class.
The item which differs from other members of its class in the Feature's value.
The extent to which the values of the Feature of the Entity and the Comparison_set are similar to each other.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Distributed_abundance
d: There is a Location and an abundant or large Theme. The Location and Theme are largely coextensive, i.e. occupying the same area.

fes.d: The Theme covers or fills the Location.
Location is the object or area that the Theme fills or covers.
This FE identifies the Degree of abundance with which the Theme covers or fills the Location.
The time during which the Theme and the Location are positioned relative to each other.

name: Distributed_position
d: This frame involves a static (primarily spatial) relationship between a Location and a Theme, in which the Theme is located in many or all subregions of the Location, and is thus construable as covering it. The Time when the covering configuration holds, and the Subregion of the Location that is involved may, optionally, be indicated. Prepositional and verb targets of this frame differ in the ways they can participate in forming sentences; one of the most important differences is that prepositions may modify the entire sentence to describe the event (the Theme) as distributed over the Location. Some members of this frame specifically indicate that the configuration is attractive or unattractive; this is indicated by the semantic types Positive_judgement and Negative_judgement respectively. Some of the non-verb LUs of the frame (esp. around.prep) refer to multiple possible positions that might be occupied by a single Theme, often accompanied by "somewhere": These same LUs may refer a vague sequence of locations occupied by a single Theme: All or virtually all of the verbs used statically in this frame can also occur in the frame Filling, producing pairs such as the following: Please note: adorned, covered, etc are in the Abounding_with frame because of the point of view shift.

ex.t: By Summer, weeds dotted the field .
The papers around my office were too messy .
Puddles were rippling all over the roof .

fes.d: The Theme in this frame is the object which is described as standing in some spatial relation to a particular Location. Theme typically occurs as the External Argument or, with passives, as a PP Complement headed by "with" or "by".
Location is the entity or area with respect to which the Theme's spatial arrangement is described. This frame element generally occurs as an NP Object.
The part of the Location which contains or is covered by the Theme.
The time at which the Theme occupies the Location.

An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder). Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.
A description of how much of a potential profiled region actually has (or is expected to have) a Theme in it. It is normally filled by closed-class items like 'all', 'somewhere', 'nowhere', etc.

A description of how the access path to the Location interacts with time. This FE is filled only by the closed class adverbial back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Theme before). While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can background motion entirely (as in the example below).

name: Diversity
d: A Group is described as having members which are similar or dissimilar to each other. The Degree of similarity may also be expressed. Some of the nouns in this frame are transparent (e.g. range.n) whereas others denote the scale of diversity (diversity); variety.n is usable both ways but is normally transparent.

ex.t: The diversity of students here is to be applauded . INI
A range of answers were proposed .

fes.d: This FE marks constituents that express the set of objects or types whose diversity is at issue.
This FE marks constituents which express a property in respect to which the similarity of the Group is assessed.
The extent to which the members of the Group are similar to each other, in general or with respect to some Dimension(s)
This FE identifies the Time when the Group is diverse or homogenous.
The Place is the general area in which diversity occurs or exists.
This FE identifies the Manner in which Dimension is similar or different
An inanimate entity or process that causes the diversity or homogeneity.
This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Group

name: Documents
d: Words in the frame refer to any Document that has a legal status or conventional social significance. Some Documents empower the Bearer of the Document to execute the Right. Others indicate the Obligation of the Bearer. Still others show the identity or Status of the Bearer.

ex.t: They got their marriage licence from Canada.

fes.d: The holder of the document.
The authority that issues the document.
Obligation is the obligation that is imposed on the Bearer of the Document.
Right is the right of the Bearer of the Document that is authorized by the Document.
Status is the state of the Bearer of the Document indicated by the Document.
A Specification is a condition that applies to the Rights and/or Obligations described in the Document.
Document is the piece of paper that has the legal status.
The language the Document is written in, or a specification of the kind of object that instantiates it.
Descriptor covers any characterization or description of the target that is not covered by another more specific FE.

name: Dodging
d: A Dodger acts to avoid an oncoming moving Bad_entity. The motion is relative, since the Dodger may be moving.

ex.t: Mo dodged  the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust.
Jogging through the dense woods, Mo dodged the low branches .

fes.d: The Dodger acts to avoid an oncoming Bad_entity.
The Bad_entity is the oncoming entity to avoid.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Place where the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Time at which the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the dodging occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which the dodging occurs.

name: Domain
d: A Predicate is said to apply in a particular Domain. The understanding of the relation between Domain and Predicate depends on the nature of the Predicate. When the Predicate is a complete proposition, then a Domain adverbial also functions as a topic restrictor. Sentences with topic restrictors often come in pairs. When the Predicate is a simple predicate, there is no notion of topic restriction on the sentence level.

ex.t: The Normal College is geographically adjacent to the University of North Wales.
Geographically, Britain is a group of island off the mainland of Europe. Culturally , it has always been linked to the continent .

Socially and demographically the period has been dominated by two factors -- the fall in the size of families and the increase in the expectation of survival to retirement , the effects of which are still far from having exhausted themselves .

fes.d: This Frame Element denotes the Predicate which is applied to the Domain.
This Frame Element applies to the Domain in which the Predicate is said to apply.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Dominate_competitor
d: An Agent, by virtue of strength or forcefulness, controls, rules, or strongly influences some Patient in some Situation.

ex.t: The fireballing righthander looked poised to dominate the Yankees yet again, striking out seven straight batters during one stretch

fes.d: The Agent controls the Patient by being forceful and possibly aggressive.
The Patient is trying to gain control of a situation, but ends up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent.
The Situation within which the Agent is able to gain control over the Patient (thus excluding them from controlling the Situation).
The period of time over which the domination occurs.
A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.
The place where the domination occurs.
The time when the domination takes place.
The Degree to which the Agent dominates the Patient.

name: Dominate_situation
d: An Agent acts so as to be the strongest force, or most important causal factor in some Situation, to the exclusion of other competing actors.

ex.t: York dominated the game as they held the ball on offense almost the entire 70 minutes.
Is there a future for Unix in a market increasingly dominated by Microsoft?
Walz dominated the debate so completely it was almost embarrassing.

fes.d: The Agent is the most forceful and pivotal factor in the situation.
The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.
The Time when the Agent is dominant.
The period of time over which the domination occurs.
The location where the domination takes place.
A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.
The Degree to which the Agent dominates the Situation.

name: Domination
d: An Agent has a influential, controlling position in a Situation, and is the primary causal factor in the development of the Situation, leaving other Competitors unable to take controlling positions. Two perspectives are taken on this frame, one where the Agent is viewed as controlling primarily the Situation, and another where the Agent is viewed as primarily influencing the other Competitors in the Situation.

fes.d: The Agent has a controlling position in the Situation.
The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.
The Competitors are trying to gain control of a situation, but end up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent .
The time when the domination takes place.
The location of the dominationw
The manner of the domination.
The length of time over which the domination takes place.
The Degree to which the Agent dominates.

name: Dough_rising
d: The LUs of this frame describe a lump of Dough expanding as gas develops inside it. This is part of a process where, in order to produce a lighter, more easily chewed bread, Dough is leavened with yeast, baking soda or in another fashion to add gas to it before baking.

ex.t: I've got no frozen boxed meals, and no other real options to make something to keep me going while my pizza dough rises.

fes.d: The paste made out of any cereals (grains) or leguminous crops by grinding, with some water added, which expands in volume as a result of leavening before baking.
The length of the interval during which the Dough rises.
The Time when the expansion of the Dough takes place.
The Speed at which the Dough expands.

Any description of the rising of the Dough which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
A setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the event takes place. This FE also covers conditions that are causally connected to the event of the Dough rising.
The amount by which the volume of the Dough increases.
The entity or state of affairs that leads to the event of the Dough's rising.

name: Downing
d: An Agent disables a flying or floating Patient, causing it to be unable to support itself in its current medium.

ex.t: It's rumored that she downed a helicopter with a precisely fired arrow.

fes.d: The Agent forces the Patient to come to the ground.
The Patient is the entity that is being forced to the ground.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
The Result of causing the Patient to come to the ground.
An act performed by an Agent that enables them to force the Patient to the ground.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The time at which the event takes place.
The location at which the event takes place.
An event which causes the Patient to come to the ground.
An object used by the Agent to facilitate bringing down the Patient.

name: Dressing
d: A Wearer puts on an item of Clothing, which then occupies the Body_location.

ex.t: You didn't have to dress like a pirate to impress me. INI
He put on his thickest pair of gloves and then went back out to see if he could move them now. INI
Jack put on his watch - on his right wrist, and checked the time.

fes.d: The individual that puts Clothing on their body.
Clothing is used for the item of clothing that the Wearer ends up wearing.
The body part that the Clothing ends up covering.

Any expression which describes a property of the donning event which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Clothing's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Wearer or Clothing during the act.
The Means is an act whereby the Wearer puts on the Clothing
This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.
This FE identifies the Duration of the Wearing that results from putting on the Clothing.
The Place indicates where the Donning occurs.
The Explanation indicates why the Wearer puts on the Clothing.
The time when the Wearer puts an item of Clothing on.
An action that the Wearer intends to accomplish by putting on Clothing.

name: Drop_in_on
d: A Visitor arrives at the Host_location as a guest of the Host, for the purpose of achieving a Purpose. The Purpose is often social in nature, i.e., the visit itself constitutes a goal.

ex.t: I'm gonna drop in on Kieth for a while.

fes.d: The Visitor arrives at the Host_location to visit the Host for a Purpose.

Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Visitor moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor the Host or Host_location. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

The Host is the person highly associated with the goal location of the Visitor, and who allows the Visitor onto his/her territory, and possibly to make use of available resources. The Host and Visitor and in a host-guest relationship.

A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Visitor arrives.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Visitor arrives at a location associated with the Host.
The Host_location is a place primarily associated with the Host.
The Containing_event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the visiting takes place.
The frequency with whic hthe Visitor drops in on a Host.
The length of time that the Visitor remains with the Host.
The larger area within which the visiting takes place.
This FE indicates that the visiting is a particular instance in a series of repeated visiting events.
A state of affairs that explains why the Visitor is making a visit.

name: Dunking
d: An Agent temporarily places a Theme into a Substance, often with the intention to remove it later. The Substance may be metonymically represented by its container. The Theme may be partially or completely submerged.

ex.t: She dunked her sandwich into some tomato soup.

fes.d: The Agent places the Theme into a Substance.
The Theme temporarily goes partially or completely into the Substance.
The Substance is the fluid into which the Theme is placed. This may be metonymically represented by the container of the fluid.
The way that the Agent puts Theme in the Substance.
The location in time when the dunking occurs.

name: Duplication
d: This frame involves a Creator making a duplicate, the Copy, of some Original entity. A Source, the location of the Original, and Goal, the location of the Copy, may be expressed.

ex.t: The teacher copied the problem onto the blackboard.
His handouts were poorly photocopied  by his assistantfrom my originals .

fes.d: The Creator produces the Copy based on the Original. It is normally expressed as an External Argument.
The Original is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object:
The Copy produced by the Creator is frequently not expressed. However, when Copy does occur, it is usually expressed as the External Argument of verbs:

The Source is the location from which material is copied, i.e. the location of the Original. Unlike the FE Source in other domains and frames, there is no actual movement of either Copy or Original from this location. Source is usually expressed by a PP Complement.
The Goal is the location to which material is copied. Unlike the FE Goal in other frames, there is no actual movement of any entity to this location. Goal is usually expressed as a PP Complement:
This FE designates the character of the medium in which a Copy is made. Usually, it is expressed as PP-in or AP.
An intentional action performed by the Creator that lets them bring about the duplication.
Manner of performing an action
Result of an event
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase that describes a primary participant, either the Creator or the Copy/ Original.
Degree to which event occurs.
The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
When the event occurs.
Where the event takes Place.
The Explanation for which an intentional act is performed.
The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
The way in which the Copy matches or does not match the Original.
The Iterations is the number of times the Original is copied.
The Frequency is the frequency with which the Original is copied.
An entity that participates in much the same way as another participant (Creator, Copy, or Original), although it is characterized as being less focal to the action.

name: Duration_description
d: An event or state (here termed an Eventuality) or time-Period is described in terms of the Degree to which its duration diverges from a standard. As is usual for gradable attributes, the standard of comparison is normally based on the expected duration for the type of Eventuality or Period. (In conjunction with the comparative construction, the standard may also be based upon an explicit value.)

ex.t: After a lengthy discussion with the Foreign Minister, Mr. Qian Qichen, they met the Prime Minister.
The lengthy period which most party leaders have already spent in Parliament before gaining office certainly gives them time to acquire suitable skills.

fes.d: A situation, action or event whose duration is being described. The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively: The lecture was short. We had a lengthy conversation.

Sometimes these adjectives describe simply a period of time, rather than an event or state. The Period almost invariably occurs as the modified noun with an attributive adjective: We waited for only a short time. Use of the drug over a lengthy period can cause memory loss.
Degree to which event occurs

name: Duration_relation
d: A Period or Eventuality is related to its Duration. Alternatively, an Entity may stand in metonymically for an Eventuality that it is involved in.

ex.t: You wouldn't last five minutes!

fes.d: A situation, action or event whose duration is being described. The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively:
Sometimes a period of time, rather than an event or state is described.
The amount of time that the Eventuality, Period, or Entity lasts.

An item which is metonymically related to an Eventuality. Some common eventualities that are metonymically entailed are the effect of the entity in its capacity as an instrument and the existence of the entity.

An individual that deploys a resource to receive a benefit. The construction that introduces this FE is idiosyncratic, combining with last (in this frame), cost, and take--and more marginally see (in "saw me through the winter") and keep (in "It 'll keep me for a while .") In this frame, the resource maps onto the Entity, and the benefit is the Eventuality.

name: Duration_scenario
d: An Event or Period has a particular Duration. The Duration may be characterized in several different ways: as a Durational direct measure, a Degree of deviation from an expected Duration, or as a Count of Units of standard, known duration.

fes.d: The Period whose the duration Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.
The feature of an Period which is under discussion, namely the duration.
A quantity or other characterization of the Period's absolute duration.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Duration from the norm.
A standard measure, having a known duration.
The number of Units which are equivalent to the Duration of the Period .
An process whose duration is measured.

name: Dying
d: A Protagonist is near or approaching death.

ex.t: But a dying patient is still a living patient.

fes.d: The FE Protagonist is the being or entity that dies.
The location where the dying event happens.
The Explanation why the dying event occurs.
When the dying event occurs.
How long the Protagonist is dying.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
How often the dying event occurs.

name: Dynamic_situation_scenario
d: This frame denotes simple Events in which an Entity is in a dynamic situation, usually punctually or continually changing to conform to the situation encoded in the Event_endstate. This frame also covers situations in which there is no significant difference between the pre- and post-states, but the dynamic situation that occurs between them is notably temporally bounded.

fes.d: When the event occurs.
Concrete or abstract entity
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Name of the event which occurs.
Where the event takes place.

name: Dynamism
d: A physical Exerter, Action, or Force exerts energy at a level specified by the target. This frame covers both individual-level/static uses ("an INTENSE person") as well as stage-level/dynamic uses ("an INTENSE look"), although the individual-level meaning seems more basic. Exerter, Action, and Force belong to a Core set. This frame also covers several productive metaphor cases. In the first one, movement or change caused by a social entity is conveyed as energy exerted by a physical entity. 'Social' here encompasses entities that are economic, political, technological, historical, cultural, and intimate: Relatedly, the influential effect of an psychological entity is described in terms of energy exertion by a physical entity. 'Psychological' includes the intellectual, emotional, and creative: Both metaphors appear to involve a third metaphor, which is the anthropomorphization of processes (see examples directly above) or inhuman entities (e.g. in nature): Further, there is a metonymy wherein energy exerted by people carrying out an activity characterizes instead a central object or other component of the activity: Compare to: Level_of_force_exertion.

ex.t: Although an energetic and able warrior, Charlemagne tended to direct battles rather than fight in person.
She dumped a mug on the bedside table with such vigor that steaming coffee spashed out.
Swing the racket with dynamic force.

fes.d: The Action that exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.
The Exerter which exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.
This FE describes the energy exertion of the Exerter, Action, or Force.

The Degree to which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy. Where Degree is expressed by a comparative or superlative form of the target, the FE is marked on the target (as well as on the rest of the comparative/superlative expression, if present):
The Time during which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy.
The Force that exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.
The Circumstances under which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy.
The location where the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts its energy.
The Domain is the field in which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts its energy.

name: Earnings_and_losses
