d: An Earner receives Earnings by providing Goods to a Buyer; providing the Goods also generally entails a cost, which may or may not be included in the consideration. This frame emphasizes the effect on the Earner and often generalizes across an indefinite number of transactions with various parties. Some of the LUs (e.g. earn.v) primarily refer to the to the Earnings without reference to cost, others to the amount the Earnings differ from the cost, emphasizing either a net loss (e.g. loss.n) or net gain (e.g. net.n).

ex.t: This reflects the 15 % jump in earnings over 1994 .
We made nearly two million on resales alone last year .
After a $ 1.5 million loss , the company is in no state to continue .

fes.d: The Buyer is the source of the Earnings of the Earner.
The Earner is involved in a transaction or set of transactions as the party that receives payment.
Earnings are the money given to the Earner in a transaction, generally in exchange for Goods.
Goods is anything including labor or time, for example, which is exchanged for Earnings in a transaction.
In some cases, earning is described per unit of Goods.
This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.
The means by which the Earner gains money.
Any description of the action of earning which reveals correllated details, especially characterizations of the Earner which influence the event.
A state of affairs that the Earner intends to bring about as a result of participating in the Commercial Transaction.
The location where the Earner makes their Earnings.
The time when the Earner makes their Earnings.
This FE identifies an event during which the Earner receives Earnings in a transaction.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the event of earning or losing logically follows.

name: Eclipse
d: An Obstruction blocks an Eclipsed entity partially or completely from view. The positions of the Obstruction and the Eclipsed entity are often reported relative to a Vantage_point.

ex.t: A small green bulb concealed behind the panel flashed on momentarily .

fes.d: The entity which blocks the Eclipsed entity from view.
The entity which is blocked from view.

The position from which an observer, if an observer were present, would have their view of the Eclipsed entity blocked by the Obstruction. Phrases such as "from view" and "from sight" are assumed to indicate that the Eclipsed entity is not visible from any Vantage_point. This frame element includes direct reference to observers. .
The extent to which the Eclipsed entity is blocked from view.
The part of the Eclipsed entity which is blocked from view.

name: Economy
d: A Political_region, often a nation, has an economic system, theEconomy, defined by the level of production and consumption of goods and services. The Market_type or Domain may be specified.

ex.t: The Canadian economy will continue to expand in 2005.
Medical industry is a new force in the industrial economy of Lin'an.

fes.d: The Political_region is the nation, state, or other political body within which an economic system exists.
The Economy is the state of the Political_region as defined by the production, consumption, etc. of goods and services.
The Domain of the state for which the Economy is being considered.
The type of economic market in which the Economy exists.
A further depction of the Economy.

name: Education_teaching
d: This frame contains words referring to teaching and the participants in teaching. A Student comes to learn either about a Subject; a Skill; a Precept; or a Fact as a result of instruction by a Teacher. Some of the nouns (schoolmaster, -mistress) in this frame refer to administrative positions and do not take relevant frame elements; these will be moved. Frame-Element relations: Several Frame element relations hold in this frame. There is a core-set {Material, Teacher} (possibly also including Institution); these FE's can fill the subject slot of the teach-type verbs. There is another core-set {Precept, Subject, Skill, Fact, Role} to do with what is learnt. In addition, the FE Qualification may occur with Subject and Role Phrases expressing Qualification also very often include information about the Subject (see below), which is to be annotated on the second layer.

ex.t: Dad taught me that if you work hard, you will be OK - no matter what happens.
What Our Cat taught Me  About Marketing!
For two years she taught me French

fes.d: One who instructs a Student in some area of knowledge or skill.
One who is instructed by a Teacher in skills or knowledge.
An educational establishment, such as a school or college.
The area of knowledge or skill which is taught by a Teacher or to a Student.

This FE identifies the Level of a student in his/her education. This is distinct from the goal or qualification towards which a student is working (Qualification ). The above are both Levels, in contrast to:
A formal Qualification such as an academic degree or a certificate for which a student is aiming.
Degree to which event occurs
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
Manner of performing an action
An intentional action performed by the actor (Student or Teacher depending on the profiling of particular words) that lets them achieve the instruction or learning they are attempting.
Result of an event
The time when the teaching occurs.
The Place is the location within which the teaching takes place.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
An action which the Student is able to perform as a result of instruction.
A guideline for correct behavior. In most cases, this concerns morally or socially desirable actions.
A piece of information that the Student is informed of by the Teacher.
Educational Material, such as books, tapes, or videos, used by a Teacher or a Student to acquire skills or knowledge.
A role, typically professional or vocational, that the Student is meant to be able to fill as a result of their training.
FN: a program of lectures or other matter dealing with a subject
The state-of-affairs that the Teacher hopes to bring about by teaching.

name: Electricity
d: Lexical units in this frame refer to Electricity, in particular as a form of energy harnessed for particular uses (such as powering machines). The Source of the Electricity may also be expressed, or incorporated in the meaning of the LUs.

ex.t: A compound to generate wind electricity was built on the other side of those mountains.
China's hydroelectric dam is being built primarily for flood control and energy production.

fes.d: Electricity is the physical force that is used as power.
The Source of the Electricity.
A characterization of some property of the Electricity.
The intended Inherent_purpose of the Electricity.

name: Elusive_goal
d: An Experiencer does not achieve a Desired_goal. Typically, the Experiencer is the object of the verb. Metaphorically, a pursued entity is not captured. This frame is a metaphorical extension of the Evading frame. The Evading frame concerns literal motion of two self-directed entities, one of which moves in such a way as to successfully prevent the other from capturing it. In the case of the Elusive_goal frame, however, there is no literal motion, but rather a Desired_goal that is not "captured" by the Experiencer that would like the Desired_goal to be true or known.

ex.t: Success eludes me.
His point escaped  the entire audience.
A simple truth has evaded so many of us.

fes.d: The Experiencer does not achieve a Desired_goal, or capture a pursued entity.
Desired_goal identifies the goal that is not achieved or the entity that is not captured.
This FE identifies the Time when the Experiencerr fails to achieve a Desired_goal .
This FE identifies the Place where the Experiencer fails to achieve a Desired_goal.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the goal is not achieved.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Experiencer fails to reach a goal.
The length of time during which the Experiencer does not acheive the Desired_goal.

name: Emanating
d: In this frame an Emission emanates from a Source along a Path or to a Goal.

ex.t: The light emanates from the tower.
The uranium particles radiate from the nuclear plant .

fes.d: The Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which the emanating takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.
Degree to which the emanation occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Emission.
This FE is an expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Emission
The amount of time for which emanation occurs.
The Emissions are discharged out of the Source .
This FE is the point at which the Emission ends up as a result of the motion.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the emanating occurs.
This FE is a description of a trajectory of emanation which is neither a Source nor Goal.
The rate at which emanation occurs
This FE identifies the time when the emanation occurs.
This is the means of conveyance of the Emission .
The Source is the location from which the Emission emanates.
The Form is the state in which the Emission is emitted.
This FE identifies the result of the emanating.

name: Emergency
d: This frame characterizes the situation or state of affairs in which someone should or must act to prevent a Undesirable_event from occurring. Often, an Entity affected by the Undesirable_event is more salient than the event itself and is mentioned in its place.

ex.t: Jo had a peanut butter chocolate candy emergency.

fes.d: The potentially damaging event that should be prevented or ameliorated.
The individual or valued object that is threatened by a worsening condition.
The conditions in which the Undesirable_event occurs; or, the circumstances that explain the impending threat to the Entity.
The location where the emergency situation arises.
The domain of the situation which the emergency is affecting.
This FE identifies the experiencer within the emergency action chain, often relating the person or group who feels or is threatened by the emergency.
When the Emergency occurs.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The period within which an Emergency has occurred.
How long the Emergency takes place.
How often the Emergency occurs.

name: Emergency_fire
d: A fire which burns and requires an emergency-type response.

fes.d: The total material currently involved in combustion, including both the parts of the Fuel currently undergoing chemical alteration and the partially ionized gas that results from this process.
The entity that is undergoing rapid chemical alteration leading to damage or destruction.
Any description of the Emergency_fire event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (loudly, urgently), and general descriptions comparing events.
Name given to the burning Emergency_fire
This FE identifies the Place where the Fire is burning.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire is burning.

name: Emitting
d: In this frame a Source_emitter discharges its Emission along a Path or to a Goal. The Sub-source is only present when the actual Source_emitter is also given or is present in a possessive. In (3) we would tag 'his' as Source_emitter on a second layer because the inalienable possession on the Sub-source indicates the Source_emitter

ex.t: (1) The factory exudes toxic fumes from three large chimneys.
(2) Light is emitted  from the tower .
(3) Noxious odors are emitted from his feet .

fes.d: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Source_emitter emits the Emission
This FE identifies the Time when the Source_emitter emits the Emission.
The Source_emitter is the item from which the Emission are discharged.
The Emissions are discharged out of the Source_emitter .
The Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which emission takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.
Degree to which emission occurs
Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Emission or Source_emitter.
This FE is an expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Emission
This FE is the point at which the Emission ends up as a result of the motion.
The Means by which the Source_emitter emits.
This FE is a description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source_emitter or Sub_source nor Goal.
The Sub-source is the subregion of the Source_emitter which emits the Emission.
The rate at which emission occurs.
The Explanation for which the Source_emitter emits the Emission
The amount of time for which the Source_emitter emits the Emission.
This is the means of conveyance of the Emission.
The Form is the state in which the Emission is emitted.

name: Emotion_active
d: This frame has similarities to Experiencer_subject, but here the verbs are more 'active' in meaning. (For example, they often occur in negative imperatives, e.g. "Don't worry!''). They also differ from Experiencer_subject verbs in that they occur with Topic expressions and can be used in the present progressive: *Pat is fearing the exam. This frame can be thought of as a blend of a basic emotion frame with Cogitation.

ex.t: Pat is still worrying about the exam.

fes.d: The FE Experiencer indicates the one who is actively expressing emotion over the Topic. It usually occurs as the subject of the verb.
The Experiencer's emotion generally is about something. This is indicated with a Topic which usually occurs in a PP-Complement.
The FE Degree indicates the degree to which the Experiencer expresses the emotion.
The FE Manner indicates the manner in which the active emotion is expressed.
The FE Result indicates what happens due to the Experiencer actively expressing emotion.
An action performed by the Experiencer which brings about the active emotion.

name: Emotion_directed
d: The adjectives and nouns in this frame describe an Experiencer who is feeling or experiencing a particular emotional response to a Stimulus or about a Topic. There can also be a Circumstances under which the response occurs or a Reason that the Stimulus evokes the particular response in the Experiencer.

ex.t: Mr. Whiskers is upset that there are no more cat treats.
The furious parent stormed into the office.
Franz gets infuriated at the thought of his ex-wife remarried.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.
The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
The Degree is the degree to which the Experiencer feels the emotion.
The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.
The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in. [Here we know that the scenes are filled with jubilant Experiencers.]
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.
The Manner is the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Emotion_heat
d: This frame contains verbs that describe emotional experiences and participate in the locative alternation, as in the following examples: While these words might seem to be like support verbs for emotion nouns such as anger, the same verbs can be used in the absence of such nouns, as in:

ex.t: I was boiling with anger.
Anger was boiling inside me.
His remarks made me boil inside.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the individual that experiences the Emotion.

The Emotion experienced (usually restricted to words such as anger, fury, rage, passion) can occur as the External Argument or in a PP Complement. Alternatively, there may be no expression of Emotion separate from the target verb:
The Cause of the Emotion can be expressed in a PP Complement headed by at:
The words in this frame can occur with an overtly expressed Seat of the Emotion. This frame element occurs as a PP Complement:
Degree to which event occurs
Manner of performing an action
Topic is the entity that the proposition or propositions conveyed relate to, that they are about. Had someone communicated to the capital about the flagrant disregard of the religious law ?
The Expression is the words or behavior through which the Emotion is expressed.

name: Emotions
d: An Experiencer has a particular emotional State, which may be described in terms of a specific Stimulus that provokes it, or a Topic which categorizes the kind of Stimulus. Rather than expressing the Experiencer directly, it may (metonymically) have in its place a particular Event (with participants who are Experiencers of the emotion) or an Expressor (a body-part of gesture which would give an indication of the Experiencer's state to an external observer).

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.
The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.
The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.
The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus. Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Emotions_by_possibility
d: An Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State can be described as characterized by a particular emotion as evoked by a possibility in their future (Stimulus) or concerning a given Topic.

Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State can be described as having said emotion.

d: An Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State has an emotion as brought on by an Stimulus or Topic.

ex.t: The joyful reunion took place on Sunday.
The Polish-born Pope was driven past jubilant crowds.
I am glad about the sheep .

The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State can be described as having said emotion.

d: An Experiencer can be described as having an emotion as induced by a Stimulus.

ex.t: The children enjoyed noise games and sing-songs.
The pleasures of eating are fleeting.
Diners delight in counter culture cuisine.

This FE sums up what is expressed in the main clause, often with a VPing.

name: Emotions_success_or_failure
d: A Topic or Stimulus fails or succeeds at causing an emotion in an Experiencer, which is conveyed by an Expressor or manifested in a State or description of an Event.

ex.t: They were dissatisfied with the arrangements.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State can be described as having said emotion.

name: Emphasizing
d: An Agent who is engaged in an Undertaking accords a Degree of importance to a Consideration that influences the success of an Undertaking. As a consequence, the Agent acts in a way that reflects that judgment of importance.

ex.t: Our company emphasizes marketing tried and true products and services.INI
In fact, most search engines place little weight on words placed in meta tags when creating their relevancy rankings.INI
The emphasis is on the fundamental principles from which the automotive technologies of the future will develop, rather than on present-day processes.

fes.d: An event or state of affairs, an attribute, or an entity whose properties have the potential to influence the success of the Agent's Undertaking.
This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.
The Undertaking is a process or state or field of activity in which the Agent participates.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.
The Agent is the individual who devotes time, concentration, or other resources to a Consideration that is important for the success of a larger Undertaking.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by assigning the specified level of importance to the Consideration.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that allows the Agent to respond to the importance of the Factor to the Undertaking.
The Competing_consideration is another factor that is relevant to the Undertaking to which the Agent devotes less attention or effort.
The time period during which the Agent attaches a specified degree of importance to the Consideration to further the success of the Undertaking.
The location in which the Agent attaches the specified level of importance to the Consideration.
Any further description of the Agent's placing of importance on the Consideration.
The Artifact is a physical object designed with some Consideration in mind, such that it functions to facilitate the Undertaking.
The Action is performed with importance placed on the Consideration.

This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times. In the future, we will further distinguish Particular_iteration, which is intended to pick out a particular iteration from a series.
The state or quality of an entity involved in the action that holds during the action.

name: Employee_scenario
d: The sequence of events in which the Employee hires on with an Employer, holds a Position, and finally leaves the Position.

fes.d: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task. It often varies over the lifetime of employment.
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

name: Employer_scenario
d: The sequence of events in which the Employer hires an Employee, employs them in a Position for some Duration, and finally lets them go from the Position.

fes.d: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

name: Employing
d: An Employer employs an Employee whose Position entails that the Employee perform certain Tasks in exchange for Compensation.

ex.t: I employed him as Chief Gardener for ten years.

fes.d: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
The FE Employee denotes the person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
The Employer is the person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
The FE Field identifies the field in which the Employee is employed.
The FE Manner identifies the way in which an Employer hires an Employee.
The FE Place identifies the location where the Employer hires the Employee.
The FE Position indicates a particular type of employment.
The FE Purpose identifies what the Employer intends to accomplish through the hiring of the Employee.
The Task indicates the action/duty that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
The FE Time identifies the time at whcih the Employer hires the Employee.
The FE Duration identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.
The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.
This FE describes a characteristic of the Employee.
The Subgroup is the department or subdivision of the institution that the Employee is a member of.

name: Employment_continue
d: This is a non-perspectivized frame representing the middle stage of the Employment_scenario, in which there is a stable employment relationship between the Employee and the Employer.

fes.d: The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues the employment.
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the relationship between an Employer and an Employee develops.
This FE identifies the place where the Employee works for the Employer.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer employs the Employee.

name: Employment_end
d: This is a non-perspectivized frame representing the final stage of the Employment_scenario, in which the relationship between the Employer and the Employee comes to an end. There are two different ways in which the relation ends, represented in the Firing frame (in which the Employer is agentive) and the Quitting frame (in which the Employee is agentive).

fes.d: The person whose employment relationship with an Employer ends.
The person (or institution) whose employ the Employee leaves.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an employment relationship between an Employer and an Employee ends.
This FE identifies the place where the Employer/Employee relationship is ended.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
This FE identifies the Time when the Employer/Employee relationship ceases.

name: Employment_scenario
d: An Employee and Employer enter into an employment relation, wherein the Employee remains employed for some Duration of time, and finally the relationship ends either by the Employee leaving the job or the Employer letting go (or firing) the Employee. To each of these events there are concomitants, such as agreeing to/signing a contract for entering employment, compensation and performance of a service for the employment period itself, and severance for the dissolution of the relationship. There are several other events involved, including preparatory actions on the part of the Employer (posting the Position), the prospective Employee's part (looking for a job), or both (job interviews). In addition, there is the possibility of change in the relationship of Employer and Employee during the employment period, such as a change in Position (e.g. promotion, demotion) and a change in Compensation (e.g. raise, paycut).

fes.d: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

name: Employment_start
d: This is a non-perspectivized frame representing the initial stage of the Employment_scenario: the formation of the employment relationship between the Employer and the Employee.

fes.d: The person who enters an employment relationship with an Employer, thereby obligating themself to perform assigned Tasks in order to receive Compensation .
The person (or institution) that enters an employment relationship with an Employee.
Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing assigned Tasks in the course of their employment.
This FE identifies the Field which the Employee enters as they take up employment with the Employer.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the employment relationship between an Employer and an Employee comes about.
This FE identifies the place where the Employer and the Employee enter into the employment relationship.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Task identifies the assignment that the Employee is obligated to do when she enters the employment relationship with the Employer.
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer and an Employee establish an employment relationship.

name: Emptying
d: These are words relating to emptying containers and clearing areas of some substance or items. The area or container can appear as the direct object with all these verbs, and is designated Source because it is the source of motion of the Theme. Corresponding to its nuclear argument status, it is also affected in some crucial way, unlike Source in other frames. Some words in this frame, such as empty, may also occur with Path or Goal expressions, e.g.

ex.t: The players emptied the bucket over his head.

fes.d: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying.
The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of".
The Source is the region or container which is emptied of something. In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object.
The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.
The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.
The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.
Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying.
The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.
The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.
The Result of the Agent emptying the Source.
This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source.
The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying.
The location where the emptying takes place.
The time at which the emptying takes place.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The reason why the Agent empties the Source of the Theme.

name: Encoding
d: A person (Speaker) expresses a Message or mental content, broadly understood, in a particular Manner. The content may be emotional, as in intellectual, as in or linguistic, as in

ex.t: Humans express  feelings through words
Formulate the idea carefully
Phrase your question as a comment.

fes.d: Speaker, the person who encodes the Message, occurs as the External Argument of all the verbs:
The Message is almost invariably expressed in an NP Object. (The only exceptions occur with the verb express, which is occasionally used with that-clause complements.) BUT:

For most of the words in this frame, some expression of Manner or Medium is obligatory. As in other frames, Manner expressions characterize the action (in this case, the speech act performed by the Speaker). However, a wide range of Manner expressions occurs in this frame, including the following types:
Medium expresses the Medium of communication, such as the language used or the specific type of text in which the Message occurs:
The Addressee is the person to whom the communication is directed.
An act done by the Speaker whereby they achieve the phrasing of the Message.

name: Encounter
d: This frame describes Individuals who unintentionally come together to form a Group. Alternatively, a grammatically more prominent Party_1 meets by chance a Party_2, expressed as an oblique phrase.

ex.t: I encountered Jim on my way to class.

fes.d: The Group describes the resulting formation of the Individuals.
The Individuals are self-movers who unintentionally meet up.

Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the encountering event. It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_2 previous to the by chance meeting.
A grammatically less prominent participant in the encountering event. It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_1 previous to the by chance meeting.

Any description of the unintentional meeting which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects and general descriptions comparing events In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Individuals or Group that also affect the action.
The Means descibes the way in which the Individuals came together to form the Group.
The Time when the encountering event happens.
The Place where the encountering event happens.

name: Endangering
d: An Agent or Cause is responsible for placing a Valued_entity at risk. Endangering_act, Place, Time, Reason, and Circumstance may also be specified.

ex.t: His actions have imperiled his immortal soul!
I admit that I endangered you all by attracting the killer's notice.

fes.d: An (non-sentient) entity or state of affairs that leads to the peril to the Valued_entity.
The entity which may be negatively impacted as a result of the emperilment.
The sentient entity which causes the risk to the Valued_entity.
The specific event or state of affairs brought about by the Agent or Cause which endangers the Valued_entity.
The Manner describes an aspect of the endangering act that is not directly related to the cause, intermediate action, or entity involved.
The location where the Valued_entity is put in danger.
The time when the Valued_entity is put in danger.

name: Endeavor_failure
d: Some individual or group ceases to be able to sustain an Endeavor (a long-term activity involving economic interaction with the public, often a business venture). Unlike Business_failure and Locale_closure, the Endeavor need not refer to an organization or business tied to a specific location or locations.

ex.t: Exxon went under.

fes.d: The Endeavor is rendered unable to continue its regular operations.
The Explanation is named as one of the causes of failure.
The Time of the failure.
The Place of the failing Endeavor.
The Circumstances that caused failure. Compared to Explanation, this describes situations or environments that lead to failure, not a specific reason for failure.
The Manner describes the way in which the Endeavor failed.
The Containing_event is an event within which the failure occurs.
A Depictive describes something about the Endeavor.
The degree to which the Endeavor fails.
The means by which the Endeavor fails.

name: Enforcing
d: An Agent acts to ensure that a Rule (often a constraint on behavior) is being followed. The Agent's action is according to a general plan for Rules (such that implicit in the Rule is the affordance to certain entities to ensure that the Rule is followed). The Rule may be specified for the Duration for which it is in effect.

ex.t: Why don't we enforce the 20000 gun laws currently on the books across the nation?
Computer systems can ruthlessly enforce rules and standards indefinitely.
Can a landlord enforce rules upon tenants?

fes.d: The Rule is the set of constrants on behavior that the Agent implements (i.e., forces others to obey or face consequences).
The length of time for which the Rule is or is not in effect.
The Time at which the Agent enforces the Rule.
The Place at which the Rule is or is not enforced.
The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Rule into effect.
A cause, reason, or other explanation for the enforcing of the Rule.
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Rule.
The Agent, often an institution, governmental organization, or arm thereof, puts into effect (i.e., enforces) a Rule.
The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event.
The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to enforce the Rule.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent enforces the Rule.
This FE describes how fully the Rule was enforced.
This FE describes the medium through which the rule was enforced. It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent.
The Outcome is the failure or success of enforcing the rule.

name: Entering_of_plea
d: The Accused enters a Plea in answer to the Charges. In most jurisdictions, the possible pleas are innocent, guilty, or nolo contendere. Accused persons may stand mute, in which case, the court usually enters a plea on their behalf. Compare to: Citing.

ex.t: He made it clear that he would plead guilty to indecent assault.
An innocent plea was entered on her behalf by a judge at an earlier hearing.

fes.d: The judge of the court in which the accused enters a plea.
The person entering the plea in court.
The crime with which the Accused is charged
The Plea that a defendant makes.
When the event occurs.
Where the event takes place.
The Court is the institution before which the plea is entered.

name: Entity
d: This frame is for words that denote highly schematic entities.

ex.t: We found an unusual wooden object in the desert.

fes.d: Salient parts that make up the Entity.
Formational_cause indicates the action that brings about the features of an Entity.
This FE is used for the Name of an Entity.
A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to.

name: Entourage
d: A group of Individuals form a group, the Entourage, which remains co-located with the Attended_person. The Entourage may have a specific Purpose for following the Attended_person, such as to protect or serve him or her, or the Purpose may be vague (e.g., to be near a person of power).

ex.t: Just before eleven o'clock, one of the consultants came to do a ward round, followed by his entourage of junior doctors and medical students.
The CEO arrived with a comparatively small escort of 30 individuals.

fes.d: This FE identifies the people or things that form the Entourage.
This FE identifies the collection of entities that follow the Attended.
This FE describes a property of the Entourage rather than the Individuals and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the entourage noun when it is unambiguous.
The term used to refer to the Entourage.
The location or political locale that the Entourage exists within.
The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Entourage.
The Attended_person is followed by the Entourage.

name: Erasing
d: An Agent or Cause removes a piece of Information from a Document such that it cannot be retrieved.

ex.t: I deleted the last line from my essay.

fes.d: The person who removes the Information.
The thing that the Agent removes from the Document.
A non-agentive entity that removes the Information.
The collection of pieces of information from which the specific Information is removed.
The way in which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.
The time when the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.
The location in which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.
The means by which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.

name: Escaping
d: A Self-moving Escapee departs from an Undesirable_location.

ex.t: Benjamin escaped from Germany.

fes.d: The Escapee manages to leave the Undesirable_location.
Goal identifies any expression which tells where the Escapee ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.
covers any act performed by the Escapee brings about the escape.
Manner is used for any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion, including descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, etc.
The Undesirable_location is where the Escapee begins.
Speed idenitifies the rate at which the escaping occurs.
Vehicle identifies the means of conveyance by which the Escapee leaves the Undesirable_location.
This FE identifies the Time when the escaping occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the escaping takes place.
This FE identifies the Place where the Escaping occurs.
Depictive identifies a word or phrase describing a participant of an action.
Path describes the trajectory of motion of the Escapee.
This FE identifies the (abstract) nearness of the Escapee to being caught in the Undesirable_location.
The distance along a path away from the Undesirable_location that the Escapee travels.
The situation that explains why the (instance of) the event occurred.

name: Estimated_value
d: A Cognizer has carried out an approximate calculation or considered some Evidence and produced an approximation of the Value of a feature of an Item. There are two alternative construals in which the relationship between the feature and the Value is conceived. Either a holistic Estimation by the Cognizer is presented, or the Question that is addressed by the Cognizer's estimating is given.

ex.t: You can list a ballpark figure for shipping and handling.
Moreover, their estimate of 0.27 °C mean surface warming per century due to land-use changes is at least twice as high as previous estimates based on urbanization alone.
Our decision to trust people depends on our estimate of how trustworthy they are.

fes.d: The individual who has considered evidence or performed calculations to produce the approximation.
The position or area on the feature scale that the Cognizer has concluded the Item occupies.
The entity that possesses a feature whose Value the Cognizer has approximated.
Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which has contributed to their estimation of the Value.
The time period during which the Cognizer formed the estimate.
The location in which the Cognizer has formed their estimate.
A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a feature's Value.
An open proposition for which the Cognizer has approximated the Value of a variable.

name: Estimating
d: A Cognizer carries out an approximate calculation or considers some Evidence so as to arrive at an approximate Value for some Feature of an Item. There are two alternative construals. In one, the Feature is presented as a Question about the Item and the Value is conceived as an answer to the Question. In the second construal, a fully propositional Estimation by the Cognizer is presented which expresses the result of the Cognizer's approximation.

ex.t: Until 1971, dolphin mortality could be estimated only from analyses of vessels ' logbooks -- and the figures are probably underestimates. CNI
The UK government estimates that there is sufficient gas in the UK sector to meet UK demand for some 17 to 35 years .
The astronomers estimated how much energy was needed to create the cavities by calculating the density, temperature and pressure of the hot gas.

fes.d: The individual who considers evidence or performs calculations to arrive at an approximation.
The feature is a scalar property of the Item.
The position or area on the Feature scale that the Cognizer concludes the Item occupies.
The entity that possesses the Feature whose Value the Cognizer seeks to approximate.
Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which contributes to their estimation of the Feature's Value.
The time period during which the Cognizer forms the estimate of the Feature's Value.
The location in which the Cognizer forms their estimate.
A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a Feature's Value.
An open proposition for which the Cognizer seeks to approximate the Value of a variable.
An intentional action performed by the Cognizer enabling estimating.
Manner is used for any expression which describes a property of the activity of Estimating
Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Cognizer estimates.
A state-of-affairs enabling the estimating to occur.
This FE describes how the Estimation made by the Cognizer corresponds to reality. This FE can be represented by "correctly" or "wrong."
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Evading
d: An Evader moves under its own power to thereby avoid Capture or contact with a Pursuer, also generally moving under its own power. This frame characterizes a more specific event than Avoiding in that both the Evader and the Pursuer are moving entities. In addition, this frame differs from Escaping by requiring a Pursuer and being neutral about the prior captivity of the Evader.

ex.t: I gave my handler the slip.
He evaded capture for several hours.

fes.d: This FE is used for phrases that describe a general Area in which motion occurs when it is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element.
Path is used for any description of a trajectory of the motion of the Evader, including directional phrases.
The Evader moves under its own power to Capture or contact with the Pursuer. Normally the Evader frame element is expressed as an external argument.
This FE identifies the Mode_of_transportation that the Evader uses to move. It can either bea part of the Evader's own body or a vehicle.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Evader bringd about the evasion.
The Pursuer is going after the Evader unless they act.
This FE is used for any expression that describes the Degree to which the Evader avoids Capture or contact with the Pursuer.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the evading occurs. It is used for any expression that does not relate directly to the trajectory of motion, including speed, steadiness, and grace.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Evading is done.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Evading is. done.
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Evader evades the Pursuer, or avoids Capture.
This FE identifies the Time at which the Evading occurs.
Depictive is used to identify the state of any of the participants in the evading event.
This FE marks the Speed at which the Evader evades the Pursuer.
An actual or hypothetical event in which the Pursuer takes physical control of the Evader.

name: Evaluative_comparison
d: This frame is about the static comparison of an Profiled_item to a Standard_item, often with respect to some Attribute. In this frame, there is an inherent asymmetry between Profiled_item and Standard_item in that the two cannot be expressed jointly as a subject. Degree expressions are also found that indicate how close the items are to each other on the scale evoked by the Attribute. Furthermore, the particular value of the standard or item on a certain scale may be given by the Standard_attribute of the Profiled_attribute respectively.

ex.t: The Sun is putting on a show that rivals the most sizzling Hollywood thrillers.
Mexico's Copper Canyon rivals the Grand Canyon in sheer beauty and drama.
Peyton Manning's passing yards are equaled among NFL quarterbacks by only a select few.

fes.d: In active sentences, the Profiled_item is the grammatically more prominent one of the items that are compared and realized as the subject. .
In active setnnces, the Standard_item is the grammatically less prominent element, i.e. the object or an oblique.
This Frame Elements marks constituents that indicate in which respect Item-1 and Item-2 are equal to each other.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how close the Profiled_item and the Standard_item are to each other on the scale evoked by the Attribute.
The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on a scale.
The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to a Standard_item or Profiled_attribute.
The Comparison_set includes the Standard_item and is what the Profiled_item is judged with respect to.
The location where the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.
The time at which the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.

name: Event
d: An Event takes place at a Place and Time.

ex.t: Big earthquakes only happen along plate boundaries. INI
The party will take place on Sunday in the all-you-can-eat buffet.

fes.d: Name of the event which occurs.
Where the event takes place.
The Explanation for which an event occurs.
When the event occurs.
How long the Event takes place.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
How often the Event occurs.
The period within which an Event has occurred.

name: Event_endstate
d: The endstate of a simple event X-schema.

fes.d: Concrete or abstract entity
State of an Entity.

name: Event_initial_state
d: The initial state of a simple event X-schema.

fes.d: Concrete or abstract entity
State of an Entity.

name: Event_instance
d: This frame describes a particular instance of an event.

ex.t: These next two days will be the last two times that I'm here.

fes.d: The particular Instance of a given event. All LUs in this frame incorporate this Frame Element.
The event that occurred in one or more instances.
A property of the particular Instance.
The specific number of iterations.

name: Eventive_affecting
d: An Entity undergoes some change (the Event) that is (or is construed as) punctual. (This frame exists mainly to allow common FEs to be inherited.)

ex.t: This happens to me all the time.
The area was struck by tragedy in 1996, when an assassin killed 35 people in Port Arthur.

fes.d: This FE identifies the event which occurs and affects the Entity.
This FE identifies where the event takes place.
This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.
This FE identifies the entity, concrete or abstract.
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
How often the Event happens to the Entity.

name: Eventive_cognizer_affecting
d: An Event causes the Cognizer to accept some Content. Although the Cognizer forms an intention, it is not entailed that he/she acts.

ex.t: The divorce convinced him to get help.
The price of a factory reconditioned tool decided it for me.

fes.d: The person who perceives the Event and changes his or her mind.
The new idea that the Cognizer accepts as a result of experiencing the Event.
The Event which motivates the Cognizer to change his/her mind.
The degree to which the Cognizer's mind is changed.
Any description which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The time at which the Cognizer is affected by an outside Event.
The location where the Cognizer accepts the Content.

name: Evidence
d: The Support, a phenomenon or fact, lends support to a claim or proposed course of action, the Proposition, where the Domain_of_relevance may also be expressed. Some of the words in this frame (e.g. argue) are communication words used in a non-communicative, epistemic sense.

ex.t: The latest poll results show that support of the president is at an all-time low.

fes.d: Support is a fact that lends epistemic support to a claim, or that provides a reason for a course of action. Typically it is expressed as an External Argument.

This is a belief, claim, or proposed course of action to which the Support lends validity. Normally it is expressed as a Finite Clause Complement: Some words in this frame require the proposition to be expressed as an NP Object:
This FE identifies the degree to which a Proposition is supported.
This FE identifies the manner in which a Proposition is supported.
An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship of the Support to the Proposition.
A description of the status of the Support within its relationship to the Proposition. This proves my conclusions all by itself.
Result of an event
This FE identifies the domain (usually, time or space) for which a given Proposition is true.
The person for whom the Proposition is supported by the Support.

name: Evoking
d: Some Stimulus causes a Cognizer to think of a prior Phenomenon due to its perceived similarity.

ex.t: I burned down the malt shop where we used to go just because it reminds me of you

fes.d: The Cognizer is the person who remembers the Phenomenon .
The Phenomenon is the mental content that a Cognizer remembers.
Degree to which Cognizer perceives the Stimulus to match the Phenomenon.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including speed (quickly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Other expressions involving how the experience affects the Cognizer may also be expressed (painfully).
The Duration is the amount of time for which the Stimulus continues to remind the Cognizer of the Phenomenon.
The Explanation for which the Stimulus evokes the Phenomenon.
The Time is when the Cognizer remembers the Phenomenon.
The entity or situation that causes the Cognizer to think of the Phenomenon.
A characteristic of the Stimulus that contributes to the perception of similarity to the Phenomenon.

name: Examination
d: This frame deals with testing or examination of someone's Knowledge or skill in a particular area. An Examiner conducts an Examination to an Examinee to determine the Examinee's Knowledge and/or determine their Qualification for some privilege; this proceeds either by the Examinee demonstrating a skill or by writing responses to questions.

ex.t: At the end of the trial period all three groups took an English for Commerce examination to assess progress.
Many constables had passed the Sergeant's exam.
The only point of Mr. Baker's tests that I can devine is that they will serve to check up on the teachers.

fes.d: One who administers a test of some kind.
One who undergoes a test of some kind.
The ability, practice, or command of information on which an Examinee is tested.
A credential or status that one acquires by passing an Examination.
The Examination that somebody takes.
An act whereby the Examiner assesses the Examinee.
The state-of-affairs that the Examiner wants to bring about by giving the Examinee the Examination.
The location where the examination takes place.
The time at which the examination occurs.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Examiner that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Exchange
d: Two parties, the Exchangers, each give and receive from the other Themes. The parties are also construable separately as Exchanger_1 and Exchanger_2, in which case the Themes may be construed separately, too, as Theme_1 and Theme_2. Notice that this frame is to be differentiated from the Replacing frame, where there is no notion of trade between two parties and the focus is only on the relationship between two items that successively fulfill a function or participate in a relation.

ex.t: They swapped the island with the Neapolitan government of the day for the much smaller Capri.
Then the teams swapped their draftees.
We exchanged addresses and he told us that next year when we are in Aruba we will visit with his family there.

fes.d: In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Exchanger_2. That is, Exchanger_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Exchanger_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Exchanger_1, not necessarily that of Exchanger_2 or the group of Exchangers as a whole.
This FE identifies the place where the exchange occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers make the trade.
This FE identifies the time when the exchange takes place.
This FE identifies the Means by which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers effect the trade.

Any description of the exchange act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Exchanger_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with). Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Exchanger_2.

In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Exchangers. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Exchangers is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Exchange frame, it is possible for the Exchangers role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.
The state of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers during the exchange.
The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_1.
The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_2.
The items which change possession between the Exchangers.
This frame element denotes how often the Exchangers trade Themes.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Exchange_currency
d: A Money_owner exchanges Sum_1 in the Source_currency for Sum_2 in the Target_currency at some Exchange_service.

ex.t: After checking into the Intourist-operated $30-a-day Hotel Zerafshon, we each exchanged $50 for Uzbek currency with a shifty loiterer in the lobby at the rate .
We recently exchanged $100 for £64.00 UK pounds.
If he exchanged the money into Deutsch-marks, his 18 marks in Germany can just barely obtain four Big Macs.

fes.d: The person who exchanges Sum_1 for Sum_2.
An amount of money in the Source_currency that the Money_owner exchanges for an amount in the Target_currency.
The kind of currency of the Money_owner has before the exchange.
The amount of money in the Target_currency that the Money_owner receives in exchange for Sum_1.
The individual or institution which changes the Money_owner's money into the Target_currency.
The kind of currency that the Money_owner receives as part of the exchange.
The location where the money is exchanged.
The time when the currency is exchanged.

Any description of the exchange event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Money_owner that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The action of the Money_owner whereby the exchange is acheived.
The action that the Money_owner is attempting to accomplish with the exchange.
Currency that is being exchanged by the Money_owner.

name: Exclude_member
d: A former Member of a Group ceases to be a member as a result of the action of an Authority within the Group. (In directly democratic Groups, the Authority may consist of the Group itself as a voting whole.)

ex.t: The priest excommunicated Henry from the church.

fes.d: The person who used to belong to a Group.
A set of people standing in a semi-permanent relationship together.
An empowered subset of the Group which decides to expel its former Member.
The time when the Member is excluded.
A cause, reason, or other explanation for the exclusion of the Member.
The Place where the Member is excluded.
The Means by which the Authority excludes the Member.
The Depictive describes a participant in the exclusion event.

name: Excreting
d: An Excreter excretes Excreta.

ex.t: Principal Skinner burped on me.
Lenny and Karl pee three times a day.

fes.d: The Excreta is the waste expelled by the body.
The Excreter is the agent who excretes the Excreta.
The Source is the starting point of the Excreta's motion.
Path identifies the trajectory of the Excreta.
The Goal is where the Excreta finishes its motion.
The Manner in which the Excreter engages in excretion.
The Means by which the Excreter engages in excretion.
This FE identifieis the Place where the excretion occurs.
When the Excreter engages in excretion.
The Purpose is the motivation behind the Excreter's act.
TheFrequency is the number of times per time period that the Excreter is engaged in exctretion.
The Degree to which all of the Excreta are removed from the body.

name: Execute_plan
d: An Agent acts according to a Plan, carrying it out (or taking steps to carry it out). In some cases, the Agent is a focal participant in the Plan, although a separate Focal_participant may also be mentioned. The Plan may be specified for the Duration for which it is in effect. Note: the phrase (put) in effect is in the Being_in_effect frame.

ex.t: Health authorities say they have put measures into effect in all ports of entry and in centers of provinces.
Channing House has recently implemented a new dining program for residents on pureed diets.

fes.d: The Plan is a goal or purpose that the Agent carries out.
The length of time for which the Plan is or is not in effect.
The Time at which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.
The Place at which the Plan is or is not operational. [CHANGE: or, place where agent puts into effect? 2 fes?]
The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.
A cause, reason, or other explanation for the implementation of the Plan
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Plan. [CHANGE: may only be relevant for "implemented the policy for residents of florida only"]
The Agent, often an institution or governmental organization, puts a Plan into effect. The Agent is generally a primary participant in the Plan, but a separate Focal_participant may be specified.
The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event of executing the plan.
The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to execute the Plan.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent executes the Plan.
This FE describes how fully the Plan was executed.
This FE describes the medium through which a plan was executed. It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent.
The Outcome is the failure or success of executing the plan.

name: Execution
d: An Executioner punishes an individual (Executed) with death as a consequence of some action of the Evaluee (the Reason).

ex.t: The hooded man hanged the thief.

fes.d: The Executioner is the individual who performs the execution.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Executioner performs an execution.
The action that is taken that accomplishes the execution
Where the execution takes place.
The purpose for which the execution is carried out.
The punishment of death given to the Executed by the Executioner.
When the execution occurs.
Degree to which event occurs.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing a participant in the action.
The Executed is the person who is killed by the Executioner in retribution for the crime that the Executed was convicted of.

Any description of the execution event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Moreover, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Executioner that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Often, there is a constituent expressing the Explanation for the Judge's judgment which the Executioner is carrying out. It is usually a for-PP.
Result of an event

name: Exemplar
d: This frame concerns a specific subset of Instances of a Type which are evaluated in terms of their similarity to a conceptual prototype of the Type. The judgment of exemplariness may be made along a certain Domain.

ex.t: She is a model student.
He's the image of a good father.

fes.d: A thing or episode that is considered exemplary of a certain Type.
The category of things or events from which an Instance is picked out.
The comparative terms along which the Instance is deemed an exemplar of the Type.
A property of the particular Instance.

name: Exemplariness
d: An Entity, with regard to a particular Domain, is representative of a conceptual prototype of the Comparison_set of which it is a member.

ex.t: Virginia Woolf is a prototypical Modernist author.

fes.d: The thing being judged by its similarity to an ideal.
The group which the Entity is a member of.
The domain along which the Entity is judged to be exemplary.
The degree to which the Entity is exemplary.

name: Exercising
d: An Agent actively maintains or improves their level of phyiscal fitness. The action may target a specific Body_part, or happen through a particular Means.

ex.t: Football players exercise every day.
Don't work out your legs after a long run. CNI

fes.d: The person who is trying to improve or maintain their physical fitness.
An area of the Agent's body that the activity is direct at.
Something that the Agent uses to exercise.
A general description of how the Agent acts while exercising.
The time that the Agent exercises.
The location of the Agent while exercising.
How often the Agent works on their fitness.
This frame element describes a subtype of the more general exercise category.
The purpose for which the Agent exercises.

name: Existence
d: An Entity is declared to exist, generally irrespective of its position or even the possibility of its position being specified. Time, Duration, Inherent_purpose, and State may also be mentioned. This frame is to be contrasted with Presence, which describes the existence of an Entity in a particular (and salient) spacio-temporal context, and which also entails the presence of an observer who can detect the existence of the Entity in that context.

ex.t: Finally, Poland ceased to exist as a state for hundreds of years.
Such laws exist to prevent exactly this kind of fraud.
There IS a Santa Claus!

fes.d: Some entity, abstract or concrete, which is stated to exist.
A time at which the entity is in existence.
The period during which the Entity exists.
The reason why the Entity exists. Generally, this is more specifically the reason why the Entity was made.
The condition that the Entity exists in.
A situation, force, or entity which brings about the existence of the Entity.
Where the Entity exists.
Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Entity is declared to exist
The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Entity (or further state of affairs) to exist or not.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Expansion
d: An Item changes its physical size. The Size_change of an Item may be explicitly indicated or characterized in terms of Initial_size and/or Result_size. In the default case, expansion is along all dimensions, but sometimes the Dimension of expansion is incorporated or made explicit. This frame does not specify whether the Item gains mass or substance along with the change in size, and thus includes words that specify an increase in substance (grow.v) along with those that deny an increase in substance (stretch.v) and those that are unspecified (expand.v).

ex.t: The pile of leaves had shrunk by about half after the first haul.
The jeans stretched a little.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Item whose size changes.
Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.
This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.
Initial_size is used for the size of the Item before any change occurs. It is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit. Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-from Complement.
Result_size is the size that the Item has after the event. It is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by to.
This FE identifies the Size_change of an Item.
This FE identifies the Rate of change of the value.
This FE identifies the Duration of time that the expansion takes.
This FE identifies the Time when the expansion occurs.
Co_variable is the quantity that varies commensurately with the size of the Item, usually construed to be causally linked to the size.
This FE is used for any description of the Manner of the expansion including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
This FE identifies the Degree to which the expansion occurs.
Path is used for any expression that gives information about points on the scale of size that the Item traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement.
Where the Iteam ends up due to Expansion.

name: Expectation
d: Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer believing that some Phenomenon will take place in the future. Some words in the frame (e.g. foresee.v) indicate that the Phenomenon is asserted also to be true, while others do not.

ex.t: Michael expected Abby to demand examples.
From the look on her face Michael expected that she would say she got the job.

fes.d: This is the person who believes some Phenomenon will take place in the future. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: Pat expects that the Yankees will win the World Series.

This is what the Cognizer believes will happen in the future. It can be expressed as a Finite Clause Complement, an NP Object, or a VP Complement with or without an NP Object (see General Grammatical Observations): General Grammatical Observations: Many of the verbs in this frame allow Raising: Pat expects it to rain. In the example above, the word it is grammatically the Object of the target verb expect, but it does not express an FE. Rather, it is merely construed as the External Argument of the verb rain, which heads the VP Complement of the target. In this situation, both the raised consituent it and the VP Complement are marked with the Phenomenon FE, but are marked as separate constituents. That is because the Object can be passivized and therefore not appear adjacent to the VP Complement: It is expected to rain.
Degree to which event occurs
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
Manner of performing an action
Words in this frame may occur with a PP headed by from which expresses the Evidence on which knowledge or belief is based: I have learned from experience that poison oak can be painful.
The location where the Cognizer foresees the Phenomenon.
The time when the Cognizer makes the prediction.
An entity that serves as the focus of a predicted Phenomenon.
The time that the Cognizer expects the Phenomenon to occur. Note that it is distinct from simple Time, which is when the Cognizer is actually involved in thinking about the Phenomenon.

name: Expected_location_of_person
d: A Person usually resides or works in a Location.

ex.t: Is Mr. Adams in today? DNI

fes.d: The Location is the place of business or residence prototypically occupied by the Person.
The Person is located in or at a place that they customarily occupy.
The time period during which the Person occupies the Location.
The length of the time interval during which the Person occupies the Location.

name: Expend_resource
d: An Agent uses a Resource which is consumed and unavailable for future use.

ex.t: We exhausted our supply of oil long ago.

fes.d: The Resource is exhausted over time by being used.
The Agent uses the Resource.
The Agent uses the Resource for a Purpose.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
This FE identifies the place where the Agent exhausts the Resource.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent exhausts the Resource.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent exhausts the Resource.
The degree to which the Resource is depleted by the Agent.

name: Expensiveness
d: A Payer gives up (or potentially gives up) the use of an Asset (generally money) in order to achieve an Intended_event. This event is often more specifically described as gaining possession of some Goods or receiving a Service. In the majority of cases, the Payer is described generically (INI), and the situation depicted answers the question of how much of an Asset would have to be given up to receive the Goods or bring about the Intended_event.

ex.t: It 'll cost Sandra's parents fifty grand a year for her to attend that school.
That book would cost you more than twenty dollars to bind in a local book bindery.
Stamps used to cost only five cents. INI

fes.d: The FE Goods is the item(s) whose price is being assessed. Goods is usually an External Argument:
The person whose Asset is given up in order to achieve an Intended_event. This FE is often expressed as INI.
The price of or payment made for the Goods.
The place where a transaction would take place, generally where Goods and services are created or sold.
This FE identifies the Degree to which Goods are cheap or expensive.
The event that the Payer brings about by deploying the Asset.
The time when a transaction takes place.
The amount of an Asset relative to some measure of the Goods

name: Experience_bodily_harm
d: An Experiencer is involved in a bodily injury to a Body_part. (In some cases, no Body_part need be indicated.) Often an Injuring_entity on which the Experiencer injures themselves is mentioned.

ex.t: I think that I hurt myself pretty bad back there.
He smacked his head on the mantel getting up from poking at the fire.

fes.d: The location on the body of the Experiencer where the bodily injury takes place.
The event in which the bodily injury takes place.
Manner in which the injury takes place.
The place where the harming event occurs.
The being or entity that is injured.
The time when the harming event occurs.
The Experiencer injures him/herself on an Injuring_entity.
The extent to which the Experiencer is affected by the injury.
The number of times that the injury happens to the Experiencer.
The period of time during which the Experiencer repeatedly receives bodily injuries.
The number of times that the Experiencer has an experience of bodily harm.

name: Experiencer_focus
d: The words in this frame describe an Experiencer's emotions with respect to some Content. A Reason for the emotion may also be expressed. Although the Content may refer to an actual, current state of affairs, quite often it refers to a general situation which causes the emotion. With certain verbs, the Circumstances can be expressed in a finite clausal or wh- complement which may optionally be preceded by a Null NP Object: Note: This is not how it is currently tagged.

ex.t: My enjoyment of the movie was considerably impaired by the seven-foot guy sitting in front of me.
Smithers takes great pleasure in collecting matchboxes.
Sergio derives great pleasure from smoking.

fes.d: The Experiencer experiences the emotion or other internal state.

Content is what the Experiencer's feelings or experiences are directed towards or based upon. The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion.
The Explanation is the explanation for why an Experiencer experiences the particular emotion.
The Degree to which the experience occurs.
Manner of performing an action

The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Experiencer that reflect his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
