The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Content.
The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the particular experience.
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in. Here we know that the ceremony was filled with nervous Experiencers.

The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.
The time at which the Experiencer is in the specified emotional state.

name: Experiencer_obj
d: Some phenomenon (the Stimulus) provokes a particular emotion in an Experiencer.

ex.t: Nightmare on Elm Street scared me silly.

fes.d: The Experiencer reacts emotionally or psychologically to the Stimulus.
The Stimulus is the event or entity which brings about the emotional or psychological state of the Experiencer.
The Degree is the degree to which the Stimulus brings about an emotion in the Experiencer.
Depictive identifies a phrase which describes a state of the Experiencer.
The Manner in which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.
The Means by which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.
The Result of the Stimulus affecting the Experiencer.
The Circumstances is the circumstances under which the Stimulus brings about the experience.
The reason why the Stimulus causes the emotion in the Experiencer.
The Time when the Experiencer has an emotion as caused by the Stimulus.

name: Experimentation
d: An Experimenter conducts an Experiment based on a Hypothesis. This Experiment contains a Control_group or Control_group_member which is compared with a Treatment_group or Treated_individual in order to determine the Result.

ex.t: Johann's experiment proved the new drug was effective in treating the disease.
Jacob placed the control group under a strong light for 20 hours each day.
Rolf tested his hypothesis in Vienna in 1973.

fes.d: The Experimenter is the individual conducting the Experiment.
The group of entities in the Experiment which have not been treated and are compared to the Treatment_group or Treated_individual.
An individual entity of the Experiment which is left untreated and then compared with the Treatment_group or the Treated_individual.
A group of subjects that receive Treatment and are compared to the Control_group or Controlled_individuals.
An individual subject that receives treatment and is then compared to the Control_group or Controlled_individual.
The amount of time the Experiment lasts.
The Place in which the Experiment is conducted.
The Time at which the Experimenter conducts the Experiment.
A property that belongs to either the Control_group or the Treatment_group. Usually expressed by a PP.
The Result depicts the outcome of the Experiment.
A Descriptor identifies a characteristic or description of the Experiment or the Subjects not captured by any other frame element.
The test or Experiment conducted by the Experimenter using a Control_group and a Treatment_group.
The Hypothesis is a conjecture as to the result of an Experiment. The Experiment takes place in order to prove the Hypothesis as correct or incorrect.

In this frame Control_group and Treatment_group can be combined and expressed as Subjects. This FE can also be used for a generic individual on whom the Experiment is being conducted (see second example).
A tool used in conducting the Experiment. Usually expressed by a with-PP.
The Topic is the subject that the Experiment is studying.

name: Expertise
d: This frame concerns people's knowledge or skill in certain domains. It does not concern acquaintance or familiarity with people. With adjectives as targets in this frame, we annotate on two FE layers.

ex.t: FE Layer-1: He is an experienced programmer.
FE Layer-2: He is an experienced programmer.

fes.d: The person whose expertise is assessed.
Skill identifies the Protagonist's talent or ability to do things with one's hand or body.
The area of knowledge (as opposed to a practical skill) in which the Protagonist 's experience is assessed.
Degree to which event occurs
A product of behavior that shows the Protagonist's skill or lack of skill.

This frame element can only occur in place of a skill expression. It refers to the prototypical patient in an action involving the Protagonist. For instance, in the following sentence the children are experts at some (contextually given) action such as rolling the hoops. Some children were quite expert with wooden hoops.
This frame element denotes a role in which the protagonist has developed his expertise. In many cases, the Role noun secondarily evokes the Skill that is at issue.
The Manner give further description of the way in which the Protagonist exhibits their skill or lack of skill.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.
The Time when the Protagonist has the expertise.

name: Explaining_the_facts
d: A Question about the reason or cause of a known State_of_affairs is presented as being answered by the existence of a particular Fact. The exact chain of reasoning, including the answer itself, of which the Fact is a part is not specified. Contrast this frame with the Evidence frame which casts a Support (a fact) as providing Evidence for, or conclusively proving, the Proposition (another proposed fact). Thus, there is no open question in the Evidence frame.

ex.t: Ruby's orange vest marked with the words "service dog" accounts for why the 3-year-old goes along.
The nation's history explains why the current conflict succumbs to, and yet simultaneously transcends, the stereotype.
Then that I exist is explained by A and B having come together.

fes.d: A Fact which can be connected by a chain of reasoning to the State_of_affairs.
A Fact whose cause is under consideration.
This FE identifies how much of the State_of_affairs is explained by the Fact.
This FE indicates salient characteristics of the Fact considered as an explanation.
An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship between the Fact and the State_of_affairs.
The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Fact an explanation for the State_of_affairs.
An open proposition concerning the cause of the State_of_affairs.

The state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the Concessive.

name: Explosion
d: Due to chemical, nuclear, or other reactions, an Explosive explodes, potentially causing damage to the surrounding area. The Explosive is often, but need not be, a weapon.

ex.t: The bomb exploded in the middle of the plaza.
Nearby, a mine detonated, causing minor damage to the tank.
The car bomb explosion left a massive crater.

fes.d: The Explosive releases a large amount of force, destroying itself and causing damage to the surrounding area.
The Time when the explosion occurs.
The location where the explosion occurs.
The Victim is targeted by the explosion or inadvertantly damaged by the explosion. Typically expressed by an on-PP.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the explosion occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The means by which the Explosive explodes.
A description of the explosion not specifically covered by other Frame Elements.
The strength of the explosion, or to what degree it damaged the affected areas or objects.
How often an explosion occurs.

name: Exporting
d: An Exporter moves Goods across a border from an Exporting_area to an Importing_area.

ex.t: Several companies actually make most of their income by exporting goods out of the country.
Exportation into nations of "special interest" is essentially prohibited.

fes.d: The conscious entity, generally a person, that moves the Goods across a border out of the Exporting_area. Very often, an Exporting_area will metonymically stand in for the person or persons directly responsible for the movement of the Goods. In such cases the constituent should be labeled Exporter on the first layer and with the appropriate locational FE on the second layer.
A mobile entity directed by the Exporter that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Exporter that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Exporter that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
The items of value whose location is changing.
This FE identifies the state-of-affairs that the Exporter is attempting to bring about by exporting.
A state of affairs that explains why the Exporter moves the Goods across the border.
This FE identifies the time when the Exporter moves the Goods.
This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action
The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.
Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.
The place where the Goods are initially, before the the Exporter moves them.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Exporting event belongs to.

name: Expressing_publicly
d: A Communicator publically communicates some difficult-to-express Content which they (or a social group of which they are a member) have had for some time. The Content may not have been previously communicated due to inability or social stricture. In cases where the individuals addressed are a smaller group than the public at large, a separate Addressee may be expressed.

ex.t: Those grievances can be aired during Board meetings. CNI
Saddam voiced his joy when he was told Spain's new government had left the US-led military coalition in Iraq.

fes.d: The Communicator is the person who expresses the Content (whether spoken or written).
The Addressee is the person to whom the Content is communicated.
The attitude or feeling that the Communicator had not previously expressed.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Communicator that also affect the action (eagerly).
An act whereby the Communicator communicates the Content.
The emotional or physical state of the Communicator that leads to their communication.
Medium is the observable action or product of the Communicator.
The state of the Communicator during the statement.
The time when the Content is communicated.
The FE specifies the place where the communication takes place.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
The Purpose is the desired result of public expression.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the communication and any of its participants. Quite often, Circumstances secondarily provide an Explanation for the particular communication.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the particular public expression logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the expression, but not in all cases.

name: Extradition
d: A Suspect in a Current_jurisdiction is forced by Authorities (of the Current_jurisdiction) to go to the Crime_jurisdiction, i.e. the jurisdiction which requested that the Suspect be handed over for trial for a crime which he or she is suspected to have committed in the Crime_jurisdiction. The purpose or reason for the extradition may also be expressed.

ex.t: The fraud was extradited from Venezuela to the US.

fes.d: The Authorities act on behalf of the Current_jurisdiction, giving up the Suspect to the Crime_jurisdiction.
The jurisdiction (generally a nation) the Suspect starts off in.
The jurisdiction (generally a nation) to which the Suspect is sent.
The Suspect is forced to go to the jurisdiction where a crime he or she is suspected of took place or is being tried.
The Purpose for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect. .
The Explanation for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect. .
This FE indicates the basis in law of an extradition.
The time at which the Suspect is moved.
A description of the manner of the extradition.
A description of the Authorities or Suspect during the extradition.
The act of the Authorities which brings about the transfer from the Current_jurisdiction to the Crime_jurisdiction.
The location where the extradition occurs.

name: Extreme_point
d: An Entity that has characteristics which change over time is at a point or in a phase of its development in which, compared to other actual or expected stages of development, it possesses extremely high or low powers or intensity. The high or low level of development correlates with the occurrence of a Marker, a product produced by the Entity or an event in which it participates, which is indicative of the Entity's abilities or intensity.

ex.t: The Tang Dynasty was the high point of the Silk Road's importance.
Meeting Fiona Bennett was the LOW POINT of my summer.
It must be remembered that this man was born at the zenith of the Victorian age and witnessed the glory of Britain at her greatest.

fes.d: An concrete or abstract entity that possesses characteristics that change over time.

A point or phase in time when, viewed across the actual or expected development, the Entity's powers have reached an extreme high or low point. The point or phase is often identified metonymically by reference to a product created by the Entity or an event involving the Entity.

name: Extreme_value
d: An Entity possesses a Value for a certain Attribute which is extreme when compared to the values either of other entities or to values of the same Entity at other points of time.

ex.t: Airfares hit a 10-year low today. DNI
Today's temperature high was 71F, and the low was 50F. INI
The index hit a post crash high of 2,423.9. DNI

fes.d: The Entity whose Value of a particular gradable Attribute is extreme.
The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.
A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.
The period for which values of a particular Attribute of one or more entities are compared.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The Domain for which there is a Value of an Attribute of an Entity.
A characterization of some property of the Extreme_value.

This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.
The reason for which the Extreme_value event occurs.

name: Facial_expression
d: The words in this frame refer to facial Expressions and the Possessors of those Expressions.

ex.t: His lackluster smile revealed his disappointment.

fes.d: Manner of Expression.
Degree to which the Expression occurs.
This is the Expression made.
This is the person who exhibitis the Expression.

The Expression may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause - the Possessor's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement as in: .
The part of the face saliently exhibiting the Expression.
The emotion that is conveyed by a particular Expression.
An entity toward which the Expression is directed.
The state of affairs perceived by the Possessor which leads to an Internal_cause (emotion, etc.) which then gives rise to the Expression.
The period of time for which the facial Expression is held.

name: Fairness_evaluation
d: In this frame an Action is evaluated with respect to how fairly, justly or equitably the Action affects the Affected_party. An Actor may also be identified, who performs the Action and may be characterized as fair, unfair, etc. based on how these actions affect the Affected_party. Grounds may also be identified.

ex.t: Smithers was being very fair about the distribution of supplies.
Smithers was being very fair about distributing the supplies.
The decision was fair to all involved.

fes.d: The Actor is the individual who performs the Action and can thus be characterized with repsect to how that Action affects the Affected_party.
The Action is judged based on how just and appopriate it is to the Affected_party in a particular situation.
The Grounds is the event or state that requires some decision or action in response to it for which the Actor is judged.
The Affected_party's treatment is what determines the evaluation of the Actor's Action.
The Degree is the extent to which the Action or Actor is evaluated as being fair or unfair.
The Parameter is the area in which the Action is judged.
A holistic characterization of the description of the Actor, including depictions of the Actor's state in terms of how it affects the entire description.

name: Fall_asleep
d: A Sleeper goes from wakefulness to an altered state of consciousness where they are largely unaware of their environment. The LUs of this frame are differentiated by how quickly and deeply the state is entered and what causes the change (especially whether it comes about naturally as a result of sleepiness or is brought about by injury).

ex.t: I dozed off at about 1am.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
The Sleeper is the entity that falls asleep.
This FE identifies the Time where the event occurs.

name: Fall_for
d: A Victim comes to have incorrect beliefs as a result of exposure to a Deception. The Deception is necessarily orchestrated by one or more agents, though these are not expressible by the LUs in this frame.

ex.t: The public was too clever to fall for the type of propaganda prevalent in London at the time.

fes.d: The Victim has false beliefs as a result of exposure to a Deception.

The Deception is perceived by the Victim, leading to false beliefs. The Deception, orchestrated by an agent or agents with the intention of deception, may be any misinformation, event, or situation perceived by the Victim.
The Time when the Victim falls for the Deception.
The Place where the Victim falls for the Deception.
A description of the way Victim is deceived which is not covered by more specific FEs.
The Degree to which the Victim believes the Deception.

name: Fame
d: An Entity is well-known among a wide range of people (in general or in a particular domain) for a particular Reason, which may be a behavior, characteristic, or some other associated item. In the case of events, fame entails a large number of people being aware of the event's occurence; in the case of concrete entities, including humans, fame entails awareness of existence. In both cases, often fame is accompanied by awareness of the Entity's significance in historical, cultural, or social contexts.

ex.t: Shakespeare was famous during his life because he performed in front of Queen Elizabeth I more than anyone else.

fes.d: The Entity which is widely known and recognized.
A modifier expressing the degree of fame of the Entity.
The Time during which the Entity is famous.
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is considered famous.
A state of affairs that provides an explanation (via reasoning, causation, etc.) for the level of fame of the Entity.
The behavior, attribute, or associated entities that provide the reason for the Entity being famous.
The length of time during which the Entity is famous.
The location where the Entity is famous.
The Role underwhich the Entity become famous.
The way in which the Entity becomes famous.

name: Familiarity
d: An Entity is presented as having been seen or experienced by a (typically generic and backgrounded) Cognizer on a certain number of occasions, causing the Entity to have a certain degree of recognizability for the Cognizer.

ex.t: Susanna Fulton's work is new to me.
Two of these frames were new to me as a beginning professor.
This was as new to him as the rest of the outcity.

fes.d: A concrete thing or abstract phenomenon or fact that is assessed in terms of how well recognizable it is to a Cognizer.
The (typically non-specific and backgrounded) sentient being for whom the Entity possesses a specified level of recognizability.
The deviation of the actual level of recognizability of the Entity from the level specified by the target.

This FE identifies the role filled by a particular participant of the clause headed by the target. In so doing, it relates the specification of a level of familiarity to another background state of affairs by indicating that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills a second kind of role in the background, either generically or in some specific instance.
This FE describes the Cognizer as being in some state during the event.
A situation or source from which the Entity is made more recognizanble to the Cognizer.

name: Fastener
d: The Fastener is an artifact created to close a Container (e.g. coat, jar). Sometimes, the Container_portal rather than the Container is expressed.

ex.t: The door seal prevented air from getting in and the kids' screams from getting out.
She has an antique ivory button at the front and another vintage button on her apron.
NIST designed a high pressure seal for the extension sleeve using a series of metal washers to load the window under pressure.

fes.d: This FE identifies the item that is closed with the Fastener.
The artifact created to close a Container.
This FE identifies the active zone of the container where the Fastener is located.
This FE identifes the material from which the Fastener is made.
This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Fastener.
An individual or individuals that bring the Fastener into existence.
The time at which the Fastener comes into existence.
The term used to refer to the Fastener.
An indication of the subtype of the Fastener.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Fastener is made.

name: Fear
d: An Experiencer, Expressor, or State can be described as characterized as having an emotion of fear concerning a particular Topic or as evoked by a Stimulus.

ex.t: I was scared by a bump in the night.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.
The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.
The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.
The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus. Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.
The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, or State can be described as having said emotion.

name: Feeling
d: In this frame an Experiencer experiences an Emotion or is in an Emotional_state. There can also be an Evaluation of the internal experiential state. Inalienably possessed aspects of the Experiencer frequently stand in for the Experiencer.

ex.t: John feels anger towards his mother.
Martha feels angry.
Dr. Hibbert feels good.

fes.d: The Experiencer experiences the Emotion or is in the Emotional_state.
The Emotion is the feeling that the Experiencer experiences.
The Emotional_state is the state the Experiencer is in.
The Evaluation is a negative or positive assessment of the Experiencer regarding his or her Emotional_state.
The thing or state-of-affairs that leads to the Experiencer feeling the Emotion or Emotional_state.

name: Feigning
d: An Agent acts in such a way as to give the incorrect impression to observers that a particular State_of_affairs holds.

ex.t: Jordan feigned a love of jazz music to get her phone number .

fes.d: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that a State_of_affairs holds.
This is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object: Pat falsified the papers.
The Copy produced by the Creator most commonly occurs as the External Argument of a predicative use of an adjective or noun target: The painting is a fake.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.
Degree to which event occurs
The State_of_affairs is a an event, a state, or a property that the Agent wants others to believe have occurred or hold.
An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the feigning of some State_of_affairs.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the feigning event logically follows.
How often the Agent engages in the Feigning event.
The Time when the Agent feigns something.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The amount of time that the Agent feigns something.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs as being in some state during the feigning action.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The place in which the Agent feigns something.

name: Fields
d: An individual or group (Practitioner) or a part of their work life (Work) is defined professionally by the Activity that they typically engage in. Alternatively, the Activity may be indicated by a Salient_entity conventionally associated with it.

ex.t: Chris was in the construction industry for 20 years before coming to GSCM.
My career was in oil and gas.

fes.d: An activity that defines a group of people in their professional capacity.
The individual, group, or organization that engages in the Activity as part of their profession.
A physical or abstract entity that is characteristically associated with the Activity.
A phase of a Practitioner's career that is spent engaged in an Activity.
The subfield of the Activity that the Practitioner is engaged in.
The location where the Practitioner engages in the Activity.
The Time when the Practitioner engages in the Activity.

name: Fighting_activity
d: A generally large group of people, the Combatants, are engaged in a chaotic, violent, and usually protracted Fight amongst themselves. There are no distinct sides, and generally no particular goal (compare Hostile_encounter). The Fight may be described as having a Manner or Degree of violence. Time and Place may also be expressed.

ex.t: The gladiators entered the fray.

fes.d: The Combatants participate as fighters in the Fight.
The violent activity.
When the Fight takes place.
Where the Fight takes place.
The manner of the Fight.
This is the Degree of violence of the Fight.
An activity that engaged in by the Combatants while fighting.
The Issue over which Fight happens.
The amount of time for which the Fight takes place.
The means by which the Combatants engage in the Fight.
The weapon or other instrument used by the Combatants.
The state of affairs that (some of) he Combatants wish to acheive by fighting.

name: Filling
d: These are words relating to filling containers and covering areas with some thing, things or substance, the Theme. The area or container can appear as the direct object with all these verbs, and is designated Goal because it is the goal of motion of the Theme. Corresponding to its nuclear argument status, it is also affected in some crucial way, unlike goals in other frames.

ex.t: Lionel Hutz coated the wall with paint.

fes.d: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.
The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location.
The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion.
The Path is the trajectory of the motion.
The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.
Degree to which the filling occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action.
The Manner in which the filling occurs.
The Means by which the filling occurs.
The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.
The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal.
When the filling occurs.
Where the filling takes place.
The purpose for which the Agent fills the Goal.
The Instrument with which the filling occurs.
The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs.
An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Fining
d: The Payer is (legally) forced to pay a Fine by an official Speaker as a punishment for some action (the Reason). The Speaker represents an entity which receives the payment. Compare to: Citing.

ex.t: They were fined approximately $3.1 billion dollars for their knowing, malicious injury to consumers.

fes.d: The Speaker is the person who imposes the Fine upon the Payer.
The Instrument with which the fining is performed.
The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward.
Where the event takes place.
The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
When the event occurs.
The Payer is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:

A description of the event (or state) not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a for-PP, e.g. I admire you for your intellect. For some words in this domain, the Reason frame element is obligatory. That is to say, the overt expression of this frame element may only be omitted when the reason for the judgment is understood from context. For example, the sentence 'I blame you!' can only be uttered when it is clear what the addressee is being blamed for.
The Result of an event.
The money given to expiate some debt for transgression.
In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods.
This FE is any Unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.
The imposition of a debt due to culpable behavior.
The Degree to which the Fine is punitive to the Payer.

name: Finish_competition
d: A Competition comes to an end, with a Competitor tying, winning, or losing against an Opponent (or opponents) according to their Score. (In the symmetrical situation of a tie, the Competitor and Opponent may be jointly mentioned as Competitors.) According to the Score that the Competitor and Opponent have achieved, they may receive a Rank or a Prize. The Margin may also be mentioned.

ex.t: Unbelievable--he lost the gold medal by just .02 points!
Looks like it will came to a draw between Woods and Stephenson.

fes.d: The individual involved in the Competition.
The individual that the Competitor has been competing against.
The individuals who compete against each other.
A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Competitors afterward.
The amount by which the Competitor 's and Opponent 's Scores differ.
The rank (according to Score) that a Competitor acheives.
A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Competitor according to Score or Rank.
The event in which the Competitors compete with each other.
An action of the Competitor that results in the outcome of the Competition.

Any description of the Competition which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Competitor that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The time at which the Competition takes place.
The location at which the Competition takes place.
This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Finish_game
d: A Player finishes a Game, possibly with an outcome of winning or losing. A Game is an activity that is considered recreational, and is valued for associated pleasure, as well as social interaction, material reward, or status. Not all games can be won or lost. Those that are specifically competitions are defined in the inheriting frame Finish_competition. In some LUs, the Game is DNI.

ex.t: John won the lottery!
John lost.

fes.d: An activity the Player participates in.
The individual participating in a Game.

Any description of the Game which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Player that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action of the Player that results in the outcome of the Game.
The time at which the Game takes place.
The location in which the Player finishes the Game.
The purpose for which the Player wins or loses the Game.
The degree to which the Player wins or loses the Game.

name: Fire_break
d: This frame pertains to Fire_breaks, entities intended to prevent a fire from traveling in a direction. They are constructed by removing combustible/flammable material from the predicted path of the flames.

ex.t: The firefighters created several fire breaks at the outskirts of the wildlife sanctuary to prevent fires from reaching the precious "inner sanctum".

fes.d: The constructed entity that is intended to prevent a fire from reaching a protected area.
An individual or individuals that bring the Fire_break into existence.
Any indication of what makes up the Fire_break, including components, ingredients, etc.
The term used to refer to a Fire_break.
The time at which a Fire_break comes into existence.
An indication of the subtype of Fire_break.
The use for which a Fire_breakis intended.

name: Fire_burning
d: A Fire burns Fuel, resulting in damage and possibly complete destruction of the Fuel.

ex.t: A fire that started on Saturday afternoon, the High Glade Fire - located on the Mendocino National Forest's Upper Lake Ranger District - continued to burn actively on Sunday.
Since the fire is near a road and also on part of the Appalachian Trail, the Forest Service said a main concern is the safety of the public.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire is burning.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire is burning.
The total material currently involved in combustion, including both the parts of the Fuel currently undergoing chemical alteration and the partially ionized gas that results from this process.
The entity that is undergoing rapid chemical alteration leading to damage or destruction.
Any description of the Fire event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Name given to the burning fire.
The amount of time that the Fire burns.
Descriptive phrase describing the fire.
The state or category of the affected entity after the event.
The part of the affected entity that undergoes the process evoked by the target.

name: Fire_emergency_scenario
d: This frame characterizes any scenario in which the presence of a fire necessitates an emergency response in order to mitigate damage directly caused by the fire.

fes.d: The fire which causes an emergency response.
The length of time between the declaration of a Fire as in an emergency state and the conclusion of the emergency.
This FE identifies the Place where the fire emergency scenario occurs.
The individual or group that is responding to a fire emergency with directed action.
Directed action leading to recovery, rescue, or general mitigation of distress due to an ensuing fire emergency.
This FE identifies the Time when the fire emergency scenario occurs.
The Victim(s) affected negatively by the fire emergency event.

name: Fire_end_scenario
d: This scenario begins with a Fire burning, transitions as the Fire goes out, and ends with the Fire dissipated.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire goes out.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.
The combustion process that is coming to an end.
This FE describes the how near the Fire is to going out.

name: Fire_going_out
d: A Fire goes out.

ex.t: The fire is expected to burn out within a week.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing an undergoer of an action during their participation in the event.
This FE identifies the state of the Fire that affects the nature of the event.
This FE identifies the Result of the event.
This FE identifies the Place where the Fire goes out.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.
The combustion process that comes to an end.
This FE describes the how near the Fire is to going out.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Fire_stopping_scenario
d: The Fire_stopping_scenario begins with a Fire in process, transitions with the action of an Agent to end the Fire, and ends with the Fire having stopped burning.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent puts out the Fire.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.
The individual or group that causes the Fire to no longer burn.
The combustion process that the Agent causes to end.
This FE describes the how near the Agent is to putting out the Fire.

name: Firefighting
d: This frame characterizes the situation or state of affairs in which someone acts to prevent a Fire_disaster from occurring, accelerating, or affecting any area not identified as a Controlled_area. The named Burn_area, targeted by the Fire_disaster, is more salient than "fire" itself and is often used for reference instead. The organizational methods for Firefighting are of utmost importance in this frame.

fes.d: The fire that Firefighters target.
The individual or group who respond(s) to the Fire.
The time when the Firefighter fights the Fire.
This FE identifies the location of the Firefighters as they attempt to fight the Fire.
The manner in which the Firefighters are fighting the Fire.

The desired result of the firefight. It may either directly refer to the state of affairs that is desired, e.g. or the state of affairs may be implicit in an (abstract or concrete) entity that is desired by the firefighters, e.g.
An instrument with which an intentional fire-fighting act is performed.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs as being in some state during the firefighting action.

name: Firing
d: An Employer ends an employment relationship with an Employee. There is often a Reason given for the action.

ex.t: He fired me as annotator for being too slow.

fes.d: The person who is let go by their Employer.
The person (or institution) that end an employment relationship with an Employee.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employer fires an Employee.
This FE identifies the Place where the Employer fires the Employee.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer fires the Employee.
The action that the Employee is relieved from doing for the Employer .
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer fires the Employee.
The Explanation for which the Employee is terminated.
The means whereby the Employer fires the Employee

name: Firing_point
d: A location from which a Detonator activates a distantly-located explosive device.

ex.t: Locating the firing point of remote control IEDs is no easy task.
The first task is to determine where he located his firing point.

fes.d: The location from which the Detonator activates an explosive device.
A place that a Firing_point is located with respect to.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Firing_point.
The name of the locale.
The Detonator is located at the Firing_point when he or she activates the explosive device.

name: First_experience
d: An implicit experiencer has an Experience for the first time. Some LU's may specifically imply an agentive activity.

ex.t: In Italy the term was first used by the Venetians in 1546
This time, the comet was first seen on the night of 19th October, 1805 by European observers Jean Louis Pons, Johann Sigismund Huth, and Alexis Bouvard

fes.d: An event happens for the first time within the Context.
A spatial, cultural, or personal delimitation within which the Experience occurs for the first time.

name: First_rank
d: An Item is located at the top end of a scale of importance or social rank (or some other Attribute) in comparison to other members of a Contrast_set (usually, implicit) that is otherwise similar in kind to the Item. Oftentimes, the limits of the Contrast_set are determined by an expression of the Limits_of_consideration.

ex.t: The main problem is that the administration has not yet clarified "Regime change." INI
Oh, he had a great many concerns -- chief among them his own boredom.
Their primary objective in Bosnia was bringing about a lasting peace. INI

fes.d: An Item is the foremost thing in the Contrast_set.
This FE identifies the domain (usually temporally or spatially defined) within which the Item is primary among its kind.
The Contrast_set is a group of entities similar to the Item out of which the Item is the most preeminent.
The Attribute of the Item which is under consideration.

name: Fleeing
d: A Self_mover responds to a (real or imagined) danger by moving away from it.

ex.t: She had fled from DCS facilities several times before..
Pakistanis in US trying to flee to Canada hit roadblocks.
Anderson's division suddenly bolted north from Devil's Den, flanked out III Corps almost entirely, and shattered the entire Corps.

fes.d: Self_mover is the living (or self-directed) being which moves under its own power.
Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion.
Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion involving a landmark which is neither a Source nor a Goal. This includes "middle of path'' expressions.
Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion.

An expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.
The time when the motion occurs.
An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.
The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement.
The state of the world which exists because of the motion of the Self_mover
The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.
The amount of time for which the Self_mover moves.
This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves.
The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place. Any specified or implied Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place.
The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.
External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover to move.
The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.
The entity used by the Self_mover in getting away from the undesirable Source.

name: Fluidic_motion
d: In this frame a Fluid moves from a Source to a Goal along a Path or within an Area.

ex.t: The blood spurted from the wound.
The water gushed into the house .

fes.d: Area is the setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place on an unspecified Path.
This FE describes the phsyical extent of the motion of the Fluid.
The amount of time for which the Fluid moves.
Goal is the location the Fluid ends up.
The Path is the trajectory along which the Fluid moves.
The Source is the location the Fluid occupies initially.
This is the rate at which the Fluid flows.
The Fluid is the entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way.
The Time when the Fluid flows.
The Configuration encodes information about the amount, arrangement, and unitization of the flow. .
The Manner in which the Fluid flows.
The Explanation is the reason for the fluidic motion.
This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Fluid throughout the action.
This FE identifies the result of the Fluid moving.
The Place describes the location of the motion which has a specified Source, Path or Goal.

name: Food
d: This frame contains words referring to items of food.

ex.t: Specialties include deep fried shredded beef , duck , prawn dishes and hand-made noodles.

fes.d: This FE indicates a characteristic or description of the food.
This FE identifies a particular Type of the food item.
A part of the Food.

name: Food_gathering
d: A Gatherer removes Crop ripe and ready to an accepted degree. The Crop comes from a Source where it has been grown and matured.

ex.t: They harvest their pumpkins in the Autumn. INI
We bring in the tobacco from the fields during the summer.
The stage at which the peppercorns are harvested from the vine decides their colour . CNI

fes.d: The Gatherer is the agent gathering the Crop.
Crop is item being collected together by the Gatherer.
For what length of time the Gatherer was gathering the Crop.
The Manner in which the Gatherer gathers the Crop.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Crop is gathered.
The greater geographic location where the Gatherer gathers his Crop.
When the Crop gathering action occurs.
An action that the Gatherer intends to accomplish by gathering his Crop.
How often the Gatherer collects his Crop.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
The Source is the ground where the Crop is gathered from.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
This FE describes the amount of effort put into the food gathering event.
The person on who's behalf the Gatherer gathers the Crop.

name: Foreign_or_domestic_country
d: A Current_country is identified as matching or not matching the instance of the Discourse_salient_country.

ex.t: Foreign sales account for only 20% of IBM's income .

fes.d: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up the Current_country.
The location that the Current_country is a part of.
The country or countries that the speaker is indicating in the current instance, which may match or be distinct from the Discourse_salient_country.
ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales.
A place that the Current_country is located with respect to.
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Current_country which is not covered by more specific FEs.
The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.

The country that has been featured in the discourse, or that the speaker/hearer identify with or are located in; it serves to identify the Current_country by specifying it as the same or different. This FE is incorporated in the targets of this frame.

name: Forging
d: An Agent produces a Forgery, an entity that they intend to pass off as a particular (instance of) a Standard. An instance of the Standard may actually exist that served as an original that is copied by the Agent, or the Standard exists only as an idea.

ex.t: So who was it that faked the photo "showing" Jane Fonda and John Kerry with the Vietcong?

fes.d: The Agent is the person that creates a Forgery with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.
The Forgery is the product that the Agent creates with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the forging event logically follows.
An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by producing the Forgery.
The Standard is the actually existing or imagined (kind of) thing that the Agent wants to pass the Forgery off as.
An entity manipulated by the Agent in order to produce the Forgery.
The location in which the Agent makes a Forgery.
The time at which the forgery takes place.
The way in which the Forgery does or does not match the Standard.
An entity corresponding to the Standard which the Agent scrutinizes in order to copy.

name: Forgiveness
d: A Judge refrains from imposing, or demanding a punishment for an Evaluee who has committed an Offense.

ex.t: God forgives repentant sinners.
Won't you forgive me for keeping it a secret?

fes.d: The Judge holds the Evaluee responsible for the Offense.
The Evaluee is subject to the judgment of the Judge for having committed the Offense.
The Offense is the illicit or unpleasant act committed by the Evaluee.

name: Forgoing
d: AForgoer decides not to partake in something ordinary that is otherwise Desirable.

ex.t: Chuck often skips lunch.

fes.d: The Forgoer decides not to partake in the desirable activity or event.
Desirable identifies the event or activity in which is the Forgoer does not partake.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Manner the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Place where the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Time at which the the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Explanation for which the forgoing occurs.
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Forgoer does not partake in the Desirable.

name: Forming_relationships
d: Partner_1 interacts with Partner_2 (also collectively expressible as Partners) to change their social relationship.

ex.t: I befriended the little pony by giving him a piece of apple.

fes.d: The individual who comes to form a relationship with Partner_2.
The individual whose relationship with Partner_1 changes.
The individuals whose relationship is changing.
The action that Partner_1 or the Partners take in order to bring about the change in the relationship.
The time when the relationship changes.

Any description of the event including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Partner_1 or Partners that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
A salient state of Partner_1, Partner_2, or Partners which affects the perception of the formation of relationship.
The length of time that the changed relationship status lasts.
Where the relationship is formed.
The state-of-affairs that the Partners or Partner_1 hope to bring about by changing their status.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Forming_relationship event operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
How often the Forming_relationship event occurs.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Fragmentation_scenario
d: A Whole fragments or breaks into Parts, or alternatively a part, Part_1, breaks off from the rest of the item, called Part_2.

ex.t: Last year, it broke off from the Ross Ice Shelf and began drifting out to sea.
The calved ice broke into three large icebergs, named A22, A23 and A24.

fes.d: The Whole is a single entity which breaks into Parts.
This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from fragmentation of a Whole.
Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the external argument of a verb.
Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement.
This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing any of the undergoers of the fragmentation.
Manner of performing an action
Degree to which event occurs
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
This FE identifies the Time when the fragmenting occurs.
Where the breaking occurs.
The hard surface against which the Whole (or Part_1) breaks.
An action or state that enables the fragmentation.

name: Freeing_from_confinement
d: An Agent causes a Theme which was held captive to be free from a Location_of_confinement, against the wishes of the captors.

ex.t: Two men disguised as guards sprung a convicted killer from prison last night.

fes.d: The Agent causes the confinement or captivity of the Theme to end, against the intentions of the captor.
The Theme is the person or object which is released by the Agent.

Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The action of the Agent which brings about the release.
The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Agent sets the Theme free.
The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Agent releases the Theme.
The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.
The Time identifies when the Agent frees the Theme .
The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The state of the world when the event of setting free occurs.

name: Frequency
d: This frame has to do with the repetition (and especially the frequency of repetition) of an event. Many of the adjectives and adverbs in this frame are based on nouns in the Calendric_unit frame.

ex.t: China will have to face a high frequency of sand storms in the years to come.

fes.d: This FE is used for any (bounded) Event whose frequency or iteration is described.
The extent to which the actually observed rate of occurrence of the Event or Salient_entity differs from the expected rate.
The Interval is a noun modified by the target word. The target word specifies the frequency of the Interval .
The Time_span is the length of time of the Interval. This FE is incorporated by most of the lexical units in this frame.
The number of times per unit of real or scanning time that an Event or Salient_entity is encountered.
An entity which the implicit cognizer encounters with the specified frequency.
The frequency feature of the Event or Salient_entity that is under discussion. All the lexical units in this frame incorporate this frame element.
The Time when the Event has a particular frequency.
The Group in which the Event or Salient_entity is frequent.

name: Friction
d: A Theme moves on or against the surface of a Static_object. (Alternatively, Themes moves against each other simultaneously). The Theme exerts pressure on the surface and experiences resistance to its movement.

ex.t: Smithers' boots scraped on the floor.

fes.d: The physical entity which moves over the suface of the Static_object .
A non-moving physical object over a surface of which the Theme moves.
Two moving entities whose surfaces move against each other.
The way in which the Theme moves against the Static_object
The setting in which the motion of the Theme happens
The amount of friction produced in the Theme's motion.

name: Friendly_or_hostile
d: Two parties or individuals are on the same side or on different sides of a (typically military) conflict. The two sides may be expressed jointly as the Sides, or separately as Side_1 and Side_2. In many cases only Side_1 is mentioned, leaving Side_2 as the perspective from whom the description is being given (typically the speaker/writer).

ex.t: We received a tip from a friendly local about a possible attack. DNI
Infiltration from hostile forces is a constant threat. DNI

fes.d: Side_1 is the party or individual in a relationship with Side_2. Side_1 is the primary protagonist of the frame, and is denoted by noun and adjective targets.
The party or individual with whom Side_1 bears an adversarial or friendly relationship.
The Degree to which the relationship holds.
The time period during which the Sides have the indicated relationship with each other.
The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Sides having the relationship indicated logically follows.
This FE indicates a property of Side_1 or the Sides.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The location where the two Sides have an adversarial relationship.
A joint expression of the two Sides with a friendly or hostile stance towards one another.

name: Front_for
d: An individual or organization, the Front, serves as a cover for an Illicit_activity or an Illicit_organization.

ex.t: The laundromat is a front for the Yakuza.

fes.d: The Front acts as a legitimate individual, organization, or enterprise, but is truly a cover for an illicit organization or activity.
The existence and activities of the Illicit_organization are concealed by the Front.
The Illicit_activity of the Illicit_organization is concealed by (the activities of) the Front .
The time at which the deceptive activity occurs
The state-of-affairs that the Front is attempting to bring about.
The place where the fronting occurs.
The action taken by the Front to ensure successful deceit of authorities.
Any description of the similarity of the event to some other event, particularly descriptions of the Front that also affect the details of the action.

name: Frugality
d: The words of this frame describe how a Resource_controller spends money or other Resources for a particular purpose . They can be applied to the Resource_controller or to their Behavior in particular instances. These words indicate a judgment of how conservatively the Resource_controller guards their Resource.

ex.t: Margeret has always been penny-wise.
Bill squanders his money.
To spend the surplus now would be needlessly profligate .

fes.d: The Resource_controller is the individual whose frugality or generosity is being described. Person typically occurs as the External Argument or, in some cases when Behavior is also expressed, in an of-PP:
Some specific Behavior may be described as frugal or extravagant, rather than attributing the characteristic directly to the Resource_controller.
This FE is the resource which the Resource_controller expends.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a Resource_controller is frugal or profligate.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Fugitive
d: A Fugitive avoids recapture by or on the authority of Authorities in relation to a Crime which the Fugitive has committed or is suspected of having committed.

ex.t: He is in fact a fugitive of the law and you must inform the police if you see him.
Only two years earlier she had been on the lam from charges of embezzlement.

fes.d: The Fugitive has escaped and/or is evading capture by law enforcement Authorities.
The facility where the Fugitive was being held.
The Authorities want to take (or retake) the Fugitive into custody on suspicion of having committed a Crime.
The crime of which the Fugitive is wanted. This FE also covers expressions that indicate suspicion of crimes, convictions, and sentences.
This FE identifies the general Place where the Fugitive is located.
The Time when the Fugitive is evading law enforcement.

Any description of the state of being imprisoned which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The reason for which the Fugitive is avoiding capture.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Fugitive is on the run.

name: Fullness
d: A Container is in a state of fullness/emptiness with respect to some Contents. Note the connection between words in this frame and those in the Containers, Emptying, and Filling frames.

ex.t: John carried a bucket full of water.

fes.d: Container is used for the entity whose fullness is being described.
Contents is used for the stuff that is present/absent in the Container.
The extent to which the amount of Contents in the Container diverges from the maximal expected amount for the Container.
The Time when the Container is full.
The amount of times the Container is empty per unit of time.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Container's fullness to the end.

name: Function
d: An Entity is designed for or exists to perform an Activity or fulfill a Role.

ex.t: This platform will serve as a great stage for tomorrow's play.
The ropes serve to tie things together.

fes.d: The Entity is an object or person that performs the Activity or fulfills the Role.
The Activity is the action that the Entity performs.
The Role is the position or duty that is occupied by the Entity.
The Descriptor provides additional information about the Entity .
The Duration that the Entity performs an Activity or fulfills a Role.
The Manner in which the Entity functions.
The Means by which an Entity functions.

name: Funding
d: A Supplier gives funds to a Recipient to fulfill a need or purpose (Imposed_purpose) of the Recipient. Often, the Imposed_purpose appears as a direct object of the target verb instead of the Recipient. With these, the Imposed_purpose can either be metonymically linked to some Recipient, in which case the Recipient FE is marked as DNI: or it can explicitly encompass the Recipient, in which case the Recipient part is annotated on a second FE layer: . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . the senator's

ex.t: The University funded Paige so that she could complete her doctorate.
Investors financed the software start-up.DNI
Lobbyists backed the senator's campaign for president.

fes.d: Supplier is the person or entity that funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.
Recipient is the person, people, or organization funded by the Supplier.
Imposed_purpose is the intended purpose of the funding.
The Circumstances are the conditions under which the funding is supplied.
This FE is the Explanation for which the Supplier gives funding to the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.

Any description of the funding event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Supplier that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
This FE expresses the Means by which the Supplier funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.
This FE designates the period over which the Supplier engages in (multiple) funding acts.
The Place where the Supplier funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.
The Source of the funding.
The Time at which the Supplier gives funds to the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.
Money is the specified currency or amount of funding.
The Purpose for which the Supplier funds the Recipient.

name: Gathering_up
d: This frame describes an Agent's gathering of Individuals (people or entities) into a group, the Aggregate, defined by relative proximity. Compare this frame with Congregating, and contrast it with Amalgamating.

ex.t: The police gathered the suspects into a line-up.

fes.d: This FE identifies the aggregate that results from the gathering. It may be expressed either as an adjunct result phrase or as a direct object of a target verb.
Agent is the person who gathers Individuals.
This FE identifies the time when the gathering event occurs, if specified. The crowd assembled at dawn.
An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the gathering.
This FE identifies the place where the gathering event occurs. He assembled the children in the hall.
This FE identifies the entities that come together to form an Aggregate.
The way in which the Individuals are gathered up.
An Instrument that the Agent uses to gather the Individuals together.
The state of affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by gathering.
This frame element is defined as the number of times the Gathering_up event occurs per some unit of time.
This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the Gathering_up event occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
Goal designates the location where the Individuals might end up.
The Co-participant participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist.
The Path is the trajectory of motion that the Individuals take.
The Source is the location where the Individuals are at the beginning of the gathering event.

name: Gesture
d: The words in this frame have to do with non-verbal communication. Topic is not normally expressed with these words. This seems to be related to the absence of a verbal code in cases of gestural communication. Topic can be viewed as a partial characterization of a Message, but such partial characterization is either difficult or irrelevant in the absence of a verbal code.

ex.t: I gestured with my hand for him to come over.

fes.d: This is the sentient entity that communicates a Message non-verbally. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: The teacher gestured us into the room.

This is the person to whom a non-verbal Message is communicated. It may be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement: The teacher gestured us into the room. The teacher gestured to us to enter the room.

This is the content of non-verbal communication. It may be expressed as a that-clause Complement, a to-marked infinitive VP Complement, or a directional PP Complement: The teacher gestured that it was time to leave. The teacher gestured to us to enter the room. The teacher gestured us into the room.
Manner of performing an action
An act performed by the Communicator that results in the successful transfer of a Message.
The Body_part is the specific body part of the Communicator which gestures.
When the gesturing occus.
The Place is where the gesturing occurs.
The Indicated_entity is the entity which the Communicator is pointing out to the Addressee as meaningful.
An Instrument that the Communicator uses to gesture to the Addressee together.

name: Get_a_job
d: A new Employee obtains a Position with an Employer, with which there are certain Tasks associated; in exchange for the performance of these Tasks, the Employee receives Compensation from the Employer.

ex.t: I signed on with YouTube to make them a new GUI.

fes.d: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
The person who enters an employment relation with an Employer.
The person (or institution) that the Employee enters an employment relationship with.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee enters an employment relationship with an Employer.
This FE identifies the place where the Employee enteres an employment relationship with an Employer.
The label given to a particular type of employment.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employee enters an employment relationship.
The action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
This FE identifies the Time when an Employee signs on with an Employer.
The action by which the Employee enters an employment relationship.
The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.

name: Getting
d: A Recipient starts off without the Theme in their possession, and then comes to possess it. Although the Source from which the Theme came is logically necessary, the Recipient and its changing relationship to the Theme is profiled.

ex.t: I got two whistles from John.

fes.d: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The Theme is the object that changes possession.
The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.
The Place denotes where the Getting takes place.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Explanation refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.
When the event occurs.
The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Theme.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.
The state that either the Recipient or the Theme end up in after the acquisition.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The Beneficiary is an entity which the Recipient passes the Theme to, or shares the Theme with.
Any condition or situation that serves as a very general background, against which the further importance of the Getting is understood.

name: Getting_scenario
d: In this scenario, the Recipient begins without the Theme, then acquires the Theme from a Source.

fes.d: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The Theme is the object that changes possession.
The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The Explanation refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

name: Getting_triggered
d: A System interacts with the environment (which may include a volitional agent) and goes into operation in accordance with its intended purpose.

ex.t: The alarm went off as she walked through the entrance.
The bomb must have triggered accidentally.

fes.d: The System interacts with the environment and activates.
Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the System (quietly).
Where the System goes off.
The time when the System triggers.
The number of times the triggerent event occurs in a particular time period.

name: Getting_underway
d: A Self_mover begins the motion away from a relatively deprofiled Source location. The focus is on the motion rather than on the location that is being departed. The label Self_mover here also includes vehicles that are steered by an intentional agent.

ex.t: After a lunch of sandwiches on paper plates, we get under way.
When I got going for the day I had horrible pain down my buttocks and leg.
We got going via Tikul and after a light lunch finally found the pottery place recommended in the guide,

fes.d: The Self_mover is the volitional agent that moves.
Source refers to the starting-point of the Self_mover's motion.
Path is any description of the Self_mover's trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.
Goal is any expression that tells where the Self_mover ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.

A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Self_mover begins the motion.
This FE identifies the Time when the Self_mover begins the motion away from the Source.
The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Self_mover when she begins the motion away from the Source.
The length of time of the Self_mover's absence from the Source.
The Mode_of_transportation is the transportation device that a human Self_mover uses to travel.
The journey is the trip or expedition on which the Self_mover embarks.
The Direction in which the Self_mover begins to move.

name: Getting_up
d: A Protagonist leaves the place where they have slept, their Bed, to begin or resume domestic, professional, or other activities. Getting up is distinct from Waking up, which is concerned only with the transition from the sleeping state to a wakeful state.

ex.t: I rose from bed, threw on a pair of camouflage shorts and drove my little Toyota Corolla to a construction clearing a few miles away.
One recent Monday, for example, Joe rose from bed extra early to catch an administrator at 8:30 am.
In the summer I get up early and get some miles in on my bike before the kids and Ange wake up. INI

fes.d: The person or animal that has slept in a particular place and now leaves it to engage in other activities.
The place where the Protagonist has slept.
The time when the Protagonist leaves their place of sleeping.
The Purpose for which the Protagonist gets out of Bed.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that affect the action (eagerly, carefully).
The New_situation is the situation the Protagonist finds him or herself in upon getting up from Bed.
The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the getting up event takes place.
A state of affairs that the Protagonist is responding to in getting up.
The length of the interval for which the Protagonist is not in Bed after getting up.
The location in which the Protagonist's Bed is situated.

name: Getting_vehicle_underway
d: A Driver prepares a Vehicle for travel by placing it in the normal location for the operation of the vehicle or by detaching it from a place where it was held.

ex.t: Throughout Irish history, countless generations of exiles have cast off from the shores of Ireland.
"Good," said Matt as he pulled the car out of the parking space.
The next day, after weighing anchor, we cleared Longboat Pass Bridge, and exited the ICW into the open waters of the Gulf of Mexico.

fes.d: This is the being, typically human, that prepares the Vehicle for motion, and will control it once it is in motion.
The device--such as a car, boat, spaceship,. etc.--which is used for transport and is prepared for travel by the Driver.
Any expression which describes the location that the Vehicle has been stationed at.
The location that the Vehicle is intended to travel to.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Driver that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The state of the Driver or Vehicle during the preparations.
The action performed by the Driver by which they prepare the Vehicle for travel.
Result of the Driver's action.
An individual or vehicle that is also involved in the preparations.
This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the preparation of the Vehicle takes place.
The Place describes the location where the Driver prepares the Vehicle for motion.
The length of the time that the Vehicle remains in the state of readiness.
