Any description of the vehicle operation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Operator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action which enables the Operator to operate the Vehicle, or which more directly causes the Vehicle to operate.

name: Operating_a_system
d: An Operator manipulates the substructure of a System such that the System performs the function it was created for. This frame differs from the Using frame in that this frame does not profile the purpose of an agent but rather their manipulation of an entity (System/Instrument). In the case of using, the Agent need not manipulate the Instrument at all, as in: Mrs. Adams used the room as a place to hang the family laundry to dry.

ex.t: This true story of domestic bliss was related to me by a friend of mine who for a time operated a bar in San Francisco.
A California man has plead guilty to federal charges that he ran a pyramid scam which defrauded nearly 7000 investors.

fes.d: The entity that the Operator gets to perform its intended function.
The invididual who manipulates the substructure of the System.
This FE identifies the place where the Operator runs the System.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Operator runs the System.
This FE identifies the time when the Operator runs the System.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Operator runs the System.

Any description of the running of the System which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Operator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Duration denotes the length of the time interval in which the Operator runs the System.

name: Operational_testing
d: A Tester uses a concrete or conceptual Product in order to determine either whether it works or to find out how well or in which manner it works. The Tester may have particular Unwanted_characteristics in mind that they are specifically looking for. The operational test may also be carried out under a particular set of Circumstances that are typically relevant to the functioning of the Product.

ex.t: Sun has (hopefully) already tested it for compliance.
The Velcro hook and loop closure system has been tested under wet conditions and retains its holding power after 10,000 open and close functions. CNI INI
Roe revisited the compound and tested it as a mosquito repellent.

fes.d: The person who uses the Product to see if it is intact or to ascertain its characteristics during operation.
The entity that the Tester uses to ascertain whether it is intact.
An entity or property whose presence would impair the acceptability or usefulness of the Product.
This FE is used for a Means action which the Tester carries out in testing the Product.
An action that the Tester intends to accomplish subjecting the Product to a test of its functioning.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Tester uses the Product in order to evaluate its functioning.
This FE identifies the extent to which the Tester examines the Product.
This FE is the position of the Tester during the act of testing. Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP.
The desirable state of affairs which the Tester hopes to find to obtain when using the Product.
The Time when the Tester uses the Product to evaluate its functioning.
The FE Circumstances is used for circumstances that obtain during the test procedure. These are typically relevant to how the Product functions.
The length of the time period during which the Tester continuously or repeatedly operates the Product to determine its operational characteristics.
The location in which the test is carried out.
A use to which the Product is put .
A variable of behavior of the Product which is specifically evaluated.
The length of time from when the testing event began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The Result of the Operational_testing.

name: Opinion
d: A Cognizer holds a particular Opinion, which may be portrayed as being about a particular Topic.

ex.t: John thinks that it looks better back .
Well, my opinion about that is none of your business.
What 's your take on the recent oil crisis ?

fes.d: The Cognizer is the person whose Opinion is in question.
The Cognizer's way of thinking, which is not necessarily generally accepted, and which is generally dependent on the Cognizer's point of view.
The events or states-of-affairs that form the basis for the Cognizer's Opinion.
A phenomenon that the Cognizer is considering with respect to their Opinion. Note that this extra-thematic frame element occurs freely with nouns, but only in very restricted contexts with verbs.
The level of firmness with which the Cognizer holds an opinion. It refers to the amount of convincing that they would need to change their mind.

Any description of how the Cognizer holds an opinion which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quiet(ly)), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect their thinking (presumptuous(ly), cold(ly)).
Role describes the presuppositional terms of the Opinion by placing the Topic or the Cognizer of the Opinion into a category.
The aspects of the Opinion (and its Topic, if any) which are under consideration.
The Time at which the Cognizer has the Opinion.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Opportunity
d: An Agent has a choice of whether or not to participate in some Desirable_event because of an Opportunity, a situation not completely under the Agent's control and usually of a limited duration.

ex.t: It would be pleasant in the opportune absence of the clergyman to have a dance . DNI
Her opportunities to apply to a good school are then limited .
Now was their big chance ! DNI

fes.d: The situation during which the Desirable_situation is possible. For nominal LUs, this is generally in the second layer and contains the target.
The sentient agent that may or may not participate in the Desirable_situation.
A situation or event that the Agent can participating in during the period of the Opportunity.

name: Optical_image
d: This frame describes non-artifact Images resulting from an interation between light and some kind of matter, usually a Source entity.

ex.t: I could see John's silhouette in the corner as I entered the dimly lit room.

fes.d: The optical representation of the Source.
The entity from which the Image's form is based on.

name: Ordinal_numbers
d: An Item is picked out either by the order in which the members of a set would be encountered by an implicit cognizer, or by the order in which the members of a set participate in an event or state which serves as the Basis_of_order. The former case usually involves a Starting_point for going through the set, while the latter involves a Basis_of_order, which is normally an event that the Item along with other members of its Comparison_set has participated in. Note that Item should be annotated on a second layer, except in cases when the noun structure the ordinal participates in is predicative.

ex.t: The first car from the left is a Magosix.
The first car from the left is a Magosix.
Barney was only the second Asian student at my college.

fes.d: The kind of entity that the Item belongs to.
A usually spatial reference point from which the implicit cognizer scans across the members of the Comparison_set.
A kind of event in which the members of the Comparison_set, including the Item, participate in a certain order.
The entity picked out by the implicit cognizer as occupying a certain place in the ordered Comparison_set.
A set of entites of which the Item is a member and which are ordered either by the Basis_of_order or by the order in which the implicit cognizer focuses attention on them.

name: Organization
d: This frame describes intentionally formed human social groups (here termed Organizations) with some definite structure and Members. They may be relatively informal, consisting only of a group of individuals who are aware of who is and who is not a fellow member, or they may be complex and long-lasting, such as the Roman Catholic Church or the Conservative Party.

ex.t: Lucien is in the brotherhood.

fes.d: The entity of which the individuals are Members.
A person belonging to an Organization.
The reason for which an Organization is formed.
The interval during which the Organization exists.
A name given to the Organization for identification.
The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.
This FE describes the general location where the Organization operates, but does not indicate the possessor of the Organization.
Any description of the Organization not covered by a more specific frame element.

name: Origin
d: An Entity began its existence in the context of a Origin, which can be a place, culture, time period, text, etc.

ex.t: The Christian origin of this quote is from Isaiah 22.
Dinosaurs originated from Antarctica?

fes.d: The item whose Origin is under discussion.
The place or culture where the Entity was produced.

name: Others_situation_as_stimulus
d: An Experiencer feels an emotion as evoked as an Other.

ex.t: One might pity the frail old man in East Berlin.
She appealed for compassion for sufferers.
I feel for women who also long to have children but can't.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
The Other is the person that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.
The Explanation is the explanation for why the Other evokes a certain emotional response.
The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Other evokes its response.
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the feelings of the Other.

Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the feelings of the Other which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.
The Time when the Experiencer feels for the Other.
The Situation is the circumstances or topic about which the Experiencer feels an emotion.
How often the Other gets sympathy from the Experiencer.

name: Out_of_existence
d: An Entity has ceased to exist.

ex.t: Theses termites are history.
Hillary is toast after Texas and Ohio.
They are gone because you killed them all.

fes.d: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.
This is the Place where the Entity (saliently) does not exist.
A point at which the Entity (saliently) does not exist.
This FE labels the Explanation of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.
This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.
The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.
The way in which the Entity disappears.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Pardon
d: An Authority excuses an Offense that an Offender has committed, with the effect of ending or preventing any punishment.

ex.t: President Ford pardoned her after it came to light she was being held in Japan as an "enemy alien" and was secretly working to subvert the broadcasts DNI
President John Quincy Adams granted them a pardon and remission of the fine. DNI

fes.d: This FE denotes the offender that seeks or gets the pardon.
Authority is the organization or person taht grants the pardon.
This FE denotes the the illegal act that the Offender is pardoned for.
Explanation is the cause for pardoning an Offender.
This FE denotes the time when the pardon is given
An intentional action performed by the Authority that accomplishes the pardon.

Any description of the act of pardon which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Authority that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location at which the pardoning takes place.
An action that the Authority intends to accomplish by pardoning

name: Part_edge
d: This describes a part_whole relationship where the Part provides the boundary between the Whole and what is not that object. The Part can exist along a continuum of width. It can be modified by an Orientation that specifies the particular portion of the edge of a Part_prop which describes a property of the Part.

ex.t: We came to the southern edge  of the town  .

fes.d: This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.
An undivided entity having all its Parts.
A property relating to the Part of a Whole.
Part is that which forms a boundary between the Whole and what is not the object.

name: Part_inner_outer
d: This frame concerns Parts of objects that are defined relative to the center or edge of the object. The Part is a part of the Whole and the Part_prop describes a property of the Part. In cases where the Target is an adjective, it has a special relationship with the noun that it modifies such that a phrase which is a syntactic argument of the noun is semantically available to fill the argument structure of the adjective, as in "the outside row of the class"

ex.t: She discarded the exterior of the walnut.
She preferred a sparse church interior .
The inner shelf of the bookcase was lying on the floor.

fes.d: This element describes the Part of the larger Whole.
An undivided entity having all its Parts.
A property relating to the Part of a Whole.

name: Part_ordered_segments
d: In this frame a Part is part of a larger Whole comprised of parts that are ordered. The Parts can be ordered temporally (first to last and vice versa) or vertically (down to up and vice versa). The Part can be modified by the Part_prop or the number of the part can be given by Ordinality.

ex.t: I sat through the first interminable act  of the play  .
Tess finished a  dissertation chapter .
The first level of rock consisted of sediment from the Neolithic period.

fes.d: This is the number of the sequence of Parts.
A property relating to the Part of a Whole.
A part of a larger Whole.
An undivided entity having all its Parts.

name: Part_orientational
d: In this frame, there is a Part of a Whole in which the Part is defined with respect to the canonical or inherent orientation of the Whole. In cases where the Target is an adjective, it has a special relationship with the noun that it modifies such that a phrase which is a syntactic argument of the noun is semantically available to fill the argument structure of the adjective, as in

ex.t: the front row of the class
The top shelf of the bookcase was lying on the floor.
The bottom was missing.

fes.d: A piece of a larger Whole.
A property relating to the Part of a Whole.
An undivided entity having all its Parts.

name: Part_piece
d: This frame is concerned with transparent nouns denoting a Piece of a Substance. Also present is Piece_prop which is a property of the Piece, e.g. relating to its size. .

ex.t: Kim ate a tiny morsel of cake

fes.d: A Piece made of a substance. The specific whole entity from which the Piece comes is not specified. Thus, the following sentence is not in frame: A piece of the TV fell of the floor.
A property relating to the Piece.
The Substance is what the Piece is made of and may describe the type of larger whole from which it came.

name: Part_whole
d: This frame is concerned with nouns denoting a part or parts of a Whole entity . The Part is not defined relative to the Whole's orientation, center, or edge and is not ordered. We also annotate properties of the Part, e.g. relating to its size.

ex.t: Kim forgot a large part of the story.
Abby ate only the top half of the cake.

fes.d: A Part of a larger Whole.
An undivided entity having all its Parts.
A property relating to the Part of a Whole.
This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.
A system of organization of the Parts within the Whole, of which a Part is identified with a Name .
A label applied to a Part of a Whole in order to identify the Part within some System.

name: Partiality
d: This frame has to do with the bias or lack of bias of a Judge making an assessment concerning two or more Sides. The Sides may stand opposed to each other in a dispute or be alternatives in a situation of choice. The Domain in which the Judge is partial or impartial may be expressed as well as the Degree of bias or lack thereof. In sentences in this frame one may also find expressions of Manifestation_of_bias, i.e. expressions that tell us how the Judge's bias is realized.

ex.t: The judge made a biased decision.

fes.d: This Frame Element marks the person whose objectivity in making assesment is being evaluated.
This Frame Element marks one of the Sides in a dispute or one of the alternatives in a situation of choice.
This Frame Element marks phrases jointly expressing both Sides in a dispute or all of the alternatives in a situation of choice.
The second-mentioned of the Sides to a dispute or alternatives in a situation of choice.
This Frame Element marks expressions of a Domain or parameter with respect to which the Judge exhibits bias or lack thereof.
This Frame Element marks expressions that tell to what extent the Judge exhibited or lacked bias.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how the bias of the Judge expresses itself in their behavior or actions.
The Dispute is the situation in which there is some conflict between two sides.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.
The reason for the partiality.
This FE denotes the time when the partiality occurs.
The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Decision_maker.
The Manner is the way in which the Decision_maker embodies the bias associated with him or her.

name: Participation
d: An Event with multiple Participants takes place. It can be presented either symmetrically with Participants or asymmetrically, giving Participant_1 greater prominence over Participant_2. If the Event is engaged in intentionally, then there is typically a shared Purpose between the Participants. It is, however, possible that an expressed Purpose only applies to Participant_1.

ex.t: MATAC looks forward to your participation in helping promote telework in the Mid-Atlantic region.
FOAP provides participants with comprehensive clerical skills. DNI
FOAP provides participants with comprehensive clerical skills.

fes.d: The individuals or entities that have been participants in an Event.
Participant_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in an Event with multiple Participants.
A grammatically less prominent participant of an Event with multiple Participants.
An Event with multiple Participants, who may or may not be involved intentionally.
The Time when the multiple-participant Event occurs.
The location where the Event involving multiple Participants occurs.

Any description of the Event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). When the Participants are understood agentively frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of them that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
An action that the Participants or Participant_1 intend to accomplish by performing the action indicated by the Event.
An intentional action performed by Participant_1 or the Participants that contributes to bringing off the Event.
The extent to which Participant_1 contributes to the Event's coming off.
A group, location, or institution conventionally associated with an Event.
This FE describes the length of time for which participation occurs (usually appears as a for-PP)

name: Partitive
d: A Subset is profiled against the Group it belongs to. The Subset may consist of a single member. Frequently, the Group is actually a generic sample of a full population, and the Subset is representative of the relative proportion.

ex.t: Of all scenes that evoke rural England, this is one of the loveliest.
As of 5:30 p.m. Moscow time, 23 out of 46 miners stranded in the Zapadnaya-Kapitalnaya mine have been rescued
1.5 out of 10 respondents preferred Shrub over Ferry

fes.d: A Subset belonging to the Group.
The Group of entities which includes the Subset.

name: Passing
d: An Agent physically transfers a Theme to a Recipient. The Agent is not under control of the Theme's motion after the initial input of energy. Compare with Bringing and Sending. In the former, the Carrier is in constant control (even physical contact) with the Theme. In the latter, the Sender plans the motion of the Theme and places it in circumstances such that it travels along the specified path (or to the specified goal), but under the power of a separate individual.

ex.t: Pat passed me the ball.

fes.d: The Agent is the one who passes the Theme. The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.
The FE Theme is generally an NP Object that is passed to the Recipient.
The FE Source is the starting point of the passing action
The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
The FE Recipient is the entity which possesses the Theme as a result of the passing.
The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.

The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which passing takes place when the passing is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.
The state of a participant during the passing action.
The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.
An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme. It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.
The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).
The time at which the passing of the Theme occurs.
A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Passing_off
d: An Agent acts in such a way as to cause others to think that an Item is an instance of a particular kind of Simulated_entity.

ex.t: He had, under the name of Armitage, passed her off as a member of one of the most distinguished families of the capital.
He undoubtedly believes you are the impostor who palmed himself off at Bar Harbor as the Baron von Kissel.
Knowing his likeness to the family of Lord Polperro she palmed him off on them as a distant relative.

fes.d: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.

Any description of the passing off event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the Item being perceived as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.
The Item is the concrete or abstract entity that the Agent misleadingly represents as a particular (kind of) Entity.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by passing the Item off as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the passing-off event logically follows.
The Simulated_entity is a particular individual or a token of a particular type that the Item is represented as.
The Place is the location that is the setting for the passing off event.
The Audience denotes the people that the Agent intends to mislead into thinking that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
The time at which the Agent gives the impression that the Item is the Simulated_entity.

name: Path_shape
d: The words in this frame describe the "fictive" motion of a stationary Road. Some of the targets cast the scene primarily in terms of the Path_shape: Some of the words in this frame imply a Source or Goal which is expressed by a direct object: Other members of the frame refer to a Direction: Yet others indicate a Path which requires mention of a landmark:

ex.t: The long mountain road meandered through the woods.
The path entered the garden on the west side.
Then the path bears a little to the right.

fes.d: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the Road. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
The trajectory that would be followed by one moving on the Road.
Any expression which tells where the fictive mover travelling along a Road would end up.
A physical path that a virtual moving entity can be imagined to travel along. The bike trail zigzagged through the woods.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of the kind of motion a hypothetical mover would have (including steadiness, grace, and general comparisons) count as Manner expressions.
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.

This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.
Extent to which the described configuration deviates from the norm for a Road.
An state of affairs involving the Road that allows the Road to be in the specified configuration.
Result of an event
The Speed is the rate at which an imaginary traveler on the Road would move.
Depictive phrase describing the character of the Road.
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
The configuration formed by the entire Path along the Road.
The direction in which a "fictive" mover would travel along a Road.

The time when the fictive motion takes place. This may describe the time when the Road or a particular piece of the Road existed, or it may implicitly describe the time when an actual motion event occurred on the Road.
The state-of-affairs that the Road brings about by being in a particular configuration.

name: Path_traveled
d: A Path, a series of connected locations, is traversed by a Theme, moving under its own power or under the influence of a physical force. The Path may be described in various terms depending on whether it is bounded or not. If it is bounded, the Path may be identified by its Endpoints, which may be presented separately as Source and Goal.

ex.t: For Earth, these perturbations slowly change the eccentricity of the planet's orbit around the Sun.
From the eyewitness accounts, as well as satellite data, videos and photos, Brown and his team have worked out the meteor's path through space.
Its period around Saturn is just under one Earth day, meaning that it really barrels along, to cover its 700,000 mile orbit in such a short time.

fes.d: The series of interconnected locations that the Theme traverses.
The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.
The Goal is the endpoint of the Path.
The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Path.
The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Path.
An entity relative to which the Theme moves on its Path .
The Direction is the direction or directions the Path runs.
A setting location through which the Path goes.
The Length is the distance the Path extends.
The moving object whose motion describes the Path.

name: Patrolling
d: An individual or group, the Patrol moves through and examines a Ground in order to ensure that it is in a generally Desired_state_of_affairs, particularly that it is safe and contains no dangerous Unwanted_entity. Rather than moving through the Ground, the Patrol may simply move such that all the (relevant portions of) Ground can be observed and checked.

ex.t: Detective Jones patrolled the northern half of the building.
Security guards patrolled for intruders while the game was in progress.

fes.d: The person (or group) who inspects the Ground to see that it is safe.
The area that the Patrol inspects with to ensure its safety.
An entity whose presence would impair the desirability or safety of the Ground.
This FE is used for the Means by which the Patrol examines the Ground.
The desired outcome of the patrolling. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for, or a to-marked VP Complement.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Patrol inspects the Ground.
This FE identifies the extent to which the Patrol examines the Ground.
This FE is the position of the Patrol during the act of perception. Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP.
The desirable state of affairs which the Patrol hopes to ensure by visiting Ground.
>The Time when the Patrol examines the Ground.
The circumstances under which the Patrol examines the Ground.
An entity used by the Patrol to scrutinize the Ground.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
A description of one of the participants in the patrolling event.
An indication of the members of the patrol.
The length of time of the patrol.
The Co-participant patrols along with the Patrol.
The Patrol may move around in a Vehicle.
The Possessor is the organization (usually a nation or group of nations) that orchestrates the patrol.

name: Pattern
d: This frame describes the interrelation of a collection of Entities; they may be physical entities or shapes in a recognizable configuration, a pattern of events, or a relation among abstract entities. The pattern is not the individual Entities nor the set of Entities, but an abstraction of their interrelations, as a gestalt.

ex.t: The Cougers are playing in a Wing-T formation tonight.
The auditors noticed a suspicious pattern of withdrawals from the maintenance account .
The digits of irrational numbers do not repeat in any kind of pattern

fes.d: The entities whose interrelations form the pattern.
The name of the pattern, such as "wing-T".
A descriptor of the pattern, such as "regular".

name: People
d: This frame contains general words for Individuals, i.e. humans. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have an Age, Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

ex.t: A man from Phoenix was shot yesterday.
She gave birth to a screaming babyyesterday.
I study 16-year-old female adolescents.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Person is the human being.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.

name: People_along_political_spectrum
d: An Individual belongs to a group that is categorized in terms of the political views on particular issues that the members of the group tend to share, in opposition to other groups that hold different beliefs on the issues. The views on particular issues that the Individual shares with the other members are assumed to result from general principles or beliefs rather than being accidental or temporary.

ex.t: Leftists vow huge protests during inauguration

fes.d: The Individual who is referred to in terms of their place along the political spectrum.
The location in which the Individual resides.
A set of issues that is used to identify a sub-set of the group members.
The Origin is the place where the Individual was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Individual.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Individual which is conceived of as persisting over time.
The Age is the length of time the Individual has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Individual belongs.
A phrase that indicates more precisely the location in political space of the Individual relative to the center of the region designated by the target.

name: People_by_age
d: This frame contains words for individuals as viewed in terms of their age. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

ex.t: He is a 12-year-old kid.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The human being of a certain age.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.

name: People_by_jurisdiction
d: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, who are governed by virtue of being registered in a certain Jurisdiction. Alternatively, they may be conceptualized with respect to their governance by a political or religious Authority They may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

ex.t: A Somali national entered our office.

fes.d: The Jurisdiction is the place where the Person typically resides and by whose Authority he is governed.
The Person is the human being.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
The politically or religiously legitimated persons who govern the Jurisdiction.

name: People_by_military_specialty
d: The LUs in this frame refer to Fighter in Military_organizations according to their specialty in general or their function at a particular place and time. The Fighter may be part of a nation-state's armed forces or may be a member of an irregular military organization.

ex.t: The IED injured the left door gunner.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Fighter was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Fighter has a military specialty.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Fighter which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Fighter.
The Age is the length of time the Fighter has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Fighter belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Fighter is associated.
The Fighter may have a Rank in the formal or informal military organization to which s/he belongs.
This FE identifies the place where the Fighter is stationed, or primarily operates from.
The Fighter belongs to the military of the Loyal_side.
This FE identifies a more specific Type of specialty that the Fighter has.
The Compensation is the payment that the Fighter receives for performing military service.
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of military membership with respect to permanency, time or duration of duty, payment basis, and so on.
The military organization to which the Fighter belongs.

name: People_by_morality
d: This frame contains general words for Individuals, i.e. humans, whose specific acts or general behavior is evaluated against standards of morality or rightness. The Person may have an Age, Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

ex.t: Columbus: Was he a Hero or a Villain?
There are endless disputes about this sort of thing, both in and out of the courts, because wrongdoers will say and do anything to avoid getting punished.
There are endless disputes about this sort of thing, both in and out of the courts, because wrongdoers will say and do anything to avoid getting punished.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Person is the human being.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
A domain of activity in which the Person exhibits behavior on which they are judged in terms of its morality.

name: People_by_origin
d: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their Origin. The Origin is generally incorporated, but may occasionally be specified separately. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

ex.t: I'm a proud Brit.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life. In this frame, it is generally incorporated in the lexical item, but may be separately specified as in the following:
The Person is the human being whose Origin is specified.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.

name: People_by_religion
d: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their Religion. The Religion is generally incorporated, but with some lexical units it is specified separately.

ex.t: The bells call the faithful to evensong DNI
A 90-year-old Baptist claims to have seen God personally in his backyard.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Person is the human being.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is conceived of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
The religious belief system that the Person follows.

name: People_by_residence
d: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their proximity of residence. This relationship may be defined either symmetrically (as Residents) or asymmetrically (in terms of a Known_resident and a Indicated_resident). The Residents or the Indicated_resident may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity specified.

ex.t: The dead included homeowner Todd Underfoot, 33, his wife Spring Back Underfoot, 32, their housemate, Luisa Life, 46, and two of the Underfoot's three children.
I have a Swedish roommate that translated for me!

fes.d: The individual(s) that serve(s) as a reference point for the definition of the Indicated_resident due to the proximity of residences.
The place in which the Residents or the Indicated_resident reside.
A person or group of people defined in terms of the fact that they reside in the proximity of the Known_resident.
The Age is the length of time the Indicated_resident has been alive.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Indicated_resident.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Indicated_resident which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The individuals who reside in proximity to each other.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Indicated_resident belongs.

name: People_by_vocation
d: This frame contains words for Individuals as viewed in terms of their vocation. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

ex.t: Humphrey Bogart was a great actor.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Person is the human being.
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within an organization.
This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.
The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.
This FE identifies the Type of the vocation that the Person practices.
The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.

name: Perception
d: A Perceiver perceives a Phenomenon. The general Perception frame is an inherited background to all frames that have to do with some sentient being responding to changes in the environment, independently of the sensory modalities. The inheriting frames may specify the modalities (see, hear, taste, smell), or may emphasize the experiences or acts of the perceiver (peek, eavesdrop), or the properties of the perceived phenomena (clank, rattle, thump).

fes.d: The FE Perceiver refers to someone whose cognitive state or experience (e.g. knowledge, beliefs, ideas judgments or classifications) is being described.
The Perceiver is the entity or event which causes the perceptual experience of the Perceiver.
Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.

name: Perception_active
d: This frame contains perception words whose perceivers intentionally direct their attention to some entity or phenomenon in order to have a perceptual experience. For this reason we call the perceiver role in this frame Perceiver_agentive. Comparing the Perception_active frame to the Perception_experience frame, we note that for some modalities there are different lexical items in each frame. For instance, whereas Perception_active contains the verb phrase look at, Perception_experience contains see. For other sense modalities, we find the same lexical item in both frames. To illustrate, consider the verb smell. This first sentence exemplifies the Perception_active use of the verb smell: This second sentence exemplifies its Perception_experience sense:

ex.t: She gazed upon him fondly.
Smell this to see if it's fresh.CNI
I smell something rotten.

fes.d: The Perceiver_agentive performs some action in order to have a perceptual experience. It is expressed as an External Argument:

Phenomenon indicates the entity or phenomenon to which the Perceiver_agentive directs his or her attention in order to have a perceptual experience. Typically, it is expressed as an Object with verbs.

Body_part identifies the part of the body used as a sensory organ of the Perceiver_agentive, typically expressed in a with-PP. This frame element occurs infrequently in this frame, because most of the target words intrinsically imply what part of the body is used (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb feel does take this frame element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way as other modalities . Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question.
This FE is the position of the Perceiver during the act of perception. Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP.

Direction is used for all path-like expressions that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception, with the exception of those indicating the location of the Perceiver_agentive (which would be marked Location_of_perceiver)
State is used for predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the perceiver's attention is directed to it:
State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon.
Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of active perception as such: closely, carefully, etc.

The Means indicates the tool or method the Perceiver_agentive is using to actively perceive the Phenomenon. May be confused with Direction in cases with through-PP, but is referring more to the instrument used than the path used.
When the activity of attempting to perceive occurs.
Some action that the Perceiver_agentive is trying to accomplish by directing their own attention.
The general location within which the act of perception takes place.
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Perception takes place.
An entity or state-of-affairs that the Perceiver_agentive hopes, fears, or expects to find within the Phenomenon.
Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver_agentive.

The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_agentive. This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon. .

name: Perception_body
d: This frame contains words describing physical experiences that can affect virtually any part of the body. The body part affected is almost always mentioned with these words. It is typically expressed by the noun heading the external argument, and this noun is typically accompanied by a possessive determiner that refers to the possessor of the body part, as in the first example below:

ex.t: My head hurts!
Nuadu, aching in every bone, had not made a sound.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the being who has a physical experience on some part of his or her body, or internally. Often information about this frame element is incorporated as a possessive determiner into the constituent expressing the Body Part, in which case it is not tagged separately (from Body Part), as shown below: My legs hurt! Sometimes, however, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument in its own right: I hurt all over! Here, the phrase all over can be considered a kind of generalized Body Part expression, and the pronoun I expresses the Experiencer independently. With nouns and adjectives in this frame, the separate expression of the Experiencer is more common: I have a pain in my leg.

This FE is the location on the body where the physical experience takes place, typically expressed as External Argument, often as PP complement: My legs are a little sore. I'm a little sore in my legs.
The Explanation describes the cause of the perception the body is experiencing.
Degree to which event occurs
Manner of performing an action
The Subregion is the specific area of the Body_part which experiences the sensation.

name: Perception_experience
d: This frame contains perception words whose Perceivers have perceptual experiences that they do not necessarily intend to. For this reason we call the Perceiver role Perceiver_passive. Comparing the Perception_experience frame to the Perception_active frame, we note that for some modalities there are different lexical items in each frame. For instance, whereas Perception_experience has see, Perception_active has look at. For other sense modalities, we find the same lexical items in both frames. To illustrate, consider the verb smell where I smell something rotten exemplifies its Perception_experience use and Smell this to see if it's fresh exemplifies its Perception_active sense. This frame also includes words which are not specific to any sense modality, including detect, perceive, perception, sense.

ex.t: Abashed, realising that he had overheard her conversation with Victoria, Sheeley didn't try to make excuses.
She smelled the wine on Paul's breath, and bade him to sit down.

fes.d: This FE is the being who has a perceptual experience, not necessarily on purpose. It is typically expressed as an External Argument.
This FE is the entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs. .

The Body_part is the location on the Perceiver_passive's body where the perceptual experience takes place. It is typically expressed in a PP. This Frame Element occurs less frequently than others, because many target words imply that a particular part of the body is involved (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb feel does take this Frame Element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way other modalities are. Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question.
This FE identifies the Location_of_protagonist during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a from-PP.

This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.
The State indicates predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the Perceiver_passive experiences it.
State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon. . . .
Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of perception as such: clearly, loudly, etc.
The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.
The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.
The Time at which the Perceiver_passive or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

An element of the discourse that serves to contextualize the Phenomenon, with which it is directly related (i.e. filling a frame-element role of the Phenomenon or vice-versa). It contrasts with other contextually relevant elements that potentially (but do not actually) fill the same role.

This FE signifies that the state-of-affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state-of-affairs would be expected given the state-of-affairs in the concessive clause.

A situation which pertains during the event. This frame element is primarily used to highlight the event denoted by the target against a (potentially partially) causal or concessive background state-of-affairs.
An expression of how often the event occurs.
The general location within which the act of perception takes place.

The Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver_passive. It can be distinguished from locative postnominal modifiers of the Phenomenon in negative contexts. In this example, it is implied that Pat looked behind the bar and did not find Kim there.

The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_passive. This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon. .

name: Performers
d: This frame contains words for Individuals as viewed in terms of their participation in artistic performances. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

ex.t: Smithers is an actor.

fes.d: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
The Person is the human being. (Note that the Person FE is incorporated in the LU actor.n, so the FE need not be explicitly marked unless an overy Person is named.)
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is conceived of as persisting over time.
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within a performance.
This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.
The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.
This FE identifies the Type of performer the Person is.
The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.

name: Performers_and_roles
d: A Performer has a certain Role in a Performance and plays their part by following the directions in the Script for that particular Role.

ex.t: Margaret Thatcher played Juliet in a school play.
"Pulp Fiction" starred John Travolta and a lot of other big names.
Mel Gibson starred in "Braveheart" as the leader of a Scottish rebellion.

fes.d: The Audience experiences the Performance.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.
The Performers generates the Performance which the Audience perceives.
The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.
The music which may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how. It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including script, screenplay, libretto, book, and choreography.
This FE indicates the subtype of Performance, including dance, theater, film, etc.

Role identifies one of the possible relations that the Performer can have to the Performance. The Role (s) a Performer has in the Performance will determine which parts of the Script should be performed by the Performer, as the Script is written in terms of which Role (s) each set of instructions applies to. In the fields of theater, movies, ballet, and opera, a Role generally corresponds to a character in the story of the Script, while other types of performance may use more general Roles like lead violinist.
This FE identifies the Time when an event occurs.
This FE identifies the Place an event occurs.
Manner of performing.
The person that performs alongside Performer2.
The person that is also in the Performance, alongside Performer1.
How long the Performer is in the Performance.
This is an appraisal or description of the performance event.

name: Performing_arts
d: The Performers, together with behind the scenes Personnel, execute a Performance according to a Script and/or Score. The purpose of the Performance is to create an experience for an Audience, who then judge its merits. Performances may be in many different Mediums and be of various Types. This frame is very elaborate in modern society and there are a number of traditions and practices typically (but not necessarily) related to Performances: The Performance is preceded by many practice sessions in which the Performers and other Personnel attempt to improve the quality and/or fidelity of their individual and collective performances to the Script and/or Score. The Audience members pay a fee to experience the Performance. The Performers (and Personnel) receive payment for contributing to the Performance. Often there are other individuals involved in the specifically financial aspects of the Performance and Performers. Critics act as part of the Audience and then write reviews that evaluate the merits of the Performance, describing the Performance to other potential Audience members. Due to the high quality of previous Performances, Performers can become famous, i.e. well known and liked. Those who like them particularly well become fans of the Performer. (Shared with writers...)

fes.d: The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.
The Personnel, including writers, producers, stage hands, key grips, etc., contribute to the Performance without actually being directly perceived by the Audience.
The Audience experiences the Performance.
The experience generated by the Performers and perceived by the Audience .

The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how. It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including script, screenplay, libretto, book, and choreography.
The Score may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.
This FE indicates the Type of Performance, including dance, theater, film, etc.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.

name: Personal_relationship
d: The words in this frame have to do with people and the personal Relationships they are or can be a part of. Some of the words denote people engaged in a particular kind of Relationship, others denote the Relationship, yet others the events bringing about or ending the Relationships. Many of the words presuppose an understanding of states and events that must have occurred before another event takes place or before a person can be classified in a certain way.

ex.t: And of course that drippy boyfriend of hers backed her up.
As the happy couple took their places there was a stir and a rising babble behind them.
Pattie is living proof that if you live with a man, you discover a lot you didn't know when you were just dating him.

fes.d: That partner in the Relationship who is realized as the subject of verbs in active form sentences, or of adjectives in predicative uses. When the target word is a noun (e.g. mistress, lover, bachelor), that noun is annotated as Partner_1 and, if there is one, the other member of the Relationship is Partner_2. When there is a word other than the target that refers to Partner_1, that word is tagged rather than the target.
That partner in the Relationship who is not expressed as the external argument.
The joint construal of both Partners in the Relationship.
Degree to which event occurs
Depictive phrase describing the Partners.
Manner of performing an action
An act whereby a focal participant achieves an action indicated by the target.
The Relationship between Partners.
The length of the relationship.
The source of the relationship.

name: Personal_success
d: A Person is in a state of prosperity and/or renown after some period of development or hardship in an Endeavor. LUs in this frame invoke a developmental path that is related to the goal one should have in a Person, such that the Person, after traversing a path of development (including hardship, effort, and time), completes or does not complete these goals. Note that this distinguishes an event's success in this frame from Successful_action.

ex.t: Framenet is enjoying huge success.
He had a long and successful career in banking.

fes.d: A sentient being or group of beings that is prosperous or well known after being involved in some Endeavor.
The time when the Entity is determined to be successful.
A qualification of the level of success that the Entity achieves.
An event that the Person is involved in which leads to their state of prosperity or renown.
An explanation of why the Person or Endeavor achieves its goal of prosperity or renown.
The area in which the Person achieves success.

name: Physical_artworks
d: A physical object, the Artifact, is produced by a Creator to stimulate the perceptions, emotions, or cognition of an audience. Though it need not, in many cases, the created Artifact is intended to represent an actual or imagined entity or event, the Represented. The Represented may be specifically shown in a particular state (State_of_represented).

ex.t: Sir Denis Mahon is the owner of the most important private collection of Italian Baroque paintings.
He presented Eddie with a watercolour painting and a bouquet of flowers to his wife Frances
I just took a picture of the screen and plan to share it with 6.4 billion of my closest friends on the Internet tonight.

fes.d: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use.
The use for which the Artifact is intended.
An individual or individuals that bring the Artifact into existence.
The time at which an Artifact comes into existence.
The term used to refer to an Artifact.
An indication of the subtype of Artifact.
Any indication of what makes up the Artifact, including components, ingredients, etc.
The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Artifact.
A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is portrayed.
This FE identifies a characteristic, description, or evaluation of the Artifact.
The location where the Artifact is presently located.

name: Physical_entity
d: An Entity exists in some Place at some time.

fes.d: Salient parts or substances that make up an Entity. At this level of abstraction, not every Entity is conceived of as having parts, though any normal entity has them.
A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.
Indicates the action (or causer) which made or makes the Entity what it is.
A label applied to a specific Entity. Not usual for general words inheriting from this frame, but common for Locales.

This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to. When a subtype is signified by some more specific FE, like Formational_cause, we use that more specific FE instead of Type, so this FE is most often needed when there is a vague or unknown relation between a name that indicates the Type and the Type of Entity in question. This FE is normally found as a pre-nominal modifier.
A place that a physical Entity is located with respect to.

name: Piracy
d: The words in this frame describe situations in which a Perpetrator forcibly seizes control over a Victim's Vehicle to gain some end.

ex.t: French farmers have hijacked a lorry and destroyed its load of strawberries.
But attackers have hijacked cars waiting at traffic lights and road junctions by simply opening the passenger door, jumping in and forcing the driver to a more deserted area.

fes.d: This is the person (or other agent) who forcibly seizes control over a vehicle to gain some end.
This is the means of transportation which gets under the control of the perpetrator. Example: The terrorists hijacked the plane.
This FE describes the people that are suffering as a result of the Perpetrator's action.
Degree to which event occurs
The unlawful seizure of a Vehicle by a Perpetrator.
Manner of performing an action
An act performed by the Perpetrator by which the seizure of the Vehicle is accomplished.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
Where the event takes place.
When the event occurs.
This is the place to which the vehicle is directed.
This is the place from which the vehicle is taken away.
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by piracy.
The situation that the Perpetrator had in mind which lead to the decision to perpetrate the particular act of piracy.
An object that the Perpetrator uses in taking control of the Vehicle.
The number of times that the Vehicle is seized in acts of piracy.

name: Placing
d: Generally without overall (translational) motion, an Agent places a Theme at a location, the Goal, which is profiled. In this frame, the Theme is under the control of the Agent/Cause at the time of its arrival at the Goal. This frame differs from Filling in that it focuses on the Theme rather than the effect on the Goal entity. It differs from Removing in focusing on the Goal rather than the Source of motion for the Theme.

ex.t: David placed his briefcase on the floor.

fes.d: The Agent is the person (or other force) that causes the Theme to move.
The Theme is the object that changes location during the Placing.
The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it changes location.
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.
The FE Goal is the location where the Theme ends up. This FE is profiled by words in this frame.

Any expression which describes a property of the placing action which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
The Degree indicates the degree to which the placing occurs.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme of the placing.
The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the placing of the Theme.
This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.
The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme is to stay in the Goal location.
The Place indicates where the Placing occurs.
The Explanation indicates why the Placing occurs.
Time is when the Placing occurs
The Area is the setting into which the Theme is placed.
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.
The Speed is the rate at which Placing occurs.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the placing action.

This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Placing_scenario
d: This frame represents the abstract scene in which an Agent manipulates a Theme's location, thus affecting a Goal which ends up co-located with the Theme. This frame is primarily for Inheritance.

fes.d: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.
The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location.
The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion.
The Path is the trajectory of the motion.
The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.
Degree to which the filling occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action.
The Manner in which the filling occurs.
The Means by which the filling occurs.
The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.
The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal.
When the filling occurs.
Where the filling takes place.
The Instrument with which the filling occurs.
The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs.
An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Planned_trajectory
d: A Theme traverses a trajectory. This trajectory consists of a Source, Path, and Goal. If the Theme is sentient, the anticipated trajectory will usually be equivalent to the planned trajectory. If the the Theme is non-sentient the anticipated trajectory will usually be the result of various forces acting upon the Theme.

ex.t: The dog went that waytowards the ice cream factory.

fes.d: The Theme is the entity that traverses the trajectory.
The Source profiles the region where the Theme has travelled from (i.e. the region where the Theme's movement began).
The Path is the region upon which the Theme travels. It is any region in between the Source (where the Theme departed from) and the Goal (where the theme will eventually arrive).
The Goal profiles the region at the end of the Theme's Path. This is the region where the Theme movement stops.
The Descriptor provides additional information that characterizes one or more of the aspects of the trajectory: the Source, the Path, or the Goal.

name: Planting
d: This frame describes a situation in which the Agent puts the Theme into the Ground for the purpose of growing.

ex.t: He recently planted some old apple trees. INI

fes.d: The Agent plants the Theme.
Theme is the item planted by the Agent.
The Instrument is used by the Agent as a tool to help obtain the Theme. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)
For what length of time the Agent plants the Theme.
The Manner in which the Agent plants the Theme.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent plants the Theme.
The failure or success of an attempt.
The greater geographic location where the Agent plants the Theme.
When the planting event occurs.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by planting the Theme.
How often the Agent cultivates the Theme.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The Ground is the background or context to which the Agent pays attention in his agricultural efforts.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
The Depictive describes a participant in the Planting action.
The Co-participant is an entity that participates in the planting event in a coordinated way with another participant.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the planting event logically follows.

name: Plants
d: The LUs in this frame refer to biological entities other than human beings and animals, which are labeled by the FE Plant.

fes.d: The living organism belonging to the kingdom Plantae.
A quality of the Plant.
A characterization of the Plant not covered by another frame element.
The location from which the Plant originated.

name: Point_of_dispute
d: The answer to a Question is under discussion in a Group, which still has a difference of opinion among its members. The prominence of the Question relative to others can be indicated by a Status expression.

ex.t: Firstly, it is quite clear the issue in this context was not so much apostasy as much as it was treason.
The question in Finucane's case is this: will an inquiry bring out the truth?
It remains an issue of central importance to women .

fes.d: The Question is an open proposition the answer to which is under dispute.
The Group are the persons or organizations who have different points of view on the Question.
The Frame Element Status is used for expressions that indicate the relative importance of a Question with respect to the other topics that are disputed.
A characterization of the Question, often with regard to its complexity or whether it has been resolved or not.
The area of human experience which the Question concerns.
A state or event within which the Question arises as a problem for the Group.
The time interval during which the Question exists as a problem for the Group.
An individual or individuals from whose point of view the Question is a point of dispute within the Group.

name: Political_actions
d: A less-powerful person or group of people (the Activists) engages in an activity aimed to inconvenience or weaken a more powerful person or group (the Institution) to seek redress, in the form of a series of Demands, for the wrondgoings committed by the Instituion.

ex.t: The workers were striking for better wages and better benefits.
The strike against the corporation lasted for 6 weeks.

fes.d: The person or group of people that act out against the Institution in an attempt to have their Demands fullfilled.
The Institution is the company, factory, political party / institution, or entity that yields authority over the Activists.
The Demands are the guarantee(s) given by the Institution to the Activists that act to correct or address the issues or state of affairs that were grievous to the Activists.
The Duration is the length of time that the political action takes to be resolved.
The Manner in which the political action is carried out.
The Means by which the Activists carry out the political action.
The Place is the location where the political action occurs.
This FE is the subtype of the general category of action taken by the Activists against the Institution.
The result of the event in which the Activists act against the Institution.

name: Political_locales
d: This frame covers words that name Locations as defined politically, or administratively.

ex.t: Berkeley is a wonderful city.

fes.d: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up a Locale.
The location that the Locale is a part of.
A stable bounded area. It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.
ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales.
A place that a Locale is located with respect to.
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.
The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.

name: Popularity
d: An Evaluee, which can be a person or an object, has an amount of acceptability or utilization based on general (often non-aesthetic) desirability. The Judge who determines the Evaluee's desirability may be mentioned.

ex.t: Frank Sinatra is cool again.
Web 2.0 is so in right now.

fes.d: The person or object that is being evaluated for its desirability.
A description of how desirable the Evaluee is.
The person who decides how desirable the Evaluee is.
The time when the Evaluee is judged to be desirable.
The geographic area where an Evaluee is considered desirable.

name: Posing_as
d: An Agent behaves as if they were a particular individual or type of Simulated_entity with the intent of misleading observers of their behavior. This is generally accomplished by altering their normal appearance (especially dress), mannerisms, voice, and other observable characteristics.

ex.t: The belfast bank robbers posed as police.
These groups are masquerading as mainstream groups, yet after taking a closer look you see they are the most extreme.

fes.d: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that they are a particular individual or type of Simulated_entity.

Any description of the posing event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the his or her being perceived as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
The type or individual that the Agent gives the impression of being.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by posing as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the posing event logically follows.
The location where the Agent gives the impression that they are the Simulated_entity.
The time at which the Agent impersonates the Simulated_entity.

name: Position_on_a_scale
d: This frame contains words that describe an Item's static position on a scale with respect to some property Variable.

ex.t: Dried fruits are especially high in fibre, as are pulses.
Despite the fact that the local land was rich in silver, by 1865 most of the mining traffic through Las Vegas was of propectors headed to California or Northern Nevada in search of gold.

fes.d: Item identifies the entity whose scalar property is specified.
Variable is the scalar property that the Item possesses. Soda is high in sugar.
The Value is the position or range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies. This is normally implicit in the LU.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the scalar property of an Item holds with respect to some Variable.
Domain describes the set of Items for which the Variable 's position is determined.

name: Possession
d: An Owner has (or lacks) a Possession.

ex.t: The river's part of my manor, but of course it also belongs to the River Police.
It's a nuisance having to abandon my belongings, though.

fes.d: The entity that owns a posession.
The thing which is owned by the Owner. Ex.: I have twenty bucks. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)
State of the Owner or Possession.
The way that the Owner possesses the Possession.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Owner has a possession.
The reason for which the Owner has the Possession.

name: Possibility
d: A Possible_event is deemed to have all pre-conditions satisfied; in other words, it has some probability of occurrence, if some (generally implicit) further Condition pertains.
