The Condition, whether overt or implicit, often concerns the decision of an agent to attempt to bring the Possible_event about. The primary implication is that certain other aspects of the situation that might have been expected to prevent the Possible_event, usually lack of capability or permission, do not pertain. This frame is confusable with the Capability frame, which specifically involves an Agent who is presented as needing only the decision to perform an Action in order to successfully perform the Action.

ex.t: You ca n't burn glass . INI
You can have two more if you want .
This sense of lack can never be satisfied .

fes.d: The Possible_event has met its preconditions, and will occur if some further Condition holds.
The Circumstances under which the preconditions of the Possible_event are met.
An entity, event, or state that brings about the possibility of the Possible_event.
The state-of-affairs that does not hold, but if it did, the Possible_event would occur.
The time at which the Possible_event can occur.

name: Post_getting
d: The stage after which the Recipient has acquired the Theme.

fes.d: The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.
The entity which has just come into the possession of the Recipient.
The way that the Recipient has the Theme
This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Post_getting event occurs.

name: Post_giving
d: The stage immediately after the Donor gives the Recipient the Theme, i.e. when the Recipient has possession of the Theme and the Donor no longer does.

fes.d: The individual that has just given the Theme to the Recipient and no longer has the Theme.
The entity that the Donor has just given to the Recipient.
The way that the Donor lacks the Theme.
The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

name: Post_lose_possession
d: The subframe of Relinquish in which the Owner (= Donor) no longer has the Possession (=Theme).

fes.d: The entity that no longer owns the posession.
The thing which was owned by the Owner. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_possession event occurs.

name: Post_receiving
d: The state-of-affairs immediately after the Recipient has come into possession of the Theme offered by the Donor.

fes.d: The person who has just acted to come into possession of the Theme.
The person who has just given the Theme to the Recipient.
The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.
The way that the Recipient has the Theme
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

name: Post_transfer
d: The stage after the Theme is in the possession of the Recipient.

fes.d: The individual that has just given the Theme away.
The entity which has ended up in the possession of the Recipient
The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.
The individual that has ended up with the Theme.
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_transfer event occurs.

name: Posture
d: An Agent supports their body in a particular Location. The LUs of the frame convey which body part is the Point_of_contact where the Agent is supported, what orientation the body is in, and some overall arrangement of the limbs (especially the legs) and the torso.

ex.t: He knelt down, hand on heart .

fes.d: The Agent is the individual whose body is in a particular posture. The Agent FE is generally expressed as the external argument of verbs:
A description of the position of the Agent. The Location of the Agent is frequently expressed and generally occurs as a PP Complement:
Degree to which event occurs
The Agent's state throughout the time they are in a particular posture.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
A state of the Agent which crucially depends on their posture.
This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Agent held a certain posture.
The Purpose for which the Agent holds the posture.
The length of time for which the Agent holds the posture.
The part of the body that provides support to the Agent's body in the posture.

name: Practice
d: An Agent enacts an Action that is intended to be performed again at one or more later Occasions. The goal of practicing is to ensure that the action at the later Occasion(s) comes off flawlessly.

ex.t: I practiced my song for the play.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs intentionally in order to prepare for a later Occasion.
The Agent performs the Action in preparation for later performances of the same type.
This FE identifies the place where the practicing occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent performs an intentional act.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent practices.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent practices.

Any description of the practicing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the Action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The later enactment or enactments that the Agent expects to perform. Note that the Agent does not have to have specific Occasions in mind.
The period of time during which an Action is repeatedly practiced.
The number of times that the Action is practiced.
A person who participates in a practice event along with the Agent.

name: Praiseworthiness
d: The Behavior of an Evaluee is described in terms of the reaction it deserves from somebody, such as praise, blame or admiration.

ex.t: It was honorable of you to help that person.

fes.d: The Behavior of the Evaluee is being judged as worthy of a particular reaction.
This FE indicates the Behavior on which the assessment of praiseworthiness is based.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the judgement or reaction is deserved.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Prank
d: A Joker, by means of a Prank, arranges to deceive a Victim, with the result that some harm or embarrassment comes to the Victim.

ex.t: They always play pranks on me.

fes.d: The Prank is a device, strategy, or system designed to mislead and cause harm and amusement to a Victim (and possibly others observing the prank).
The Prank is orchestrated by a Joker.
The Joker intends to mislead and cause harm to the Victim by means of the Prank.
A description of the Prank.

name: Pre_getting
d: The state of the Recipient prior to the acquisition, i.e. before the Recipient gains possession of the Theme.

fes.d: The individual that is about to gain a possession.
The entity which is about to be acquired by the Recipient.
A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_getting event occurs.

name: Pre_giving
d: The stage of giving just before the Donor discontinues possession of the Theme, yielding it to the Recipient.

fes.d: The individual that has possession of the Theme and is about to transfer possession to the Recipient.
The entity which is in the possession of the Donor, which later ends up in the possession of the Recipient.
The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.
The individual who is about to come into possession of the Theme.
This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_giving event occurs.

name: Pre_lose_possession
d: Subframe of Relinquish where the Owner (=Donor) has the Possession (=Theme).

fes.d: The Owner is the entity that owns the Possession.
The Possession is the thing which is owned by the Owner. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_posession event occurs.

name: Pre_receiving
d: The state-of-affairs immediately before the Recipient gets the Theme which describes the Recipient's possession of the Theme.

fes.d: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.
The person who has the Theme and is about to give it to the Recipient.
The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.
A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme.
This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_receiving event occurs.

name: Pre_transfer
d: The stage before the transfer has taken place, with the Theme in the possession of the Donor.

fes.d: The individual that is about to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.
The entity which is in the possession of the Donor.
The way that the Recipient or Donor possesses the Theme.
The individual who is about to receive the Theme.
This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_transfer event occurs.

name: Precariousness
d: A Theme has the potential of falling from its current Location, which would likely result in damage.

ex.t: Now, balanced easily and firmly, he stood on the ledge outside in the slight, chill breeze.
A ball will sit there perfectly balanced on a jet of water (or air).
Joey teetered into him sometimes, losing his balance from extreme exhaustion.

fes.d: A valuable entity which might fall and be damaged.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of precariousness from the expected value given the Theme and the state indicated by the target itself.
The event of falling, incorporated in the LUs of this frame.
An entity which may cause the Theme to fall.
A particular location in which the Theme is at risk of falling. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location put the Theme in danger.
The time period during which the Theme is in danger of falling.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the state of precariousness of the Theme logically follows.
The Situation under which the Theme is safe or unsafe from falling. Most expressions of Time and Place also express the Situation and should be labeled as such on the 2nd FE layer.
The Domain in which the Theme has a degree of precariousness. Usable only in metaphorical sentences.
This FE describes the Theme as being in some state during the action.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
Any description of the holistic properties of the balancing situation.
The location where the Theme is supported.
An event or state that results from the instability of the Theme.

name: Precipitation
d: Water in some solid or liquid form (the Precipitation) falls from the sky at a particular Place and Time, lasting for a particular Duration. The Rate or Quantity of precipitation may also be indicated.

ex.t: It rained in Berkeley yesterday.

fes.d: The water in liquid or solid form that falls from the sky is the Precipitation. This FE is incorporated in many LUs in this frame.
The Quantity of Precipitation that falls within a certain Duration.
The Quantity is the amount of Precipitation that has fallen in a precipitation event or events. It is usually measured as the height that the Precipitation attains if prevented from further movement.
The area which experiences precipitation.
The amount of time for which the precipitation event lasts.
When the event occurs.
The Explanation is the reason for the precipitation event.
The way in which the precipitation falls.
This FE identifies the temperature of the precipitation.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Predicament
d: An Experiencer is in an undesirable Situation, whose Explanation may also be expressed.

ex.t: The insurers ended up in the bind of having to pay 15 years' taxes.
He was in a bit of a pickle and make no mistake!
What a mess we 're in now!

fes.d: The Experiencer is in an undesirable Situation.
This FE identifies the undesirable Situation the Experiencer is in.
This FE identifies the Explanation of the Situation.
Thiis FE identifies the Time when the Situation is in effect.
The location where the Situation occurs.
The Domain in which the Experiencer has the problem.

name: Predicting
d: A Speaker states or makes known a future Eventuality on the basis of some Evidence. Instead of (or in addition to) a Speaker, a Medium may also be mentioned. Likewise, a more general Topic may be stated instead of an Eventuality.

ex.t: The Weather Centre predicted that it would be warmer but wet for the weekend.
Another seer who forecast a Tory majority -- without compromising his impartiality -- was Sir Robin Day .
Based on current calculations, the European market is forecast to grow 18.1% by the end of next fiscal year.

fes.d: The Speaker makes a prediction.

This FE marks expressions that indicate an event or state that is predicted to occur or hold at a future time. A single Eventuality may be expressed discontinuously in a raising construction. This FE is also used for expressions that denote entities with variable attributes about which the Speaker makes predictions.
Evidence marks expressions that denote a set of facts on the basis of which the Speaker makes the prediction.
This FE identifies the Time when the prediction is made.
The Place where the Speaker makes the prediction.
Manner marks any description of the Speaker's prediction making that is not covered by more specific FEs. Note that this FE does not cover modifiers such as 'correctly' or 'accurately'.
This FE marks expressions that indicate for what future time an Eventuality is predicted.
This FE indicates the Accuracy of the prediction.
Descriptor describes a characteristic of the Eventuality.
The Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the prediction.
The Topic is the subject matter to which the prediction pertains. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.
An act whereby the Speaker makes a prediction.

name: Preference
d: An Experiencer has a greater desire to participate in some Event, as against another (contextually recoverable) event which exhibits a specific Contrast with the Event. Alternatively, the Experiencer may have a greater desire that some Focal_participant participate in the Event. The Location_of_event may also be mentioned.

ex.t: Why do women prefer manly faces?
I prefer open source programs over proprietary ones.
Other customers prefer to send us an order together with a cheque.

fes.d: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.
The change that the Experiencer would like to see.
This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.
The Degree is the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.
The way in which the Experiencer desires something.
The Explanation shows why the Experiencer wants the Event to occur. This FE occurs frequently as a PP complement headed by for.
The Purpose_of_event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.
The time that the Event would ideally occur.
The Location_of_event is the place involved in the desired Event.
The Time is when the Experiencer desires something.
Where the event takes place. Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame.
The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something.
An alternative Event or Focal_participant that is less desirable for the Experiencer.

name: Preferred_alternative_scenario
d: In this scenario, there are two mutually incompatible scenes, the Profiled_possibility and the Opposite_possibility, leading respectively to a preferable Positive_consequence and a dispreferable Undesirable_consequence.

fes.d: The situation presented explicitly as a possible for agents to influence that leads to a better situation, contrasting with the implicit Opposite_possibility that leads to a worse situation.
The implicit situation that is mutually exclusive with the Profiled_possibility. It is presented as leading to a less desirable situation, the Undesirable_consequence.
The preferable situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.
The less desirable situation that follows as a result of the Opposite_possibility.

name: Preliminaries
d: This frame describes means actions (Preparatory_acts) that are taken by an Agent for the purpose of preparing for a later act. Contrast this frame with a scenario involving earlier versions of some entity being superseded by later versions (e.g., preliminary results, advance copy).

ex.t: This update lays the groundwork for future improvements.

fes.d: The Agent uses the Preparatory_act to acheive a Purpose.
The action performed by the Agent that is a preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose. The Preparatory_act may also be expressed by a result of such an act.
The ultimate goal or purpose of the Agent, which the Preparatory_act enables.
A characteristic of the Preparatory_act, Agent, or other participant.
The extent to which the Preparatory_act is distant from the achievement of the Purpose.
The area, field, or domain for which the preliminary action is relevant.
The time at which the Preparatory_act takes place.
The place where the Preparatory_act takes place.
The part of the larger process that is preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose.

name: Presence
d: An Entity exists at a particular Location, at a particular Time, as observed by an implicit observer. A Depictive and/or Duration phrase is often found. This frame differs from Existence in that the Location is profiled as a ground where an observer is conceived of as confirming the Entity's existence. In some cases, the Location may be recoverable from phrases that primarily express peripheral information:

ex.t: Liquid water was present on the surface of Mars billions of years ago.
Urate was present in varying concentrations in the bathing solution only.
No one was present. DNI

fes.d: The Entity whose existence at the Location is confirmed.
The Location of the Entity. The Location is conceived as a ground for an event of inspection to determine the presense of the Entity.
The time when the Entity is present at the Location.
A separate description of the state of the Entity when it is present.

The time period during which the Entity is present. In this frame, Duration may be expressed with for preceding an event which stands for the duration of the event. In cases where the Entity is sentient, there may be an inference that the Entity's intent is to be present so as to participate in the event.
The purpose of the Entity.
A characterization of the presence or absence of the Entity.
The degree to which the Entity is present.

name: Presentation_of_mitigation
d: A Mitigating_situation is presented as occurring against the backdrop of a more preferable situation and a less preferable situation that, while expected, feared, or hoped for, did not or will not occur; the Mitigating_situation is thus, so to speak, sandwiched between a better and a worse situation, both of which are relevant in the discourse. Understanding the Mitigating_situation is therefore dependent on understanding the better and the worse situations, one or the other or both of which normally have already been mentioned or strongly evoked in the discourse. The relation of the Mitigating_situation to these situations may be filled in by discourse-level inference, as in the first example below, or implied by contrastive intonation, as in the second example. When the Mitigating_situation clause involves a negation, like in the first example above, the non-negated form is generally taken to be the worse situation - potentially also in combination with previous discourse context. (i.e. Perhaps there's been a blizzard. The better situation is that a blizzard did not occur. The mitigating situation is that a blizzard occurred, but I don't have to go to school. The worse situation would be that a blizzard occurred, and I also have to go to school.) Targets in this frame frequently occur in constructions that obscure the full In this example, there is a fragment ellipsis construction that depends on the semantics of the immediately preceding context. Lexical Units of this frame also frequently occur with the use of or that conveys a speaker self-correction or hedge. The function of this sort of or is to introduce contradictory possibilities without endorsing any of them. In combination with targets of the Presentation_of_mitigation frame, or joins a clause that represents the better situation to a second clause (or fragment) marked with an LU of this frame, with the overall intent of saying that even the less preferable alternative is still suitable to carry forward the point that the speaker wishes to express: The humorous point in this example is that, even if their drab lives are not transformed (the better situation), at least their drab furniture will be, while the worse situation is that everything simply remains drab. Note that this example, and most examples involving or, occur with the Shared_completion construction, meaning that two parts of the sentence have to be annotated: the shared part of the first clause and a fragment directly marked with a Presentation_of_mitigation LU. This frame is to be distinguished from two related frames, Concessive and Conditional_scenario. In Concessive and its daughter frames, either a Main_assertion or a Conceded_state_of_affairs FE (or both) are present, and both FEs, even though seemingly contradictory, are simulateously true. Here, however, only the Mitigating_situation actually occurs. Targets in this frame may be embedded in larger Concessive constructions, such as the below with although, where the better situation is made explicit (in negated form): In Conditional_scenario, a Profiled_possibility and its Consequence, as well as an Opposite_possibility and its Anti_consequence, can be presented. Neither of the possibilities is asserted as true, nor is a desirability scale with better and worse ends evoked.

ex.t: At least I don’t have to go to school.
Ava, anyway, knew who he was.
Mitigating_situation:

fes.d: The Mitigating_situation is the situation that actually occurs. It is presented in a discourse to mitigate the fact that a better situation did not occur - since the FE is still preferable to an even worse situation.

name: Preserving
d: In this frame an Agent preserves a Patient in order to prevent it from decaying. A Medium may be used.

ex.t: Bill mummified John.
Tess pickled the beets in vinegar.
The Smiths dried the apples.

fes.d: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act that leads to the preservation.
Medium is the substance in which the Patient might be submerged to be preserved.
The Patient is organic matter that undergoes the preservation.
The Instrument with which an an Agent performs the Preserving.
The Means by which the Agent preserves the Patient.
The Manner in which the Agent preserves the Patient.
The Place where the preserving occurs.
The Time when the Agent preserves the Patient.
The Purpose for which the Agent preserves the Patient.
Result of an action.
The amount of Time for which the process of Preserving is ongoing.
The Depictive phrase describing one of the participants.
The extent to which the Patient is preserved from decaying.

name: Prevarication
d: A Speaker communicates about a Topic in such a way as to mislead an Addressee, either by telling outright lies or by presenting a message in a misleading form.

ex.t: I lied to you about your Christmas present.

fes.d: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a deceptive Message to the Addressee.
The person that receives a Message from the Speaker.
Topic is the entity to which the proposition or propositions relate, that they are about.
The location at which the deception occurs.
The time at which the deception occurs.
The (communicative) action performed by the Speaker in order to deceive the Addressee.
The length of Time that the Speaker spends on the Topic.
The goal of the Speaker's deceit of the Addressee
The extent to which the Speaker deceives the Addressee about the Topic.
This FE describes how often the Speaker discusses the Topic with the Addressee.

name: Prevent_or_allow_possession
d: An Agent or Potential_hindrance keeps a Protagonist from having a State_of_affairs that they need or desire, or, despite the possibility of preventing the possession, they allow the Protagonist to have the State_of_affairs.

ex.t: His parents deprived him of food for days on end.
Our lonely city starves us of original live music.
Employees were denied overtime pay and meal breaks. CNI

fes.d: The Potential_hindrance is the force which keeps the Event from happening, or does not prevent it.
The is the situation, state-of-affairs, or state of having a possession that the Protagonist is kept from having.
The Time is when the Potential_hindrance keeps the Event from taking place.
The Place is where the Potential_hindrance keeps the Event from taking place.
The Agent is the person who keeps the Event from happening.
The Protagonist is the person who is kept from having the State_of_affairs.
The reason why the Agent keeps the Protagonist from having the State_of_affairs.
The length of time for which the Protagonist is denied the State_of_affairs.
How it is possible that the deprivation event occurs.
This FE marks the frequency with which the Protagonist is prevented from having the State_of_affairs.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of prevention and which the prevention is taken to be a part of.

name: Preventing_or_letting
d: A Potential_hindrance or an Agent (via their actions) keeps an Event from taking place, or despite the possibility of prevent the Event, do not do so. Lexical units which indicate that the event is not prevented, e.g. allow.v, are marked with the semantic type "Negative". Some lexical units, like avert and avoid indicate that the Potential_hindrance or Agent would have been affected if the Event occurred. Unlike in the Thwarting frame, the Potential_hindrance or Agent does not directly prevent the actions of an individual, but rather affects the world in such a way that an Event cannot occur.

ex.t: Rain prevented the ball game from taking place.
He could have stopped the riot .
The government narrowly averted a coup .

fes.d: The Potential_hindrance is the force which keeps the Event from happening, or does not.
The Event is prevented from occurring by the Preventing_cause or the Agent.
The Time is when the Potential_hindrance or Agent keeps the Event from taking place.
The Place is where the Potential_hindrance or Agent keeps the Event from taking place.
The Agent is the sentient being which keeps the Event from happening.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
A situation that accompanies the preventing or allowing.
Any description of details of the event that influence the overall understanding and impression, such as the attitude of an Agent (casually) or the overall nature of the event (the same way).
The action performed by an Agent that brings about the prevention or allowing.

In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function. First, it applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. The second subgroup consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier. What that role is depends only on the predicate heading the modifier phrase.
A description of the Agent or an entity of the Event while they are involved in the action.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
A category that the Event fits into, which dictates the Event's being permitted or prevented (in accord with some implicit Principle.)
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
How often the event occurs.
The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about with their action.

name: Price_per_unit
d: A Product is offered by a Seller at a particular Price such that some total cost for the Buyer in the transaction is a multiple of the Price.

ex.t: Additional telephone rates may apply.

fes.d: A commodity, item, or service being sold by the Seller at a certain Price.
The amount of money that the Seller charges the Buyer for a Product.
The entity that offers a Product at a certain Price.
The person who purchases the Product at a particular Price.
A description of the Price, usually characterizing its position on a scale of expensiveness.

name: Prison
d: This Frame deals with Penal_institutions. They are run by an Operator and may be intended to hold certain kinds of Inmates. Penal_institutions may have a special Name and their Location may also be indicated.

ex.t: He's in Pelican Bay state penitentiary.

fes.d: The Frame Element Operator marks expressions that indicate which level of government operates the Penal Institution.
Inmates marks expressions that indicate the group of people a Penal Institution is intended to hold.
This FE marks expressions that are the Name of a Penal Institution.
This FE marks expressions that indicate the Location of the Penal Institution.
The level of security maintained at the prison.
The locale which serves to confine individuals, generally for the purpose of punishment. This FE is incorporated in each LU in this frame.
A subpart of the Penal_institution.
This FE is used to describe a salent characteristic of the Penal_institution not otherwise specified.

name: Probability
d: This frame characterizes the likelihood that a Hypothetical_event will happen as a position on a scale of impossible to inevitable. The likelihood can expressed as numerical Odds or a metaphorical representation of the Position on a scale.

ex.t: There's a 20 % chance that you'll succeed.
The odds that he'll actually do it are one in a million.

fes.d: A numerical representation of the probability that a Hypothetical_event will occur.
A metaphorical representation of the position on the scale of likelihood that the Hypothetical_event will occur.
The event that is expected to happen with a certain likelihood.

name: Process
d: This frame describes a complex event which lasts some amount of time, consisting of a beginning stage, a stage where the process is ongoing, and a finish or end. In some cases the process may pause, and then possibly resume. In this frame and its subframes, the distinguished argument is a Process, and there is no reference to an Entity which undergoes this Process or an Agent which initiates this Process. In formal terms, this frame refers to an overall controller x-schema (Narayanan 1997) with subframes corresponding to parts of the x-schema.

ex.t: I'm in the process of writing it down.

fes.d: The Reason for which an event occurs.
Name of the Process which occurs.
Where the event takes place.
When the event occurs.
Manner of performing an action
Result of an event
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Process_completed_state
d: A Process is finished and can no longer proceed.

ex.t: The project is complete.

fes.d: Where the event takes place.
This FE identifies the name of the Process that occurs.
When the event occurs.

name: Process_continue
d: An Event continues at a certain Place through Time. (Note that often when 'continue.v' occurs with definite time points, it denotes Resumption, which is out of frame here.) NB: Refer to Process frame.

ex.t: Pyongyang agreed to suspend its withdrawal while talks continued with Washington.
Missions and different plans proceed according to Islamic law provision.

fes.d: Depictive phrase about the state of a focal participant.
Manner in which the Event is continuing.
This FE identifies the Duration of time over which the Event is ongoing.
Name of the Event which is continuing.
Where the Event takes place.
The Explanation for which the Event occurs.
When the Event occurs.
The Next_subevent of the overall Event.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Process_end
d: A Process comes to an end.

ex.t: The project came to a close.

fes.d: Name of the event which occurs.
The Final_subevent of an event.
Where the event takes place.
The Explanation for which the event ends.
When the event ends.
Degree to which the event occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event.
Manner of performing the event.
Result for the event.
The number of times that the event is repeated.
The amount of time it takes for the Process to end.

name: Process_initial_state
d: The initial State of an Entity in an event; part of the Event X-schema. NB: Refer to Event frame.

fes.d: The overall process which is about to begin.
The point at which the Process begins.
The length of time that the Process remains ready to begin.

name: Process_pause
d: The Process stops making progress towards completion, but should resume and continue.

fes.d: The Process which is halting.
Where the pause takes place.
When the pause in the Process occurs.
Degree to which the event occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
Manner of performing an action.
The Result of the pause.
The Final_subevent of an event.
This FE identifies the Explanation of the pause.
The amount of time that a Process remains stopped.
The number of times that the Process stops.,

name: Process_resume
d: An event resumes at a certain Place and Time. NB: Refer to Event frame.

ex.t: Both matches will resume tomorrow, after a day of rest.
Negotiations between Israel and the Palestinian authority have resumed.

fes.d: The amount of Time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
The Process which is being resumed.
Where the event takes place.
The Explanation for which an event occurs.
When the event occurs.
The number of times that the Process resumes.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Process_start
d: An Event begins at a certain Time and Place. Reason may also be indicated. NB: Refer to Event frame.

ex.t: The project began.

fes.d: Name of the Event which occurs.
Where the Event takes place.
The Explanation for which an Event occurs.
When the Event occurs.
The Initial_subevent of the Event.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
Manner in which an action is performed.
Result of the Event.
The period of time for which the Process is ongoing after it has started.
The number of times that the specified type of Event begins.

name: Process_stop
d: A Process stops at a certain Time and Place. Reason may also be specified. A Duration may be included in order to indicate the length of the persistence of the Paused-state before action resumes. NB: Refer to Process frame.

ex.t: The strident, static-like hiss ceased abruptly.
The use of railway-owned vehicles on aggregates traffic ceased altogether in 1989.

fes.d: The Process which is halting.
Where the event takes place.
This FE identifies the Explanation of an event occur.
When the event occurs.
Degree to which the event occurs.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
Manner of performing an action.
The Result of an event.
The Final_subevent of an event.
The amount of time that a process remains stopped.
The number of times that the Process stops.,

name: Process_stopped_state
d: The State of an Entity after an Event has stopped, i.e. part of an X-schema. NB: Refer to Event frame.

fes.d: The overall event which is stopped.
The point at which the Process is not continuing.
The length of time that the Process does not resume.

name: Process_uncompleted_state
d: A Process is in a state where it can no longer be completed.

fes.d: Where the state takes place.
This FE identifies the name of the Process that occurs.
When the event occurs.

name: Processing_materials
d: An Agent alters some Material in some useful way by means of some chemical or physical Alterant. Typically, this involves placing a reagent in contact with the Material, or applying heat, pressure, etc. Often a specific Agent and/or Result is mentioned. The Alterant is often incorporated in the target, as in tin.v, galvanize. (The Preserving frame is a special case of Processing_materials, in which the Material is immersed in the Alterant for the Purpose of preventing decay.) Processing_materials is distinguished from Filling in that the Material in Processing_materials is fundamentally altered (often chemically), rather than simply being covered with a different substance.

ex.t: Native Americans dyed textiles with dyes made from cedar strips.
Watering cans are often galvanized to prevent rust.

fes.d: The Agent is a person who applies the Process to the Material.
The Alterant causes a change in the Material.
The Material is altered by the Agent in some useful way.
The purpose for which the Agent processes the Material.
The result of the processing action, whether intended or not.
The length of time during which the application of the Alterant is applied to the Material
The location in which the Materials are processed, often a purpose-built facility such as a tannery or water treatment plant.
The point in time or period during which the treatment of the Material takes place.
The part of the Material which is affected by the process.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in processing the Material.
The dimension or aspect of the Material that is processed.
A holistic description encompassing all the details of an act of processing, often indicated by giving a characteristic of the Agent that affects the action.

name: Procreative_sex
d: This frame exists to define a type of Sex where the intended result is procreation.

fes.d: The set of entities engaged in or subjected to procreative sexual contact.
One party present for procreative sex.
Another party present for procreative sex.
This FE describes the length of time that an entire sexual encounter can last, including but not necessarily implying the length of all stages of the encounter.
A description of the sex act which is not covered by more specific FEs. In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of one or more Participants that also affect the action.
This FE identifies the Means by which Participants accomplish a sexual act.
To be clear: the place FE describes the overall location of the Participants of the sexual activity and nothing else.
This FE relates the relative time of occurrence of the sexual activity.
For a sexual act, the Domain describes the specific realm of the contact between Participants; for example, phone sex.
This FE identifies the justification of a sexual act, for at least one of the Participants.

name: Product_delivery
d: In order to facilitate the purchase of Goods which start off in a location distant from a Purchaser, a Deliverer transports and hands off the Goods to a Purchaser or (more indirectly) a Goal location which is accessible to the Purchaser.

fes.d: This is the person who completes the movement of the Goods after having transported it.
The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.
The objects being delivered.
The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.
The state of the Goods or the Deliverer during the action.

Any description of the delivery event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The individual who purchases and receives the Goods.
The state-of-affairs that the Deliverer hopes to bring about by delivering to the Purchaser.
A state-of-affairs that explains why the Goods were delivered.
When the delivery takes place
An additional theme delivered along with the main Goods.
A container in which the Goods is delivered.
The location at which the delivery takes place.
The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Goods.
The conditions under which the delivery takes place.
The location of the Goods before the delivery process begins.
The intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the Goods to the Goal.
The path along which the Goods move while being delivered.

name: Product_development
d: An Developer develops a Product, in some cases for a Company.

ex.t: The development of a profitable product will be necessary for the company to stay afloat. INI
Heinrich will develop a great new product for Apple someday.

fes.d: The person who develops the Product.
The entity which is developed by the Developer.
The organization for which the Developer develops the Product.
The location where the Product is developed by the Developer.
The Time when the Product is developed by the Developer.
The manner in which the Product is developed.
The use for which the Product is intended.

name: Product_development_scenario
d: An Developer works to create progress on an Entity. The Entity typically goes through three stages of development: the conceptual process (Achieving_first); the development process (Product_development); and the manufactuing process (Manufacturing). The Entity can also undergo additional processes such as designing, engineering, prototyping, and testing.

fes.d: The Developer is the person who develops the Entity.
The Entity is the item developed by the Developer.
The Time when the Entity is developed by the Developer.
The location where the Entity is developed.
The organization for which the Entity is developed by the Developer.
The Purpose for which the Developer develops the Entity.
The Explanation for why the Developer developed the Entity.

name: Product_line
d: A specified Designer or a Brand creates and distributes a Collection of related Products. The individual Products may all be part of a set or may just be related by season or other arbitrary reason.

ex.t: The new Gucci line is due out in early Spring.
He gave her the entire Oscar de la Renta springcollection for her birthday.
Clorox now produces a line of eco-friendly cleaning products.

fes.d: The company that produces the Collection of Products.
The set of Products produced by the Brand.
The individual items produced by the Brand.
A characteristic of the Collection or individual Products.
The name of the Collection of Products produced by the Brand.
The person who designs the Collection.

name: Progression
d: An Entity changes from a Prior_state to a Post_state in a sequence that follows a pre-defined plan, expectation, or model of change. The change is usually assumed to be an improvement for the Entity. Because this frame is describing change according to some known model of the Entity, the Prior_state and Post_state are backgrounded, and often implicit. This frame is not equivalent to the frame Improvement_or_decline for two reasons. Firstly, Progression implies a smooth or multi-stage change involving several different states of the Entity in an expected sequence, while Improvement_or_decline may be simple or complex, in accord with an expected sequence or not. Secondly, progression along an expected sequence does not necessarily mean that things get better (or worse) for the Entity. This is clear in the case of progression of a disease, since different ailments have very different expected sequenes, with initial onset leading to expected disappearance (for cases like the cold), or to permanent impairment (in the case of Parkinsons), or to death (in many forms of cancer). However, it is more confusing in the very common case of the progress of a biological Entity from birth to death, where this frame often emphasizes the phases of the lifespan where the organism increases in ability, thus reaching a more desirable state. Plans are also spoken of as progressions, and because the expected sequence is towards the goal of the agents that formed the plan, these uses of the progress frame also emphasize improvement.

ex.t: Their offensive armament has developed from short range missiles to long-range ballistic weaponry in a relatively short period .
The maturation of warhead technology is, perhaps, not far off .
Recovery in our major overseas markets has progressed tentatively and increased spending by consumers and government does not appear to be benefiting this

fes.d: The object that undergoes change.
The former state of the Entity.
The state of the Entity following an advance.
The time at which the progress occurs.
The rate at which the change happens.
A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way).
The period over which the progress occurs.
The amount of advancement that the Entity has attained.
The relevant dimension of development.
An event or state of affairs that brings about the development of the Entity.
The location where the Progress occurs.
This FE describes the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames
How often the Progress event occurs.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Prohibiting_or_licensing
d: In this frame a State_of_affairs is prohibited (or allowed) by a Principle. Raising constructions are common in this frame. Because laws and principles usually focus on what is not allowed, the words of this frame that are synonyms of prohibit.v are considered more basic, and the words that are synonyms of permit.v are marked with the semantic type "Negative". In this frame the Principle which prohibits the State_of_affairs is not an agent who denies permission to a specific individual or group of individuals, and thus differs from the Authority in the Deny_permission frame.

ex.t: Guns were prohibited in the airport .
Code 1425 bans large trucks in the tunnel.
Children were not permitted in the office. CNI

fes.d: A moral, legal, or social norm which rules a State_of_affairs to be inadmissible behavior or an outcome of behavior.
The Place is where the prohibiting occurs.
The Time is when the prohibiting occurs.
The Circumstances are the conditions under which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.
The reason for which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.

name: Project
d: An Agent, which may be an individual or group, is engaged in a complex Activity. A larger Goal which motivates the Agent carrying out the Activity may be indicated. Instead of a particular Activity, a Field of endeavor may be indicated. The project may also have a Name and the Time when as well as the Place where it is ongoing may be specified.

ex.t: The New Car Assessment Program (NCAP) is dedicated to helping the public buy a safer car.
The school will continue with its project to end all violence related to racism, xenophobia and intolerance.

fes.d: The individual or organization that carries out the project.
An area of human endeavor, typically scientifc in nature, in which the Agent's Activity falls.
What the Agent (an individual or the members of an organization) are dedicated to doing.
A name given to the project for identification.
The larger aim that the Agent is pursuing by carrying out certain coordinated measures.
An entity (abstract or concrete) which is involved in an implicit Activity.
A description of the manner in which the Agent performs the Activity associated with the program.
The length of time over which the project is lasts or is slated to last.
Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the Activity of the project as the Agent.
The ongoing plan of action which allows the Agent to pursue the Activity.
The time at which the Project is ongoing.
The location where a Project is pursued.
This FE is used to describe a characteristic of the Project.

name: Proliferating_in_number
d: The number of entities that make up the Set changes from an Initial_number to a Final_number. Alternatively, the situation can be described in terms of an Initial_state and a Final_state. In some cases the Attribute (i.e., number) or Difference in number may be mentioned.

ex.t: How has the proliferation of cellular telephones affected your amateur mobile operation? INI INI
The number of rural poor has dwindled from some 250 million to 26 million.
Problems in the banking industry proliferated dramatically in the 1980s.

fes.d: The Attribute is the number of entities that make up the Set.
The group of entities, possibly construed as a collective, whose number changes.
The number of entities by which the Set increases or decreases.
Any expression that gives information about points on the number scale that the Set traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement.
The number of entities in the Set afterwards.
The initial number of entities in the Set.
The rate of change of the value.

The Correlated_variable is an ordered progression of positions or values (most often a sequence of spatial locations) that the (dependent) Attribute is measured against. The Correlated_variable is metaphorically mapped onto the progression of time, and in the absence of this FE, changes in the number in the Setare simply measured against (forward-directional) time.
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Degree to which event occurs.
The Circumstances under which the proliferation takes place.
The Group within which the number of entities in the Set changes in the specified way.
The Time is the time-frame in which the change in number occurs.
The length of time over which the change takes place.
The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Initial_number of entities in the Set.
The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Final_number in the Set.
A location where the Set changes in number.
A description that presents the Set's state before the change in the number of entities making it up as an independent predication.
A description that presents the Set's state after the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.

name: Prominence
d: An Entity stands out perceptually in comparison to other members of its type.

ex.t: Pilot Mountain in NC is very prominent.
First, from the Saturday images, the most prominent feature is a sharp spike emerging from the tailward side of the nucleus.
I was left with a deep and conspicuous scar (about 10cm long) which felt uncomfortably tight and itchy.

fes.d: The Entity for which the saliency Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.
The feature of the Entity which is under discussion, namely perceptual salience.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the prominence from the norm or from the value for another Entity.
The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular salience.
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular degree of prominence.
This FE refers to the location where the Entity has a prominence of some Attribute.

name: Proper_reference
d: A speaker marks explicitly that he intends to describe an Entity in a more restricted sense than it was used in the immediately preceding discourse, and that therefore his Intended_referent is different from the one that the hearer might have picked out based on the way the Entity label was previously used.

ex.t: Of these, nowadays there are 308 within the city proper, and 534 if suburbs are included.
Of these, nowadays there are 308 within the city PROPER, and 534 if suburbs are included.
The writing in the WSJ is always excellent, with the majority of its writing staff located in New York proper.

fes.d: The name of a particular entity that otherwise might be interpreted as having a broader reference.

The entity that the speaker intends to refer to using the Entity in a more restricted sense. The Intended_referent is typically a part of the referent that the hearer might have identified based on the broader use of the Entity.

name: Proportion
d: Criteria exist that identify a particular Subset of a Group of things into members and non-members. In this frame, a comparative relationship is determined which indicates the size of the Subset relative to the larger Group, expressed as the Ratio.

ex.t: Urban areas have> a higher teen suicide rate than rural areas.

fes.d: A representation of the conditions upon which membership to a Subset of a Group is determined.
The members of a Group that fulfill particular Criteria to belong to a Subset of the Group.
A general collection of entities which are judged against the Criteria to determine membership in a Subset.
A description of how the Ratio compares to expectations.
The numerical representation of the size of the Subset relative to the size of the Group.

name: Proportional_quantity
d: The Denoted_quantity is (generally) an imprecise characterization of the quantity of Individuals or a Mass, made with reference to a relatively easily and precisely imaginable Reference_quantity.

ex.t: It took about three hours, but we 're done now.
But there were barely 300 in the whole district. DNI
Put in right around a pinch and a half. DNI

fes.d: The quantity denoted by phrases headed by the Target.
A substance that is being quantified.
A collection of entities, either quantifiable physical beings (e.g. toads) or quantifiable units whether physical or not (e.g. dollars).
A property of the Denoted_quantity.
A relatively precise quantity in some oft-used form that is used as the basis for defining the Denoted_quantity.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Protecting
d: Some Protection prevents a Danger from harming an Asset.

ex.t: The rubber on her sneakers protected her from the mud.
The coral reefs shielded the coastline from the worst of the waves.
A growing number of sustainable farmers are preserving agricultural variety and protecting biodiversity by raising ?heritage? or ?heirloom? varieties.

fes.d: The person, entity, or action that prevents harm to an Asset.
The place where the Danger threatened the Asset.
The time when the Danger threatens.
A situation that could damage the Asset.
Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protection which might be lost or damaged.
An event involving the Protection that removes the Asset from potential harm through the Danger.
An entity directed by a volitional agent acting as a Protection which interacts with an undergoer to accomplish the security of the Asset from harm by the Danger.

Any description of the protecting event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases of agentive Protection, it may indicate salient characteristics of an agent that also affect the action (carefully).

Tthis FE is used for phrases that describe the protecting event as a whole. It applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. It also applies to descriptions of the protecting event as a role filler in another frame.
A description or characteristic of the Protection.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the act of protecting logically follows.
FN: This FE denotes the length of time in which the Asset is protected.
FN: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
FN: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the protecting event.

name: Protest
d: A Protester (or Protesters) expresses a strong opinion either in support of or against an Issue, or the Action(s) of a Side which relate to the Issue. The public expression of support or opposition often involves multiple Protesters participating in an orginized assembly in a public area.

ex.t: Several hundred Tibetans, already worried by inflation, took to the streets to protest at the new measures.
Fourteen people were killed in the demonstration for the unemployed.

fes.d: The individual (or individuals) who holds an opinion on an Issue or Side.
The matter, usually concerning a course of action, which the Protester has an positive or negative opinion about.
The party or individual (generally associated with a particular position on an Issue) that the Protester sides with.
The Degree to which the Protester supports or opposes something, or expresses views on the Issue.
The time period during which the Protesters express their opinions.
The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Protester's expressing his or her views on the Issue logically follows.
An action taken by a Side or a view that the Side takes on an issue which the Protester either supports or opposes.
This FE describes the person or element that is protesting.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

Any description of the a Protest which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protester that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The location where the Protester takes Sides on an Issue .
The length of time of the protest.
The frequency with which the protest occurs.

name: Provide_lodging
d: A Host provides a temporary Residence for a Lodger.

ex.t: We housed her in our home for a while.

fes.d: The Host is the individual (or group of individuals) that own or control the Residence and allow the Lodger to temporarily stay there.
The Lodger is the individual who is given permission to lodge in the Residence.
The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Host provides lodging.
The Time is when the Host provides a Residence to the Lodger
The Place is where the Host provides a temporary Residence.
The Purpose is the goal of the Host in allowing the Lodger to stay.
The Explanation is the cognitive cause of the Host's granting of permission.

Any description of the provision of lodging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Host that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action of the Host whereby they communicate or enact the granting of permission to stay in the Residence.
The location controlled by the Host which the Lodger stays at temporarily.

name: Proximity_image_schema
d: A Profiled_region is picked out which is near to (or far from) the Ground to a certain Degree. The Profiled_region cannot contact or overlap the location of the Ground, as this is categorically different--see Contact_image_schema and Collocation_image_schema.

fes.d: A region of space located relative to a Ground that is maximally relevant near the Ground, with decreasing applicability away from the Ground.
An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.
The amount of deviation from an idealized expected distance of the Profiled_region from the Ground.
A region of space located relative to a Ground that is not relevant near the Ground, with increasing applicability away from the Ground.

name: Public_services
d: This frame concerns permanent organizations (the Institutions) that are intended to help members of the Target_group in a particular Domain with a Service_action. Most or all relevant members of the Target_group have a direct relationship with the Institution.

ex.t: The Red Cross Tracing and Message Service is a service for finding and reuniting families separated by war and disaster.
First and foremost, Radio-Canada is a public service.
The California Child Protective Service investigated the family based on a complaint filed by the son's former principal.

fes.d: A permanent organization with a socially important purpose.
The concern of the Institution-- broadly speaking, the aspect of society that they affect.
The members of the public whom the Institution is intended to serve.
The action performed or enabled by the Institution for the Target_group.

name: Publishing
d: A Publisher makes a Work of an Author (or authors) available to some public Audience for general enjoyment, examination, and reference. The Medium of a Work can vary; examples include books, TV programs, movies, and radio shows. Publication normally involves a number of other events, such as editing and advertising of the Work, and mass production and sales of a represenation of the Work; thus in the most elaborated version of publication, there are a number of other potential roles, such as editor, publicist/advertizer, distributor, printer, etc., but none of these show up as separate, syntactically distinguished roles for the LUs in this frame.

ex.t: Doubleday is publishing my newest novel next week.
I 'm publishing my next one with Random House .

fes.d: The entity that acts on behalf of the Author to release the Work to the public.
The format utilized by the Author to create the Work.
The creation of the Author that is made public by the Publisher.
The date when the Work is available or is expected to be available.
The subset of the population that the Work is targeted towards or released to.

The person or entity that is responsible for the detailed construction of the content of the Work. It is normally expressed in place of the Publisher FE, but the Publisher may cooccur with Author, appearing as an adjunct.
The situation that the Author or Publisher hopes to bring about by publishing.
The location where the Publisher releases the work.

Any description of the action that clarifies, in a holistic way, the details of how the publication event unfolded, including comparisons to other events ('the same way') and states of performers of the action that influence the act itself ('peevishly').
The action taken by the Author or Publisher that makes the Work publicly available.

name: Punctual_perception
d: A Perceiver briefly perceives a Phenomenon, often resulting in partial or uncertain perception. A Body_part that enables the perception may be mentioned, either metonymically replacing the Perceiver or in addition to the Perceiver.

ex.t: I 've been waiting here to catch a glimpse of the snow leopard for seven hours.
If you go in there, you 'll get an eyeful. INI

fes.d: The being who has a perceptual experience, generally construed to be not on purpose.
The entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs.
The Body_part is the location on the body where the perceptual experience takes place. It is typically expressed in a PP.
The Location_of_protagonist during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a from-PP.

This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.
The state of the Perceiver during the event of perception.
The perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver.
Any description of properties of perception, such as: clearly, loudly, etc.
The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.
The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.
The Time, generally construed as punctual, at which the Perceiver or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.
The length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Purpose
d: An Agent wants to achieve a Goal, or an object. A Means has been created or is used to allow the creator or a user to achieve a Goal. The Goal is a state of the world that does not currently hold but which the Agent wants to realize and is planning and/or working towards. In some cases, it is difficult to decide whether a noun phrase metonymically stands for the Agent or the Means (e.g. The goal [of this paper/seminar/project] is to determine ...). We mark these phrases as Agent on the first layer but also annotate them as Means on a second annotation layer. In some cases a Restrictor on the Goal state of affairs can be given prominence as a separate constituent. Talking about Goals frequently includes the mention of a Domain to which the Agent's Goal is relevant.

ex.t: The modest American goal of a threefold increase in capacity recognises this fact .
The object of the tutorial is to help a student concentrate on his writing skills
The prime goal of the programme was to help develop processes of scientific thinking in children .

fes.d: The volitional actor who intends to achieve a goal.
The action or state of affairs that the Agent wants to achieve.
A Means is an object or action that is used or designed to achieve a particular Goal.
This frame element expresses a sphere of activity within which an Agent has a Goal.
This Frame Element expresses a time period during which an Agent had a particular Goal.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a spatial or temporal or individual framework relative to which the Goal is said to hold. More than one Restrictor can be mentioned.
This FE marks expressions that indicate an Attribute for which it is the Agent's goal that it have or reach a particular Value .
This FE marks expressions that indicate which Value the Agent wants the Attribute to reach.

name: Putting_out_fire
d: An Agent causes a Fire to no longer burn.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing an actor or an undergoer of an action during their participation in the event.
This FE identifies the state of an Agent that affects the nature of the event as the Agent brings about the end of the Fire.
This FE identifies the Result of the event.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent puts out the Fire.
This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.
The individual or group that causes the Fire to no longer burn.
The combustion process that the Agent causes to end.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent puts out a Fire
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent puts out the Fire.
This FE describes the how near the Agent is to puting out the Fire.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Quantified_mass
d: This frame contains transparent nouns (and some adjectives) denoting quantities of a Mass or of Individuals. As opposed to aggregate words such as group, set, these Quantity do not have a status as Wholes on their own. Initially, at least, we have annotated both Quantity of Masses and of Individuals in this frame, though we may split the frame along these lines later on.

ex.t: He found them in the deluge of papers on his desk.

fes.d: The Quantity-denoting Target word.
A substance that is being quantified.
A collection of entities.
A property of the Quantity.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Quantity
d: This frame contains nouns denoting Quantities of a specified Entity and their numerical Values. Note that the nouns in this frame DO NOT convey a gradable amount on thier own.

ex.t: His heart attack was caused by a high cholesterol level.
His cholesterol level was 124 mg/dL.

fes.d: Entity identifies the concept or substance being quantified by a Quantity.
Identifies the Quantity-denoting target word.
Value identifies the numerical amount of the Entity.
A characterization of the Quantity.

name: Quarreling
d: A group of Arguers (also expressible as Arguer1 and Arguer2) express incompatible opinions or beliefs about an Issue.

ex.t: We bickered about semantics for an hour.

fes.d: A group of people in an argument.
A person who is arguing with Arguer2.
The person who is being argued with by Arguer1.
The the thing the the Arguers are arguing over or about.
The frequency with which the Arguers have a disagreement.
A state of the Arguers, Arguer1, or Arguer2 which saliently affects the perception of the action.
The amount of time that the Arguers spend in the altercation.

A description of the dispute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Arguers that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The action that the Arguers perform in order to quarrel with each other.
The equipment, language, or other entity that the Arguers use to pursue their argument.
The degree to which the argument has been finished.
The state-of-affairs that the Arguers or Arguer1 hope to bring about.
The location at which the Arguers quarrel
The time when the argument takes place.

name: Questioning
d: The words in this frame have to do with a Speaker asking an Addressee a question which calls for a reply (as opposed to making a request which calls for an action on the part of the Addressee).

ex.t: We asked Ruby what kind of food they ate.
Yeats was able to interrogate the spirit world about his relationship with Maude.

fes.d: The person asking a question generally occurs as the External Argument of verb and noun targets:

The Addressee is most frequently the NP Object of a target verb. However, with the verb inquire, Addressee can only occur as an of-PP and with a noun target, Addressee occurs in a PP Complement or as a possessive :

The Message, or content of the question, usually takes the form of a direct quote or an embedded question with a verb target: With noun targets, Message is not common (as Topic occurs more frequently). However, Message does occur in a PP Complement with the noun question:
Topic occurs very frequently in this frame with both noun and verb targets. It generally occurs as a PP Complement:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the question:
Manner of performing the request.
The body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal Cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal Cause is expressed in a PP Complement:
The time at which the questioning occurs.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Quitting
d: An Employee voluntarily leaves the service of an Employer.

ex.t: Leah quit her job after one month because of an evil force.
It's Time for Glenn Hubbard to Quit as CEA Chair
Its chief executive officer has resigned amid a reorganization that will also eliminate about 20 percent of its work force.

fes.d: The person who is obligated to perform some task in order to receive compensation.
The person (or institution) in whose employ the Employee stood.
The Field that one works in.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee leaves the job.
This FE identifies the place where the Employee quits the employment of the Employer.
The label given to a particular type of service that the employer quits.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employee quits the employment of the Employer.
This FE identifies the Time when an Employee quits the employment of the Employer.
The Explanation for which the Employee quits.
The means whereby the act of quitting is accomplished

name: Quitting_a_place
d: A Self_mover leaves an initial Source location. The Path by which the Self_mover departs, and the Intended_goal of the Direction may also be mentioned. In many words which evoke this frame, there is an additional implication that the Self_mover is discontented with the Source location.

ex.t: I left San Francisco for Vancouver.

fes.d: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion. (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)
Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.
The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.
A second moving object that moves in coordination with the Self_mover.
The state of the Self_mover during the action.
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.
The direction in which the Self_mover goes.
The time at which the motion takes place.
The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.
The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.
The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.
A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.
The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.
A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.) The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.
The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

name: Race_descriptor
d: This frame covers LUs that describe the race of a Person.

ex.t: Carlos is hispanic, or so he says.

fes.d: The Person whose race is being described.

name: Range
d: There is a certain physical Distance within which some other entity can participate in an Event (typically perception or manipulation) with the Participant. Alternatively, the Event may be indicated metonymically by a Instrument . [Note the connection with *Distance, Sufficiency, and Capability. Words in this frame can generally be paraphrased "close enough to be able to".]

ex.t: I'm sorry, but he was well within the blast range.
They are now within our missile range.
They are now within our missile 's range.

fes.d: A type of occurrence whose effects extend a certain distance.
An entity that is conceived as driving the Event.
An entity which is deployable by the Participant to interact with things within a certain distance.
The spatial extent over which the Participant can interact in an Event.
The conditions under which the description of a Participant's range holds.

name: Rank
d: This frame contains nouns denoting a rank or level within an established hierarchy.

ex.t: His rank is colonel.

fes.d: The Rank itself, usually denoted by the noun.
An entity which holds a particular Rank.

name: Ranked_expectation
d: An Entity is rated as unexpected for its context in terms of its magnitude. Either some different type of Entity with a different scope would be expected, or a different amount of the Entity. Although there are some words that overlap between this frame and Completeness, the words in this frame indicate specifically that the magnitude of the Entity is different from what is expected, rather than grading an entity as to whether all its parts are present.
