Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.
The individual in whose interest it is to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.
An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain
An individual that has to provide the Required_entity or see to it that the Requirement state of affairs holds.

name: Rescuing
d: An Agent saves a Patient or an Asset from a Harmful_situation.

ex.t: Israeli commandos rescued the hostages and left.
His German shepherd saved him from drowing once.
She saved my life on the bridge yesterday.

fes.d: The sentient being who rescues the Patient or Asset from the Harmful_situation.
The living being who is rescued by the Agent.
The entity that is judged to be valueable which might be lost or damaged by the Harmful_situation.
An event that occurs which could result in injury or harm to the Patient or Asset.
The time at which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.
The way in which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.
The location at which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.
The setting in which the rescuing act takes place.
The tool with which the Agent saves the Patient or Asset.
The means by which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.
The purpose for which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.
The extent to which the Patient or Asset is actually saved.

name: Research
d: A Researcher (an individual a group or institution) attempts to answer a Question by means of consulting literature, observation, or conducting experiments in a particular Field pertinent to the Question. The Question may be underspecified in the form of a Topic.

ex.t: Simmons and Nadel did research pertaining to Ardea purpurea and Egretta garzetta in 1998

fes.d: The people engaged in a research endeavor.
An area of inquiry.
A significant unanswered open proposition which the Researcher is attempting to resolve.
A phenomenon or idea involved in a Question.
The time when the research is carried out.
The experimentations, observations, or other procedures performed by the Researcher in order to find an answer to the Question.
A group of entities that are studied by the Researcher to answer the Question. The studied group need not be the only kind of entity that provides evidence for answering the research Question.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Researcher that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Purpose indicates an action that the Researcher intends to accomplish by performing research.
The Duration_of_state is the period of time over which the research takes place.
The physical place where the research is carried out.
The Type, or subclass of research.

name: Reserving
d: In this frame, a Booker brings about a situation where an Organization plans to provide Services to a Client at a particular Scheduled_time. The Organization has authority over when Services are provided to whom. The Booker usually has to communicate and negotiate with the Organization to plan the Services for a mutually agreeable Scheduled_time. Usually, there is a Payment as well. In many cases, the Booker may be the same as the Client or the Organization. When the Booker is also the Organization providing the service, as in the first sentence below, we annotate Booker on the first layer and Organization on the second. Realizing that the Booker is also the Organization providing the service is an inference, as we can see by comparing the following two examples. In the first, it seems clear that the hotel is providing the service. In the second, it is clear that the hotel is not providing the service. In the frequent case where the Booker is the same as the Client, we annotate Booker on the first layer and Client on the second. Client is on the second layer since, in most cases, it is an inference that may be wrong. For example, in the following sentence, the annotation indicates that Patrick is the Client. However, it is also possible that Patrick is reserving a table for a party that doesn't even include himself:

ex.t: We can book you a boatride on the Somme or a special tour of the Louvre .
Now booking trips to Cancunfor only $50 ! CNI INI
The hotel gave us a reservation for two nights .

fes.d: The entity that is intended to receive the Services of the Organization.
The goods or labor that the Client requests the Organization preserve for future consumption or rendering.
The entity that enters into its records the request of the Client to retain Services in the future.
The future point in time when the Client arranges for the Organization to provide Services.
The entity that contacts the Organization directly. In many if not most cases, a Booker is also a Client, but the roles may also be separated, e.g. a travel agent.
Any description of the event as a whole ("the same way") or a characteristic of the Booker during the action that holistically affects the event ("sloppily").
The location the Booker performs the action.
The situation that the Booker intends to bring about by reserving.
An action or methodology used by the Booker to bring the reservation about.
The time at which the reserving event takes place.
The amount paid to the Organization in exchange for the Services.

name: Reshaping
d: In this frame a Deformer deforms a Patient possibly against a Resistant_surface such that it undergoes a shape-change from its canonical or original shape into the Configuration, a new shape. Some of these words indicate that the Configuration is an undesirable alteration of the norm, and in such cases the lexical unit is marked with the semantic type Negative_judgement. This frame does not include senses that specifically indicate causing harm to a living being.

ex.t: Ellen crumpled the paper into a ball.
Michael flattened the can against his head.
Mix butter and sardines very thoroughly , mashing them with a fork until you have a smooth paste. CNI

fes.d: The Deformer is the one who does the reshaping.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Deformer affects the Patient.
The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.
The FE Means identifies the means by which the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.
The Patient is the entity acted on and that undergoes a change.
The Place indicates where the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.
The FE Time identifies when the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.
The Result is the shape the Patient becomes.
The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Deformer presses the Patient.
The Locus is the locus of the reshaping action; it is essentially a simultaneous Instrument and Resistant_surface.
The Cause is an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The FE Iterations indicates the number of times the reshaping has occurred.
The Explanation indicates a state of affairs that the Deformer is responding to in performing the reshaping.
The degree to which the Patient is reshaped.
The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the reshaping.
The location that the Patient ends up in.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The conditions under which the Patient is shaped.
The state of the Patient with respect to the change that the Deformer brings about by making the adjustment.
A state that holds of the Patient or a relation that holds among the constituent parts of the Patient as a result of the arranging action.

name: Residence
d: This frame has to do with people (the Residents) residing in Locations, sometimes with a Co-resident.

ex.t: Peter lives in New York.
Sue is an inhabitant of Los Angeles.

fes.d: The individual(s) that reside at the Location.
The place in which somebody resides.
A person or group of people that the resident is staying with or among.
Frequency at which event occurs.
The state of a Resident during their residence.
Manner of performing an action
An act of the Resident that enables them to reside in the Location.
This FE refers to the Time when the Resident resides.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Resolve_problem
d: An Agent resolves an outstanding Problem by finding its solution, explanation, answer, etc. Alternatively, some non-agentive Cause may resolve the Problem. The Means, Degree, Time and Place may also be expressed.

ex.t: As it turns out, putting all of my eggs in one basket completely solved all of my problems.
Students finally worked through all of the difficult problems by working together.

fes.d: The Agent finds the solution or explanation to the outstanding mystery or Problem.
The Problem is the predicament or mystery that is resolved.
The Cause is the non-Agentive event or state of affairs that brings about the resolution of the Problem.
The Means is an intermediate action taken by the Agent in order to resolve the Problem.
This FE indicates the Time at which the Problem is resolved.
This FE indicates the location at which the Problem is resolved.
The Degree to which the Agent or Cause resolves the problem.

Any description of the resolution, such as secondary effects ( quietly ) or comparisons of events ( the same way ). In agentive cases, Manner may also describe salient characteristics of the Agent which affect the action. ( carefully, dilligently, deliberately etc. )
The Resultant_situation is any situation which arises as a result of resolving a Problem .
The Outcome is the failure or success of resolving a Problem .
The Containing_event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the resolution of the Problem occurs.
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Problem is resolved.
The Instrument is an entity used for resolving the Problem .
This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the resolution of a Problem .
This FE identifies the length of time taken to resolve a Problem . The government resolved the beach ball crisis in just 22 hours.
Role is used for the capacity in which the Agent resolves a Problem or the role of the Problem in being resolved, and is expressed in as-PPs.
Frequency describes how often the Agent or Cause resolves this problem.
This FE identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the Problem is resolved.
A person who participates in resolving a Problem along with the Agent.
The state of affairs that the Agent is trying to bring about by solving the Problem in the specified way.

name: Respond_to_proposal
d: A Speaker addresses a Proposal made by an Interlocutor, either agreeing to it or rejecting it. Agreeing entails a social responsibility on the Speaker to bring about some state of affairs encoded in the Proposal.

ex.t: They were rebuffed again in the larger city of Provo. CNI
Last month Mr Duisenberg delivered a sharp rebuff to Mr Welteke.
He rebuffed Singh's every overture, relentlessly pursuing a cap on India's nuclear capability.

fes.d: The Speaker is the person who communicates the reply or response.

This is the person who made the Proposal to the Speaker and to whom the Speaker communicates their response. This frame element stands in for the Proposal and is only licensed when the Proposal can be understood from the context.
As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in".
The Proposal is the prior communication or action to which a response is given.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly).
Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.
This FE identifies the Means by the Speaker responds to the Proposal .
The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker mental or emotional state.
The location in which the Speaker makes a verbal response.
The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.
An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of response events.
Role denotes the capacity in which the Interlocutor is judged.
The Group is the set of people within which the Respond_to_proposal is occuring.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.

name: Response
d: An Agent performs a Response action in consequence of a Trigger event. In many cases, a non-agentive Responding_entity causes the Response after the Trigger occurs.

ex.t: I respond to earthquakes by hiding under my desk.

fes.d: The means action whereby the Agent responds to the Trigger.
A non-agentive entity that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
An event that impinges upon the Agent or Responding_entity and produces a Response from it.
The point in time when the Agent or Responding_entity manifests its Response to the Trigger .
A characterization of the Responding_entity, Agent, or their Response action.
The location in which the Response action takes place.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the Response action.
The intentional Agent that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
A particular feature of the Responding_entity or Agent that is involved in the Response action.
The capacity of of the Agent is their Response act.

name: Response_scenario
d: A Trigger elicits a Response by some Responding_entity or an Agent.

fes.d: A non-agentive entity that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
An event that impinges upon the Agent or Responding_entity and produces a Response from it.
The means action whereby the Agent responds to the Trigger.
The intentional Agent that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
A characterization of the Responding_entity, Agent, or their Response action.
The location in which the Response action takes place.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the Response action.
The point in time when the Agent or Responding_entity manifests its Response to the Trigger .

name: Responsibility
d: An Agent is responsible for having intentionally performed an Act or for being the or a primary instigator behind the Act. There is often a sense of negative evaluation of the Agent for having done so. Note: the noun responsibility in this frame frequently occurs with take and claim. These words are considered controllers (rather than supports), as they express events of communication rather than the static relationship of responsibility.

ex.t: It has been determined that a relatively unknown terrorist group is responsible for the recent attacks.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Act that the Agent performs intentionally.
The Agent performs the intentional act.
This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.
The Domain within which the Agent acts.
The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.
The length of time over which an Act was committed multiple times.
The Result of the Agent performing the Act.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.
This FE gives a description of the Intentionally_act event.
The degree to which the Agent bears responsibility for performing the Act.

name: Rest
d: One Part of a larger Whole has been mentioned, is inferrable, or is available in the discourse setting and the previously unmentioned part, the Rest, is now mentioned.

ex.t: The lenses , like the rest of the exoskeleton, are made of calcite.
They see social policy work as a natural complement to bureau work.

fes.d: A Part of a larger Whole that has been mentioned in prior discourse or is available in the discourse setting.
The previously unmentioned part of the Whole.
The larger entitiy or group that is fully made up of the Part and the Rest.

name: Result_of_attempt_scenario
d: An Agent and their Action succeed or fail inasmuch as the result of an Action matches the Goal that they hope to bring about by the Action.

fes.d: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal.
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
This FE identifies the means by which the Goal is achieved (or not).
This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails.
The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the Action.
The place where an attempt succeeds or fails..
A participant function in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.
This FE is applied to expressions which indicate the prevailing physical conditions for the event, or some concurrent states of affairs.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.

This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part.
The extent to which the Action succeeds or fails.

name: Resurrection
d: A Protagonist which had been dead returns to life.

ex.t: He'll come back from the dead at 11:03PM exactly, since that's what his suicide note indicated.

fes.d: The being or entity that becomes living again.
The time at which the resurrection occurs.
An explanation of how the state-of-affairs came to pass.
The state of the Protagonist before resurrection.
The state of the Protagonist which results from resurrection.
The state of the Protagonist during the resurrection.
The location at which the Protagonist returns from the dead.

name: Retaining
d: In this frame an Agent continues to possess a Theme for a Duration of time.

ex.t: In her heart she must retain bitterness against those who had killed him.
I kept the iPhone Sally gave me.

fes.d: The person who has possession of the Theme.
The entity which the Agent possesses for a Duration.
The amount of time for which the Agent is in possession of the Theme.
The location where the Agent keeps the Theme.
The way the Agent retains possession of the Theme.
The time at which the Agent has possession of the Theme.
The means by which the Agent retains the Theme.

name: Reveal_secret
d: A Speaker reveals Information that was previously secret to an Addressee. In some cases, the Addressee is expected to keep the Information from other parties. The Information may be damaging to the reputation of the Speaker. Instead of (or in addition to) a Speaker, a Medium may also be mentioned. Likewise, a Topic may be stated instead of Information. Some lexical units in this frame imply that the Addressee has already been confronted with the Information.

ex.t: Could it be true that Martin himself was the one who spilled the beans on Pops and Brad's planned wedding?

fes.d: The Speaker is the sentient entity that reveals the Information (whether spoken or written).
The Addressee is the person to whom the Information is revealed.
Information identifies the content that the Speaker reveals to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.
The Topic is the subject matter about which the Speaker is speaking. It normally only appears with noun targets, or in special constructions.

Manner is any description of the revelation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the revelation (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully, maliciously).
The degree to which Information is revealed.
An act whereby the Speaker makes a revelation.
The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to the revelation.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.
The state of the Speaker during the statement.
The Time when the revelation is made.
The FE specifies the Place where the Information is revealed.
An alternative description of expressed action.

This FE is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion. In Release 1.2, this FE has various frame-specific names including Location of perceiver, or Location of participant; it was even (incorrectly) labelled Place in some frames.
This FE identifies an event during which the Speaker reveals Information.
The medium in which the secret Information origninally resided.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole especially any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames.
This FE describes the length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
Frequency is defined as the number of times the Reveal_secret event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."
A characteristic of the revealed secret.

name: Revenge
d: This frame concerns the infliction of punishment in return for a wrong suffered. An Avenger performs a Punishment on a Offender as a consequence of an earlier action by the Offender, the Injury. The Avenger inflicting thePunishment need not be the same as the Injured_Party who suffered the Injury, but the Avenger does have to share the judgment that the Offender's action was wrong. The judgment that the Offender had inflicted an Injury is made without regard to the law.

ex.t: (1) They took revenge for the deaths of two loyalist prisoners.
(2) Lachlan went out to avenge them.
(3) The next day, the Roman forces took revenge on their enemies..

fes.d: The Avenger exacts revenge from the Offender for the Injury.
This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.
Depictive identifies a phrase describing the actor of an action.
The Offender has committed the earlier Injury for which the Avenger seeks revenge.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the revenge is performed.
This frame element refers to the Manner in which the Avenger exacts their revenge from the Offender.
The Avenger carries out a Punishment in order to exact revenge on the Offender.
This FE identifies the Place where the revenge occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the revenge is performed.
The Injury is the injurious action committed by the Offender against the Injured_Party. This Frame Element need not always be realized, although it is conceptually necessary.
This FE identifies the Result of inflicting punishment for a wrong suffered.
This FE identifies the Time when the revenge occurs.

This frame element identifies the constituent that encodes who or what suffered the Injury at the hands of the Offender. Sometimes, an abstract concept such a person's honour or their blood is presented as the element that has suffered the Injury. These also constitute instances of Injured_party
The length of time that the Avenger seeks revenge for the Injury.

name: Revolution
d: An Agent brings about a radical change in leadership by removing the Current_leadership and potentially dismantling the Current_order, outside recognized means of doing so (e.g., elections).

ex.t: Recent reports indicate that the local troops have mutinied against their superiors.

fes.d: The individual or group within a society that overturns the Current_leadership.
The people currently in power, whom the Agent attempts to overthrow.
The currently-existing system of authority or government.
The location of the revolution.
The time when the revolution takes place.
The means by which the revolution is carried out.
The degree to which the Agent defeats and removes the Current_leadership or removes the Current_order.
A description of the Agent or revolution not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Rewards_and_punishments
d: An Agent (the punisher or rewarder) performs a Response_action on an Evaluee for a Reason, the Evaluee's actions or beliefs. Means and Instrument may also be indicated. The goal of the punishment/reward is to discourage/encourage the actions or beliefs. Words in this frame presuppose that a judgment of the Evaluee has occurred and that the Evaluee is (or becomes) aware of the judgment. This judgment was performed by a cognizer which is either the same as the Agent, or, minimally, a representative of the same institution.

ex.t: His punishment of the prisoners was too harsh.
Her punishment was too harsh.
The penalty for this crime is death.

fes.d: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment has made and to whom reward/punishment is dealt. With verbs, the Evaluee is typically expressed as Object.
Manner of performing the reward or punishment.
The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward.
Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Agent's judgment. It is usually a 'for'-PP, e.g.
Result of the reward or punishment.
Where the event takes place.
When the event occurs.
The Agent is the person doing the rewarding or punishing.
The Instrument with which the reward or punishment is carried out.
The Purpose of the reward or punishment.
The reward or punishment given to the Evaluee by the Agent.
Degree of reward or punishment.
Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the reward or punishment.

name: Ride_vehicle
d: In this frame a Theme is moved by a Vehicle which is not directly under their power. The Source, Path, Goal, or Area of the motion may be indicated. The Distance traveled or the Speed of motion may also be indicated. A Route or Roadmay be present and the Manner in which the Theme moves may be given. There is shared vocabulary between this frame and Carrying and Operate_vehicle. It is differentiated from Operate_vehicle in that the vehicle is not under the subject's control. It is differentiated from Carrying because the vehicle is not being used to transport goods.

ex.t: Mrs. Smith rode on the train.
Sally flew 3000 miles from San Francisco to New York.
Every day, Martin rode the bus on highway 880.

fes.d: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle.
The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a PP-complement or the direct object.
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.
The Path describes the trajectory of the motion.
The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion.
The Distance is the extent of the motion.
The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes.
The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs.
The Area is the location where the motion takes place.
The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels.
The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles.
The state of the Theme or Vehicle during the motion.
When the riding takes place.
A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme.
The Purpose for which the Theme rides a vehicle.

name: Rising_to_a_challenge
d: A Protagonist, by exerting great effort, comes to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity that is judged to be difficult for them to participate in, either due to their inherent properties or due to temporary Circumstances.

ex.t: In conclusion, our staff rose to the challenge in developing the necessary training programs and delivery methods.
Dr Runcie rose to the occasion with a simple address. DNI
There was still clearly much to do, but the governor and his staff had begun to rise to the task.

fes.d: The Protagonist who is exerting effort to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.
The Activity that the Protagonist expends efforts towards.
The extent to which the Protagonist exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity as a result of expending effort to get themselves ready.
The Circumstances under which the Protagonist exerts effort to meet the pre-conditions necessary for engaging in the Activity.
An entity, event, or state of affairs that causes the Protagonist to expend the effort necessary to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.
A characteristic or behavior of the Protagonist that is considered when judging whether the Protagonist might participate in the Activity.
An action performed by the Protagonist which enables them to overcome the difficulties and engage in the Activity.
The time at which the Protagonist through expenditure of effort becomes capable of engaging in the Activity. crisis.
The location in which the Protagonist expends effort to become capable of engaging in the Activity.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (eagerly).

name: Risk_scenario
d: An Asset is in a particular Situation, which has a likelihood of leading to or inviting a Harmful_event which will negatively affect the Asset.

fes.d: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.
An event that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.
The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset, the Situation, and state indicated by the target itself.
The Time during which the degree of safeness holds.
The Place at which the degree of safeness holds.

name: Risky_situation
d: A particular Situation is likely (or unlikely) to result in a harmful event befalling an Asset. The Situation may be a state, an activity, or some focal entity that must be inferred to be part of some larger Situation involving both it and the Asset. Although the idea of a harmful event is crucial to the understanding of this frame, it is not expressible as an argument of the LUs in this frame. See the Run_risk frame for discussion on differentiation regarding the noun risk.

ex.t: Is climate change dangerous for mankind?
Customers can make complaints about unsafe products.
The primary risk is to our infrastructure.

fes.d: The Situation which may lead to a harmful event.
Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Situation and the state indicated by the target itself.
A particular location for which the Situation is safe. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location make various Situations safe or unsafe.
The time period during which the Situation has the specified level of safety.
The Domain in which the Situation is safe.
A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset.
How often the Asset encounters the Risky_situation.
The Circumstances in which an Asset is at risk.

name: Rite
d: This frame concerns rituals performed in line with religious beliefs or tradition.

ex.t: In certain fertility rites in Burma , a woman desirous of offspring is required not only to approach the King Cobra but to plant a kiss on its mouth .
He was ordered a priest in 1944. CNI

fes.d: This is the religious or cultural leader who performs and/or leads the rite.
The FE Member describes the member of the religious or cultural group who participates in/undergoes the rite.
Organization identifies the institution in which the rite is prescribed.
The action that is taken to perform the ritual.
Manner of performing the rite
When the rite is performed
Where the rite takes place.
This FE identifies the Instrument used to perform a particular rite.
This FE identifies the state which the rite is hoped or intended to bring about.
The type of ritual or ceremony being performed.
This FE indicates an object on which a rite is performed.
Rites may confer a New_status on a participant (e.g. rank, membership).
The Guardian is the member of the Organization who instigates the rite for someone of which they are a guardian.

name: Roadways
d: This frame involves stable Roadways which connect two stable Endpoints, the Source and the Goal. Being physical objects, these Roadways may have Names and Characteristics; they are also made of a Material. They also cover ground, so they may have a Path or a Relative_location that the travel occurs in.

ex.t: We crossed the brick road.
I prefer to travel on highway I-80.
This is the only highway between Lodi and Sonoma.

fes.d: The Roadway is the roadway that connects locations.
The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.
The Goal is one of the Endpoints of the Roadway treated as a goal.
The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Roadway.
The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Roadway.
The Name is the name of the Roadway.
This is the setting through which the Roadway goes.
The Use is the purpose of the Roadway.
The Direction is the direction or directions the Roadway runs.
The Relative_location is where the Roadway is located.
The Material is what the Roadway is constructed from.
The Frequency_of_use is the state of the Roadway with regard to the number of people who are using the Roadway or typically use it.
The Abundant_entities are the entities which occupy the space denoted by the Roadway.
The Length is the distance the Roadway extends.
A subpart of the Roadway.

name: Robbery
d: These are words describing situations in which a Perpetrator wrongs a Victim by taking something (Goods) from them. In some cases, the Source location from which the Goods were taken is used to metonymically refer to the Victim. The robbery can be done in a particular Manner (for example, forcefully) and via a specific Means (for example, by threatening the Victim). As opposed to Theft, Robbery focuses on the harm to the Victim and on the Source location from which the Goods have been removed, rather than the Goods themselves.

ex.t: Half of the team held up the tellers while the others were stationed to report the arrival of police.

fes.d: The Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) that takes the Goods away by force or threats.
The Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the Goods before they are taken away by the Perpetrator.
The Goods are anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.
Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location. This FE is realized in compound nouns as follows:
The Means indicates the means by which the Robbery takes place.
The Manner describes the way in which the Robbery took place.
The Place is where the Robbery occurs.
The Time indicates when the Robbery occurs.
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by the robbery.
The state of affairs that the Perpetrator has in mind which leads to the decision to commit the robbery.
The number of times a robbery event occurs.
Co-participant denotes a person that participates in a coordinated way in robbery event as the primary protagonist, the Perpetrator.

name: Rope_manipulation
d: An Agent manipulates a linear entity (the Rope) to form a Knot.

ex.t: Harry tied the rope into a slipknot.
Patty and Selma knotted the ties of their aprons.

fes.d: The Agent is the sentient being who manipulates the Rope.
The Instrument with which the Rope is manipulated.
Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
When the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
The Means by which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
The Explanation for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
The basically linear object which is manipulated by the Agent to produce a Knot.
The stable configuration of a Rope which results from tying.
Manner in which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

name: Rotting
d: In this frame a Patient, which is an organic substance, undergoes the natural process of decaying from an Initial_state to a Result.

ex.t: The leaves rotted into a mass of slime.
The dresses decayed from their former beauty.

fes.d: The Patient is the entity that undergoes a change.
The Place is where the rotting occurs.
The Time indicates when the rotting occurs.
The Explanation indicates the reason for which the Patient rots.
The Result is the result of the change of phase of the Patient.
The Initial_state is the original state of the Patient.
The Duration indicates the amount of time for which the Patient rots.
The Speed is the rate at which the Patient changes.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
The Degree expressions that indicate to what degree the Patient has changed.
The number of times that a rotting event takes place.

Any description of the Rotting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (horribly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
A state of affairs that entails the Patient decaying.

name: Run_risk
d: A Protagonist is described as being exposed to a potentially dangerous situation that may end in a Bad_outcome for him- or herself. An Asset which is in danger of loss may stand in for the Bad_outcome. There is no implication that the Protagonist intentionally exposes themself to the risky situation. The Protagonist may be attempting to achieve some Purpose, which involves being in a dangerous situation. The Severity of risk involved may also be expressed. NOTE: This Frame is currently in the process of being changed so that some instances of at risk.n will be moved to the Being_at_risk frame, and some will be moved to the Risky_situation frame. In the Being_at_risk frame, risk is almost always supported with at, and its external argument is the Asset. Risky_situation uses of risk include the following: but (possibly ; still under discussion) not: The most imminent RISK is that our infrastructure may not be able to handle the load. In the Risky_situation frame, the external argument is the Situation, and the Bad_outcome in not expressible. The verb risk.v will remain in the Run_risk frame, in the sense of he risked his life for his country. The construction run risk also will remain in the Run_risk frame.

ex.t: There was a risk of fire.
Original thinkers incur greater risks to their careers than their pedestrian colleagues.
Smoking poses a risk to your health.

fes.d: The person who is at risk of some Bad_outcome
The place where there is risk.
The probability of something bad happening to the Protagonist.
The time when the risk pertains.
A situation that the Protagonist would like to avoid.
Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protagonist which might be lost or damaged.
The Action that creates the risk.
The Frequency with which the Protagonist runs risks.
The desired action or goal that the Protagonist hopes to bring about.
An Explanation for why the Protagonist has put the Asset is in a dangerous situation.
The number of times that the Protagonist risks an Asset.
The Circumstances indicates the state of affairs under which the risky situation holds.
The Protagonist intends for his/her actions to benefit Beneficiary in some way.

name: Sacrificing_for
d: An Agent sacrifices an (often abstract) Asset in exchange for a Benefit which is deemed better or more worth having.

ex.t: We never sacrifice quality for price.
What are you willing to sacrifice to get a chance at winning?
Most people in that position probably would have compromised their principles. INI.

fes.d: The Agent gives up the Asset in hopes of receiving a greater Benefit.
The item which is sacrificed by the Agent.
State of the Agent or Asset.
The way that the Agent sacrifices the Asset.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
This FE indicates the Time when the Agent gives up the Asset.
The reason for which the Agent gives up the Asset.
The Agent hopes to receive or gain advantage from the Benefit as a result of giving up the Asset.

name: Satisfying
d: This frame describes an Agent or an Entity meeting or not meeting a Standard. Alternatively, an action or occurrence may be construed as an Event that meets or fails to meet the Standard.

ex.t: Will my coursework satisfy the requirements for admission?
He satisfied his son's wish by buying him a Wii.

fes.d: The volitional Agent who is in line with a Standard.
The non-agentive Entity that is in line with a Standard.
An occurrence or action that brings about the satisfaction or nonsatisfaction of a Standard.
The condition or requirement that the Agent, Entity, or Event satisfy (or not).
The Manner in which the Standard is satisfied.
The Means by which the Standard is satisfied.
The Time in which satisfaction of the Standard occurs.

name: Scarcity
d: The Quantity of a Collection occurring in a Place has a particular Measure, which is related to the amount generally needed.

ex.t: There is evidence that volatile materials have always been scarce on the Moon .
A global effort to tackle water scarcity is getting underway. INI
It is the scarceness of these precious metals that adds to their luster. INI

fes.d: The Collection whose Quantity is under consideration.
The feature of an Collection which is under discussion. This FE is incorporated by all the lexical units in this frame.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Measure from the norm or from the value for another Collection.
The Time during which the Collection is in the state of having a particular Measure for the Quantity.
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Collection has a particular Measure for the Quantity.
The measure of the Quantity, which is incorporated by the lexical units.
The location in which the Collection occurs.

name: Scheduling
d: An Agent schedules an Event to take place at a specified Scheduled_time and Place.

ex.t: Gina scheduled a dentist appointment for Monday in Berkeley.
Christa set up an afternoon meeting to discuss the new prototype.

fes.d: The sentient being who schedules an Event to take place at a Time and Place.
The incident that the Agent has scheduled to take place at a Time and Place.
The time at which the Event is scheduled to take place.
The location where the Agent has scheduled the Event to take place.
The person for whom the Event was scheduled by the Agent.
The frequency with which the Agent schedules and Event.
The means used by the Agent in order to schedule the Event.
The Agent's motivation for scheduling the Event.
The cause for the scheduling of the Event.
The way in which the Agent schedules the Event.
This FE describes the time at which the scheduling occurs.

name: Scope
d: An Event is described in terms of the diversity of entities that are affected or considered in the Event. Alternatively a Salient_entity which enables or brings about the Event can be similarly described.

ex.t: The U.S. government believes that China has not revealed the full scope of its program.
A key question is how U.S. deployment of ballistic missile defense will affect the pace and scope of Chinese strategic modernization.

fes.d: The state-of-affairs that affects a set of entities.
The feature of an Salient_entity which is under discussion.
The entity which enables or causes the Event being judged.

name: Scouring
d: A Searcher looks all over a Ground in order to find a Sought_entity. The Sought_entity is not presupposed to exist. The search activity is not concerned with the state of the Ground, which is the case in the Inspecting frame, but only with the finding of the Sought_entity, which is desirable.

ex.t: The newcomers combed the area looking for minerals
Scientists scoured the ice samples for signs of life.
Mulder rummaged through his toilet kit for a plastic razor.

fes.d: The person who is looking all over the Ground for the Sought_entity.
The location that the Searcher covers in looking for the Sought_entity.
The entity that the Searcher wants to find.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.
This FE specifies the length of the interval during which the scouring activtiy takes place.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.
An entity manipulated by the Searcher to examine the Ground.
The action of the Searcher that allows them to search the Ground.
The state-of-affairs that the Searcher hopes to bring about by searching a Ground.
The Time when the Searcher scoures the Ground.

name: Scrutinizing_for
d: A Cognizer examines a Ground closely, alert to the presence of a Phenomenon.

fes.d: The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it.
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.
The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.

name: Scrutiny
d: This frame concerns a Cognizer (a person or other intelligent being) paying close attention to something, the Ground, in order to discover and note its salient characteristics. The Cognizer may be interested in a particular characteristic or entity, the Phenomenon, that belongs to the Ground or is contained in the Ground (or to ensure that such a property of entity is not present). Some words in this frame allow alternate expressions of the Groundand the Phenomenon:

ex.t: We searched the yard  for my contact lens.

fes.d: The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument:
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon. This FE can be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement.
Phenomenon identifies the property that belongs to an entity or that the entity contains. Typically, it is expressed as a for-PP.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
This FE is used for the Means by which the Cognizer to scrutinize the Ground.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
Direction is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver, that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.
Some of the words in this frame occur with a constituent that expresses the desired outcome of the Scrutiny. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for or a to-marked VP Complement.
The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument:
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.
The Time when the Cognizer is scrutinizing the Ground.

name: Searching_scenario
d: A Cognizer seeks a Phenomenon within the Ground.

fes.d: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground in order to find instances of a type of Phenomenon.
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.
The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.
The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.

name: Secrecy_status
d: A Phenomenon, which may be an activity, state or object, is purposefully hidden from the awareness of a potential Cognizer. The person responsible for the hiding of the Phenomenon is not part of this frame and cannot be syntactically realized. The potential Cognizer may be realized, but is in fact rarely expressed. A period of Time during which the Phenomenon is secret may be indicated.

ex.t: Few people would use ATMs if the content of their transaction was secret from their bank and there was no paper trail verifying the transaction. .
The protesters were not on her list, and weren't allowed in, despite the fact that the meeting was public.
Student disciplinary matters are confidential and should only be discussed with appropriate university officials

fes.d: The Phenomenon is the activity, state or object that is purposefully hidden from the awareness of a potential cognizer.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Phenomenon is hidden from cognizers.
A period of Time during which the Phenomenon is hidden from the awareness of potential cognizers.
The Cognizer is the person who might become aware of the Phenomenon if it was not concealed.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: See_through
d: A Cognizer realizes that a State_of_affairs (or Focal_entity within the State_of_affairs) is meant to deceive (the Cognizer is not necessarily the intended victim of the deception). The Cognizer comes to this belief by perception and reasoning, and not, for instance, by being informed of the true state of affairs.

fes.d: The Cognizer realizes the existence of a deception and is not misled by it.
The State_of_affairs is intended to be perceived and taken to be true even though it is not.
The Focal_entity is a part of the deception (possibly also the agent behind it) which is perceived by the Cognizer to be misleading.
An act performed by the Cognizer which enables them to figure something out.
Medium is the text created by the Cognizer to communicate that they came to believe a specified State_of_affairs.
Some verbs in this frame may occur with postverbal Topic expressions
The Degree to which the Cognizer comes to understand the State_of_affairs.
Depictive phrase describing the Cognizer.
Manner of performing an action
The location at which the Cognizer realizes the State_of_affairs.
The time at which the Cognizer discovers the State_of_affairs.

name: Seeking
d: A Cognizer_agent attempts to find some Sought_entity by examining some Ground. The success or failure of this activity (the Outcome) may be indicated. NB: This frame should be compared to the Scrutiny frame, in which the primary focus is on the Ground.

ex.t: John looked for his pencil.

fes.d: The person who attempts to find the Sought_entity.

This is the entity to which the Cognizer_agent pays attention. It is referred to as Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Sought_entity. This FE can be expressed as an NP Object (first example) or as a PP Complement (second example).
This is the entity that the Ground may contain. Typically, it is expressed as a for-PP. Some words in this frame allow alternate expressions of the Ground and the Sought_entity.
The Manner of performing an action.
An act of the Cognizer_agent that allows them to look for the Sought_entity.
The failure or success of an attempt.
A spatial setting larger than the Ground in which the Seeking event occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the Seeking occurs.
An action that the Cognizer_agent intends to accomplish by performing the search.
This FE identifies the amount of effort put into an attempt.

name: Seeking_to_achieve
d: An Agent intends and takes steps towards bringing about a State_of_affairs or, metonymically, towards acquiring a Sought_entity .

ex.t: Libya sought nuclear weapons in the 1960s.
North Korea sought several billion dollars in cash from the US during bilateral missile talks.
The talks in Berlin ended without agreement after Bora Bora sought to link large-scale economic assistance to joint recovery operations.

fes.d: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a State_of_affairs or to obtain a Sought_entity.
The entity that the Agent attempts to acquire.
The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to acquire a Sought_entity.
This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a State_of_affairs or at acquiring the Sought_entity is made.
This FE identifies the amount of effort put into an attempt.
This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.
The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.
The place where the Agent is seeking to achieve a particular State_of_affairs or to acquire a Sought_entity.
The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.
The time period over which the attempts at achieving a State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity take place.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by bringing about a particular State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity.
A state or event that the Agent wants to bring about. The Agent may but need not be a participant in that State_of_affairs.
A proposition from which the occurrence of the seeking event follows.
An individual or organization that helps the Agent bring about the State_of_affairs or delivers the Sought_entity to the Agent.
This FE introduces the underlying situation(s) in which seeking occurs.
This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the Sought_entity or State_of_affairs .

name: Self_control
d: An Agent actively (yet not always with success) attempts to keep themselves from participating in an Event. The Agent is usually pushed to the Event because of an internal urge.

ex.t: He couldn't help but peek.

fes.d: The Agent who tries to keep an Event from taking place.
The Event is the action or state of affairs that the Agent wishes to prevent.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The Place is where the Agent attempts to prevent the Event from taking place.
The Time is when the Agent prevents the Event from taking place.

name: Self_motion
d: The Self_mover, a living being, moves under its own direction along a Path. Alternatively or in addition to Path, an Area, Direction, Source, or Goal for the movement may be mentioned. Many of the lexical units in this frame can also describe the motion of vehicles (e.g., as external arguments). We treat these as belonging in this frame. Self_motion most prototypically involves individuals moving under their own power by means of their bodies. Many words also specify the manner of motion (swim, walk). This frame contains mostly words that fit this prototypical scenario, but the frame itself does not specify whether a separate vehicle is impossible, necessary, or unspecified. Lexical units that involve separate vehicles are associated with FEs that are not appropriate for the more general case of motion, so they are placed in the Operate_vehicle or Ride_vehicle frames (e.g., He drove across the country, She flew to Europe).

ex.t: She walked along the road for a while.
The cars scooted slowly towards the intersection.

fes.d: Self_mover is the living being which moves under its own power. Normally it is expressed as an external argument.

Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. This includes "middle of path'' expressions.
Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.

Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Note that this FE should not be used for cases when the same phrase could be used with the same meaning with a non-motion target, since these should be annotated with the Place FE.
The time when the motion occurs.
An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.
The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement.
Result of an event
The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves.

The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place. Any specified or implied Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place. This FE can be differentiated from Area by the fact that the annotated phrase can be used in the same meaning with non-motion targets.
The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.
External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover to move.
The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.

The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.
The shape of the overall Path travelled by the Self_mover.
An event or circumstance that would not be expected given the nature of the particular Self_motion event.

name: Sending
d: A Sender plans the Path (along with Source and Goal) of a Theme and places it in circumstances such that it travels along this Path under the power of some entity other than the Sender. This frame also has a Recipient distinct from the Goal, as both can be present: This frame contains verbs that participate in the ditransitive construction, with a recipient as the direct object, as in the following: Certain Verbs in this Frame focus on the initial sending act, while others do not. For example, I sent it rapidly can either mean the act of sending was initiated quickly or that it moved quickly. However, the in following sentence: I exported/dispatched it rapidly, meaning that the act was begun quickly, both types of verbs are included.

ex.t: I sent the manuscript to England to Bill.
I forwarded the grain to a dealer in Frankfurt.
I sent Bill the manuscript.

fes.d: This is the person who initiates the movement of the Theme and, unlike Carrying, does not accompany it.
Path along which movement occurs. I shipped the books along Interstate 65.
The end of the path and intended goal of the sending. I sent the logs to the shed.
The beginning of the path, similar to source except that it serves to define the path. I sent wood from Illinois to California.
The objects being sent. I mailed the books to Alaska. Note that Theme may be multiply instantiated. They maileda questionnaire with a return envelope.
The mode of sending employed. I shipped the crops by bigrig .
Degree to which event occurs
Depictive phrase describing the Sender or Theme
This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme. Pat threw the Javelin 50 meters.
Manner of performing an action
This is the recipient of the sent Theme. Tess mailed a letter to Abby
The Purpose of the sending.
The Explanation for the sending.
When the sending takes place
An additional theme sent along with the main Theme.
A container in which the Theme is sent.
A spatial setting encomnpassing the Source location, where the Sending event takes place.

name: Sensation
d: This frame contains nouns that refer to sensations in different modalities. The FE Source is used for the phenomenon that gives rise to the sensation in question. The FE Percept is used for the characteristic quality of the sensation. In cases of veridical perception these are not typically distinguished from one another; we use the FE Percept as the default in these cases. With some nouns in this frame it is possible to express the being who experiences the sensation, or the part of the body of such a being. We mark such expressions with the FEs Perceiver_passive and Body_part, respectively. (The -passive part of this label serves to distinguish this FE from the Perceiver-Agentive FE used in other frames.)

ex.t: The huge sand dunes, perpetually changing, make for a surreal sight.
Endill heard the noise of glass smashing, plaster crumbling and furniture being broken.
The feel of his strong fingers enclosing her small palm came as something of a shock to her system.

fes.d: This FE is only expressed with certain nouns in this frame, and then only with the help of a support verb, such as have: With most nouns in this frame, a perceiver can only be expressed as the subject of a perception verb such as detect or sense: In sentences like these the perceiver-denoting expression is not annotated because it is introduced by another perception word, which is treated independently in a different frame.

This is the entity or phenomenon which gives rise to the sensation. In cases of veridical sensation, this FE is not typically distinguished from Percept. Most of the phrases that express this FE can be paraphrased as from-phrases, e.g. The first sentence, in which the object of the prepostion of is a definite NP, can be roughly paraphrased by the second sentence, which replaces the of-PP with a from-PP. This shows that the phrase of the garlic in the first sentence expresses Source. On the other hand, the third sentence, in which the object of the preposition of is a bare noun, cannot be so paraphrased. The bare-noun of-PPs express Percept rather than Source. Source can be expressed as the External Argument of a support verb, e.g.

The FE Percept is used for phrases that express the characteristic property of a sensation. Typically this characteristic property is described with reference to the entity or phenomenon that produces the sensation---that is why this FE can be difficult to distinguish from Source. It is possible for Source and Percept to be expressed separately, however: In cases in which it is impossible to distinguish between Source and Percept, Percept is used as the default FE.

This FE is assigned to phrases expressing the body part in which a sensation is located. Since touch is the least localized of sense modalities, words relating to haptic sensations are the ones most likely to occur with this FE: Words for other sense modalities can occasionally express this FE as well:
A characterization of the sensation not covered by a more specific FE.
This FE is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.
The Time when the sensation is perceived.
This FE describes how strong the sensation is.

name: Sent_items
d: A Sent_item is prepared for, received after, or involved in a process of Sending, which may involve a particular kind of Transport_means. The Sent_item has an (intended or actual) Sender and Recipient (or a Source and Goal). As a physical object, the Sent_item can be located in a Place.

ex.t: The shipment from Romania is destined for the Iraqi Police Forces.
Postage became more affordable and mail to the President gradually increased.
I 'll arrange for her to collect Bertha 's mail.

fes.d: This is the person or organization who initiates the movement of the Sent_item and, unlike in the case of Carrying, does not accompany it.
The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.
The beginning of the path, similar to source except that it serves to define the path.
The objects being sent.
The mode of sending employed.
This is the recipient of the sent Sent_item
When an interaction with the Sent_item occurs.
The place in which the Sent_item is located.
Any characterizations or evaluations of the the Sent_item that introduce another frame, in which the Sent_item figures.

name: Sentencing
d: During a court appearance, a Sentence, generally a punishment, is imposed on the Convict by a Court, usually represented by a judge.

ex.t: The judge sentenced Martha Stewart to 2 years in prison for insider trading.

fes.d: The Convict is given a Sentence by the Court.
The Court imposes a Sentence on a Convict.
The Sentence is imposed on the Convict by the Court.
This FE denotes the type of sentence.
This FE denotes the duration of the sentence.
The Time when the Convict is sentenced.
The illegal action of which the Convict has been found guilty and for which they are punished.
The location of the sentencing Court.
The state that the Convict is in at the time of their sentencing.

name: Separating
d: These words refer to separating a Whole into Parts, or separating one part from another. The separation is made by an Agent or Cause and may be made on the basis of some Criterion.

ex.t: I divided the class into groups in alphabetical order .

fes.d: The Whole is a single entity or an aggregate of entities which is separated into Parts. It is usually the NP Object of a target verb.
This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from separation of a Whole:
Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the Object of a verb.
Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement. First,
With causative uses of these verbs, an Agent separates or divides something. The Agent is usually expressed as the External Argument:

This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which is used as the basis for separation. Criterion is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of.... As with the frame General.Joining (above), words in this frame can be used statively, as in The rooms are separated by a partition, inchoatively, as in The group separated or causatively, as in I separated the laundry.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent who separates or the undergoers of the separation.
Manner of performing an action
Degree to which event occurs
An act of the Agent that accomplishes the separation.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
The Cause is the non-agent that brings about the separation.
The Recipients are the groups who come into possession of the Parts of the Whole.
This FE identifies the Time when the separation occurs. .
Where the separation occurs.
The Instrument used to cause the separation.
The Agent's intent for separating the Whole.

name: Sequence
d: The words in this frame describe entities that occur in some temporally-ordered sequence. The entities thus have some sort of relation between them that might be described by the Relative_time frame. However, at this time, this frame has no Frame Relation with that frame (though this is still under discussion). Additionally, it should be noted that the words in this frame have a metaphorical link to the words in Shape.

ex.t: Describe in detail the sequence of steps taken during an emergency.

fes.d: This entity occurs in some sequence with Entity_2.
This entity occurs in some sequence with respect to Entity_1.
Entities that occur in some temporal order.
A characterization of the sequence in which the entities occur.
This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the sequence.

name: Serving_in_capacity
d: An Agent occupies a Role in some institution. This Roleis (usually) temporary and can be occupied by other entities at different periods of time. It is common for a Duration of the Role to be mentionned.

ex.t: Chris served as chairman of the boardfor one year.

fes.d: The Agent is the entity that occpuies the Role.
The Role that the Agent occupies.
The Duration of time that the Agent occupies the Role.
The Descriptor modifies the Agent .
The Time when the Agent served in the Role.
The location where the Agent served in the Role.

name: Set_of_interrelated_entities
d: A group of Component_entities along with their interrelations is viewed as a Complex.

ex.t: By definition, no external forces act upon an isolated system of particles.
Earth is a contained system which receives energy from the sun.

fes.d: The entities that function together as a unit.
The unit formed by the Component_entities.
Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.
A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.

name: Set_relation
d: A Superset has several members, a part of which is the Subset. This frame exists largely for the purposes of inheritance.

fes.d: The Superset is the larger collection of entities that includes the Subset.
The Subset comprises a part of the Superset.
Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The Time at which the set relation holds.
The location at which the set relation holds.

name: Setting_back_burn
d: A Firefighter sets a controlled fire to remove fuel from a currently incompletely controlled fire.

fes.d: The Firefighter is the person making the firebreak.
The Flame is what is created by the Firefighter.
The Flammables is the the object that is burned in the back fire.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Firefighter that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An event brought about by the Firefighter that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
This FE describes the Firefighter as being in some state during the action.

name: Setting_fire
d: This frame describes either the creation of a Flame by a Kindler or non-sentient Cause, or the igniting of Flammables by a Kindler or a Cause.

ex.t: Taliban militants recently set fire to several schools.
The fire ignited. CNI

fes.d: The Kindler is the person performing the intentional act.
The Flame is what is created by the Kindler.
The Flamables is the the object that is set on fire by the Kindler.
The cause of the fire.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Kindler that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An event brought about by the Cause or the Kindler that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
This FE describes the Kindler as being in some state during the action.

name: Setting_out
d: A Self_mover begins a journey at a Source location, in a particular Directiongenerally setting out with an Intended_goal in mind.

ex.t: At about 1:00 in the morning, climbers set out for the summit.
The expedition set out from Granada early in March, leaving only one hundred men to garrison the fort which overlooks the city.
After that the earl set out south with his host, and Kari went with him, and Njal's sons too.

fes.d: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion. (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)
Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.
The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.
A second moving object which the Self_mover moves to follow.
The state of the Self_mover during the action.
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.
The direction in which the Self_mover goes.
The time at which the motion takes place.
The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.
The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.
The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.
A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.
The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.
A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.) The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.
The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

name: Severity_of_offense
d: In this frame an Offense is described in terms of the legal or other punishing action that can be taken in response to the offense.

ex.t: He committed an indictable crime .

fes.d: The Offense is the action, crime, or event which is described in terms of what legal or punishing action can be taken against the offender.
The legal Code under which the severity of the offense is determined.

name: Sex
d: Participants in a Sex act engage in or are subjected to sexual contact. Often the LUs in this frame are suggestive euphemisms which refer to non-sexual physical contact, Giving/Receiving scenarios, frames related to travel, physical orientation, body metonymy, biological necessity, or a simple completion of Activity.

fes.d: The set of entities engaged in or subjected to sexual contact.
One party present for sex.
Another party present for sex.
This FE describes the length of time that an entire sexual encounter can last, including but not necessarily implying the length of all stages of the encounter.
A description of the sex act which is not covered by more specific FEs. In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of one or more Participants that also affect the action.
To be clear: the place FE describes the overall location of the Participants of the sexual activity and nothing else.
This FE relates the relative time of occurrence of the sexual activity.
For a sexual act, the Domain describes the specific realm of the contact between Participants; for example, phone sex.
This FE identifies the justification of a sexual act, for at least one of the Participants.
This FE identifies the Means by which Participants accomplish a sexual act.

name: Sexual_reproduction_scenario
