The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.
This FE identifies an event during which the Agent attempts to achieve a Goal.
Re-encoding presents the success or failure event as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Successful_action
d: The Means action by which a deprofiled agent (the Protagonist) has attempted to achieve a Goal, is finished and the actual outcome of the Means action has been resolved, so that it either specifically matches the Protagonist's intent (e.g. success) or does not match it (e.g. failure). In an alternative construal, an Instrument stands for the Means action that the deprofiled agent undertakes in order to achieve the Goal.

ex.t: Why our bid was successful. DNI
Your attempt to unsubscribe was unsuccessful, please try again later. DNI
Well I did end up replacing the old co axial cables with new monster ones and it did the trick. DNI

fes.d: The action that the agent undertakes to achieve the Goal.
The Goal is what the agent attempts to achieve by performing the Means action.
An entity directed by the agent as part of the Means action in order to accomplish the Goal.
The place where Means action succeeds or fails.
This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails
The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the successful action expressed by the target takes place.
The Protagonist is the deprofiled individual who makes an attempt to achieve a Goal by performing the Means action, which may involve using an Instrument.
This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt involving a particular Means or Instrument succeeds.
A participant function of an Instrument or Means in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.

This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part

name: Successfully_communicate_message
d: A Communicator speaks to an Addressee in such a way that the Addressee understands and fully appreciates the truth and/or relevance of the Message.

ex.t: Marred by overblown writing , this first novel by Wilbur Smith 's wife effectively conveys some of South Africa 's problems .INI
He conveys vividly the absurdity of a situation , but he is incurious about the underlying processes which shape it. INI
We've got to get the message through to them before they become sexually active.

fes.d: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.
The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.
Message A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.
The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.
The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.
The Means by which the Communicator communicates.
The time at which the communication takes place.
The degree to which the Communicator's efforts are effective at making the Addressee understand and appreciate the Message.

name: Sufficiency
d: An Item is located on a Scale relative to a critical value which is determined by some Enabled_situation. Generally, when the Enabled_situation is left unexpressed the Enabled_situation is interpreted to be the desirability of the Item being located within a particular range on the Scale. With many of the adjectives of this frame, the Scale is not explicitly mentioned; in such cases, the Scale is usually the quantity, incorporated in the meaning of the targets themselves, though in the case of adequacy, etc. the Scale referred to is quality.

ex.t: I probably have enough. DNI DNI
I was mad enough to scream.
I was too mad to keep myself from screaming.

fes.d: The entity whose scalar property is specified.
The Scale is the attribute of the Item that is being described.
This FE identifies the Enabled_situation by which the critical value is judged.
The Degree frame element indicates a modification of the value indicated by the target.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Suicide_attack
d: An Assailant attacks a Victim, intending to die in the process. In the prototypical case, the attack is designed to kill the Assailant, as when a pilot deliberately crashes a plane into the target.

ex.t: The terrorist suicide attack on U.S. troops early last week caused more damage than initially reported.
They kamikazed the base in the middle of the night!

fes.d: This Victim is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's suicide attack.
An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.
The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.
This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.
This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.

The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describeing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the Attack occurs.

This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.
The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Suitability
d: This Frame is concerned with evaluating an Evaluee as being suitable for a Purpose or a User, presupposing some choice that is being made about which Evaluee to use for the Purpose or User. An LU like suitable.a thus implies that, given a particular Purpose or User, the Evaluee is one which could be or ought to be chosen. The Evaluee may be deemed suitable to a greater or lesser Degree. This frame has some similarity to the compatibility frame where two Items are evaluated with respect to their compatibility with each other against some background.

ex.t: (1) We need to build more houses suitable for local residents.
(2) These chips are not verysuitable for parallel processing.
(3) We are not sure about the Cathedral's suitability for Philharmonic concerts.

fes.d: This Frame Element marks constituents expressing the entity that is judged to be more or less suitable for some Purpose or User.
This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Degree to which the Evaluee is suitable for the Context.
This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Purpose for which the Evaluee is judged to be suitable or unsuitable.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a User to whom

name: Summarizing
d: A Communicator processes some information (either from textual or real-world/perceptual sources) regarding a State_of_affairs into a concise form (a summary) that contains the essential content in briefer form, and communicates this summary to an Addressee, or records it in a Medium. The State_of_affairs may be represented directly (e.g., outline what happened, the situation abroad), or as a textual source (summarizing the documents), or metonymically as some focal entity (a synopsis of the candidates). Some LUs, such as summarize and synopsis entail a preexisting body of information that has been processed into a briefer form by the Communicator. Others, such as outline and blueprint are compatible with, but do not entail, a preexisting, fully fleshed-out concept. E.g.,

ex.t: Frank has already summarized some of the reactions on his weblog.
Director Van Auken gave a brief informational synopsis of each applicant.
He boiled down the argument for domestic wiretapping in one plainspoken and effective, if also deceptive, line...

fes.d: The Communicator creates and communicates the summary of the Information.
The Communicator communicates the summary to the Addressee.
The State_of_affairs is summarized by the Communicator.
The textual or other Medium through which the Communicator summarizes.
The content that results from the summarization.
The time at which the Communicator makes the Summary.
The location where the Communicator communicates.
Any description of the details of the action beyond the identity of the participants and the setting, especially descriptions of the Communicator that affect the action.
An action performed by the Communicator that brings about the communication.
The state-of-affairs that the Communicator is attempting to bring about by communicating.
The amount of time taken by the Communicator in creating and conveying the Summary.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Supply
d: A Supplier gives a Theme to a Recipient to fulfill a need or purpose (Imposed_purpose) of the Recipient.

ex.t: Habituating the ground nesting chimp groups is done by provisioning them with sugar cane. CNI INI
I have equipped my leech troopers with tiny subspace displacement thingummies. INI
She sat down on her bed, carefully folding her clothing and packing it into the small carryall Starfleet had provided her for the journey.

fes.d: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.
The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The object that is given to the Recipient .
The Place where the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Explanation for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Time is when the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Purpose for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Means by which the Supplier acquires or gives the Theme to the Recipient.

Any description of the supplying event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Supplier that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is supplied.
The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.
The period over which the Supplier engages in (multiple) supplying acts.
An additional theme which is supplied along with the main Theme.
The source of the Theme.

name: Supporting
d: A Supporter assists to strengthen the Supported by lending itself in material aid (or abstract assistance in the case of metaphorical uses).

ex.t: The bottom of the wall is supported by the foundation.
Many legislators have supported the industry in the past.
The revetment layers buttressed the mud-mortared cobblestone core wall.

fes.d: The Supporter acts to benefit the Supported by providing additional strength or stability.
The Supported is given strength through the assistance of the Supporter.
The measure to which the Supporter's assistance brings the Supported added strength and support.
The time period during which the Supporter supports the Supported.
An entity used by the Supporter in service of the Supported's strength by support.
This FE identifies the Manner in which a Supporter supports the Supported. .
An action that the Supporter undertakes in service of the Supported's strengthening.
This FE identifies the Place where the support occurs.
This FE identifies when the support occurs.
The situation that the Supporter wishes to bring about by supporting the Supported. .
A state-of-affairs from which the accomplishment would be predicted.
A clause describing the event as a whole.

name: Surpassing
d: In this frame a Profiled_item is higher that its Standard_item on a scale with respect to some Attribute. The Extent of the difference between the Standard_item and the Profiled_item may also be mentioned. Furthermore, the particular value of the standard or profiled item on a certain scale may be given by the Standard_attribute of the Profiled_attribute respectively.

ex.t: Notices for the Shield Theater's production of Macbeth surpassed all previous reviews .
Radio WKRR far surpasses all radio stations among rural radio stations  as the leading source of regional news  .
We surpassed father's skills  before we were 12  .

fes.d: The FE Standard_item denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Item with regard to the Attribute.
The Profiled_item is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Attribute.
The Attribute is a property that evokes a scale along which the Item is located closer to one extreme in comparison to the Standard_item.
The Extent is the degree to which the Item surpasses the Standard.
This FE identifies the Time when the Item is higher on the scale than the Standard.
The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on a scale.
The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to an Attribute or Standard_item.
The Comparison_set includes the Standard and is what the Item is judged with respect to.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Surrendering
d: In this frame a Fugitive presents himself or herself to the Authorities to be subject to the criminal process.

ex.t: The bank robber surrendered to Berkeley police.
Norte is expected to surrender to police tomorrow on tax fraud charges .

fes.d: The Fugitive is wanted by the Authorities and turns himself or herself in to the Authorities.
The Authorities are the officials, government or otherwise, who are in charge of initiating the criminal process.
The Place is the location where the surrendering occurs.
The Time is when the Fugitive surrenders.
The Charges is the offense for which the Fugitive is wanted.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Fugitive surrenders to the Authorities.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.

name: Surrendering_possession
d: A Surrenderer is compelled to transfer a Theme to a Recipient.

ex.t: Shortly after the boy surrendered the gun, the three remaining warriors made a rush for liberty.
He finally surrendered the item after cops and Secret Service agents showed up at his home Saturday.
D?Augustino yielded the weapon to Herrick.

fes.d: The person compelled to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.
The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The object that changes possession.
The Place where the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.
The Time is when the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Purpose for which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Means by which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.
The Manner is the manner in which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Surrendering event itself and any of its participants.
This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.
This FE identifies the Result of an surrendering event.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Surrounding
d: A Figure surrounds a Ground. The Ground location is presented as more likely to be a known location than the location of the Figure. Some lexical units entail more-or-less complete surrounding in two or three dimensions (e.g. surround.v), while others entail surrounding on only two sides (e.g. astride.prep, straddle.v). Like other locative relations, the Figure may be any of a movable entity, an immovable entity, or an event. This frame resembles the Adorning frame, in that both involve a Figure "covering" some Ground, but the Surrounding frame differs in that the Profiled_region is not coextensive with the Ground, as it is in the Adorning frame, and, in fact, unusually for a locative relation, the Ground entity is normally smaller than the Figure. For this reason, the verbs of this frame are often used in the passive (restoring the normal relationship of stative subjects to oblique elements). In addition to several lexical units of this frame originating as metaphorical extentions of much more specific posture descriptions (straddle.v, astride.prep), this frame is itself used in a productive metaphor, involving abstract entities metaphorically "impinging" on other entities (in terms of derivative similarity, control, etc.), as in the following: Common abstract entities that serve as Figure include emotions ('the hopelessness surrounding them'), as well as theories, arguments, and collective philosophies ('Ageism surrounds us, but passes largely unnoticed'). This metaphor arises from the normal invited implicature of this frame that the Figure may physically impinge on the Ground, either protecting it, or limiting its motion, or even supporting it.

ex.t: The hand around the sword-hilt was no less impressive than the sword .
The drug war straddles the border of the US and Mexico .
that led to Dolce and Gabbana to base their autumn/winter D and G collection around her style in 2008

fes.d: The Figure is the entity located with respect to the Ground.
The Ground is the area that the Figure surrounds.
The Time during which the Figure is located around the Ground.
This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.
This FE identifies the Distance between the Figure and some reference location (generally, the deictic center or the Ground). WARNING: Probably not relevant for this frame.
The area or zone immediately external to the Ground. This FE excludes Figure and is only used in particular constructions such as the following:

An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target. This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, and directly.

An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative). This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access.

name: Surviving
d: A Survivor manages to avoid being negatively affected, despite encountering a Dangerous_situation. The negative effect is most often death, destruction, or a metaphorical construal of one of these.

ex.t: Wilderness Survival: Could You Survive the Wild?
More than 400 of the 600 residents rode out the hurricane in Gulfport's 11-story high-rise beachfront facility.

fes.d: The Survivor lives through a Dangerous_situation.
The Dangerous_situation is one in which people are likely or expected to be negatively affected.
The location where the Survivor (primarily) lives during the Dangerous_situation.
The time at which the surviving takes place.
An action performed by the Survivor that enables them to live throug hthe Dangerous_situation.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Survivor survives.
Depictive is a description of the Survivor, during or after the Dangerous_situation.

name: Suspicion
d: A person or group, the Authority, believes that another person, the Suspect is a participant in a criminal Incident.

ex.t: The police suspect Noah Rogers of aiding the robbery last night at Shop-n-drive.

fes.d: The Authority is the group or person who suspects the Suspect of criminal activity.
The Suspect is the target of the Authority's suspicion.
The (typically criminal) Incident in which the Suspect is suspected of being involved.
When the suspecting takes place.

name: Symmetrical_collective_reciprocality
d: Perspective of Reciprocality in which the Protagonists are viewed as essentially identically participating in the Reciprocal event, relation, or situation, not differing in agency, affectedness, or presumed cognitive or conversational accessibility.

fes.d: All the participants in an event or situation, viewed as symmetrically contributing or participating in the situation.

name: System
d: A Complex with a particular Function is formed out of Component_entities. The function may be expressed by reference to a Salient_entity involved in the working of the Complex.

ex.t: The body's immune system can be mobilized against cancer.
The sewer system carries wastewater from homes and businesses to the Water Pollution Control Plant for treatment.

fes.d: The entities that function together as a unit.
The unit formed by the Component_entities.
The activity that the Complex entity performs by virtue of its Component_entities interacting.
Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.
A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.
The kind of entity that the Complex operates on as part of its Function.

name: System_complexity
d: A System is perceived as complex depending on the intricacy of the interconnectivty of its parts or components. These individual parts or components do not function as frame elements in this frame, even though they are implied by its definition. A Dimension may also be defined which situates the System within a certain domain.

ex.t: San Diego freeways are a complex array of poorly maintained roads.
Childrens' toys are simple to assemble.
The hierarchy is complexin structure.

fes.d: The complete entity or system whose complexity is under consideration.
The Dimension provides domain specific information about the System.
This frame element situates the System within a certain domain.

name: Take_place_of
d: A New filler occupies a Role or serves a Function after the Old filler ceases to occupy the position. In many cases, the Role or Function is implicit.

ex.t: Gas can substitute entirely for petrol.
Sometime in the 1880s gas replaced oil for manufacturing fuel.
Twelve years later, oil replaced coal as the energy of choice.

fes.d: The new filler of the Role that was previously occupied by the Old filler.
The category that the New and Old entities fit into as a result of the Function they serve.
The (generally desirable) state of affairs that the New and Old entities are involved in bringing about.
The entity that occupied the Role or served the Function before the New filler.
The time at which the New takes up the Role previously occupied by the Old.
A Degree of replacement is generally only possible when New entities replace Old entities in multiple contexts.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). The rapidity of replacement is also indicated as Manner.
The domain in which the New and Old entities function.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Taking
d: An Agent removes a Theme from a Source so that the it is in the Agent's possession.

ex.t: Milton took the can of beer out of the refrigerator.

fes.d: The person who takes possession of the Theme.
The Agent takes possession of the Theme.
The location of the Theme prior to the taking.
Where the taking takes place.
When the taking takes place.
The Manner of the taking.
The intermediate action taken by the Agent to take the Theme. .
The Purpose for the taking.
The Explanation for the taking.
The larger event which contains the Taking event. .

name: Taking_captive
d: An Agent begins preventing a Captive from moving despite a tendency or desire on the part of the Captive to do so.

ex.t: Authorities recently captured several suspects who were hiding in a remote mountain area.
High value target has been quietly and safely secured.

fes.d: The entity which is captured.
The Agent brings the Captive into custody.
The instrument with which the capturing is carried out.
The reason for the confinement.
This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
When the event occurs.
The purpose for which the Agent takes the Captive into custody.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in capturing the Captive.
The Cause is the non-sentient entity which is responsible for restricting the movement or location of the Captive.
The description of one of the participants in the capturing event.
The larger event which contains or during which occurs the event of taking the Captive captive.

name: Taking_sides
d: A Cognizer has a relatively fixed positive or negative point of view towards an Issue. A Side in a debate concerning an Issue or an Action of a Side may stand in for the Issue. The Cognizer's Degree of alignment may also be specified.

ex.t: In interviews , it seems like everyone is completely against this expenditure .

fes.d: The individual that holds an opinion on an Issue or Side.
The matter, usually concerning a course of action, which the Cognizer has a positive or negative opinion about.
The party or individual (generally associated with a particular position on an Issue) that the Cognizer has an opinion about.
The Degree to which the Cognizer supports or opposes something.
The time period during which the Cognizer has the indicated point of view towards the Issue.
The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Cognizer's taking the indicated view on the Issue logically follows.
An action taken by a Side or a view that the Side takes on an issue which the Cognizer either supports or opposes.
This FE describes the person or element that is taking a side.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

Any description of the Taking_sides which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The location where the Cognizer takes Sides on an Issue .

name: Taking_time
d: An Activity takes some Time_length to complete. If an Agent is involved they may stand in metonymically for the Activity. For some LUs (e.g., fast, speedy) the Degree to which the Activity is conceived of as taking less time than usual can be expressed.

ex.t: How long will this take?
The ride was speedy and often bumpy.
Under high-pressure situations, police officers are very fast at reacting to danger.

fes.d: The event which requires some Time_length for completion.
The durational feature of the Activity.
The amount of time required for the Activity.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Time_length from the norm.
The Time at which the Activity takes place.
Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Activity takes a particular amount of time.
The individual who performs the Activity.
Duration is the length of time from the beginning of the Activity to its end.

name: Talking_into
d: A Speaker expresses through language his wish to get the Addressee to act. The Addressee forms an intention to act and does so.

ex.t: You think I talked Peter into giving me those earrings, don't you?
Don't let a shop assistant talk you into buying a so-called "orthopaedic" bed -- there's no such thing.

fes.d: The Speaker intends through the use of language to get another person to act.
The wish for action on the Addressee's part that the Speaker expresses.
The person that the Speaker seeks to influence to act.
Act of the Speaker that enables them to persuade the Addressee.
An entity that the Speaker gets the Addressee to give to them.
The state of affairs that the Speaker hopes to bring about.
An entity that the Speaker manipulates to get the Addressee to perform the Content.
The location where the Speaker talks the Addressee into performing the Content.

name: Tasting
d: An Agent ingests or begins to ingest a Food item that they have not had before with the intention of determining its quality on some scale. A Purpose for trying the Food may be explicitly mentioned.

ex.t: Most people will never try dog.
I tasted the soup to see if it had enough salt.

fes.d: The person who eats or drinks the Food.
The entity being tasted or ingested by the Agent.
The method in which the Food is eaten or drunk if not covered by the FE Instrument.
The object that the Agent uses to try the Food.
A more specific description of what the Agent hopes to determine by trying the Food.
The time at which the Agent tries the Food.
The location where the scene of an Agent trying Food occurs.\
A characterization of the Agent as they try the Food.

name: Team
d: A Team is a group with shared goals and works toward them together in a coordinated fashion.

fes.d: This FE identifies the people or things that form the Aggregate.
This FE identifies the collection of entities that are the Team.
This FE describes a property of the Aggregate rather than the Members and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.
The term used to refer to the Aggregate.
The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.
The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Aggregate.
The job, obligation, or goal worked towards jointly by the Members of the Team.
The broader organization (if any) that members of a team belong to.

name: Telling
d: A Speaker addresses an Addressee with a Message, which may be indirectly referred to as a Topic. Instead of (or in addition to) a Speaker, a Medium may also be mentioned.

ex.t: I told him about the party.

fes.d: The Speaker is the sentient entity that produces the Message.
The Addressee receives the Message from the Speaker.
The Message is the communication produced by the Speaker.
The Topic is a general description of the content of the Message.
The Manner describes the way in which the Speaker delivers the Message.
The Means describes the way the Speaker accomplishes the task of giving the Addressee the Message.
This FE is the Medium in which the Message is expressed.
The Time during which the Speaker informs the Addressee of the Message.
Place is the location in which the Speaker informs the Addressee of the Message.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Message is expressed. This FE is often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.
This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the telling event.
The FE Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Temperature
d: An Entity has a Temperature characterized by the target. The Temperature is a value of the temperature Attribute. Note that in this frame, the Entity does not experience the temperature, but is merely described as being in a certain externally verifiable state. Thus is not in frame but rather in Subjective_temperature.

ex.t: The pan is already too hot to touch.
The walk-in was freezing, but it was better than hanging out in the kitchen.
Open a window; I'm too hot.

fes.d: The Entity for which the temperature Attribute is under consideration.
The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.
A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the temperature Attribute.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Temperature from the norm.
The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Degree for the temperature Attribute.
Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Temperature.
A part of the Entity that has the specified Temperature value.

name: Temporal_collocation
d: A Trajector is identified as occurring at the same time as some better-known Landmark. We consider sequenced calendric units (e.g. Tuesday, 1987, January) as periods for the purposes of this frame. Some lexical items allow certain types of frame elements while disallowing others (e.g. *During Tuesday...). Several words of this frame (e.g. now.adv) have deictic incorporation of the Landmark_period.

ex.t: He tried to take care of that on his last visit .
I especially like brunch on Sunday.
Dinosaurs lived in prehistoric eras.

fes.d: The entity that occurs at some time.
The event which designates the time at which a trajector occurs.
This FE describes the state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.
The period that occurs with respect to some other time.
The period in which a trajector takes place. This period can be cyclical and, in that case, is interpreted contextually.
The event that occurs at some time.
The entity which designates the time of some trajector. Note: this FE is infrequent or non-existent in English and is included for completeness.

name: Temporal_pattern
d: A salient Subevent has a Pattern of recurrence within a larger Process.

ex.t: Tony's fingers tapped rhythmically on the keyboard

fes.d: The larger event that is characterized by the recurring Subevents.
The salient, punctual event that is construed as part of a Process.
A characterization of the Pattern in which the Subevents recur.
The Pattern that can be detected in the recurrence of the Subevents of the Process .
An indication of a conventionally recognized subtype that the Pattern belongs to.

name: Temporal_subregion
d: A Subpart of a Time_period is picked out. In some cases, the part (as opposed to the entire Time_period) may be described by a Subpart_property. The Time_period may be indicated by an event which takes place during the Time_period.

ex.t: I nearly kicked my TV this afternoon after watching the shambolic end of the Austrian Grand-Prix .
Jack Yan looks at how the branding profession will be affected in the early 2000s by globalization .
The late part of the afternoon is the worst time to get things done .

fes.d: The part of the Time_period which is profiled.
Some description which pertains specifically to the Subpart (rather than the Time_period).
A temporal span conceived of as a whole.
This FE indicates the Time that is being referred to.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Temporary_group
d: A Temporary_group is formed from members of a Parent_organization for a particular Purpose. The Temporary_group does not exist independently within the Parent_organization. It is under the control of a Container_possessor, which also controls the Parent_organization.

ex.t: They came upon another of Whipple's scouting parties, Under Lieutenant S.M. Rains, and wiped out the entire twelve-man detachment.
A guard detachment from the Royal regiment was traveling with the main force to secure high-value prisoners.

fes.d: The group formed temporarily from a larger group for a particular purpose.
The people belonging to the Temporary_group.
The reason for which an Temporary_group is formed.
The interval during which the Temporary_group exists.
A name given to the Temporary_group for identification.
The location or political locale that the Temporary_group is contained within or is responsible to.
This FE describes the general location where the Temporary_group operates, but does not indicate the possessor of the Temporary_group.
Any description of the Temporary_group not covered by a more specific frame element.
The Parent_organization is the larger group from which members are selected to be part of the Temporary_group.

name: Temporary_leave
d: A Person takes leave from his or her routine Activity (such as work or school) for a Duration of time. The Duration can be any length of time, as long as the absence is temporary.

ex.t: The claimant should then submit medical certificates for the duration of their absence from work.INI
He took three month's leave and went to our world assembly at Caux. DNI
Negroponte, who is on a two-year leave of absence from MIT, decided to stay on to the end of the present academic year.

fes.d: The person who is absent from his or her Activity for a Duration of time.
This FE describes the activity or responsiblilities from which the Person is taking a temporary leave.
The amount of time the Person is absent from his or her Activity. This can also be expressed as a description of a duration, as shown below:
The place in which the Person spends his or her leave.
The kind of leave being taken by the Person.
A characterization of the absence.
How often the absences occur.
The Explanation for the Person's absence.
The Person's intended purpose for the temporary leave.
The time at which the leave occurs.

name: Temporary_stay
d: A Guest stays for a time at a Location, which is not his or her permanent residence, for some Duration. The Location is often the permanent residence of a Host.

ex.t: I usually stay with my aunt at her summer house when I go to Seville.
For a few days my father lodged at a hotel with a buddy who was a biology student.

fes.d: The Guest remains for a relatively short period of time in the Location.
The Location where the Guest spends a short amount of time.
The length of time that the Guest remains at the Location.
Another person who, along with the Guest, is temporarily living at the Location.
The time at which the temporary stay takes place.
The Host is living at the Location on a permanent basis, and is allowing the Guest to stay there.
The activity that the Guest hopes to achieve by the stay.
An action of the Guest that brings about their ability to stay at the Location.
Any description of the type of event by comparison to other events (the same way) or by characterizing a state of the Guest that affects the action.
The average number of times the event occurs over a period.
The number of times that the event occurs.
A description of one of the participants in the temporary stay, or of the staying state-of-affairs in general.
The Place indicates the larger physical setting of the temporary stay.
A state of affairs that provides an explanation for the temporary stay.
This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time of the temporary stay, and which is taken to be a part of the stay.

name: Temporary_transfer_scenario
d: In this scenario, the Theme begins in possession of the Lender and ends up in the possession of the Borrower, with the expectation that the Borrower will return the Theme after a Duration of time.

fes.d: The object that is transferred from the Lender to the Borrower for a Duration.
The person or institution who gives the Theme to the Borrower for a Duration.
The person or institution who receives the Theme from the Lender for a Duration.
The amount of time in which the Borrower has possession of the Theme.

name: Terms_of_agreement
d: A condition that is set out in an Agreement imposes Requirements on a Party or parties, with respect to some Regulated_entity. If the conditions are not met, the Agreement as a whole ceases to be valid or, more specifically, a Desired_state_of_affairs cannot occur. (The Desired_state_of_affairs typically is an interaction between the parties that benefits one or both sides.)

ex.t: Breach of contract occurs where one of the parties fails to perform any one of the contract terms .
Breach of contract occurs where one of the parties fails to perform any one of the contract terms .
What are your conditions for a peaceful settlement?

fes.d: A mutual commitment to an obligation made by two or more parties.
A salient entity, an activity or behavior by the parties to the agreement to which a particular stipulation pertains.
The Requirements that a particular stipulation of the Agreement imposes on one or both of the parties.
An event or state of affairs that is desirable to some or all of the parties to the Agreement and which is conditional on the Requirements being met.
A party who demands that certain Requirements be met before they will enter into an Agreement or allow a Desired_state_of_affairs to be realized.
A description of the Requirements that are imposed by the Agreement.

name: Terrorism
d: A Terrorist commits a violent or otherwise harmful Act upon a Victim in order to coerce or terrorize a government or populace. The Act may be committed in particular for political or ideological reasons, and is often directed at civilians, as opposed to government or military officials. It is most often in violation of one or many laws.

ex.t: Their terrorism against civilians will not be tolerated.

fes.d: The Terrorist commits the Act of terror for political or ideological gains.
The Act is the harmful action performed by the Terrorist or terrorist organization.
The Victim is most directly affected or harmed by the Act of terrorism.
A Terrorist may be part of a larger group or Organization of such people.
Any characterization or evaluation of the Terrorist or Act.
The Manner in which the Terrorist commits the Act.
The intermediate action performed by the Terrorist in order to comit the Act.
The location in time when the Act takes place.
The location where the Act takes place.
The action or state-of-affairs that the Terrorist is trying to accomplish by commiting the Act.
The Instrument is used by the Terrorist in order to inflict harm or commit the Act.

name: Text
d: A Text is an entity that contains linguistic, symbolic information on a Topic, created by an Author at the Time_of_creation. It may be a physical entity that is made of a certain Material etc. It may be constructed for an Honoree.

ex.t: It was a good book.

fes.d: The Author is the person who produced a particular Text.
The Text is the entity that contains linguistic information. This an incorporated FE for each LU in this frame.
The person for whom the Text is produced.
The Time at which the Text was created.
What a Text is made of (if applicable).
This is a text in which the Text is located.
The Genre or sub-Genre of the Text.
The use for which the text was produced; its purpose.
The smaller texts that make up the Text.
Topic is what the Text is about.
The Title of a Text. NOTE: when the Title is expressed in an appositive clause, it is labeled as Text on the first layer and Title on the second.
The Medium is the language in which a text is composed, or the physical medium (radio, ink) in which it is distributed.
The region where the Text is sold, circulated, or otherwise popular.
A characteristic of the Text

name: Text_creation
d: An Author creates a Text, either written, such as a letter, or spoken, such as a speech, that contains meaningful linguistic tokens, and may have a particular Addressee in mind. The Text may include information about its topic, although the latter is not an FE in this frame.

ex.t: I penned a letter concerning racism to Congress.
The brothers said not two words to each other.
Jot any notes you need below the line in red pen only.

fes.d: The Author produces a particular Text.
The Components are the parts that the Author uses to construct the Text.
The entity which results from the act of writing or speaking.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
Where the event takes place.
Manner of performing an action. This frame includes some peculiar examples of manner phrases. Write it in pen. Write it in ink.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Text is created.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
This FE identifies the Time at which the text is created.

This is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by to, or as the direct object, or as the first object in a double object construction.
Beneficiary identifies the person in whose honor or for whose benefit the Text is created.
This FE describes the form in which the text is presented.
The Explanation for creating the text.
The language in which the Text is represented or the physical materials upon which the Text is recorded.

name: Theft
d: These are words describing situations in which a Perpetrator takes Goods from a Victim or a Source. The Means by which this is accomplished may also be expressed.

ex.t: I can't believe he pickpocketed my gold watch !
I had to pilfer from the office just to get by . INI
Snatching purses from little old ladies is not a living . CNI

fes.d: Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) that takes the goods away.
Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the goods before they are taken away by the perpetrator.
Goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.
Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the theft occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Perpetrator takes the Victim's Goods.
This FE identifies the Place where the theft occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which a theft occurs.
This FE identifies the Explanation for why a theft occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the theft occurs.
An object used by the Perpetrator in taking possession of the Goods.
The number of times that a theft occurs.

name: Thermodynamic_phase
d: This frame describes the attributes of a thermodynamic Phase of Matter.

ex.t: The molten stateof the lava.

fes.d: The Matter is the physical substance or entity being described in terms of a Phase.
The state of the Matter being described.

name: Thriving
d: An Entity is in a state such that it participates in a preponderance of states and events which are desirable for it. For living entities, this may entail a proliferation of instances of the entity, or of desirable properties associated with the (single) entity. For non-living entities (economies, political locales, academic topics, etc.), this entails a proliferation of instances, or of activities that lead to instances, or any attribute that would prevent the entity from disappearing. This state is conceived of as temporary, or at least contingent on a number of changeable factors. Words expressing the opposite state, i.e., a lack of such positive activity, are also in this frame.

ex.t: In the 1920s the peach industry flourished in Upson County.
Construction companies thrive on public projects.

fes.d: The Entity is experiencing a period of desirable events or states.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The Time during which the Entity thrives.
The Place where the thriving takes place.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
The category in which the Entity thrives.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
The Explanation for why or how the Entity thrives.
This FE describes the state of the Entity. It is often incorporated into the LUs of this frame.

name: Thwarting
d: In this frame a Preventing_cause interferes with the ability of a Protagonist to complete an intended Action. The Protagonist may not be mentioned in the sentence, in which case the Action is an endeavor that an individual or group of individuals hopes to accomplish. In this frame it is necessary that the Protagonist is unable to successfully complete the Action.

ex.t: Noriega's troops foiled a coup attempt.
He prevented her from running away.
He was foiled in his attempt to overthrow the government.

fes.d: The Preventing_cause is the agent or force who keeps the Protagonist from completing her or his planned Action.
The Protagonist is the individual or group of individuals who have a planned Action which is prevented by the Preventing_cause
The Action is the action or event certain individuals desire to bring about which is prevented by the Preventing_cause.
The Time is when the thwarting occurs.
The Place is where the thwarting occurs.
The Manner in which the Preventing_cause thwarts the Action of the Protagonist.
The Degree to which the Action is thwarted.
The Explanation for why or how the Protagonist and/or Action was thwarted by the Preventing_cause.
This FE is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Time_period_of_action
d: LUs in this frame denote a period of time in which an Enabled_action becomes possible. The Duration of this time period can be both exact and inexact. An Agent who performs the Enabled_action may be mentioned as well.

ex.t: Allow a three-day window for delivery. DNI

fes.d: The action that becomes possible through the existence of the period of time.
A quantity or other characterization of the period of the time in which an Enabled_action is allowed. In this frame, the duration may be exact or inexact.
The Agent is the one who performs the Enabled_action.
The Whole is the larger time period to which target is a part of.

name: Time_vector
d: An Event is identified as occurring at a particular Distance and in a particular Direction from a Landmark_event. The lexical units incorporate the Direction and, in some cases, the Landmark_event. This frame builds on the Direction frame, further specifying the Domain as Time. This frame will receive some of the lexical units currently found in Relative_time.

ex.t: Tell me that a week from now.
Some twelve months after I had graduated, I had my first job interview

fes.d: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the reference point in which the Event is anchored.
This FE marks expressions that indicate the amount of time that lies between the Target and the Landmark_event.
This FE marks expressions that indicate whether the Target is prior or subsequent to the Landmark_event on the time line.
This FE indicates the Event temporally located with respect to the Landmark_event.

name: Timespan
d: The words in this frame describe a period of time, as opposed to a point in time.

ex.t: The best time of year for planting tends to be fairly regular.

fes.d: A quantity or other characterization of the State's duration. In this frame, the duration can be inexact.
An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.
The Whole is the larger moment in time of which the target is a part.
Any characterization or evaluation of the timespan not covered by a more specific FE.

name: Timetable
d: A Timetable of Events is a mental object deliberately created, modified or kept by a Cognizer. The Timetable is often modified by an adjective depicting a Period_of_iterations or a dependent noun expressing the Events of the Timetable. Note that this frame does not include the physical representation of a timetable. As of now this frame does not have an inheritance relationship, but in the future a *Mental_object frame will be developed from which Timetable will inherit.

ex.t: Changes to an employee's work schedule should generally be approved prior to the change actually occuring.
The science students had very full timetables; these consisted mainly of lectures, with some lab sessions and problem classes or tutorials.

fes.d: The mental schedule of times at which the Events are set to take place.
The events which are to take place at specified times acording to the Timetable.
The sentient entity who keeps the Timetable.
The time period within which the Timetable repeats.
The time at which the Events on the Timetable transpire.
The purpose for which the Cognizer keeps the Timetable.
A characterization of the Timetable.

name: Tolerating
d: The words in this frame describe an Experiencer's feelings of tolerating with respect to some Content. A Reason for the toleration may also be expressed. Although the Content may refer to an actual, current state of affairs, quite often it refers to a general situation which causes the emotion.

ex.t: He could not tolerate the smell of coconut .

fes.d: The Experiencer experiences tolerance with respect to the Content.

Content is what the Experiencer's feeling of tolerance is directed towards.. The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion.
The Explanation is the explanation for why an Experiencer tolerates the Content.
The Degree to which the toleration occurs.
Manner of performing an action
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer tolerates the Content.
The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the tolerated experience(s).
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.

The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.
The time at which the Experiencer is in the state of toleration.

name: Tool_purpose
d: A living entity intends a Tool to be able to fulfill a generic Purpose. The material from which the tool is created can be something natural or something manmade, including another tool.

ex.t: The use of a saw is to cut down trees.

fes.d: A Purpose is a generic goal associated with the Tool.
A Tool is the object or process that has been designed specifically to achieve a Purpose.
A description of the Purpose.
The sphere of activity in which the Tool is typically used.

name: Topic
d: A stretch of linguistic discourse or a Text that a Communicator produces has a Topic that it is about.

ex.t: Chapter 5 discusses the issue of transubstantiation.
Smither's essay is about plane spotting.
Ostrovsky addresses monetary policy in Chapter 5.

fes.d: The Topic is what a Text is about.
A set of propositions that is coherent in being about a Topic
The Communicator is the person who has produced a Text on a Topic.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate to which Degree the Text is about the Topic
This FE marks expressions in which Manner the Topic is treated.
The Frame Element Status is used for expressions that indicate the relative importance of a Topic with respect to the other topics that a Text is about.
The time at which the Communicator produces Text on a Topic.
The reason for which the Text or Communicator presents the Topic.

name: Touring
d: A Tourist experiences an Attraction, a location with a unique history or other societally recognized individual character, with the goal of seeing and learning about it. Typically, the Attraction has a source of information about the Attraction--a guide, pamphlets, or displays.

ex.t: We toured the Grand Canyon.

fes.d: The individual that is seeking an experience at an Attraction.
The societally-recognized unique location that the Tourist experiences.
The state of the Tourist or the Attraction during the tour.
The perceptual background against which the Attraction is experienced by the Tourist.
Any description of the details of the event in terms of how they compare to other events (the same way) or in terms of how the state of the Tourist affects them (happily, obliviously).
The Means indicates a method the Tourist is using to participate in a tour.
The time that the touring takes place.
Some action that the Tourist is trying to accomplish with touring. This is generally (at a minimum) for the purposes of entertainment and learning.
The location where the touring takes place.
The amount of time the touring activity lasts.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
The Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the touring event with the Tourist.

name: Toxic_substance
d: A Toxic_substance causes death or harm when introduced into or absorbed by a living organism, the Victim. The Toxic_substance may be specified to be produced by or contained in a Toxin_source. The Toxic_substance may affect the Victim as a whole or a particular Body_part (understood here to include organs and other sub-systems). A Degree of harmfulness can be specified and the Toxic_substance may develop its effect only under particular Circumstances.

ex.t: The main product , sulphide , is toxic to cells
They are better tolerated and are less toxic in overdose
The reason he was close to danger was because an extremely poisonous beetle was crawling down his shoulder.

fes.d: The Victim is the being or entity that is capable of being harmed by the Toxic_substance.
Degree is the degree to which the Toxic_substance is harmful to the Victim.
The Body_part defines the part of the Victim's body that is harmed.
A fact or action that explains why the Toxic_substance has a harmful effect on the Victim .
This FE marks expressions that indicate the substance which potentially causes harm to a Victim.
A set of circumstances, often the relative amount of the Toxic_substance that is present, under which the Toxic_substance is specified to have or lack a toxic effect.
A living organism, object or process that produces a Toxic_substance.
Type identifies the kind or sort of Toxic_substance.
Temporal period for which the substance or source remains toxic to the victim.

name: Transfer
d: This frame involves a Donor transferring a Theme to a Recipient.

ex.t: I transferred $20 to his account.

fes.d: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The object that changes ownership.
The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.
Where the event takes place.
The Explanation for which an event occurs.
When the transfer occurs.
The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.
The action whereby the transfer of the Theme from the Donor to the Recipient is effected.
Any description of the transfer which is not covered by more specific FEs
This FE identifies the purpose for which a Theme is transferred

name: Transfer_scenario
d: In this scenario, the Theme begins in the possession of the Donor and ends up in the possession of the Recipient. Alternatively, these two participants may be jointly construed as Transferors.

fes.d: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
The object that changes ownership.
The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.
The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.

name: Transition_to_a_quality
d: An Entity ends up with a particular new Final_quality. There is only one lexical unit, go.v, that evokes this frame directly in English, and it combines only with a limited set of Final_quality types, such as undesirability (bad, sour), insanity (crazy), inability (limp), or posture (prone). However, the frame itself is intended to cover situations with arbitrary Final_quality types. As such, frames describing simple state change should inherit from this frame, incorporating the Final_quality FE as part of the background meaning of the frame.

ex.t: The milk has gone sour already .

fes.d: Where the change takes place.
When the change occurs.
The length of time that the Entity retains the Final_quality.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Entity which undergoes a change so that it possesses the Final_quality.
The quality that the Entity has at the end of the event.
The period during which the Entity is in transition.
This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity adopts Final_quality.
A characterization of the kind of Group members that the Entity pertains to, and which are saliently affected by its change.
Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.

name: Transition_to_a_situation
d: An Entity ends up in a Final_situation. This frame should be compared to the more general Transition_to_a_state, which also includes changes to a Final_category and a Final_quality. This frame should be compared to Process_start and Activity_start. Unlike Process_start's Process FE and Activity_start's Activity FE, the Final_situation need not be conceived of as an ongoing event. Also, there is no emphasis on the temporal profiling in Transition_to_a_situation other than the before (where the Final_situation is not true) to the after (where the Final_situation is true).

ex.t: I have come to appreciate good coffee .
We have come to expect three meals a day .
When the history of our times comes to be written , They Organized Themselves to Death will be the only possible epitaph .

fes.d: Where the change takes place.
When the change occurs.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Entity which undergoes a change, ending up in the Final_situation.
The period during which the Entity is in transition.
This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_situation.
The type of individual things that have an instance of the Entity and which are saliently affected by its change.
Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.
The Entity's situation after the change.

name: Transition_to_state
d: An Entity ends up in a Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality which it was not in before. Some members of the frame (e.g. grow.v) tend to emphasize a gradual change, while most members of the frame do not indicate whether a change is gradual or not. This frame should be compared to Undergoing_change. Undergoing_change is different in that it much more emphasizes the difference between the pre- and post-states of the Entity. This shows up both in Undergoing_change's increased occurrence with Initial_category and Initial_state (change from red to blue) and in its increased occurrence with Final_category (changed into a toad) rather than Final_situation or Final_quality (?changed to red vs. became/turned red). In addition, when Undergoing_change occurs with the Final_category frame element, it presents a deep difference between the Initial_category and the Final_category, so that it is humorous to say 'she turned into a Republican', because it presents this as a fundamental change of identity; compare to 'she became a Republican', which is quite normal. In a less humorous example, someone can 'turn into a Mac user', strongly implying that they no longer use their former operating system, while if they 'become a Mac user', this is either as a replacement of other OS's or potentially as an addition to the use of other OS's.

ex.t: Why I became an Emacs user
I left the ministry and became an atheist.
Surprisingly, various veteran organizations also turned vehemently antiwar.

fes.d: Where the change takes place.
When the change occurs.
For how long the Entity remains in the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Entity which undergoes a change, ending up in the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.
The quality of the Entity after the change.
The category that the Entity ends up in after the change.
The period during which the Entity is in transition.
This FE describes the state of the Entity before becoming occurs.
This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.
This FE describes the category of the Entity before becoming occurs.
The individual entities related to the Entity which are saliently affected by its change.
Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.
The Entity's situation after the change.

name: Transitive_action
d: This frame characterizes, at a very abstract level, an Agent or Cause affecting a Patient. This frame is inherited by many lower-level frames.

fes.d: Agent is the entity that acts on another entity.
Patient is the entity that is being acted on and that may but need not undergo a change.
An Event in which an Agent acts on an entity.
Depictive phrase describing a participant in the event.
The Result of a transitive action.
An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Time at which the event takes place.
The location at which the event takes place.
An event which causes the Patient to be affected in some way.

name: Translating
d: A Cognizer produces a Target_symbol which represents, in the Target_representation format, a Content that pre-exists in the form of a Source_symbol in a Source_representation format.

ex.t: This word is sometimes translated as ` girl '. CNI
They all wore symbolic black clothes over bright yellow T-shirts and all spoke in Welsh, their statements being translated into English afterwards. CNI
His texts were translated from French into Scots by Carl Gronau.

fes.d: This is the person who carries out the translation.
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.
The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.

Any description of the translation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Cognizer which accomplishes the translation of the Content.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.
The representation system into which the Content is rendered by the Cognizer.
The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.
An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.
The Medium is a text produced by the Cognizer in which she uses a Target_symbol to express Content from a Source_representation system.
The location where the translation takes place.
The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by translating.

name: Transportation_status
d: A Rider is being transported in a Vehicle, or is moving on foot.

ex.t: Mounted police officers are a common sight in this village.
You mean to say they are on foot?

fes.d: The Rider is being transported by a Vehicle.
The Vehicle carries the Rider.

name: Trap
d: A Deceiver sets up a Trap in order to cause a Victim to have an incorrect understanding about a situation. The Deceiver anticipates that this will lead the Victim to take a course of action (including doing nothing) which causes the Victim harm.

ex.t: Setting a trap for your opponents is usually a good strategy.
It's a trap!

fes.d: The Trap is a device, strategy, or system designed to mislead and cause harm to a Victim.
The Trap is orchestrated by a Deceiver.
The Deceiver intends to mislead and cause harm to the Victim by means of the Trap.
A description of the Trap.

name: Travel
d: In this frame a Traveler goes on a journey, an activity, generally planned in advance, in which the Traveler moves from a Source location to a Goal along a Path or within an Area. The journey can be accompanied by Co-participants and Baggage. The Duration or Distance of the journey, both generally long, may also be described as may be the Mode_of_transportation. Words in this frame emphasize the whole process of getting from one place to another, rather than profiling merely the beginning or the end of the journey.

ex.t: Ellen journeyed to Europe with five suitcases.
Samantha journeyed 2500 miles with her family by sea to China.
The Osbournes took a trip from Beverly Hills to London on the Concorde.

fes.d: This is the Area in which the traveling takes place. This frame element describes the enclosed area inside which travelling, of unspecified Source, Path or Goal takes place.
The Co-participant is the person or persons who accompany the Traveler on the journey.
This FE dientifies the Distance traveled.
This FE identifies the Duration of time during which the trip occurs.
The Goal is the location where the travelers end up.
The Manner in which the traveling takes place.
The action done by the Traveler by which the traveling is accomplished.
The Path is the route along which the travel takes place.
This is the living being which travels. Normally, the Traveler is expressed as an external argument.
The Source is the starting point of the trip.
The Speed is the rate at which the travel takes place.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Traveler is effected, by their body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Traveler. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
When the traveling occurs.
The Explanation for which the travel is undertaken.
The Baggage are the items necessary for travel that accompany the Traveler.
The Frequency with which the Traveler makes the journey.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Traveler travels, i.e. the future state of affairs that will hopefully come about.
The number of times the trip is traveled by the Travelers.
The Time throughout which the traveling repeatedly takes place.
This FE applies to expressions that indicate documents, money, tickets, etc. which allow people to engage in travel.
The state of the Traveler during the journey.
The affect of travel on a Traveler.
The Place is the location of the motion. It describes the area in which motion (with a specified Source, Path or Goal) takes place.
The direction in which the Traveler goes.
A characterisitic of the traveling event.

name: Traversing
d: A Theme changes location with respect to a salient location, which can be expressed by a Source, Path, Goal, Area, Direction, Path_shape, or Distance, as shown in the examples below:

ex.t: Start your ascent from Achintree Farm in Glen Nevis.
We crossed the desert.
She jumped across the ditch that marked the entrance to the woods.

fes.d: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not required to be an animate mover, so it is different from Self_mover.

Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, including directional expressions:

Any expression which tells where the Theme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance:

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.

This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.
Degree to which event occurs
An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way.
The Speed is the rate at which the Theme moves.
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Theme, taken simultaneously.
The direction in which the Theme goes.
The time at which the motion takes place.
The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.
The length of time that the Theme spends in motion.
The state of the Theme at the end of the event.
A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Theme.

An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, or an action that Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the Traversing occurs and which the Traversing is taken to be a part of.
