The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.
A larger conceptualization that includes the Traversing as an integral part. The Traversing expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Theme), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the Traversing.

The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Traversing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.
The Source and Goal of either a single or a repeated motion taken together as Endpoints of the Path.

The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.
The time period within which the motion event occurs repeatedly.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Treating_and_mistreating
d: In this frame an Agent is evaluated as behaving toward an Affected_Party in some Manner, which may or may not be incorporated into the target LU.

ex.t: Douglas always treated Mary well.

fes.d: This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.
This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves toward the Affected_Party. In the case of mistreat.v, this FE is incorporated.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.
The person to whom behavior is directed by the Agent.
This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.
The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.
The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.
The way in which the treating or mistreating is done.
The Domain of human behavior in which the Agent acts in a certain Manner.
The extent to which the (usually 'good' or 'bad') conduct of the Agent deviates from some standard or norm.
An explicit point to which the conduct of the Agent is compared.

name: Trendiness
d: A Behavior, attributed to an Evaluee, conforms with or is heavily influenced by a popular trend or practice, often in the realm of fashion, design, though extending social and interactional behavior in general. Trendiness differs from Popularity in adding a factor of aesthetic or other judgment to behaviors and individuals, and judging these with respect to social behavior; Popularity is about amount of acceptability or utilization based on general (often non-aesthetic) desirability.

ex.t: Wearing flowered brocaded silks was fashionable in the first few years of the decade.

fes.d: The Behavior which is trendy.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the degree of trendiness from the norm or from the value for another Behavior.
The Time during which the Behavior is trendy or fashionable.
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Behavior is trendy or not.
The Evaluee is judged to conform to some degree with popular fashion with respect to his or her behavior.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment of trendiness.
The location where the Behavior is trendy..

name: Trial
d: A trial is a process conducted in a Court before a Judge and (usually) a Jury in which the participants meet in order to decide a Case. The Prosecution attempts to prove that the Defendant is guilty of the Charges and the Defense tries to prove that the Defendant is innocent. Trials have a rich schematic structure which is only partially represented here. The Trial frame is the part of the Criminal Process frame that occurs after a crime, Arrest of a suspect, Arraignment, jury selection, etc. and before Sentencing and punishment or release. The Trial is made up of court appearances. The beginning of the Trial generally involves opening arguments, in which the Prosecution and the Defense present their respective points of view. Then during the course of the Trial, both sides present evidence, some of which is provided by witnesses with testimony, and this is then drawn upon as support for their arguments. Following the presentation of evidence, testimony, and arguments, generally culminating in closing arguments for each side, the Jury (if present) deliberates and either comes to no sufficient consensus or produces a Verdict.

fes.d: The legal label for the crime that the Defendant is accused of.
The specific room where the participants in a Trial meet.
The individual or group which is responsible for promoting the welfare of the Defendant during a Trial, usually involving the contention that the Defendant is innocent of the Charges.
The group of individuals who observe the Trial and ultimately attempt to come to a verdict.
This FE identifies the Place where the trial occurs.
The individual or group responsible for promoting the interests of the state in the Trial, prototypically including presenting arguments for the guilt of the Defendant.
This FE identifies the Time when the trial occurs.
The person charged with an offence.
The official who directs and presides over the Trial.
The Case which a Trial is convened to decide.
The way in which the Trial is conducted.

name: Triggering
d: A Cause triggers a System to operate in accordance with its intended purpose. Alternatively, an Actor (acting volitionally or not) which participates in the Cause, stands in for the Cause. The System often has the capability to detect and signal the presence of an object or the occurence of an event (metal, an earthquake). It may also be or contain an explosive device. The Means by which the Cause activates the System may also be specified.

ex.t: Smoking a cigarette will normally not set off a smoke alarm.
Suspected drug traffickers set off 12 bombs, injuring 35 people.
Joseph wriggled out of the ropes and inadvertantly triggered the burglar alarm.

fes.d: The Cause interacts with the System such that conditions are met for the System to operate.
The System interacts with or detects the Cause and activates.
The Means is a subevent which the Cause or Actor participates in which results in triggering the System .
An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.
Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's or Cause's influence on the character of the event (eagerly, quietly).
Where the triggering takes place.
The time when the triggering takes place.
The purpose of the Actor in setting off the System.

name: Trust
d: A Cognizer thinks that the Information given by a particular Source is correct. The specific Content or Topic of the Information may also be described.

ex.t: I don't trust this information.
Nobody will believe you, and people will think you're scum.

fes.d: The Cognizer is the person who has an opinion about the reliability of a Information_source or the Information from the Information_source.
The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer trusts information about.
The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.
This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer trusts the Source.
A description of an aspect of the Cognizer that also affects the nature of the trusting, or a general comparison of the state-of-affairs to others.
An object or action associated with the Cognizer which is so affected by the Cognizer's belief that it reveals the Cognizer's state.
The individual that gives Information to the Cognizer.
The text or speech which the Cognizer has heard and evaluates the truth of.

name: Try_defendant
d: A Defendant is tried by a Jury or Judge in a Court for Charges. This frame perspectivalizes the general Trial frame.

ex.t: The state will try him for fraud.

fes.d: The Judge heads the Court where the case is tried. An expression referring to the Court may also stand in for the Judge.
This FE identifies the Court in which a case is tried.
The Defendant is being tried for the Charges in Court.
This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.
This FE identifies the Time when the case is tried.
This FE identifies the Place where the case is tried.
This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.
The Defendant is tried under the laws of the Governing_authority.
The Manner of the trial of the Defendant.

name: Trying_out
d: An Evaluator participates in an Experience (or metonymically, a salient Entity of the Experience), often for the first time, in order to form an opinion about its quality. The aspect of quality that is being judged is often implicit but may be expressed as the Purpose of the Evaluator's participation.

ex.t: Have you tried my latest get-rich-quick scheme? INI
Don tried out the bike to see if it was the right size.

fes.d: The person (or metonymic manifestation thereof) that participates in the Experience.
The activity or event that the Evaluator participates in.
Entity is something that the Evaluator uses to try an Experience, and metonymically stands in for the Experience.
A description of how the Evaluator acts in having the Experience.
A description of what the Evaluator does in order to participate in the Experience.
A more explicit description of what the Evaluator seeks to learn by having the Experience.
The temporal location during which the Experience occurs.
The physical location in which the Experience occurs.

name: Turning_out
d: A State_of_affairs turns out to be true in someone's knowledge of the world. This may be recognized with evidence or in certain circumstances. The cognizer whose beliefs are affected is not expressed.

ex.t: Hybrid grass may prove to be a valuable fuel source.

fes.d: The state of affairs that a cognizer realizes.
The time at which the State_of_affairs is realized.

name: Type
d: This frame has to do with nouns denoting types of entities. The Subtype refers to a collection of members of a more general Category which have certain defining characteristics; alternatively, the Subtype refers only to the type itself, i.e. a more restrictive set of characteristics than those of the more general Category. The properties of the items that are included in the collection may be specified by the Item_Property. Sometimes the Subtypes themselves are described by some Type_Property.

ex.t: I don't like this newfangled kind of fish.
Kleo isn't our sort of people.
He argued against the formalist type of analysis of art.

fes.d: The entity which denotes a subtype of the more general Category.
The more general type that the target denotes a subtype of. This FE is obligatory and should be labeled DNI when not present.

A property of the Subtype itself rather than the members of the Category. Many Type_property adjectives (e.g. new, rare, traditional, modern, strange) make explicit that the type under discussion is just one of the types in the more general Category. Adjectives that denote properties of items in the category should be tagged Item_property.
A property of the members of the Category that helps identify (directly or indirectly) the particular set of members that are referred to by the Subtype.

name: Typicality
d: A State_of_affairs is generally, or with regard to a particular Feature, representative of its class, which may be narrowed to a specific Comparison_set.

ex.t: The Elan truly is an unusual car; the first and only Lotus with a front engined/front wheel drive layout, and the first new Lotus to be introduced since 1975.
I need a plain, vanilla example that doesn't use PRINT!
How smart is the average drug user/experimenter?

fes.d: The extent to which the Entity varies from other members of the Comparison_set.
The state of affairs which is evaluated with regard to whether it exhibits the essential characteristics of a Comparison_set.
The set of indviduals, which are of similar kind to the Entity, and to which the Entity is compared.
A property of the State_of_affairs wherein it differs or is similar to members of a Comparison_set.

name: Unattributed_information
d: A Reported_fact is presented by the speaker as deriving from statements (made directly to them or to others) of third parties.

ex.t: Four purported gang members could face death penalty in Virginia slaying of federal informant.

fes.d: An assertion of a state, event, property or existence or the assignment to a category that the speaker attributes to unnamed others.
The Time at which the Reported_fact was reported.
The span of time for which the Reported_fact has been circulating.
The reason for which or the apparant cause of the Reported_fact.

name: Undergo_change
d: An Entity changes, either in its category membership, its situation, or in terms of the quality of an Attribute. In the first case, where category membership is changing, an Initial_category and a Final_category may be expressed. In the second case, where a situation as a whole is changing, an Initial_situation and a Final_situation can be present. And in the last case, where some characterization of the Entity is changing, an Initial_quality and a Final_quality can be specified. In some cases, the types of perspective are mixed, so that, e.g., an Initial_quality is mixed with a Final_situation; this is usually considered poor style. This frame is often the target domain of motion metaphors, in which the moving Theme corresponds to the changing Entity, the Source of motion corresponds to the Initial_category, Initial_quality, or Initial_situation and the Goal of motion corresponds to the Final_category, Final_quality, or Final_situation of the Entity. By correspondence with the complex domain of motion, this metaphor introduces several FEs to the target domain of change, such as an Intermediate_state (etc.) from Path, and Tendency_of_change from Direction.

ex.t: As soon as Tiffany kissed the frog, Tiffany turned into a frog.
He chanted and the rock changed shape, becoming a great double bitted axe.
The College has changed markedly over the century since it first opened its doors.

fes.d: The concrete or abstract entity that undergoes a change.
The type of Entity that results from the change.
The category that the Entity belongs to before it undergoes the change.
The time at which the Entity undergoes the transformation.
The value of the Attribute before the change takes place.
The quality of the Attribute that results from the change.
A characteristic of the Entity for which a quality can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement, or observation.

Any description of the Change event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The extent to which the initial and final categories, situations, or qualities differ from each other.
The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.
An event or state that causes the change to take place.
A value that the Attribute assumes before the Final_value obtains.
The Initial_value and Final_value taken together as the range through which the Entity changes. The main faith of the church has changed between Orthodox, Protestant and Greek Catholic several times.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The location that the change takes place.
The Entity's situation that results from the change.
The situation that the Entity began in.

name: Undergo_transformation
d: An Entity changes from one kind of thing (Initial_category) to another kind of thing (Final_category). Whether the Initial_category is mentioned or not, the change is viewed as negating some Initial_category, and not simply adding an additional Final_category to the Entity.

ex.t: She metamorphosed from a mere coworker into a friend .
His mother had transformed into a rock star . INI
The metamorphosis of his attitude from benign neglect to active hatred was so slow he never noticed .

fes.d: The concrete or abstract entity that undergoes a change.
The type of Entity that results from the change.
The category that the Entity belongs to before it undergoes the change.
The time at which the Entity undergoes the transformation.

Any description of the Transformation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The extent to which the initial and final categories differ from each other.
The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.
An event or state that causes the change to take place.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
The location that the change takes place.

name: Undergoing
d: An Entity is affected by an Event.

ex.t: The hotel is undergoing renovations at this time.

fes.d: The thing which is affected by the Event.
A change in the world which affects the Entity.
The Time at which the Entity undergoes the Event.
The location at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

The Explanation for which the Entity undergoes the Event. The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
The Purpose for which the Entity undergoes the Event.
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Undergoing_scenario
d: In this scene, an Event occurs, and an Entity is affected by it.

fes.d: The thing which is affected by the Event.
A change in the world which affects the Entity.
The Time at which the Entity undergoes the Event.
The location at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

The Explanation for which the Entity undergoes the Event. The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
The Purpose for which the Entity undergoes the Event.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Undressing
d: A Wearer removes an item of Clothing from a Body_location (the part of the body that the Clothing is prototypically worn on.)

ex.t: Walking on sand is better if you take off your shoes. INI

fes.d: The individual who begins the action wearing the Clothing and ends the action without it.
The item that the Wearer is initially wearing but then removes.

The initial location of the Clothing on the body, before it changes location. Quite often, the location is not overtly specified and is implicitly supplied by the location on the body that the Clothing is prototypically associated with.

Any description of the clothing removal which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Wearer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Means is an act whereby the Wearer achieves the removal.
The Result of the event.
The Degree to which the event occurs.
The location at which the Wearer undresses an item of Clothing.
The Time at which a Wearer undresses.
The Purpose for which a Wearer undresses.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Unemployment_rate
d: Based on how many Individuals are employed, the Individuals as a whole are described with a Value (either a percentage or absolute number) representing the Employment of the Individuals.

ex.t: Unemployment is down, salaries are up for US chemists.
As a result, the unemployment of Roma is very high.
Today's report finds that unemployment among single mothers rose for the first time in six years in 2002. DNI

fes.d: The group of people whose employment status is considered.
The property of a group of Individuals describing how many of them are employed or unemployed.
The count or percentage of people among the group of Individuals that are of the specified employment status.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Value from the norm.
The Time during which Employment level of the Individuals has a specified Value.
The number or rate of individuals that are either employed or unemployment may be contrasted, implicitly or explicitly, with different groups.
The location where the Individuals under consideration reside.

name: Use_firearm
d: An Agent causes a Firearm to discharge, usually directing the projectile from the barrel of the Firearm (the Source), along a Path, and to a Goal.

ex.t: The Germans wouldn't stop shooting cannons at them.
Oswald fired twice through the window.

fes.d: The self-directed entity that uses and activates the Firearm.
This FE identifies the Firearm that an Agent activates so that it rapidly propels a projectile.
This FE identifies the means by which an Agent uses the Firearm.
This FE identifies the manner in which an Agent uses the Firearm.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the firearm.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent fires the Firearm.
Goal is the location the Theme ends up in, or is intended to end up in.
This is the path along which the projectiles travel.
The Source is the location of the Firearm from which projectiles originate.
Area is the setting in which the projectile's movement takes place.
This FE identifies the number of times a firearm is used.
Depicitive phrase describing the state of a participant in the action.

name: Use_vehicle
d: A Driver transports themselves and possibly other passengers (the Theme) to another location.

fes.d: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle.
The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a PP-complement or the direct object.
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.
The Path describes the trajectory of the motion.
The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion.
The Distance is the extent of the motion.
The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes.
The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs.
The Area is the location where the motion takes place.
The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels.
The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles.
When the riding takes place.
A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme.
The individual that directs the motion of the Vehicle

name: Used_up
d: Through use, a Resource is diminished in quality or quantity (up to complete attrition) such that it becomes less capable of sustaining future use.

ex.t: My entire life savings is depleted due to university and medical bills.
All significant oil and gas reserves are exhausted or have dwindled to an uneconomical level except for those of the Middle East.
Use shampoo and conditioner every day until the shampoo and conditioner are completely used up.

fes.d: The Resource is a physical entity or an ability to perform work that was used in an earlier process, typically in pursuit of a goal.
A measure of the amount of the Resource that is gone, or of the degree to which its quality is reduced.
The Explanation denotes an event or state from whose occurrence the Resource's being used up logically follows.
This FE indicates that the presence of an overwhelming amount of a kind of entity or the high intensity of an event is sufficient to bring about the used up state of the Resource.
Subregion denotes a sub-part of the Resource in which the it is specifically exhausted or worn out.

name: Usefulness
d: An Entity aids in the successful completion of a Purpose. Its Degree of utility may also be expressed. Some of the lexical units in this frame (e.g. great, good) can only express permanent, generic states of the Entity.

ex.t: A box is an ideal storage device.

fes.d: The item which is useful for some purpose.
The kind of task which is promoted by the use or presence of the Entity.
The amount that the presence of the Entity aids in the completion of the (desirable) Purpose.
This Frame Element marks expressions of a Domain or parameter with respect to which the Entity is useful.
When the Entity is useful for a Purpose.

name: Using
d: An Agent manipulates an Instrument in order to achieve a Purpose.

ex.t: For cold conditions, we recommend that you use a heat gun or a hair dryer to make the adhesive work better.

fes.d: The Agent uses the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent uses the Instrument.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the Instrument.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent uses the Instrument.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent uses the Instrument.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An entity directed by the Agent that serves to bring about the Purpose of the Agent.
An Instrument that has a function associated with it.
The Outcome is the failure or success of the Agent's using the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.
An event within which the Agent uses the Instrument. Often, the Containing_event will also give an indication of the Agent's Purpose.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."
This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
This FE identifies the population within which the Using event occurs.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Instrument or the Using act and modifies the expected value for it.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Using_resource
d: An Agent has access to a finite amount of some Resource and uses it in some way to complete a Purpose. The specific Portion of the Resource may be stated, and after the Resource is spent, it is no longer available to the Agent. The Means by which the Resource is used may be mentioned, but it is often implied by the stated Purpose or understood based on what the Resource is.

ex.t: I used half of the bag of dirt to plant the roses.
She just spends all her time sitting in front of the television.

fes.d: The person who depletes a Resource to achieve some Goal
The exhaustible commodity that the Agent has access to.
What the Agent is attempting to achieve by using the Resource.
The amount of the Resource that the Agent uses to achieve the Purpose.
A more specific description of how the Purpose is achieved by spending the Resource.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The physical location where the Resource is used.
The time at which the Resource is used.

name: Vehicle
d: The frame concerns the vehicles that human beings use for the purpose of transportation.

ex.t: I drove a limo to the school dance.

fes.d: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Vehicle.
Vehicle is the transportation device that the human beings use to travel.This FE is incorporated into each LU in this frame.
This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Vehicle. .
The frame element tells about the time and route of the service of the transportation device.
The Means_of_propulsion designates how the vehicle is moved.
The task which the Vehicle is put to. Normally, this includes the transportation of some kind.

name: Vehicle_departure_initial_stage
d: A Vehicle moves into position or otherwise changes configuration or state as preparation for normal operation. The focus of the event is on the state of the Vehicle rather than any agent which is manipulating the Vehicle.

ex.t: The flight for New York finally lifted off from Oakland International with one hundred passengers aboard.

fes.d: The vehicle which moves into position for typical operation.
Any expression which describes the location that the Vehicle has been stationed at.
The location that the Vehicle is bound for.

Any description of the preparation for motion which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Vehicle that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The state of the Vehicle during the preparations.
An event in which the Vehicle participates which causes or enables it to travel.
The Result of the Vehicle's motion.
An individual or vehicle that is also involved in the preparations.
This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the preparation of the Vehicle takes place.
The Place describes the location where the Vehicle prepares for motion.
The length of the time that the Vehicle remains in the state of readiness.
The Time when the Vehicle gets ready for motion.
The Explanation is a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Vehicle_landing
d: A flying Vehicle comes to the ground at a Goal in a controlled fashion, typically (but not necessarily) operated by an operator.

ex.t: A police helicopter landed just outside my neighborhood at around midnight last night.
The UFO touched down here, you say?

fes.d: The Vehicle comes to the ground, usually (but not necessarily) under the control of an operator.
Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.
Goal is any expression that tells where the Vehicle ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.

A Manner expression describes a property of landing which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which a Vehicle lands.
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Vehicle is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Vehicle.
Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
This FE identifies the Time when the aircraft lands.
The New_situation are the state of the Goal when the Vehicle arrives.
The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Vehicle upon arrival.
The time period within which the landing event repeats multiple times.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the landing event itself and any of its participants.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Vehicle lands at the Goal.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the landing event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of Event_description
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.
How often the Vehicle lands at the Goal.
This FE identifies the Place where the landing occurs.

name: Vehicle_subpart
d: An entity is integrated into a vehicle as a Part of a (possibly unexpressed) Whole which may refer to the whole vehicle or merely to a sub-part of the vehicle.

ex.t: The car's engine started smoking so we pulled over.
Put the bags in the trunk.
One should always wear a seatbelt while driving.

fes.d: Some Part of the larger vehicle, the Whole.
A vehicle (the Whole) which includes the Part.
The function of the part within the vehicule as a whole.
This property of the part that situates the part within the whole.
A property relating to the part.

name: Verdict
d: In this frame, which is a part of the Trial sequence, a Judge gives a Finding with respect to the Charges against the Defendant in a particular Case.

ex.t: He was convicted of fraud by Judge Judy.

fes.d: The Judge (which may be the jury, judge, magistrate or court) decides on the Finding.
This FE identifies the outcome of the Judge's deliberation or consideration. Many LUs in this frame incorporate this FE.
The person who stands accused of a crime and is subject to the verdict.
This FE refers to the Charges with respect to which the verdict is being given.
The Case on which the verdict is being given.
When the event occurs.
Where the event takes place.
This FE indicates the basis in law of a verdict.
The Circumstances under which the verdict was reached.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Judge acts.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Judge returns a particular verdict.
This FE identifies an action that the Judge performs in order to return the verdict.
The Explanation for the verdict given.

name: Verification
d: An Inspector attains a degree of certainty in the Unconfirmed_content, generally by inspecting some evidence.

ex.t: This note confirms my suspicions.

fes.d: The individual or individuals that ascertain that the Unconfirmed_content is true.
An open proposition that the Inspector decides by examining evidence. It is usually a propostion put forward which some parties would disbelieve or contest.

Any description of the verification which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Inspector that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action performed by the Inspector by which the Inspector manages to establish the truth of the Unconfirmed_content.
The amount of certainty which the Inspector achieves after the process of verification.
The state of affairs that the Inspector hopes to bring about by going through the verification.
The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Inspector verifies the Unconfirmed_content:
A tool or instrument used by the Inspector in the verification process.
The conditions under which the the verification will occur.
This FE describes a characteristic of the verification event.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
This FE describes the Time at which the verification event takes place.
This FE describes where the verificiation event takes place.
The reason for the state of the verification event.

name: Version_sequence
d: An entity goes through several versions, from initial to final.

ex.t: This is my first draft.

fes.d: The Item is one version among several versions (which may or may not yet exist), progressively getting closer to a final version.
The degree of the distance the Item is from the final version.

name: Victim_operated_IED
d: An improvised explosive device, the Bomb, is placed so as to be hidden from view or disguised as something not harmful. It is rigged to detonate when triggered by actions of an intended Victim. Possible triggering actions include stepping on a pressure-sensitive plate, activating a trip-wire, or moving an object which activates a spring-loaded device.

ex.t: We hit a VOIED and the lead truck was destroyed.

fes.d: The explosive device which activates when set off by the victim.
The type of activity that the Bomb is generally involved in. Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.
This FE indicates what subtype the Bomb belongs to.
The substance that makes up the Bomb.
The person who sets the bomb.
This FE identifies a part of the Bomb. This includes permanent, obligatory parts and mere attachments.
The term used to refer to a Bomb.
The time at which the Bomb comes into existence.
The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Bomb.
A description or characteristic of the Bomb.
The Victim inadvertantly causes the Bomb to denotate.

name: Violence
d: The words in this frame describe acts (or situations characterized by acts) that cause injury or harm. The acts may involve an Aggressor or Cause injuring a Victim, or Aggressors causing each other harm.

ex.t: Research on whether concealed carry laws increase gun violence among gang members has been inconclusive.
They committed brutality against innocent civilians.
The storm's violence last week came without warning and caused unprecedented damage to costal regions.

fes.d: The Aggressor is the person causing the Victim's injury.
The Victim is the being or entity that is injured.
Degree is the degree to which violence is done.
The Manner in which the Aggressor acts upon the Victim.
An intentional action performed by the Aggressor that results in the committing of a violent act.
Place identifies the place where the violence occurs.
Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.
This FE is any object used to cause the injury.
Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.
This FE identifies the event in which the harm is caused.
A fact or action related to one of the participants in the volient act that the Aggressor responds to in doing violence.
Iterations refers to the number of times the violent act occurs.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that inflicts harm on the Victim
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the violent event and any of its participants.
How often the violence occurs.
The Aggressors commit acts of violence upon each other.

name: Visit_host
d: A Visitor matches location with a Host by going to a place strongly associated with a Host, the Host_location (often a place of residence, employment, or government), in order to achieve a Purpose. The Host allows the use of his/her resources. The visit is often social in nature.

fes.d: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.
An individual that allows the use of his or her resources for the benefit of the Visitor.
The activity that is enabled by the hospitality of the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.
The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.
The location associated with the Host, where the Visitor arrives at and remains during the visit.

name: Visit_host_arrival
d: The Visitor arrives at the Host_location to visit the Host.

fes.d: The Visitor goes to the Host

Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Visitor moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Host_location. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.
The Host welcomes the Visitor as a guest. The location strongly associated with the Host serves as the goal of the Visitor's motion.

A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Visitor arrives.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Visitor arrives at the Host or Host_location.
The Host_location is a location associated with the Host, and is commonly the place of residence or employment of the Host.
The place where the arrival event occurs.

name: Visit_host_departure
d: A Visitor departs from a Host_location after having visited a Host.

fes.d: The Visitor departs from the location of the Host.
The Visitor departs from the Host_location, a location strongly associated with the Host.
Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'.
This FE labels any expression which tells where the Visitor ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels.
The action of the Visitor which results in their departure.
This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Visitor is moving.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.
The distance that the Visitor has traveled.
The Time at which the departure takes place.
>The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Visitor departs from the Source.
The Host allows the Visitor to use his/her resources, and to remain temporarily at the Host_location.

name: Visit_host_stay
d: A Visitor is located with a Host for a visit.

fes.d: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.

The Host welcomes the Visitor to his/her location, with which he/she is permanently associated. The Host allows the Visitor use of resources to accomplish a Purpose. During the visit, the Visitor matches location with the Host.
A state (of the Visitor) that results as a consequence of the Visitor being situated with the Host.
The activity that is enabled by the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.
The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.
The time at which a visit is made.
The amount of time that the Visitor spends with the Host.
Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (the same way) or in terms of states of the Visitor that affect the action.
A description of the position of the Visitor during the visit.
An action of the Visitor that enables their visit.
The number of instances of the described event.
A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.
The Host_location is the location permanently associated with the Host, and which the Visitor stays at temporarily for the acheiving of some Purpose.

name: Visiting
d: An Agent matches location with an Entity in order to fulfill some Purpose. Quite often, the Purpose is social- or entertainment-oriented.

ex.t: I ca n't remember how many times he visited ! DNI
Now she was on an inspection visit .
You have to visit your parents every once in a while .

fes.d: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.
The physical entity that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose. During the visit, the Agent matches location with the Entity.
A state (of the Agent) that results as a consequence of the Agent being situated at the Entity.
The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.
The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.
The time at which a visit is made.
The amount of time that the Agent spends with the Entity.
Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (the same way) or in terms of states of the Agent that affect the action.
A description of the position of the Agent during the visit.
An action of the Agent that enables their visit.
The number of instances of the described event.
A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.
A description of the state of Agent or Entity during the action.

name: Visiting_scenario
d: An Agent and an Entity become co-located. The Agent in pursuit of a Purpose, and temporarily remains with the Entity to fulfill this Purpose and then departs again, usually back to their Normal_location.

fes.d: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.
A place that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose.
The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.
The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

name: Visiting_scenario_arrival
d: An Agent arrives at a location that should help them achieve their Purpose. This situation is point-of-view-neutral.

fes.d: Agent is the object that moves under its own power.

Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Agent moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

Goal is any expression that tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Although always conceptually present and specific, Goal may sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent.

A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent arrives.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent arrives at the Goal.
The place where the visiting occurs

name: Visiting_scenario_departing
d: An Agent departs from the Source, normally bound for their normal location. This is a point-of-view-neutral conception of the departure.

fes.d: This is the individual which moves under their own power.
Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Agent, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context.
Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path.
This FE labels any expression which tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels.
The action of the Agent which results in their departure.
This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Agent is moving.
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
The distance that the Agent has traveled.
The Time at which the departure takes place.
The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent departs from the Source.

name: Visiting_scenario_stay
d: An Agent matches location with an Entity in order to fulfill some Purpose. Quite often, the Purpose is social- or entertainment-oriented. This scene is point-of-view-neutral.

fes.d: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.
The physical entity that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose. During the visit, the Agent matches location with the Entity.
A state (of the Agent) that results as a consequence of the Agent being situated at the Entity.
The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.
The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.
The time at which a visit is made.
The amount of time that the Agent spends at the Entity.
Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (the same way) or in terms of states of the Agent that affect the action.
A description of the position of the Agent during the visit.
An action of the Agent that enables their visit.
The number of instances of the described event.
A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.

name: Visitor_and_host
d: A Visitor and a Host become co-located at a location strongly associated with the Host. The Visitor is allowed by the Host to use the Host's location and/or resources for the achievement of a Purpose. The visit is often social in nature.

fes.d: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.
An individual that allows the use of his or her resources for the benefit of the Visitor.
The activity that is enabled by the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.
The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

A location strongly associated with (in the territory of) the Host, often a place of residence, government, or employment. The Visitor is allowed onto the Host_location and may be invited to make use of it or resources contained within it.

name: Visitor_arrival
d: An Agent arrives at a Goal that should enable their Purpose.

fes.d: Agent is the object that moves under its own power.

Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Agent moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.
Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

Goal is any expression that tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Although always conceptually present and specific, Goal may sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent.

A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent arrives.

The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent arrives at the Goal.
The place where the arrival occurs.

name: Visitor_departure
d: After a visit is complete, the Agent departs the Source, normally bound for their normal haunts.

fes.d: This is the individual which moves under their own power.
Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Agent, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context.
Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path.
This FE labels any expression which tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source.

Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels.
The action of the Agent which results in their departure.
This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Agent is moving.
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
The distance that the Agent has traveled.
The Time at which the departure takes place.
The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent departs from the Source.

name: Visitor_scenario
d: An Agent leaves their Normal_location and matches location with an Entity in pursuit of a Purpose. The Agent temporarily remains with the Entity to fulfil this Purpose and then departs again, usually back to the Normal_location.

fes.d: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.
A place that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose.
The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.
The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

name: Vocalizations
d: This frame is concerned with the sounds produced by animate entities by means of their vocal tracts. Descriptions of sounds from artifacts meant to emulate such sounds, or to act as vocalizing animals or people, are also treated here as figurative language.

ex.t: He woke up because of the cries of the crows outside.

fes.d: An entity that is construed as a single point source emitting sound.
The place from which the sound emanates.

The location at which sound is produced. This FE differs from Location_of_sound_source in that it does not highlight the sound's spreading from its source to the perceiver's location, which is usually indicated by the preposition "from".
The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, that is the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source.
Certain properties of the sound relating to its production, loudness, etc may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: loudly, shrilly, etc.
Expressions that indicate the loudness of the sound.
This FE idntifies the Explanation that the Sound_source produces the sound. Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.
The Path along which the sound travels away from the Sound_source.
How often the Vocalization event occurs.

name: Volubility
d: These words describe the size of message that a Speaker is judged by a (usually unexpressed) Judge to give, either in a specific occasion or Topic or in general. As in other communication frames, Medium may also be expressed.

ex.t: Graham is very shy with most people, but he gets very chatty with Mr. Roberts.
Evelyn was very voluble on the rights of women.

fes.d: This is the person who is characterized as talkative, reticent etc. It is usually the External Argument:
The Company in which the Speaker exhibits a certain communicative behavior. In this frame, Company occurs in PP Complements headed by with:

Text is rarely expressed because the quantity of information given is the focus of the frame, rather than the information content. Texts can occur as NP objects, but cannot be either direct quotes or complement clauses.
This FE is the Topic on which much or little information is communicated. Topic is far more frequent than Message in this frame.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used to communicate, as in other Communication frames. It is usually a PP Complement headed by in or on.
Degree to which the Speaker withholds or does not withhold information and conversation.
Manner in which the speaker is reticent or voluble.
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Wagering
d: A Gambler commits an Asset to a prediction that an Uncertain_situation will have a particular Outcome (or class of outcomes). He or she loses the Asset if the prediction ends up being incorrect, and gains it back plus additional winnings if the prediction ends up correct.

ex.t: He bet $30 on the horse race.

fes.d: The person who wages the Asset on a certain Outcome.
The place where the Gambler makes the wager.
The time when the Gambler makes the wager.
Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Gambler which is lost if the Gambler loses the wager.
The Frequency with which the Gambler makes wagers.
The desired action or goal that the Gambler hopes to bring about.
An Explanation for why the Gambler has put the Asset up in a wager.
The number of times that the Gambler makes wagers.
The Circumstances indicates the state of affairs under which the Gambler makes a wager.
The Gambler intends for his/her actions to benefit Beneficiary in some way.
The Gambler predicts that a certain Outcome will hold.
The Gambler predicts how an Uncertain_situation will resolve.

name: Waiting
d: A Protagonist delays a planned action because they cannot or do not want to proceed until an Expected_event occurs. The Expected_event may be evoked by reference to a Salient_entity that participates in it. If a Salient_entity is expressed, the Expected_event is typically the arrival of the Salient_entity at the Place where the Protagonist is located. Although in both frames a Protagonist/Agent is not performing some desired action for some period of time, the use of wait.v in this frame is different from that in Holding_off_on in that Waiting prominently portrays a future event that will allow the Protagonist to proceed (with doing something), whereas Holding_off_on does not necessarily imply that there is some event or state-of-affairs that will allow the Agent to proceed, rather focussing on the action that the Agent is not yet taking.

ex.t: The cat waited on top of the washer as Elmer popped the lid off the can of cat food and then pounded the can's contents onto the plate
The family was furious that their 84-year-old dad had to wait 52 hours in the emergency room.

fes.d: The sentient being who cannot proceed with their planned activities until a Salient_entity has arrived or an Expected_event has occurred.
A concrete or abstract entity that the Protagonist expects to participate in an Expected_event, typically that of arriving at the Place of the Protagonist.
The time period during which the Protagonist is waiting.
The location in which the Protagonist is waiting.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the waiting to its end.

Any description of the waiting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (patiently, anxiously).
The Expected_event is an event that needs to take place or a state that needs to begin to hold before the Protagonist can proceed with their planned activities.
The point in time, defined either as a clock time or in terms of an event that takes place, at which the Protagonist ends the waiting.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the waiting event logically follows.
This FE describes the Protagonist as being in some state during the waiting.
An action that the Protagonist intends to accomplish by waiting.

Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co-participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

name: Waking_up
d: A Sleeper transitions from a state of consciousness where they are largely unaware of their environment to a wakeful state.

ex.t: William awoke from a dream.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
This FE identifies the sleeping entity.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
This describes the state out of which the Sleeper awakens.
The Manner in which the Sleeper awakens.
The state of the Sleeper upon waking up.
The New_situation is the situation the Sleeper finds him or herself in upon awaking.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
This FE indicates an instance of the Waking_up event within an iterated series of similar events or states.
The reason for which the Sleeper awakes from the Sleep_state.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Want_suspect
d: A Suspect has been investigated and has a warrant issued for his or her arrest on certain Charges.

ex.t: Bill is wanted on murder charges.

fes.d: The Suspect is suspected of having committed a crime by the authorities who want the Suspect to enter the criminal process.
The Charges are the offenses the Suspect will be accused of committing.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Warning
d: A Speaker warns an Addressee by giving a Message that describes an undesirable situation that may affect the Addressee. The warning may alternatively be described as about Topic pertaining to the undesirable situation, or issued via a specific Medium.

ex.t: Jackson warned me that the weather could change quickly, but I guess I didn't really believe him.
We alerted officials about the possibility of containment failure as soon as we realized it could happen.
They issued the warning to only those with the highest security clearence. DNI

fes.d: The Speaker produces the Message to alert the Addressee as to possible danger.
The Addressee receives the warning from the Speaker.
The Message is the communication produced by the Speaker.
The Topic is a general description of the content of the Message.
The Manner describes the way in which the Speaker delivers the warning.
The Means describes the way the Speaker accomplishes the task of warning the Addressee.
This frame element is the Medium in which the Message is expressed.
The time period during which the Speaker warns the Addressee.
The location in which the Speaker warns Addressee.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Message is expressed (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
A characteristic or description of the telling event or of the Speaker or Addressee.
This FE indicates the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Waver_between_options
d: A Cognizer faces a choice on some Issue. They have several Options available but keep changing their mind between Option_1 and Option_2. The Cognizer may in fact act on their choice at some point but they need not; the Options can simply be considered for some time with one being favored for a while and then the other.

ex.t: Dave Hayes wavered about moving to California because so many of his friends are in Baltimore.
He had wavered between half a dozen places; it was pure chance that he had chosen Marvis Bay.
In any event, I still go back and forth on what I want to do.

fes.d: The Cognizer is the person who repeatedly changes their mind about which of the Options to choose.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which it logically follows that the Cognizer keeps changing their mind about the Issue.
The Options are the alternative courses of action or the alternative physical or concrete entities that the Cognizer can choose from.
This FE identifies the Place where the Cognizer keeps changing their mind between the Options that present themselves.
This FE denotes the Time interval during which the Cognizer keeps changing their mind about which of the Options to select.

Any description of the selecting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of the Cognizer that also affect the action.
The Issue is a question about a course of action or a choice between items.

When there is an explicitly separate construal of the Options, Option_1 is the first-mentioned alternative, typically in the form of a from-PP. When it is clear that the Cognizer actually acted on their choice, Option_1 is the alternative they embraced first before pursuing Option_2.

When there is an explicitly separate construal of the Options, Option_2 is the second-mentioned alternative, typically in the form of a to-PP. When it is clear that the Cognizer actually acted on their choice, Option_2 is the alternative they embraced after abandoning Option_1.

In the cases where the Cognizer does not act on their choice, the Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cognizer's deliberations to the end. In situations where the Cognizer does act on the Options, the Duration denotes the length of the interval during which the Cognizer repeatly changes from one option to the other.
This FE describes the number of times within a given period that the Cognizer wavers.
The Degree to which the Cognizer wavers.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Wealthiness
d: A Person or Institution is being described in terms of their wealthiness, in other words the amount of money in their possession.

ex.t: Jess is very rich.
The university is wealthy.

fes.d: The individual or individuals whose wealthiness is being described.
A group which has (or lacks) possession of some resource.
The degree of wealthiness (or poverty) of the Person or Institution.
A characterization of the entity (usually money) that the Person (or Institution possesses.

name: Weapon
d: A Weapon is an artifact created specifically to cause harm or damage. In some cases, a Use, Material of construction, Part or Type may be more narrowly specified.

ex.t: Did you, or did you not, fire this gun with intent to harm my client?
Cyra tried to swing her sword to parry, but it was to heavy.
I investigated a specialist precious metal firearms manufacturer.

fes.d: An entity prototypically used by a Wielder to cause damage.
The type of activity that the Weapon is generally involved in. Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Weapon belongs to.
The substance that makes up the Weapon.
The person (or other sentient entity) that is using the Weapon.
This FE identifies a part of the Weapon. This includes permanent, obligatory parts and mere attachments.
The term used to refer to an Weapon.
The time at which a Weapon comes into existence.
The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Weapon.
A description or characteristic of the Weapon.

name: Wearing
d: The words in this frame refer to what Clothing the Wearer (or a specific Body_part of the Wearer) has on. Many targets incorporate the Clothing item, and some targets describe the state of not wearing something (when it might be expected). NB: There is a very common metonymy in which characteristics of the clothing stand for the clothing itself, such as Such sentences should be tagged METAPHOR on the sentence level.

ex.t: I had on the most ridiculous monkey-suit you could imagine.
These two losers were wearing bras on their heads!
Do you think anyone would notice if I went topless?

fes.d: The person whose clothing is under discussion.
This FE identifies the Clothing that the Wearer wears.
The body part of the Wearer which is covered by the Clothing.
A characterization of how completely the clothing status holds.
A characterization of the impression given by the Wearer's clothing status.
The time at or during which the Wearer has the Clothing on.
NB: This FE will be mapped to Intended_wearing_location The location that the Wearer exits while wearing the Clothing.
The location whose characteristics or state the Clothing of the Wearer was intended to suit. This FE is only possible with wear.v.
The state-of-affairs that the Wearer wishes to bring about.
The location relative to the body of the Wearer that the Clothing occupies. Note that in many cases, the location is defined relative to other clothing.

name: Weather
d: Ambient conditions of temperature, precipitation, windiness, and sunniness pertain at a certain Place and Time. Further Specification of the conditions that pertain may also be indicated.

ex.t: A blustery storm blew in.
There was a thick blizzard last night.
An armada of hailstorms swept through the region.

fes.d: This FE identifies the Place where the weather occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the weather occurs.
This FE identifies a further Specification of the weather conditions.

name: Wholes_and_parts
d: A Whole is made up of multiple Parts, which themselves may not be independent of each other or of the Whole. Wholes_and_parts is contrasted with Set_relation, where the Whole is simply a set of a number of (usually independent) parts.

fes.d: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.
The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.
Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
The Time at which the inclusion relation holds.
The location at which the inclusion relation holds.

name: Willingness
d: A Cognizer would engage in an Activity if asked or otherwise prompted to do so.

ex.t: The court is willing to depart from the usual range of sentencing .
The Nicaraguan National Assembly has been reluctant to destroy the remaining stockpile.
The Turks are in grudging acceptance of terms set by EU.

fes.d: The Cognizer is the individual that is willing to engage in the Activity.
The Activity is what the Cognizer would do under certain circumstances.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Cognizer's willingness logically follows.
This FE identifies the Place where the Cognizer is willing to engage in the Activity.
This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer is willing to engage in the Activity.
The state of affairs that the Cognizer wants to achieve by being willing to engage in the Activity.
A modifier expressing the deviation of the willingness from the norm or from the value for another Cognizer.
This FE denotes the number of times the Cognizer is willing per some unit of time.

name: Win_prize
d: A Competitor claims a Prize as a result of the outcome of their participation in a Competition. Competition is meant to be construed broadly to include cases where there is no skill involved as well as cases where there is no ranking of participants, and indeed does not require that there be multiple pariticipants or a definable end of game, as in the case of winning prizes at a carnival game. All that is required to be this kind of Competition is that there is some way of determining whether a Competitor will receive the Prize. The use of win.v in this frame is similar to the Finish_competition frame, but there are a number of differences. Firstly, Win_prize focuses on what the Competitor receives as a result of their participation in a process. Unlike Finish_competition, Win_prize does not necessarily give any information about how a Competitor ranked relative to other competitors, or even if there is any system of ranking of competitors, or any end of the process that is defined as winning or losing. Win_prize only requires a system for determining which Prize or prizes go to a Competitor, if any. That is why the opposite of "I won (something)" in Win_prize is not "I lost", but rather "I didn't win anything".

ex.t: We won a car in the raffle.

fes.d: The individual or individuals involved in the Competition.
A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Competitor afterward.
The amount by which the Competitor 's and Scores differ.
The rank (according to Score) that a Competitor acheives.
A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Competitor according to Score or Rank.
An action of the Competitor that results in the outcome of the Competition.

Any description of the Competitor which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Competitor that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
When the Competition takes place.
The location where the Competition takes place.
This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a Competition.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
The event in which the Competitor competes.
The reason why the Competitor wins the Competition.
The length of time from when winning events began to be repeated to when they stopped.
The individual that the Competitor has been competing against.
The state of the world when the Competitor wins the Competition.
The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.
The state-of-affairs that prevails as a result of the Competitor winning the Competition.
The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Competitor wins the Competition.
This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the winning event operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).
This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, or a description of the state-of-affairs introduced by the winning event.

name: Withdraw_from_participation
d: An individual that is scheduled to be a Participant, or already is a Participant in an Activity or an Organization, indicates that they will no not or no longer participate in that Activity or Organization. Note that the Organization often is one that is constituted by a treaty or agreement.

ex.t: The Moslem contingent had withdrawn from the EC talks on May 27.
The right-wing nationalist Tsomet Party formally withdrew from the ruling coalition.

fes.d: The individual or individuals that are engaged or are scheduled to be engaged in an Activity.
The event that the Participant is engaged in or was scheduled to be engaged in.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the withdrawing event logically follows.
This FE identifies the Place where the Participant ends the participation in the Activity.
This FE identifies the Time when the Participant ends their participation in the Activity.
The Organization is an intentionally formed human social group with some definite structure to which the Participant belongs.
The state-of-affairs that the Participant hopes to bring about by withdrawing
The act done by the Participant that accomplishes their withdrawal.
The document that the Participant uses to communicate their withdrawal.
A description of the attitude of the Participant which also affects the character of the withdrawal.

name: Within_distance
